in writing. i voted for this report because it strengthens once again the rules on the participation of european union citizens in european elections, both as candidates and as voters. the report also refers to the whole procedure for communicating the names of the candidates elected in the european elections, the legal framework governing the verification of their credentials, the way in which the statements they must make upon taking office are made, the resolution of disputes that may arise as a result of non-compliance with certain principles relating to the voting system in each member state (for example, non-compliance with quotas, where alternation between men and women is required on lists, etc.), and the deprivation of the right to vote and the exercise of electoral rights, which in some countries such as cyprus, denmark, malta, ireland and the united kingdom are different from those in most member states.
in writing. the high number of accidents involving non-resident drivers indicates that cross-border exchange of road traffic information needs to become a necessity. a common internal market entails rights and obligations assumed by all citizens of the union. thus, drivers of other nationalities must be treated equally, regardless of where they are. access to a central database, which should not only cover deviations from traffic or parking rules, is essential. there are many cases where, following accidents in another state, the authorities are faced with the problem of identifying the domicile of the parties involved. i believe that the strengthening of the common system for verifying the validity of insurance policies should also be taken into account. i voted in favour of the proposal for a directive because i am convinced that the exchange of data on traffic offences will help to reduce the number of offences and improve safety on public roads.
in writing. i support the rapporteur's position that parliament should adopt a new directive on cross-border road fines in due course, in order to avoid a legal vacuum but also to guarantee the highest possible level of road safety in the member states. on the other hand, even citizens, who are generally unhappy when they receive a notification of a traffic offence, also consider it a positive thing that all eu citizens will be treated equally, regardless of where the vehicle is registered. it should also be borne in mind that the directive aims to achieve the objective of reducing the number of deaths caused by road accidents by 50% by 2020.
in writing. i voted in favour of this report because its stated objectives are to support citizens and road users in the union by improving the cross-border exchange of information on road traffic offences and by improving cooperation between the relevant authorities. the new directive, which retains much of the content of directive 2011/82/eu, aims to reduce the number of deaths by 50% by 2020, in addition to the objective of the old directive to reduce the number of injuries from road traffic accidents by 40% by 2020.
in writing. the senegalese commercial port of dakar is of international importance due to its geographical position. the ec negotiated, on the basis of a mandate from the council, on behalf of the eu, the renewal of the agreement between the government of the republic of senegal and the eec on fishing off the coast of senegal, which entered into force on 1 june 1981 (renewed in 2002 and expired in 2006), and of a protocol setting out the fishing opportunities and the financial contribution. on 25 april 2014, the negotiators initialled a new draft agreement and protocol which complies with the common fisheries policy (cfp) regulation for sustainable fisheries partnership agreements (sfps). i support the conclusion by the council of the agreement and protocol ((12812/14 c8-0276/2014 senegal 2014/0238 ((nle)) aimed at creating a new framework for cooperation between the european union and the republic of senegal, which will ensure: reasonable economic conditions taking into account available fishing opportunities, a basis for the conservation and sustainable exploitation of the relevant fish stocks, adequate support and sufficient conditions for the local fisheries sector, and the opportunity to develop the local fishing industry in partnership with eu vessels and to supply the eu market with quality fishery products.
in writing. — senegal is a key trading partner for the european union for a number of reasons including its strategic location and its efforts in the fight against illegal fishing. i support full commitment by the eu to promote our bilateral agreements. i consequently welcome, eight years after expiration of the last protocol, adoption of this new protocol to allow 38 vessels, fishing mainly tuna, to once again operate in the senegalese eez, subject to eur 8 690 000 of compensation over the duration of the protocol. the protocol is in strict compliance with the principles of sustainability and good governance and will provide an opportunity to develop the local fishing industry in partnership with the eu vessels. additionally it will provide the eu market with quality fish products and will not add excessive pressure on the fish stocks. i am convinced that its implementation is in the interests of both parties.
in writing. i voted in favour of this report because the new protocol between the republic of senegal and the european union has created a new framework for economic cooperation, which is beneficial for both partners. the new partnership commits the eu to employing 20% of senegalese or acp seamen on vessels fishing in senegalese waters, thus also contributing to the increase in the number of jobs in that region. the satellite monitoring of vessels will also help local authorities to combat illegal, unreported and unregulated fishing.
in writing. i voted in favour of this report today not because it is my report, but because this type of sustainable fisheries partnership agreement between the european union and third countries is a step forward. this new type of agreement is based on the new common fisheries policy, is developed and can be changed in line with the latest scientific information on fish stocks, provides for ways in which such agreements can help the labour market and industry in third countries, and, not least, can be suspended and/or terminated for breaches of commitments to combat illegal, unreported and unregulated fishing, and/or human rights violations. these guidelines should be part of all future sustainable fisheries agreements between the eu and third countries, and i hope that this will happen.
in writing. fisheries relations between the european union and the republic of senegal date back to 1981. however, no protocols in this area have been concluded or revised since 2006, leading to a stagnation of these relations. the renewal of the sustainable fisheries partnership agreement was therefore necessary. the new agreement repeals and replaces the existing agreement and has as its main objective to provide an updated framework which takes into account the priorities of the reformed common fisheries policy. the agreement is accompanied by a protocol setting out the fishing opportunities for european union vessels in senegalese waters. the european parliament report supports the conclusion of this partnership agreement, stressing that its signature will be of particular benefit to both the european union and the republic of senegal. eu-flagged vessels will thus be able to increase their economic activity in the region, new jobs will be created both in the republic of senegal and in the european union, and the fishing industry will benefit and develop from this new partnership. i voted in favour of this report.
mr president, i voted for this because we must condemn the use of torture by all means. those methods cannot be tolerated. moreover, they fail to prevent terrorist attacks. the climate of impunity regarding the cia programme still represents a menace towards the values of justice, equity and dignity on which our societies are built. we cannot forget that the concepts of democracy, human rights and rule of law are the core priorities of our society and that the issue of security should not put our values aside. member states must conduct independent, in-depth and impartial investigations on these allegations on transportation and illegal detention of prisoners in european countries in order to establish if there have been instances of complicity by some persons and to cooperate in fining and prosecuting the perpetrators of human rights violations.
in writing. i voted against this resolution because its content has moved very far from what was originally intended. the debate on the same subject last year would have been enough to raise an alarm about the values of fundamental human rights and freedoms that the european union defends today, given the excessive politicization of this subject. cia detention centers are a reality that cannot be disputed. but we must not lose sight of the fact that the information we have on what happened in these prisons is contained in a report presented to the us senate, but not owned by all political forces, and there are doubts about its contents. beyond the certainty of what happened, torture and degrading and inhuman treatment cannot be accepted in any democratic society. to do otherwise would only turn the victims into stones, and their guilt would be no less. states around the world need to be concerned about the safety of their citizens so that events like the one in new york in 2001, or the one in paris in 2015, never happen again.
in writing. together with the epp group i voted against this resolution. i am absolutely against torture and at the same time i condemn the death of over 3,000 people in the terrorist attacks of september 11, 2001. but the solution is not to point fingers at the american authorities, nor to treat them with superiority, hiding behind a cardboard screen behind which human rights are also being violated in europe. i want to remind everyone that we are at a crucial moment, the negotiations on the transatlantic treaty must be completed by the end of this year. the recent events in paris have demonstrated that we must find together a common strategy and methods to fight terrorism. i insist that we strengthen cooperation with the united states at this time. we want to be partners with them, but we are adopting a resolution with a similar content to an earlier resolution on the same subject. it's not the right solution. in addition, the u.s. senate has found and condemned acts of torture, so they are publicly debated to never happen again. i suggest we focus on what we have to do from now on.
in writing. i voted against this resolution for the following reasons: i do not think that in the current international context it is necessary, urgent or relevant to set up another commission of inquiry into cia detention centres. the us authorities are investigating and prosecuting violations of law committed under the cia's rendition and secret detention programme and have shown a willingness to cooperate with all requests from member states in this regard. member states' investigations into allegations of human rights violations in the cia programme must be based on legal evidence and respect for national judicial systems and applicable european law. i welcome the decrees issued by the us presidency ensuring that the us complies with national and international legislation prohibiting torture and cruel, degrading and inhuman treatment. i believe that the report of the us senate select committee on intelligence is a positive step in addressing the criticisms of the programme and demonstrates the willingness of the democratic political system to publicly and honestly take responsibility for the activities of the cia. it is absurd that in the current international context we do not understand the need to be united in the fight against terrorism and in the face of the danger posed by the ukrainian conflict.
in writing. i voted in favour of this resolution, which follows the publication in december of the us senate report, which revealed that in several eu member states, the authorities, as well as security and intelligence agents, had allegedly collaborated with the cia for its secret detention and extraordinary rendition programme.
in writing. — the european parliament has managed to produce a good document and i have voted in favour of it. the european union in general, and romania in particular, where i have led the investigation committee, needs to preserve a firm safeguard of our laws and values. at the same time, we want to maintain good cooperation with the usa, as long as it is understood that in the future their intelligence services will take more care to respect those values of ours.
mr president, i fully support tackling terrorism at its roots through a preventive, comprehensive and holistic approach. the best way to prevent these attacks is not through torture and violation of human rights but through education and social policies that avoid racism and other pretexts for exclusion. i do not believe that the fight against terrorism should undermine our principles of freedom of movement, human rights and the rule of law. i would like to highlight the need to share databases and intelligence on terrorism and exchange information between member states. this proposal, stated in the resolution, should be carried out without delay, as well as the creation of an anti-terrorism european intelligence agency to better counter potential terrorist attacks. that is why i voted for it.
in writing. security is one of the rights guaranteed by the eu charter of fundamental rights. the union is facing a constantly evolving terrorist threat which, over the last decade, has severely affected a number of member states in attacks that have targeted both human beings and the values and freedoms on which the union is founded. an estimated 3,500 to 5,000 eu citizens left their homes to become foreign fighters as war and violence erupted in syria, iraq and libya. in order to strengthen the security of our citizens, to defend the fundamental values of freedom, democracy and human rights, to respect international law, i support the need for a multidimensional approach to preventing and combating terrorism, as terrorism is a global threat that needs to be addressed at local, national, european and global levels. they also support measures to tackle the root causes of terrorism and radicalisation leading to violent extremism, the implementation and review of existing law enforcement measures, eu internal security and eu law enforcement capabilities, such as the adoption of an eu external strategy to combat international terrorism.
in writing. i believe that a key dimension of the fight against terrorism must be the development of policies aimed at protecting and supporting victims and their families, and therefore i believe that all member states must properly implement the rules on the rights, support and protection of victims of crime, thereby supporting citizens' fundamental right to security and freedom.
in writing. i support the resolution calling on the eu to promote an international partnership against terrorism and to cooperate with regional actors to counter the terrorist threat - from tackling the causes and preventing radicalisation, to annihilating sources of funding and training opportunities. the counter-terrorism strategy must, in my view, be based on a more intensive exchange of information and operational cooperation between national authorities to stop the movement of terrorism suspects and the illicit trafficking of arms. particular attention is needed to combat terrorist propaganda and recruitment online, which is why i support the call for internet operators and communication platform operators to cooperate with the competent authorities, as terrorist organisations increasingly use the internet for communication and planning attacks. i believe that the new roadmap that the european parliament is asking the commission and the council to adopt to combat terrorism must set out a common european strategy to respond to the terrorist threat. in this regard, it is urgent to close the legislative and operational loopholes that facilitate the flow of jihadist fighters. it is worrying that only 50% of information on terrorism and organised crime is reported by eu countries to eurojust and europol. i therefore support the creation of a european counter-terrorism platform within europol.
in writing. i voted in favour of the resolution on counter-terrorism measures. i support the adoption of a european strategy against radical networks, online recruitment and terrorist propaganda. we must insist on combating the financing of money laundering and organised crime by these groups. furthermore, we need to ask internet and online communications companies to cooperate with governments, law enforcement and civil society to combat the use of internet and social networks for terrorist attack preparation, while ensuring that freedom of expression and the right to privacy are respected. i agree that we must not give up the schengen area, but we must encourage member states to strengthen document and person checks in suspicious cases, to use data on persons from the schengen information system and to carry out fact-based checks when suspicious persons enter or leave the european union. romania protects the union's external border for some 2 000 km, thus playing a vital role in protecting union citizens.
in writing. i voted in favour of this resolution for the following reasons. eu citizens need, now more than ever, a coherent counter-terrorism strategy with concrete, immediately applicable measures that are profoundly proactive rather than reactive in addressing conflicts. such a strategy must also address the root causes of radicalisation and combat poverty, marginalisation, discrimination, corruption. it is necessary for member states to invest in education, rehabilitation, integration, social inclusion, dialogue, equality, tolerance and understanding between different cultures and religions. i welcome and support the ep's commitment to work towards the finalisation of a single passenger list directive by the end of 2015 at the latest. this instrument will allow for an efficient exchange of relevant information and enhanced border controls. the adoption of the updated eu legal framework for combating money laundering, the implementation of which will lead to the blocking of important sources of funding for terrorist organisations, is welcomed. i would stress that the lack of concrete, coordinated and effective cooperation involving all relevant actors - member states, european and national intelligence and police structures - will lead to an unprecedented scale of activity by terrorist organisations.
in writing. this resolution was in response to the growing need to try to eradicate the scourge called terrorism. recent events in paris have shown that the european union is facing a constantly evolving terrorist threat. i voted for this resolution because it underlines the need to tackle the root causes of terrorism and radicalisation leading to violent extremism, but also to maintain the eu's internal security and law enforcement capabilities, while adopting an eu external strategy to combat international terrorism.
in writing. — i have voted for the best possible text of this very important resolution. the spectre of terrorism is hanging now more than ever over the eu and we have to have the vision and courage to take all needed measures, at home and abroad, to prevent and combat such acts and persons, while at the same time safeguarding that which makes up the essence of europe, our values, liberties and rights.
in writing. the advent of the internet has revolutionized traditional communication models. unfettered access to information has brought numerous economic benefits and contributed to technological progress. the inventor of the world wide web, tim bernes-lee, argued that the internet was more of a social creation, designed to help people work together. the social impact created by non-discriminatory access to knowledge and the availability of a global information resource has at the same time required more responsibility and transparency in the use of the internet. i believe that the renewal of the mandate of the internet governance forum would provide more confidence to users and guarantee the veracity of information content. strengthening the security of cyber infrastructure will contribute to the development of electronic commerce and strengthen consumers' secure access to electronic transactions. i support the resolution on the renewal of the mandate of this forum, as i am convinced that through its mandate it will provide solutions for the stability and security of the internet.
in writing. the internet governance forum (igf) has the role and function to discuss a wide range of internet governance issues and, where appropriate, to make recommendations to the international community, based on the mandate given by the world summit on the information society (wsis) on the organisation of forums for democratic, transparent and multilateral political dialogue. i would stress that the fruitful exchanges that took place within the igf provide practical lessons, particularly on the regulatory aspects of electronic communications and on data security and privacy issues. i support the renewal of the igf's mandate by the un general assembly and the strengthening of its resources, as well as the need for a coordinated european position on internet governance, namely strengthening the sustainability of the multilateral model by making national, regional and international actors and processes more inclusive, transparent and accountable.
in writing. — i voted in favour of the renewal of the mandate of the internet governance forum, which is a multi-stakeholder forum for policy dialogue on issues of internet governance. although the renewal of the mandate is a consensual subject, i must emphasise the importance of the work of this institution. it promotes open and transparent discussions between stakeholders from all over the world, and facilitates a common understanding of how to maximise internet opportunities and address risks and challenges that may arise. it is important for the european parliament to continue to participate with a substantial delegation in future meetings.
in writing. — the internet has already transformed the world, but i am convinced that transformation is only at its very beginning. future regulation must make sure the internet remains open and truly global (i.e. not ‘nationalised’). its management should therefore be dealt with accordingly. with this in mind, i supported this resolution extending the mandate of the internet governance forum (igf) to continue guiding the development of the ‘net’. i hope that in a un-sanctioned setting (as is this wide forum – the igf) the global character of the internet will be preserved, and the process of thinking about its future will be marked by inclusiveness, transparency and accountability.
in writing. we welcome and vote for this resolution which comes to underline once again the importance of the role of the internet both globally and in the lives of each of us. the internet is a fundamental pillar of the digital single market, thus contributing to the development of the economy, trade, cultural exchanges, human interaction, but also democracy and access to information, as one of the rights of a modern, progressive and democratic society.
in writing. the objective of the internet governance forum (igf) is to fulfil the mandate of the world summit on the information society (wsis) in terms of organising forums for democratic, transparent and multilateral political dialogue. the main role and function of the igf is to discuss a wide range of internet governance issues and, where appropriate, to make recommendations to the international community. in 2015, the igf's mandate will expire, and the un must therefore renew its mandate to allow the internet governance forum to continue its role. i stress the need for a strong igf to reach a compromise between stakeholders and to support an independent, inclusive and neutral internet. the resolution supports net neutrality, worldwide internet access, support for online and offline rights, and expresses concern about the attitude of some states that censor and restrict internet access. i would stress that parliament should continue to participate in future igf meetings with a substantial delegation in order to contribute effectively to the formulation, together with the member states and the commission, of an eu approach to internet governance.
in writing. the internet has become an extremely important element of innovation, economic growth, trade, democracy, cultural diversity and human rights in today's society. the figures show that the internet is currently contributing about 4% to european gdp, and by the end of next year it will be contributing almost 6%. if we add to these concrete figures the fact that the internet has become an essential means of spreading democracy, of defending fundamental human rights, which cannot be translated into concrete figures, but is extremely important, it becomes all the more relevant why it is important to renew the mandate of the internet governance forum. there is a direct link, as seen in some countries, between internet access and the level of democracy and the rule of law. the internet governance forum can help increase internet access worldwide, which will directly lead to increased democracy in these countries. the forum's mission is to continue its efforts to ensure the legal protection of net neutrality, which is an indispensable condition for guaranteeing freedom of information and expression, stimulating economic growth and employment, by developing innovation and business opportunities related to the internet.
the report from the commission to the european parliament and the council on the mandatory indication of the country of origin or place of provenance of meat used as an ingredient led me to vote in favour of this resolution. according to that report, the existing traceability systems in the european union are not adequate for the transmission of information on origin along the food chain. it is also underlined that 90% of the consumer respondents believe that the indication of origin on the product label is important. food safety must be a major concern for all actors involved in this process, and the lack of effective regulation to ensure clear traceability of the products that reach everyone's tables is a threat to our health. consumer distrust automatically generates a decrease in product consumption which will have a major negative impact on both large and small processors. we're all going to have to lose. clear legislation in this area is a safety belt for healthy living! let's not forget that before we are politicians, we are consumers.

in writing. according to a commission survey of smes, most of them change suppliers three or more times a year in order to guarantee the required level of raw materials and quality at an affordable price. i consider that the mandatory indication of the country of origin on the label would lead to an increase in the administrative burden for smes and a significant increase in production costs, as well as an increase in price pressure for farmers, 90% of which would be imposed on consumers.
in writing. a measure that generated heated debate within all political groups. i voted against the idea that the producers of a sausage should be obliged to list all the countries in which the meat used in that sausage was produced (for example). why would you do that? not to unfairly help industry avoid costs, at the expense of consumer misinformation, as some colleagues would say, quick to conclude. but to protect romania from stupid (and unmerited) prejudices, as was the case with horse meat, when not romanian producers cheated, but the label was hungerily glued to romania, as a kind of natural location of fraud. food safety and hygiene rules must be complied with by any producer in the eu, with or without the origin label. and if a producer wants to label the origin of the meat used, he can do so, voluntarily, without any hindrance, developing a direct and special link with his consumers. we're talking about protectionism masked behind some big talk about the consumer. the debate in plenary made almost clear the equal sign between origin and quality, and origin and fraud. which is unfair.
in writing. i voted in favour of this resolution, which was born of the need and desire of consumers to be correctly informed about the composition of processed foods in the meat products they consume, but also as a result of the recent scandals caused by the fraudulent substitution of beef for horse meat. country of origin labelling will become mandatory for unprocessed meat from pigs, sheep, goats and poultry from april 2015, and will become mandatory throughout the eu following the presentation by the ec of legislative proposals on the country of origin labelling of meat in processed foods.
in writing. the ep resolution on the indication of the country of origin on the labelling of meat in processed foods is necessary because it defends several principles indispensable for a healthy and transparent system in public nutrition: correct and transparent consumer information, eliminating fraud from the system and above all ensuring the public health of europeans at all costs. at the same time, i do not believe that mandatory labelling should be a process that is implemented abruptly, without giving smes in the meat industry time to adapt to the new requirements. my votes on the resolution and the amendments to it respected the principles i have mentioned above, but at the same time they were aimed at protecting consumers throughout europe from the uncontrollable price increases that the sudden implementation of mandatory labelling may have. in this respect, and as my vote reflects, i believe that voluntary labelling of products, including the country of origin, for a buffer period of time is the optimal solution to this problem. i am in favour of greater transparency and of correct information for consumers, but i do not believe that we should subject processed meat producers and traders to immediate additional costs, which are reflected in the final price of the products supplied.
in writing. the deterioration of the situation in the african, caribbean and pacific (acp) countries has created new concerns about the political and humanitarian situation in several acp regions. this text calls on the jpa to continue to monitor the situation in the acp countries in crisis and to pay more attention to the sensitive cadres in these countries. the acp states and the eu also called for a coordinated response to the ebola outbreak in west africa. i voted in favour of this report because conflict prevention and resolution, as well as regional integration and cooperation, are essential to a better acp-eu partnership and investment relationship.
in writing. — cooperation between parties is vital to achieve the objectives of the european development fund and to ensure european policy coherence on political, economic and environmental issues. the acp-eu joint assembly has become a key player in acp-eu relations and cooperation and plays a fundamental role in achieving common understanding and agreement on issues of mutual concern. it brings more democracy to the dialogue between states and i therefore deplore declining participation by eu member states in this conference. eu member states should be fully committed in this open, democratic and comprehensive dialogue. this is why i believe we need to strengthen this dialogue, especially with the aim of achieving a strong common position in light of the conference in paris next november. the long-lasting cooperation between the eu and the acp states on the issue of adaptation and mitigation responses should be reflected in the burden-sharing of goals in the agreement. i truly hope that the resolutions and other decisions taken by the assembly will be fully implemented.
in writing. the african, caribbean and pacific (acp) joint parliamentary assembly (acppa) the eu, established by the cotonou agreement, is a multi-parliamentary assembly in which acp and eu countries are in a partnership on equal terms. i voted for this resolution because the acp-eu partnership agreement is a framework in which discussions between acp and european parliamentarians take place in an open, sincere and constructive manner in order to implement the objectives set out in the cotonou agreement. the resolution also stresses the need to strengthen political dialogue and to continue post-cotonou the analysis of both positive and negative aspects of the sustainable socioeconomic development of the acp countries, so that no acp country is disadvantaged in this framework.
in writing. the acp-eu joint parliamentary assembly has succeeded in establishing itself as a key player in the relations and cooperation of the african, caribbean and pacific states with the european union. it remains a very practical tool for monitoring political, economic and social developments in the acp states. the common objectives set are of paramount importance development of the acp states, respect for human rights and fundamental freedoms, democracy based on the rule of law and transparent and accountable governance, essential conditions for development. acp-eu cooperation is based on a common legal system and the existence of common institutions. it is welcome that the jpa provides a framework for open and democratic dialogue between european parliamentarians and parliamentarians from african, caribbean and pacific states. this is an area with difficult and controversial issues, and the existence of a frank and open dialogue with the eu can only produce beneficial effects among the acp states. the living standards, democracy and highly complex social issues in the acp countries make cooperation with the european union essential.

the next item on the agenda is the statement by the vice-president of the commission/high representative on the situation in yemen (2015/2557 ((rsp)).
president-in-office of the council on behalf of the vice-president of the commission/high representative of the union for foreign affairs and security policy. - mr president, honourable members, i am grateful for the opportunity to discuss the situation in yemen with you today. yemen occupies a strategic position along the gulf of aden and the red sea. every day, hundreds of ships headed to europe pass through the bab-el-mandeb strait. terrorist organisations like al-qaeda in the arabian peninsula (aqap) increasingly represent a direct threat to european citizens. it is in our own interest to stand by the aspirations of the yemeni people for a stable and accountable state, preserving the territorial integrity of the country. when we look back four years ago, yemen initiated a remarkable transition process, with people taking to the streets calling for dignity, social justice, and their legitimate political and socio-economic rights. ever since, the eu has stood by yemen and its people, fully supporting its demands for democratic legitimacy, accountable and participatory public institutions, and a better life for all. yemenis look to the eu to continue supporting their aspirations, at a moment when the promises of the ‘arab uprisings’ are in danger of being forgotten. today, yemen’s transition is at grave risk. its daring economic and fiscal difficulties and persisting security challenges are now coupled with the danger that expeditious solutions might lead the country to more turmoil and to the collapse of state authority. the intensification of terrorist attacks in yemen, including by al-qaida in the arabian peninsula (aqap), cannot be left unchecked. we condemn such terrorist attacks in the strongest terms and reiterate our firm commitment and enduring support to the efforts of the yemeni authorities and of the international community to tackle terrorist violence, in yemen and the broader region. terrorists can only benefit from the weakening of state authority in yemen. the last two weeks have proved decisive for the balance of power in sana’a, with what some would qualify as the final takeover of state institutions by the houthis after the seizure of the presidential palace. in response to what they deemed unacceptable pressure on the executive, the president and the entire cabinet of prime minister bahah resigned on 22 january, de facto putting the whole yemeni transition in jeopardy. we consider that the so-called constitutional declaration unilaterally issued by the houthis last friday has no legitimacy. we now call on all political forces, in particular the houthis, to take clear responsibility for their actions, starting by unequivocally rejecting violence and coercion as political tools. undermining state institutions will only result in further instability, to the detriment of all yemenis. the attacks on officials and the restriction on the movements of president hadi, prime minister bahah and a number of other ministers are clearly unacceptable. but current developments should not be seen in isolation. they are partly the result of initial flaws in the design of the transition – which largely kept traditional power structures untouched. inaction and lack of resolve on the part of the executive and traditional political parties, and enduring attempts to undermine the transition process by spoilers, chiefly led by ex-president saleh, have also been key factors in leading yemen to the current impasse. there is no other way out of the current crisis than genuine dialogue and an inclusive political process, and we hope that the announcement of the resumption of broad consultations between yemeni parties under the auspices of the un on monday will bear fruit. any long-term solution should address the underlying causes of instability, which are deeply rooted in local historical and socio-economic power-structure. the real test case will be whether yemeni parties are ready to work together constructively to foster a compromise, safeguarding the transition’s objectives. we also call on all regional actors to contribute positively to this process. it is critical for the international community to retain its unity, in order to safeguard the foundations of the yemeni transition and restore stability, while preserving yemen’s territorial integrity. it is our belief that the framework provided by the gulf cooperation council initiative, the outcomes of the national dialogue conference (ndc) and the peace and national partnership agreement should remain the reference points for the yemeni transition. we therefore urge all actors to work constructively towards a swift finalisation of a new constitution. this constitution should meet the legitimate aspirations of the yemeni people, reflect the ndc outcomes, and preserve the unity and territorial integrity of yemen, to which the eu is strongly attached. while undergoing dramatic developments in its political transition and facing security threats, yemen also urgently needs to tackle its economic situation. the government of prime minister bahah had presented a solid programme in this regard, and a number of courageous steps had been taken to conclude an agreement with the imf – in particular as regards lowering the fiscal burden represented by fuel subsidies. decisive actions are needed to improve fiscal sustainability and fight corruption in the public administration, in support of those most in need. the severe humanitarian crisis may further deepen if political stability is not restored. almost 16 million yemenis (more than 60% of the total population) are currently in need of humanitarian aid, including 10.6 million suffering food insecurity and 13.4 million without access to safe water and sanitation. widespread consumption of and addiction to qat – a mildly narcotic leaf – has a disastrous impact on water use, labour productivity, health and the crowding-out of food crops. eu humanitarian assistance in 2014 reached eur 124 million (including also eur 33 million from the commission). and the eu is committed to continue its support for the yemeni people. it is essential that all parties safeguard humanitarian principles and ensure humanitarian access on the ground. ladies and gentlemen, the eu stands by the yemeni people at this critical juncture and reaffirms its commitment to continue supporting yemen in its transition.
on behalf of the ppe group. mr president, i was a member of the european parliament delegation that visited sanaa in may 2012: it was a period of optimism about the political transition. the solution that was negotiated after ten months of protests and that resulted in the departure of former president saleh with impunity and the coming to power of president hadi, then the national dialogue and finally a transitional government, made it seem that stability was guaranteed in yemen. some even said that the negotiated transition in yemen could serve as a model for other arab countries. in the last few weeks, there has been no reason for optimism in sanaa, because the opposite of the result expected two or three years ago is happening. what we see is that the model has not borne fruit, and some even say that the transition has failed completely in yemen, because the violence developed by the armed wing of the houthis shows us that, now, everything is upside down: there is no longer any legitimate authority in sanaa and we are bewildered by this terrible spiral of violence. the obvious solution: everything must go through a political process, through a constitutional referendum, through the organisation of elections and through a genuine political dialogue which is inclusive: this has always been the european view. i would like to conclude with a more general remark. this is again a shiite offensive, a movement that wants to make believe that a revolution, that a change in the state of affairs is possible, and we know very well from experience that shiite offensives lead to long-term instability.
mr president, in fact i am addressing the council about the tremendously difficult situation of yemen, a country which is falling into chaos and where different regions are breaking away from each other. this is a hugely difficult situation, taking into consideration the new training bases operated by al-qaeda and daesh in yemen. at the same time, we are seeing a new situation where the shia are taking power in yemen – the houthis. this probably could fuel the support of saudi arabia for the sunni tribes in yemen. finally, we might see a new situation, as happened in iraq when a new government in iraq could not – or would not – do the right thing to approach the sunni tribes in order to establish a national way for the country.

in writing. yemen is a not-to-be-missed player in the geopolitical equation of the middle east. the transition in yemen has failed, and the political process has fallen victim to elite competition. all political forces, in particular the houthis, must take responsibility for their actions and reject violence and coercion as political tools. only a broad political consensus within the main political groups, establishing a real path towards a constitutional referendum and free elections, can offer a lasting solution to the current crisis. it is necessary for all parties to engage in genuine dialogue and engage in intensive negotiations in order to contribute to the swift finalization of a new constitution that meets the legitimate aspirations of the yemeni people.
we move on to the next item on the agenda, the council and commission statements on the eu framework for democracy, the rule of law and fundamental rights respectively. in this regard, allow me to invite once again secretary kalniņa-lukaševica to speak for the council (2015/2558(rsp)).
president-in-office of the council. - we have a very important debate tonight. the union is founded on values including respect for human dignity, freedom, democracy and the rule of law. these are the common values of the member states, and they are an essential element of the european union’s identity. member states have to ensure that their internal orders fully respect the rule of law and other fundamental values. the commission, parliament and the council play an important role in safeguarding these essential principles. we recognise that the european parliament plays an important role in making sure that the commission and the council carry out their duties. as you may recall, in june 2013 the council stated that respecting the rule of law is a prerequisite for the protection of fundamental rights and called on the commission to take forward the debate in line with the treaties on the possible need for and shape of a collaborative and systematic method to tackle these issues. the same month, this parliament called on the eu institutions to develop the necessary eu tools to fulfil the treaty obligations on fundamental values. the commission contributed to this debate by means of a communication in march 2014. these initiatives complemented the already-existing tools: the infringement procedure applicable in the case of a breach of eu law, and the ‘atomic bomb’ option provided by article 7 of the lisbon treaty, which allows for the suspension of voting rights in the event of a serious and persistent breach of eu values. the council discussed on several occasions how to better safeguard the rule of law in the union. in december last year the council adopted conclusions establishing an annual political dialogue among member states to promote and safeguard the rule of law within the eu. the dialogue will respect certain principles such as objectivity, non-discrimination and equal treatment. it will also respect the principle of conferred competences, and it will have to ensure an inclusive approach. this exercise will have to be based on mutual trust. the presidency will play a central role in making sure that these principles are respected throughout the debate. right now the council is working towards organising its first political debate on the rule of law in the course of this year. i am convinced that this dialogue will help us to ensure that the rule of law will continue to be a commonly-shared fundamental value underpinning this union. i thank you for your attention and am looking forward to a really good debate.
first vice-president of the commission. - mr president, the clearest way to show what the rule of law means to us in everyday life is to recall what has happened when there is no rule of law. when president eisenhower marked the first law day with these words in 1958, world war ii had been over for barely a dozen years. the memories were raw, the images and the fear etched into minds. it has now been 70 years. we commemorated the liberation of the terror camps in this very hemicycle when we last met in january. president schulz and i were at terezin only two weeks ago. seventy years, yet the alarming backdrop to this anniversary – not just the headlines but also the trends, the patterns that we see – this backdrop has come as a harsh, sobering call for vigilance. this is why i welcome this timely debate. this house’s vigilance on fundamental rights is of utmost importance. we cannot let our societies imperceptibly slip back. we cannot allow illiberal logics to take hold. there is no such thing as ‘illiberal democracy’. our union is built on a break from the past, on the principle that societies should be free and open, sheltered from arbitrariness and force. this great leap: that is what europe stands for. all too often we take all of this for granted. so i cannot repeat it often enough. there can be no europe without full respect for our common values. compromising on common values is compromising on the very fabric of european cooperation and therefore weakening it and bringing it to a standstill. the commission is dedicated to advancing fundamental rights and the rule of law. i have been entrusted by president juncker with a duty of special significance – and of huge significance to me personally: that of steering and coordinating this work. it is everyday work: mainstreaming fundamental rights is a reflex throughout the policy cycle, from inception to implementation. together with commissioners jourová and avramopoulos we form a fundamental rights project team, and i will invite other commissioners to join if necessary. our aim is to pursue with a 360-degree approach to ensure that fundamental rights are effectively enforced and protected in member states, based on information gathered on the ground. i am well aware that this house has on different occasions called for an effective and binding instrument supplementary to article 7. we can clearly all agree on the aim behind these calls, ensuring our common values are fully respected and enforced. the key issue for discussion is that of the best means to achieve this objective. to me, all institutions have important, complementary roles to play. last december the council and the member states agreed to establish an annual dialogue to that effect, and i believe that our debate today serves very much the same purpose. the commission has its own role, and in line with the treaties, in recent years it has taken firm action by exerting political pressure, but also by successfully involving the court of justice when the rule of law was threatened, for instance on the unlawful retirement of judges or on measures affecting the independence of supervisory authorities. our approach to infringements pays special attention to rule-of-law-related cases, where implementation of eu legislation raises problems of compatibility with certain aspects of the rule of law. this includes, for example, the right to an effective remedy before a tribunal, or cases where enforcement bodies have insufficient powers or independence. since december what we call the ‘ex-third pillar’ measures in police and judicial cooperation can also be subject to infringement procedures, and here, too, the commission is ready to take action. i will personally see to it that the commission acts in a non-ideological manner and assesses each case fairly and objectively, based on the facts of the case and on the law. the commission will act impartially and treats all member states equally. our purpose is not to sanction individual member states per se, but rather to address issues through targeted intervention to restore the correct application of eu law. article 7 provides for potentially far-reaching sanctions. it is not limited in scope to areas covered by eu law, but rather designed to address clear risks of a serious breach. however, past experience has shown that this instrument, which can be triggered by the commission, the european parliament or one third of member states, is not always suited to swift and effective intervention. in particular, there are situations which do not fall under the scope of eu law and cannot be said to meet the threshold of article 7, but which do raise concern regarding the respect of the rule of law in particular member states. for this reason, last march the commission established the eu rule of law framework, which sets out how the commission will react in this sort of case. it can enter into a political dialogue with the member state concerned when there is an emerging systematic threat to the rule of law, to prevent it escalating further. when such a rule-of-law crisis emerges in a member state, the framework also allows the commission to react swiftly, following an objective assessment of the situation and with full respect to the principle of equal treatment of member states. the objective is to find a solution with the member state concerned and to avoid having to trigger the mechanisms of article 7. parliament will have an important political role in supporting the commission’s efforts to convince the member state concerned to put an end to the rule-of-law crisis. parliament would be regularly informed of the progress made at each stage of the process. we are keeping a close eye on all issues arising in member states relating to the rule of law, and i will not hesitate to use the framework if required by the situation in a particular member state. let me also use this occasion to address a related issue. many of you may also wonder about the state of play concerning eu accession to the european convention on human rights, following the opinion of the court of last december. accession to the echr remains a top priority for the commission and for me personally. i strongly believe that it would lead to a further strengthening of fundamental values. however, the opinion of the court has raised a number of significant challenges, and some of them are not easy to meet – which is why i believe we need a reflection period, giving us time for consultations with stakeholders on the best way forward. though parliament has welcomed the eu rule of law framework and the annual debate in the council, i am aware that there are renewed calls to establish new additional mechanisms for the permanent and regular monitoring that the member states comply with the eu fundamental rights. my conviction and policy has always been that, if current tools do not deliver, we will have to improve them. i am always ready to reflect on how to enhance respect for our values. however, before embarking on a long discussion on possible new instruments, we must be clear on the problem at stake. can we say to our citizens that we need yet another monitoring mechanism to fight against radicalisation and extremism, or do we just need to better use the existing and recently-established tools? experience has shown that there is not so much a need for new reporting or monitoring mechanisms, but rather for the improvement of the european union’s capacity to act and intervene in certain types of crisis situations relating to the rule of law. that is why, in our view, the framework is well targeted on the key issue at stake, and much already exists in terms of reporting mechanisms and information sources on compliance with fundamental values and the rule of law in member states. numerous actors, including union institutions and agencies – particularly the fundamental rights agency (which, i must say, carries out excellent work) but also the council of europe and its venice commission, as well as many ngos – all perform regular monitoring activities and make important assessments. efforts to make this information more accessible and easier to use must certainly be encouraged. this is why i intend the annual colloquium on fundamental rights – this is something i announced in parliament at my hearing – to take place in the autumn, in october or perhaps at the beginning of november. i want all relevant stakeholders – including, of course, parliament – to take part. i would like to announce here today that i plan for the theme of this year’s colloquium to be about tolerance, namely how to prevent and combat anti-semitic, anti-muslim, anti-christian, and anti-minority hatred in our societies, which are some of the biggest challenges we face today. i hope that you will engage actively in this important event. i want it to be a visible and meaningful debate. together, by speaking up and speaking jointly, we can send a powerful political message. i think that would also mean more to our citizens than a protracted institutional debate about mechanisms because, at the end of the day, this is about societies and what binds us together: how we can combat fear – numbing fear, paralysing fear, fear of the other. that is when our common values really have a meaning – what we owe to these values, to our own history, to the future for our children and grandchildren. this is the debate and the actions that citizens expect of us.
on behalf of the epp group. jacques chevalier defined the rule of law as the type of political regime in which the power of the state is framed and limited by law. the rule of law has been and will be a major concern of any modern society, which is why values such as human dignity, freedom, democracy, equality, tolerance, security and more must be the common denominator in a united europe, an open and secure europe, which is always at the service of our citizens and our businesses. these values have been and will be inalienable and imprescriptible. a stronger europe with stronger member states is a safety belt for everyone, regardless of nationality, just as an independent and efficient judiciary can boost business, investment and job creation. the existence of any deviation from these values is likely to create insecurity, which can affect our daily lives. therefore, the existence of effective mechanisms to sanction any violation of individual fundamental rights and freedoms is absolutely necessary. the more so as these values, which enshrine the rule of law, can easily be volatilized and even democracies considered to be consolidated. the european union as a whole and romania in particular have demonstrated their capacity to create mechanisms and institutions capable of guaranteeing the security of the rule of law. the current monitoring system allows for the identification and intervention of breaches of eu law at the level of each member state. however, there is still a need for closer cooperation between the european parliament, the member states, the commission and the council to strengthen justice strategies, both at national and european union level, as a guarantee of the rule of law. ) and

first of all, what is the rule of law? citizens and those who govern them must obey the law. the rule of law also applies to the relationships between private actors in society, not just citizens and those in power. keep going. how should laws be made? how should suspected criminals be treated? how should taxes be determined and collected? all of this is part of the rule of law, because it has to be regulated by laws that have to be strictly enforced. the law, in a state of law, must always be applied equally to everyone. there are no exceptions. without the rule of law, society does not work, justice does not work, democracy does not work, the economy does not work. rule of law is the difference between dictatorship and democracy. there are no minor or major violations of the rule of law, there are violations and that's it. and every violation is a slide toward dictatorship. the rule of law also means that we must behave as the law requires. there is no rule of law when politicians change the law often because they don't like the law and it doesn't serve their own interests. that's why we have laws: so that politicians and all citizens can adapt their behavior to the law, not that politicians (because they can, right? they are in parliament or in the government) to change the law often, whenever it does not suit them. the rule of law also means that the law must be public, clear, predictable, so that everyone can adopt their own behavior towards it. parliaments have a primary responsibility for the quality, the clarity of the laws they pass.

mr president, nowadays the european union is facing an unprecedented paradox in the healthcare sector. the existence of innovative new drugs, new technologies and developments in medical science that could ensure good outcomes and long-term survival on the one hand, and on the other hand many european citizens not being able to access them, mainly due to high costs. the issue of access to medicine is not only related to one innovative drug with an unusual high price but also to innovative medicines with reasonable prices, due to bureaucratic reimbursement procedures, lack of implementation of european laws such as the cross-border healthcare directive, or even due to the blocking of other important european laws such as the transparency directive. also, to finance the cost of new high-priced medicines, generic and biosimilar medicines, uptake must be used to create headroom for the healthcare budget. a major problem is that making the best use of such developments in the area of healthcare is particularly expensive and difficult, especially for some of the member states that are relatively small or low-income countries. european patients, and especially european cancer patients, rely on innovation to access new and better treatments. for many european patients, innovative treatments are the only hope to fight their disease. eu policy-makers should make sure that regulatory decisions on the value of innovative therapies are based on what matters the most to patients, namely long-term quality survival, and also to ensure access to innovative treatments following a cost-benefit analysis performed at centralised level by the ema. we should prioritise at eu and national level more investment in research into innovative therapies and find sustainable solutions for including innovative therapies in national healthcare plans, treatment pathways and funding streams.
mr. president, because of the long periods in which new drugs are protected by patents many treatments remain inaccessible to the people who desperately need them. after a drug's patent expires, its price can drop by 99 percent, an astonishing figure that suggests how much money companies make when they have a monopoly on a drug. year after year, these companies make huge profits and, in addition, demand to expand their monopoly on medicines that could improve the health of some people, many of whom lack the opportunity. this is deeply inaccurate. this is not a problem of some developing countries, but a painful reality in the european union, including romania, where the price of medicines is often too high for people or hospitals to afford. obviously, creating a drug is not an inexpensive process and indeed better research funding is needed, but it is the citizens who should benefit from the results of medical research. more transparency is needed on the real costs of research. whatever the commission's proposed actions, i will not support the extension of patents for medicines and, by implication, for high-priced medicines that people cannot afford.
mr president, the right to health is a fundamental element of the right to life enshrined in article 3 of the universal declaration of human rights. the european union and the institutions responsible must be constantly concerned that this right does not remain a mere statement in a legislative act, but on the contrary, that it is a reality of our days. the right to health also means access to medicines. the major discrepancies between the various states are absolutely unacceptable. citizens of the european union in different countries are sentenced to death by what is an unacceptably high and unaffordable price for medicines, which is inhuman. the pharmaceutical industry must understand that it needs a partnership with the european citizen, without which it could not exist. member states should consider creating a framework within which all citizens who pay for health insurance, but not only, have access to quality, prompt and efficient health services. the european parliament, the council and the commission must be constantly concerned that the laws of the member states are in conformity with european directives and provide for clear penalties in the event of their infringement as an additional guarantee of the right to life and health. without strong action, involving partnership with the pharmaceutical industry and all the major players in the field, we will continue to have european citizens dying for days because of the immobility of the institutions.
in writing. – europe is confronted with an increasing problem of shortages and unaffordability of medicines; it is not possible anymore to have the same reaction from the commission indicating the areas of competence of the member states. it is clear that both unaffordability and shortage impact directly on the outcome of patients’ treatment, endangering the status of public health in the union. the commission needs to act and find the right balance between the protection of medical research and access to medicines. the prices required for some life-saving drugs are absolutely astronomical and the population cannot make use of the discovery if it is out of their reach. the commission has to come out with immediate proposals to improve safe, affordable and timely access and availability of medicines for patients in the union.

mr president, i would like to welcome the presence of vice-president šefčovič so soon after the adoption of the energy union strategy. the energy union must have at its core an efficient, functioning and growth and jobs-creating internal energy market. affordable prices and competitiveness for individual and industrial consumers, as well as the protection of vulnerable consumers, should be the natural consequences of a functioning market. i stress, mr vice-president, the importance of setting a minimum target of 10% interconnection for electricity by 2020 and the possibility of having 15% interconnection by 2030, but we ask the commission to report annually on the progress towards these targets. the 10% target, together with an ambitious legislative proposal to restructure the electricity market, will increase security of supply and ensure that the electricity market is better adapted to the energy transition. i welcome the proposal to create regional operational centres for the efficient planning and management of cross-border electricity and gas flows and stress the need to develop regional energy infrastructure in vulnerable areas. i regret, however, mr vice-president, that no european approach is being proposed to energy poverty. the s&d group supports the coordination at european level of national action plans, scoreboards, exchanges of good practice and a horizontal approach to energy accessibility. as part of the review of the energy efficiency and energy performance of buildings directives, energy poverty will also have to be considered a priority but unfortunately the commission does not mention the review of these directives or the legislation on ecodesign and energy labelling, which our group is calling for. the revision of these directives will undoubtedly also contribute to improving energy efficiency targets, and the commission needs to ensure that the union speaks with one voice in negotiations with third countries on improving energy security. this must be an ambitious objective that requires transparency, openness and cooperation and for which we need an action plan.
mr president, this energy union package comes at the right time for addressing the current challenges we face of less security and less supply, and we should not transform this package into a redundant reiteration of all energy policies in place today. instead we should focus on an accelerated timeline for the proposed 15 concrete actions. if we need a diversified supply, we should build more entry points and support indigenous production. if we need more investment, we should use the efsi to upgrade infrastructure investment to a fully-liquid asset class which attracts private investment. if member states are still isolated, we should re-think regional cooperation and the development of interconnections. energy capacity for the mediterranean countries and for south-eastern europe, as well as interconnecting landlocked countries in central europe to these new capacities, should be a priority for diversifying supply sources in these regions. a southern gas hub and a black sea gas hub will allow gas-on-gas competition and will replace imports of natural gas volumes under oil-indexed contracts. hub price indexation of gas is already lowering costs for consumers in western and northern countries, while intergovernmental agreements with a single supplier in eastern europe continue to crush member states’ bargaining power. ‘more europe’ can happen if we have the choice of physically buying gas from the global market. this would allow us to get the best wholesale prices and services, and this would make europe stronger on the international scene.
mr president, i want to personally thank the commissioner for the excellent cooperation we have had in recent weeks when working on and preparing this very strategic document which is presented today. energy is indeed a priority for our union, and i certainly welcome the fact that the energy union is considered as a priority by the new commission. i want to underline that it is absolutely necessary that our energy policy is well coordinated with our foreign and security policy, because – as events in ukraine are showing – energy security is directly linked to the eu’s security. today we rely on one single main supplier – russia – and this has an evident impact on our foreign and security policy, which is a kind of hostage of this situation. i consider it an absolute necessity to find alternative sources and routes, because this is the only way – by diversifying – that we can avoid in the future a situation like the current one. but we definitely need also to focus on what we already have: increased internal production, increased energy efficiency, and new and better inter-connected infrastructure. from this point of view i think we need to make use of all available sources, including the connecting europe facility, to speed up the creation of a strategic trans-european network for energy, which will allow us better distribution of all types of energy and avoid bottlenecks.
in writing. energy union means common energy resources, interconnection of networks, strengthening of member states' negotiating capacity and, not least, reducing dependence on imports. the european energy market is currently highly fragmented and its fragility is reflected in its inability to respond to external challenges. whether it is the blackmail of russian gas or the unfair competition from chinese solar panel manufacturers, the eu must react swiftly and with one voice to these challenges. i stress the importance of cross-border energy interconnections, which are intended to supply energy to neighbouring states and are a response to external blackmail. the arad szeged pipeline with a two-way pumping capacity contributes to energy security at regional level. i also note that moldova has committed itself to european values, but its dependence on russian gas is hindering its efforts. unfortunately, the iasi ungheni gas pipeline, inaugurated last year, was not put into use due to bureaucratic obstacles raised by russia. mobile landing terminals are veritable geostrategic weapons. investments in this area are urgently needed to ensure energy independence in union markets.
in writing. i welcome the adoption of the energy union strategy which will help to integrate the 28 energy markets into one. i believe that this strategy will allow better access to financing instruments for energy efficiency in buildings and transport and will help local actors to implement the smart cities programme. a more efficient functioning of the market at european level will benefit all consumers. we hope that by removing barriers, the european agency in this area will be able to better cooperate with member states to keep prices and fees at a level that is convenient, accessible and competitive for all european citizens. energy should be secure and sustainable, characterised by a higher level of competition and freedom of choice for each consumer.
in writing. the energy union strategic framework opens the debate on strengthening solidarity between member states on energy policy. this laudable initiative, supported by the social democrat commissioner for the energy union, maroš šefčovič, once again highlights the need for a common reference framework not only in terms of prices and costs, but also in terms of what it means to work with suppliers or energy-producing countries. more than ever, in the face of the challenges posed by the current gulf and eastern european context, member states need to act as one, including in negotiating the prices of imported energy. only in this way can we ensure real cohesion within the union and avoid exposing certain countries, such as romania or poland, to additional financial or energy risks. the energy union debate therefore also highlights the need for an energy policy that protects the most disadvantaged or middle-income or low-income consumers compared to the european average. european energy policies need to avoid creating new inequalities and making certain groups feel even more excluded.
in writing. – interruptions in energy supplies in recent years have shown the potential vulnerability of member states relying heavily on energy imports from single sources and have highlighted problems with storage capacity in the event of crises. the eu needs to urgently address these problems in order to create greater stability and better resistance to external shocks, and to better manage its own internal energy sources. this would also help progress towards other important eu policy objectives, such as increasing the integration of renewable energy sources into the energy mix and increasing energy independence. we also need to foster solidarity amongst member states which will provide additional security for individual countries, as well as protecting and strengthening the whole region.
in writing. the fact that europe needs a european energy union is already a reality, supported by member states. the fact that europe does not yet have a european energy union is also a reality, the cause of which lies in the member states. first, some member states are ensuring their energy security through individual actions and do not support european projects that increase europe's energy independence and strengthen its energy security. secondly, some member states do not want to break the monopoly of national companies. thirdly, member states have energy strategies which differ greatly in the directions of development. it is time for member states to take concrete action to ensure that the european commission's new energy union initiative does not go to waste.
in writing. the development of a common energy strategy for the eu member states shows that the eu is taking concrete steps on a highly pressing issue that has been geopolitically exploited by russia for years. in addition to the individual efforts of the 28 member states to reduce their energy dependence on russian gas imports, it is welcome that the european commission has taken the initiative to develop such an energy strategy. the european union is the world's largest energy importer, according to statistics, with more than half of what it uses coming from imports worth over €400 billion. it is clear that we need to reconfigure our energy relationship with russia so that we have a level playing field, fair competition and security. it is equally clear that this is becoming an increasingly distant goal, given russia's hostile actions towards ukraine. in these circumstances, the eu's opening up to countries such as the usa and canada, norway, the states of the caucasus, the middle east and africa is a priority. finding alternative sources to russian gas is vital.
in writing. – i find that the resolute response of the council in the wake of the paris shootings is commendable, it is really imperative that we address security concerns and fill in the gaps in our security strategy as fast as possible. nevertheless, the counterterrorism responses offered by the council raise a few fundamental challenges regarding some of the eu’s most important achievements in the field of freedom of movement and the schengen free travel area. before proposing the fundamental revision of the schengen rules we should firstly consider whether we have used the current rules to the best extent possible. instead of giving in to political populism and reimposing internal border controls, we should insist on more and better cooperation and information sharing among member states and among eu agencies, such as europol and eurojust.

mr president, a latin proverb says that 'everyone wants to be healthy, but often everything goes against it'. a number of professional organisations, such as the world health organisation and the american academy of pediatrics, have in recent years drawn attention to the high risk to human health posed by endocrine disruptors and other related chemicals. endocrine disruptors are chemicals that, once in the human body, prevent normal growth and development, cause negative changes in metabolism, and lead to various forms of cancer, infertility, obesity, and diabetes. the european union as a whole has a duty to make the health of its citizens a priority. in this respect, i believe that the impact studies launched by the commission in this area should focus on the potential implications of endocrine disruptors on human health and not on the economic implications for the relevant industry or trade. we can ask ourselves: what good is high-performing agriculture with high productivity, but a sick population? surely, we say we, to nothing. i therefore believe that clear rules on the control, prohibition and substitution of endocrine disruptors with certain substances considered safe are necessary to strike the perfect balance between ensuring the continued protection of human health and the environment and at the same time providing farmers with the plant protection products they need. the european commission, the council and the european parliament must urgently intervene to tackle this problem, all the more so as exposure of the population to these substances generates expenditure of over eur 30 billion in the european union, as studies by the relevant institutions show.
on behalf of the s&d group. mr president, commissioner, in a globalised economy, goods are moving with unprecedented speed and supply chains are becoming increasingly complex and spread over a much larger geographical area. the russian government's embargo on eu agri-food products provides a clear picture of the impact that a political decision can have on many european economic sectors. i join my colleagues in the committee on transport and tourism in drawing attention to the effects of these restrictions on the market for international road hauliers of agri-food products. we cannot understand the seriousness of the situation if we neglect the economic loss caused by the concluded supply contracts and lost by european carriers operating on the russian export market. the cumulative impact of the oversupply of agri-food products on the internal market, the loss of these contracts and the significant increase in the cost of transport in transit to third countries affects the whole european economy, not just one sector of it. central and eastern european countries are the most affected by this situation and, because of the internal market, the effect is felt throughout the eu. i ask the european commission to provide parliament with sufficient data on the impact of the embargo and i also ask that together we find an appropriate solution to this problem.
