in writing. the long-term european investment architecture aims to mobilise financial capital to increase the competitiveness of member states' economies, close the gap between regions and create new jobs. the stability of the european economic climate is an essential condition for attracting private capital to public projects. at the same time, a simple, bureaucratic-free framework and a uniform level of rules across all member states are needed. the added value of projects should take into account the combined benefits of the investment over the long term, rather than its strictly economic benefits. there must also be instruments to guarantee public investment in such a way as to make it as attractive as possible. last but not least, i would stress that the success of long-term investments depends to a large extent on their continuity, so clear rules should be put in place to limit the possibility for investors to withdraw their allocated amounts at any time. i am convinced that long-term investment will deliver measurable results in smart growth by supporting the digital economy and creating integrated networks in the single market, in increasing employment by facilitating the mobility of citizens and businesses, and in sustainable development by unlocking the potential of the green economy.
in writing. the european union needs to boost investment and the draft regulation responds to this need. a single european legal framework for the establishment and operation of european long-term investment funds is hereby established. these funds will be able to attract resources from institutional investors interested in long-term investments, such as pension funds, life insurance companies, etc. the legal framework provides the necessary flexibility for these funds, but at the same time contains the prudential measures they must respect to avoid speculative investments and lack of diversification of the asset portfolio. we welcome the adoption of this legal framework for long-term european investment funds which will also contribute to the implementation of the european commission's investment plan through the european fund for strategic investments.

in writing. ‒ the european globalisation adjustment fund (egf) is a financial instrument that allows for the allocation of money to people who lose their jobs as a result of the economic and financial crisis or as a result of changes in the structure of world trade due to globalisation. the budget allocated to the fund for the period 2014-2020 shall be eur 150 million. zaklady chemiczne zachem was a polish chemical producer producing semi-finished and finished chemicals for the chemical industry, paper industry, energy sector, etc. the changes caused by the economic crisis led to the suspension of production at this company, with over 600 employees being laid off between march 2013 and july 2013. an application was therefore submitted to the european commission for the mobilisation of a total amount of eur 115 205 from the egf, which was approved by the commission by adopting a decision to mobilise the egf in favour of poland at the beginning of 2015. the european parliament report found that all eligibility criteria were met and therefore supports the granting of the requested amount of the egf. i voted in favour of this report.

in writing. ‒ the european globalisation adjustment fund (egf) is a financial instrument that allows for the allocation of money to people who lose their jobs as a result of the economic and financial crisis or because of the changes in the structure of world trade brought about by globalisation. unlike the structural and investment funds, which target strategic, long-term projects, this fund provides targeted and individual support limited in time. aleo solar is a german company which has decided to close two production units in germany. the closure of the two units led to the dismissal of 657 employees in 2014. the application to the commission envisages the allocation of an amount from the egf to co-finance a coordinated package of personalised services for the reintegration of workers made redundant. following examination of the application, the commission adopted in december 2014 the proposal for a decision to mobilise the egf in favour of germany, in order to support the reintegration into the labour market of persons made redundant. the european parliament report found that all eligibility criteria were met and supports the allocation from the european globalisation adjustment fund of the requested amount. i voted in favour of this report.

madam president, every year the early phases of the budgetary procedure are always a good opportunity to reflect on what we want to achieve through spending the limited resources of the eu budget which we have at our disposal. what will be the priorities for the next year and how shall we use our eu funds in order to achieve these priorities? we all agree that the eu budget should be a budget for growth and jobs. eu money has to be used in those areas which make the european economy more competitive, stronger, and more attractive for investors and entrepreneurs. in that sense i very much welcome the approach of the rapporteur to focus this year on entrepreneurship, enterprises and employment. mr fernandes, i welcome the focus in your report on research, youth employment and sme financing. nevertheless, i also have to point out that the 2016 budget will have to address key issues such as the financing of the youth employment initiative. the commitments of the entire envelope have been frontloaded to the years 2014 and 2015 so the commission has to find additional resources to make this instrument work in the year 2016 and afterwards. in my view, the global margin for commitments is such an instrument and i really hope that it will provide sufficient resources to finance this project. all these priorities would have to be strictly tied to the obligation of the union to pay its commitments to the beneficiaries, which is a matter of credibility. we look forward to the commission proposal in that respect.
madam president, the european union must commit itself to an ambitious budget for 2016 that responds to the real needs and agendas of its citizens. that's why i have three proposals, three principles. the first direction concerns strategy: moving from a policy of promoting austerity to a creative and constructive policy for job creation or for innovation and development. the second line concerns how we think, in the principles of this draft budget, of a budget of cohesion and reduction of inequalities, based on ideas such as the youth guarantee or solidarity funds for new entrants such as romania, bulgaria or croatia, or those related to the neighbourhood policy and i would mention here the republic of moldova. the third direction concerns mechanisms, how we can allow everyone access to union funds, but also how we can ensure that the money is really used usefully and efficiently, in the interest of the citizen. commissioner, the budget is not a mere technical matter. it is more important than ever for the future of europe and i can therefore assure you that the european parliament will support you in this.

vice-president of the commission.– madam president, i would like to thank members, and i am sure we will have a very interesting time when we negotiate the budget. today’s debate has been a very good illustration of the fact that we are keenly interested in a sound financial base for our economies. let me make four very brief points. firstly, it is a crucial time to secure sustainability of growth in europe. in 2015, for the first year, we expect positive growth everywhere. i hope that will be the case also for greece despite some political changes there. should that be the case, the economy of europe would be finally coming out of a long, protracted crisis. but we will only succeed if we are fiercely determined to use the budget for that exact purpose: to help our investments and help growth. this is why my second point is: yes, the investment plan is very important because what it aims to do is to draw private sector investment on a large scale to complement what we do on the public sector side; that is essential. this takes me to the third point; if we are to succeed it will be shown in employment numbers. we know smes generate most of the jobs, so of course attention to smes is necessary; but attention to our innovative centres, to researchers and to small farmers is also necessary. this would be a predominant objective for us. last but not least, i would mention social impact and the equality that we aim for. luckily we continue to be the most equal region in the world and, even during the crisis, the gini coefficient – the most well—known measure for equality in the 28 countries – has gone down slightly from 30.9 to 30.4. but we all know that this is not across the board; that in many countries and many regions and many communities, inequality has gone up. that is why we have to be very mindful of how the benefit from our budget is spread so that it is as equal as we can possibly make it.

the next item is the report by georgi pirinksi, on behalf of the committee on budgetary control, on the annual report 2013 on the protection of the eu’s financial interests – fight against fraud (2014/2155(ini)) (a8—0024/2015).
reporting for the opinion of the committee on civil liberties, justice and home affairs. madam president, in the report on the protection of the union's financial interests we have tried to answer and include issues that are crucial to the protection of the union's financial interests, namely the protection of our money, the protection of the money of every european citizen. it's our money, all in one place, whether you're a romanian citizen, whether you're a german citizen or a citizen of any member state, and that's what we all need to understand: that we need to protect our citizens' money. european money is our citizens' money; their taxes and fees and the national public budget are paid into the european union and this is the money for european funds. i have given this explanation to everyone, so that it is clear that we are not talking about the financial interests of the union in the abstract, but about the money that actually comes from our citizens. and it's important to understand that there is a single basket into which all the money is poured, and as such, if the protection of european funds is well fought in one member state but poorly fought in another member state, everyone suffers because the money is in one place. so it's not true that if they steal more in ten member states, the rest are doing well because they're fighting their own fraud at home. and we're still here because it's common money. as such, we very much want to focus on effective combat. i thank the commission and commissioner georgieva for what they have said. i want to tell you that this is the sixth year in a row that i hear that the commission is pleased that we recommend and demand the distinction between irregularities and fraud. yes, we do, but this is not the first time we have asked for this: irregularities are administrative, fraud is criminal, but this is an old theme. i am glad that yesterday the libe committee adopted the interim report on the european prosecutor; i hope that this office with single rules to combat fraud with european funds will work throughout the european union and lead to efficiency, that is, everyone to investigate, to confiscate money and return it to the union budget.

in writing. ‒ the agreement establishing the general fisheries commission for the mediterranean (gfcm), in accordance with the provisions of article xiv of the fao constitution, was approved by the fao conference in 1949 and entered into force in 1952. amendments to this agreement were approved in 1963, 1976 and 1997. the european community acceded to the gfc on 16 june 1998 by decision 98/416/ec. the eu member states with an opening to the mediterranean and the black sea are also parties to this agreement. i voted in favour of this recommendation to establish a general fisheries commission for the mediterranean because the new agreement sets a clear overall objective, which is the biological, social, economic and environmental sustainability of living marine resources. it also introduces definitions of terms necessary for the correct interpretation of the agreement. furthermore, the functions of the gfcm are better defined, including the promotion of common fisheries management through multiannual management plans, the establishment of restricted fishing areas and the collection and dissemination of data. in this context, the new agreement integrates the core elements of the common fisheries policy with regard to the objective of maximum sustainable yield, the ecosystem, as well as the objective of the precautionary approach, reducing discards, combating illegal, unreported and unregulated fishing.

in writing. ‒ the agreement establishing the general fisheries commission for the mediterranean (gfcm) entered into force in 1952, and the european union acceded to it in 1998 by decision 98/416/ec. the eu member states of the mediterranean and the black sea are also parties to this treaty. a first amendment to this agreement after the eu's accession to it occurred in 2013 and the cgpm contracting parties signed this amended document at the 38th annual session of the cgpm in 2014. i voted in favour of this report because it highlights the main changes contained in the amended agreement, including: 1. increasing the biological, social, economic and environmental sustainability of marine living resources; 2. more precisely defining the functions of the gfcm; 3. providing for various sanctions in the event of its members' non-compliance with the rules laid down in the agreement; and 4. establishing mechanisms for the settlement of disputes between its members.
in writing. ‒ the report by my colleague from the committee on fisheries, mr gabriel mato, is one in support of the amendments to the agreement on the general fisheries commission for the mediterranean (gfcm), to which romania and bulgaria are co-signatories. the gfcm is a regional organisation whose objective is to manage fisheries and marine resources in a sustainable and rational way and to develop aquaculture in the black sea and the mediterranean sea. i believe that the gfcm, and therefore the agreement as amended today, is a very important agreement for romania and for the marine resources of our country. that is why i voted in favour of the amendments to the original agreement, which give the gfcm a clearer definition and functioning, a dispute settlement mechanism and increased powers to punish violations by signatory states.

in writing. ‒ the european semester has become, in a relatively short period of time, part of europe's institutional culture and, moreover, is increasingly part of national policy-making culture. the previous open method of coordination, one of the most direct ancestors of the european semester, was treated more or less as a joke; it was an exercise for academics more than practitioners. now we can see how very powerful member states - whether they like it or not - take the european semester seriously and explain and defend their choices. even when they try obtain exceptions from the rules, they still explain themselves in relation to those rules, which are thus confirmed and strengthened. we now have an enriched process, with a clearer social dimension (juncker's 'social triple a' is a great metaphor and - it is to be hoped - much more than that) and decent flexibility with the 'moscovici package'. it is almost mystical how europe, painfully, finds resources to fix itself after crises.

in writing.– from 25 february, the so called islamic state began a deliberate campaign to destroy cultural heritage in the nineveh province, beginning with the destruction of the mosul museum, continuing on to levelling of nimrud, hatra and khorsabad with bulldozers. three thousand years of history and unesco world heritage sites were destroyed within ten days. not only are assyrian christian and yazidi people targeted as populations, but also by means of their built environment and heritage. the destruction of religious and historical sites and patrimony works in tandem with the direct physical violence against these communities, whose historical presence is being systematically wiped out. according to the protocols of the 1954 hague convention and the principles of the geneva convention, the deliberate destruction of cultural patrimony is a war crime. the director general of unesco and ban ki-moon have condemned these acts as war crimes. the european parliament should also do the same.

in writing. the european council of 19-20 march 2015 addressed a number of issues, including the issue of a common energy policy. this subject, so important for the future of europe, must become a priority on the european union's agenda and a mechanism to stimulate cooperation and solidarity between member states. such a common energy policy should include the following elements:- a negotiated common import tariff for gas, oil and other energy sources imported by member states outside the european area. this will lead to a reduction in the unequal treatment of eastern european countries, which pay up to 7 times the price of imported energy resources. - combating inequalities by protecting economically disadvantaged consumers. subsidising access to energy for people with low incomes and implementing a common and negotiated timetable for the evolution of applied tariffs must therefore become a european priority, in order to avoid creating new means of excluding groups or regions from the benefits of a common market that is - hopefully - fairer and greener. i therefore support the initiatives taken by the european commission and the european council and hope that these energy market balancing measures will be implemented as soon as possible.
member of the commission. madam president, ladies and gentlemen, i thank you for giving me the opportunity to have an exchange with you on taxation in europe. the annual report on taxation, which we are discussing today, makes a diagnosis which i entirely agree with. the picture of corporate and personal taxation in europe is both illicit and inefficient. the lack of coordination of tax rules and practices in the member states poses fundamental problems for the union as a whole. first, tax rules too often segment the internal market in such a way that most european or foreign companies do not have full access to it and encounter obstacles that limit their growth opportunities. secondly, the tax authorities are no longer able or less able to collect the tax due to them properly. some taxpayers use aggressive tax planning to take advantage of the differences and inconsistencies between tax systems. moreover, it is clear that the member states themselves are engaged in excessive competition to attract the most mobile tax bases. thirdly, in the face of the revelation of this iniquitous system, which benefits the most powerful at the expense of all the others - and which is no longer tolerated because it is no longer tolerated - the consent to taxation is fading. the very heart of the social contract between the citizen and the public authorities is at stake. we are therefore faced with a critical situation which requires rapid and far-reaching action. my goals are the same as yours. first, we must restore tax justice within the union and the member states. finally, we must create a genuine internal tax market, a transparent and predictable framework for business to invest and for consumer confidence to be restored. and finally, we need to put taxation at the service of the political priorities of the union, whether it is the digital single market - the commission was talking about this morning - or the energy union. there are solutions, and some of them have been known for years. the implementation of these will require the commitment of all, and first of all of most of the member states, which have the final say on these issues and will have to agree on the ambitious solutions we will propose to them. the president of the commission, jean-claude juncker, has made the fight against tax fraud and tax evasion a top political priority of this commission, and i would like to dwell on this for a moment. as you know, the european commission has just taken a series of strong measures to improve tax transparency in the union, starting with a proposal for a directive on the exchange of information on tax rulings. this is to make available to all member states information on the impact of their partners' decisions on their own tax base, which goes hand in hand with a commitment to promote transparency beyond tax filings, so that the european union remains a forerunner in overall tax transparency. one possibility could be - as you recommend in the annual report on taxation - to extend to all sectors the current requirement for certain industries in the european union to disclose certain financial information on a country-by-country basis. this is a debate which the commission is prepared to have with parliament. the commission has not yet decided on the best way forward, which will require further analysis, but it intends to work hard to complete this analysis, which remains a necessary prerequisite for future common positions. the question of where profits are to be taxed is also particularly relevant in the european union, due to its unique characteristics such as the existence of a single currency area and an internal market with 28 different tax systems. we have our own rules, our own priorities, our own goals. the union can rely on the useful work of the oecd, but it cannot rely on its work alone. the commission's work programme for 2015 provides that, in the light of global developments, it will present an action plan for corporate taxation in the single market, where profits should be taxed more systematically where value is created, in order to bring production closer to taxation. the action plan will help to relaunch discussions on the accis (or ccctb) project, which should harmonise the tax base for many companies operating across borders in the european union. this would not only make the internal market more competitive but also limit the possibilities for tax manipulation by companies, which is a priority for us. this should also include actions in the shorter term to enable the implementation in the union of solutions agreed at global level, in particular at g20 level. it is expected that the commission will adopt this action plan - the second phase of our approach - before the summer, i think at the beginning of june. i am sure that your assembly, through the work carried out in the taxe and econ committees, will make a positive contribution to the preparation of this action plan. i would like to say a few words on two subjects. first, the financial transaction tax. the implementation of an ambitious framework for a national financial transaction tax is a priority that the commission shares with this parliament, as stated by president juncker in his political guidelines. the commission is encouraging tax reforms that bring in those who have benefited from costly bailout policies and that allow the tax base to be widened and the tax burden on labour to be lightened. i welcome the fact that at the last ecofin council in january, the member states participating in enhanced cooperation reiterated their willingness to create the conditions for the implementation of a european framework of harmonised national ftts as from 1 january 2016. i also note that the enhanced cooperation member states have stated that national ftts should be based on the broadest possible tax base with low rates, while taking into account their impact on the real economy and the risks of offshoring. the commission services have always offered and will continue to offer technical support to the member states in order to reach an agreement quickly, in a spirit of openness to compromise, while upholding the fundamental principles of the commission's proposal. finally, as regards indirect taxes, i would like to stress that the commission intends to present, during this term of office, a series of reforms of the vat system to improve its functioning, reduce the administrative burden and, in particular, adopt a definitive vat system. the commission prefers and will prefer a global approach because the introduction of scattered ad hoc measures would risk, particularly in the light of the negotiations in the council, leading to inconsistent solutions or even to no solution at all. this also applies to the discussion of vat rates. i would like to thank mrs kaili for her excellent report and to remind parliament that i am at parliament's disposal so that we can move forward together on this vital subject. i shall also be having an exchange with the special committee on taxation on 30 march in the spirit that should prevail, namely the spirit of transparency and cooperation between us.
on behalf of the epp group. madam president, first of all, i would like to welcome the new initiative of the european commission on the fiscal transparency package. i am convinced that the introduction of automatic exchange of information between member states on tax rulings meets the citizens' demand, and they want something simple and fair: that profits be taxed in the country where they were made and not transferred to another country by individual tax rulings or accounting tricks. we also look forward to the new action plan that the european commission has promised against tax evasion and tax avoidance. secondly, i would like to thank mrs kaili, the rapporteur, and the other colleagues with whom i have worked very well in finalising this report. i would like to stress one important sentence in this report: only through close cooperation between member states, between member states and third countries will we be able to make substantial progress in the fight against tax evasion and profit shifting.
in writing.– i welcome the fact that we have presented concrete proposals to fight tax evasion and avoidance after the unacceptable revelations of the lux leaks and swiss leaks scandals. it is clear that we must take stronger action to tackle corporate tax avoidance and aggressive tax planning. i support the inclusion of a list of practical demands in the report to make implementation of our proposals more effective. the report includes measures to reduce mismatches between tax systems and rules to extend country-by-country reporting to monitor where business profits are located and where taxes are paid. it also includes common eu criteria to define tax havens. i believe this call for more transparency and regulation represents an important step ahead in the fight against tax evasion and tax avoidance and a pragmatic tool to foster growth and strengthen the emu. i would like to congratulate my colleague eva kaili for her holistic approach to the subject of taxation policy.
in writing. the annual loss in the eu due to tax fraud and tax evasion is estimated at €1 000 billion. the fight against tax fraud must be a priority. the european parliament must be very firm in tackling these non-transparent practices that distort competition in the market. we need to have a tax policy that promotes inclusion, transparency and fairness and at the same time encourages good governance and is an effective tool for promoting social justice and reducing economic inequalities. we need policies that tackle tax evasion, reduce unfair tax disparities, encourage competitiveness and support smes. we also need measures to tackle tax havens.

mr president, the minimum wage is an economic measure that each member state is free to apply. it is a measure that applies to nationals of that state or to nationals working in that state under an individual employment contract. it cannot in any case apply to workers employed by a company outside the member state in the service sector, for example, in particular road transport. the obligation for companies to pay drivers for international transport at least the minimum wage applied in germany for the period of driving on german territory is clearly in breach of the rules of the single market, the services directive. the obligation for companies to keep separate accounts and to make them available to the german authorities is a requirement that is completely outside any national or european legislation. such a measure sets a dangerous precedent, as other member states have already announced their intention to apply similar measures which will create major problems in the eu single market. i add the new rules, outside the european regulations, imposed by other member states on drivers, as well as the aberrant fines provided for by the legislation of these states, including germany. i think it is obvious that these measures can be considered as protectionist measures. i ask the commission to continue the infringement procedure and to reach a result as soon as possible in order to limit the losses suffered by carriers in a significant number of member states, including romania.
in writing.– the recent imposition by germany of a minimum wage for freight transporters from other member states is just another in a recent row of economic protectionist measures in europe disguised as social ones. what is worrying is that, even in this house, we are hearing more and more calls against so-called social dumping from the east. we should be careful not to misuse economic terms: dumping means exporting a product to another country at a price either below the price charged on its home market or below its cost of production. this is clearly not the case at hand. the reality is that, despite eu efforts, there still are strong disparities between member states in terms of economic development, wages and production costs, just as there are differences in terms of financial backgrounds, technological development, access to finance and so on. forcing companies in other member states to artificially increase their costs, and placing on them burdensome administrative requirements, is not the way to make the eu a competitive player on the global market. if it really intends to be one, it should not be afraid of competition.
in writing. i support the minimum wage as a social and economic principle throughout the european union. this discussion is not about the minimum wage, however, but about the application of the principle of subsidiarity in european law and the principle of competitiveness in the eu economy. if we respect these fundamental principles for the unitary development of the european union, i believe we can pay more attention to the scope of the minimum wage in western countries and how the imposition of these rules affects eastern economies. the transport sector in central and eastern europe is populated by smes that provide jobs, smes that help develop a growing economy. if these smes are prevented from functioning by imposing rules they cannot comply with, then who is responsible for the loss of a considerable number of jobs? i believe in the principle of regulating the minimum wage in all economic sectors, but i do not believe that these measures should negatively affect the free movement of goods in the eu and in no way negatively affect the maintenance of the competitiveness of companies in countries such as romania. i want to create an economic environment and a market harmonized under the european principles and legislation that we have all committed ourselves to uphold.
madam president, i am a roma myself. europe’s largest ethnic minority inside the eu comprises the youngest and fastest—growing demographic segment of the population. for example, by 2020, young roma will make up one third of the new entrants to the workforce in hungary and in bulgaria. europe cannot afford another lost generation. this is a matter of human rights and basic values and it is vital to peace and cohesion in society across europe. europe cannot afford to ignore the fast growing anti-gypsy policy within its boundaries. europe, while adjusting and reinventing its own instruments for a participatory democracy, can no longer be silent in the light of the human rights violations that most european citizens of roma origin are facing in their daily existence. racism against roma is racism too and cannot – and should not – be tolerated any longer. racism and intolerance became rooted in european societies as the economic crisis deepened societal cleavages and created the premise for strengthening extremism against poor, deprived, socially—excluded european citizens, often ethnic roma. as we can see even here with our colleague, mr buonanno, racism is no longer limited to the fringes of society. it is present even here in the european parliament. what upsets me, as a roma, is that i am well enough educated not to discriminate myself. i feel sorry for him. legal means alone do not seem sufficient to counter trends and to counter discrimination. more needs to be done. anti-gypsyism, as commissioner jourová said – and i congratulate her – is one of the most acute problems facing europe today. it has for far too long been a widely—accepted policy at state stakeholders’ level, and this has to stop. therefore, in the interests of fully participatory democracy, i, as a roma, pledge myself in favour of acknowledging and assuming, through our internal european parliament political mechanism, the existence of anti-gypsy rhetoric.

in writing. in recent years, the issue of the roma minority has become a priority topic both in public debates and on the european political agenda. roma are one of the largest ethnic minorities in the european union, with statistics indicating that there are some 12 million roma living in different member states, often in difficult living conditions. although important legislative and institutional progress has been made in this time, the reality shows that there is still work to be done in the process of social inclusion of roma communities. discrimination, poverty, social exclusion, lack of education and access to basic healthcare are just some of the problems facing the roma community and we must continue to fight to solve them. the european union has developed a legislative framework aimed at increasing the social integration of marginalised groups and combating racism and racial discrimination, within the framework of overall strategic visions such as the europe 2020 strategy, the european platform for roma inclusion, the european framework for national roma integration strategies 2020. i believe that promoting policies for the social inclusion of minorities, through initiatives and actions to combat poverty, must be high on the european agenda.

vice-president of the commission. – mr president, my most sincere thanks go to the rapporteurs, ms thomas and mr fernandes. they have presented very clearly the importance of this proposed amendment for the european economy, as well as the urgent need for a decision to be taken. we in the commission, together with member states, made every effort possible to adopt as many programmes as possible in 2013 and to do so with a higher standard for quality of spending. we launched informal dialogues with member states in advance of the formal adoption of the multiannual financial framework (mff) and i can say here that, as a result of concerted efforts, the time that was taken to adopt programmes during this round of the mff was four months shorter than in the previous mff. but despite these efforts, because of the late adoption of the council regulation laying down the mff for 2014-2020 and also owing to delays involving the legislative acts, we unfortunately had the negative impact of having 300 programmes, or 47% of the programmes, that we could have adopted in 2014. as already mentioned, this is an amount of eur 21.1 billion. so, with six months lost because of the delay, all we are proposing in this technical adjustment is to use flexibility to extend this period by allowing us, as framed in article 19 of the mff regulation, for a revision of the mff before 1 may 2015. i would like to share with you three very quick points. first, staff at the commission are working very hard to accelerate adoption so we can have around eur 16 billion for 2015 and the remainder, as proposed, adopted in 2016. second, we have very much appreciated the fact that parliament’s committee on budgets has taken this issue very seriously and has worked on getting a fast proposal here in this chamber. i certainly join the rapporteurs in hoping for a positive vote. third, both ms thomas and mr fernandes talked about the need to use the flexibility that parliament has been fighting for to adjust the mff in future years. i just want to recall that we have committed to a mid-term review and revision of the mff, and we in the commission will be working on a very serious proposal when the time comes. we are very mindful of the significance of all we do and the speed at which we do it for the health of the european economy, improving our competitiveness, creating more jobs, and improving the lives of the european people. you have our commitment to act on your approval of revision immediately but also to make sure that money flows into programmes that generate opportunities and growth in europe.

mr president, i regret that the commission, which is here with us today, has not dared to use the word 'genocide', because, madam commissioner, we are discussing the genocide of the armenian people and the centenary of that genocide. the title of our resolution, which we shall be voting on shortly, is indeed this. the text very clearly calls on turkey to recognize the genocide, which is particularly important in the perspective of reconciliation between the turkish and armenian peoples. in other words, we are not adopting this resolution to criticise turkey, not to teach it lessons, but to encourage it to take a further step towards the recognition of this genocide. that is why we have taken note of the openness and apology already expressed by the present president and the present prime minister. let me say that i understand the difficulty the turks have in acknowledging the genocide. it was equally difficult for the romanians, for example, to admit their participation in the holocaust and the crimes against the jews and the roma. however, i believe we are not fully men if we do not recognize what our predecessors did. because it is not a question of history or science as mr erdogan claims: it is a question of memory and not a question of history. but the memory is the responsibility of political leaders, opinion leaders and ordinary people. it is not the preserve of scientific seminars. that's our point of view.
mr president, i will pay tribute today, like everyone else, to the memory of so many innocent ottoman armenians who were victims of the atrocities perpetrated in the context of the world war i. i would like to reiterate the call to both sides, turkey and armenia, to ratify and implement, with no preconditions, the protocols of 2009 and to take all necessary further steps towards the normalisation and improvement of their bilateral relations. it is of utmost importance to keep the memories of the past in order to prevent new conflicts and not to repeat them in the future. i would also like to emphasise the need to avoid any political instrumentalisation of such events and work together towards reconciliation. as a historian, i would conclude by saying: it is wise of politicians not to use or to misuse history for political purposes.
mr. president, today it is still a matter of diplomatic disagreement for international political actors to recognize as genocide the crimes committed against the armenian people a hundred years ago. i am convinced that we do not want to offend the turkish people by recognizing the genocide, the importance of the creation of the modern turkish state is enormous, but we cannot pretend that certain things did not happen. we can see how dark events in history still have an impact today, a hundred years later. let us learn to say things, to name the events of the past, for it always carries with it the possibility of a new beginning. we remember the armenian genocide because the armenian people and respect for human life in general demands it. let us remember to strengthen ourselves in the face of the horrors that are happening in the world today. so that what happened to the armenian people in the years after 1915 can't happen to other communities in 2015. and by the way, there's a country in the european union today where 18th and 19th century mass murderers are celebrated as national heroes.
in writing.– with this resolution, europe’s elected representatives have joined the worldwide commemorations that will culminate on 24 april. i believe that, on the commemoration of the centenary of the genocide against the armenians, we must make more efforts in order to move beyond and to build a common future, by pushing for a deep process of normalisation and reconciliation between the armenians and the turks. turks and armenians should support smaller, symbolic efforts that allow for dialogue and understanding, like last year’s statements by erdoğan, or the return of the armenian properties that were confiscated by the turkish state. this process must occur at the individual, societal, and state levels. this is a process that requires time and reconsideration of identity, as well as of history, but which is essential for both countries’ mutual trust and future cooperation. i believe that it is fundamental that we all recognise, remember and condemn these kind of tragedies, if we want to avoid them in the future. only through awareness of universal human rights, through passing on a collective memory, and through the consistent application of legal norms and international law, can these kind of crimes be prevented or stopped in their evolution.
in writing. the commemoration in the european parliament today of the 100th anniversary of the armenian genocide reminds us of the most important motivation behind the european unification movement, namely the desire to make war and crimes against humanity on european soil impossible. this sad reminder reminds us that we are in a period, which began last year and will continue, in which we mark the centenary of events full of multiple meanings for the european nations, whether we think of the moment of sarajevo, the end of the first world war or the tragedies of the great war. if we allow nationalists, xenophobes, demagogues and populists to use this series of commemorations to promote their own agenda, then we will only contribute to deepening the crisis of confidence in which europe finds itself today. we have a duty to seek those meanings which bring the peoples of europe closer together, which highlight the common values we all share. we will thus be able to help overcome the deep moral and trust crisis that is engulfing our societies, and to rediscover the energy needed to build the common european home.
madam president, it can be argued that quota systems and anti-discrimination legislation are contrary approaches to achieving the same goal. while the quota approach is based on the assumption that disabled persons cannot compete on the labour market with the same opportunities as the rest of society, and therefore working places must be reserved for them, the non-discrimination approach assumes that the issue can already be solved through the guarantee of individual rights to equal treatment and through workplace adaptations. however, the two approaches can coexist and can complement each other. in the eu the employment equality directive is a great achievement in the field of anti-discrimination. it led to the elaboration of new legislation in many states that did not have any previous provisions in this field. establishing a quota system in the eu institutions could serve as an example and could help pave the way towards a more inclusive employment system. this is one of the areas in which it can most affect the life of its citizens.
mr president, the integration of disabled people in the labour market represents one of the biggest challenges for social and labour market policies in modern societies. the recent economic crisis hit disadvantaged people hard and increased their inactivity and unemployment rates. i therefore strongly support quotas for the employment of people with disabilities. quotas are a concrete way of demonstrating a country’s willingness to integrate and provide equal opportunities for people with disabilities. since the guarantee of equal treatment for people with disabilities can lead to the establishment of foundational standards, with which the member states are expected to comply, i believe the european union institutions must be in the forefront in the adoption of quotas through the introduction of the obligation to have a certain proportion of persons with disabilities among the staff of the european union institutions. the employment quotas for people with disabilities are a means to ensure human dignity, fight inequality and reduce social disadvantages – three issues that are at the core of our political will and activity.
in writing. in most member states, people with disabilities continue to face great difficulties in finding a job or in keeping their jobs, as the unemployment rate remains high - twice that of the general population. member states and the commission need to strengthen their cooperation, because people with disabilities have the right to work in a normal environment without any discrimination against them, including at the level of the european institutions, which must set an example in applying existing provisions in this area. i believe that priority should be given to preventing the exclusion of these people from the labour market and to preserving their jobs. on the other hand, young people in such situations who are at the beginning of their journey should be supported by inclusion in various programmes of adapted traineeships with the aim of identifying the skills they can develop with a view to their placement in the labour market.
in writing. the right to work of people with disabilities must be respected and supported by the european union. such an affirmative measure is a positive element. in the european union, there are over 80 million people with disabilities, according to the european union agency for fundamental rights, while in my country, romania, there are over 700 000 people with disabilities. their presence in the european administrative system strengthens the european institutions. in this way, the eu reaffirms its human and social values of tolerance and non-discrimination. in addition to the elements mentioned in the debate, i also believe that a fair and balanced representation of these special places throughout the eu is appropriate. we know that in some countries there is not enough information about these opportunities and enough affirmative action to stimulate employment, and i believe that citizens with disabilities in those countries need to be further supported. for example, romania already occupies fewer seats in the european institutions than its share at the european level, and this under-representation is even more visible when it comes to the seats allocated to people with disabilities in romania. i think we also have to fight territorial discrimination against people with disabilities. one reason for the limited number is that the competition venues in romania are not adapted for disabled access.
mr president, i believe that a partnership with mexico and other countries on the matter of pnr is compatible with european union data protection rules and, with guarantees from both parties, is essential in order to address today’s global security challenges. the collection of personal data with detailed safeguards is a measure that we need to adopt in order to counter the threat of terrorism and to ensure the effective implementation of the european security strategy. this is why i believe that we need to move towards a european passenger name record system as well. therefore, i strongly support the commission’s agreement with mexico on the transfer of pnr data, and with other countries as well. we have to take any measure in order to assure the security and the protection of our citizens.
we need certainty that the juncker plan will help to balance european development. the principles of its application must be solidarity, fairness, transparency and, above all, the fight against inequalities. it is clear that we need fair control of the funding initiated by the juncker investment plan and i ask, in this direction, to rethink the system of approval of projects submitted for funding. large infrastructure must remain a priority and, to this end, the strategy must look at the overall need to connect the border areas of the european union to the centre. discussions on the multiplication capacity of european public investment targeted by the juncker plan, the possibility of reducing european research funding, the potential unequal distribution of funds and how they can contribute to accentuating disparities between european regions are all factors that require a careful analysis of the juncker plan. investment and action at european level is needed. however, we need to ensure that these safeguards and the actions taken to this end will work and not represent an unnecessary tax burden.
mr president, we all know how russia seized crimea from ukraine. we all know how the war started in eastern ukraine, supported by russia. hundreds of thousands of ukrainians took refuge in the neighbouring countries. hundreds of thousands of them are internally displaced. millions of people in ukraine are in need of humanitarian aid due to the combined impact of conflict displacement and extreme poverty. returnees, refugees and internally displaced persons face shortages in food, health services, basic household items, clean water and shelter. medicines are in alarmingly low supply. as we know, the eu and its member states have jointly contributed aid, directly or through different organisations and bodies. i would like to take advantage of the presence of the commissioner to make an appeal to the commission and council to take additional measures and provide support, especially by increasing humanitarian aid for ukrainian citizens.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on the mobilisation of the european globalisation adjustment fund (egf) to help france following the redundancies of 84 transport service units. according to eurostat, redundancies in the transport sector are a consequence of the global financial and economic crisis, which caused the decrease of road freight transport by vehicles over 3,5 tonnes by 13,4% in the eu and by 21% in france between 2007 and 2012. the bankruptcy and eventual closure of mory ducros resulted in the lay-off of over 2 800 employees, who now urgently need professional advice and guidance from specialist teams. that is why the financial support provided by the european globalisation adjustment fund facilitates the reconversion of displaced persons to other occupations needed on the labour market.
in writing. ‒ the redundancies in mory-ducros sas are linked to the general decline in physical output in europe, which leads to a reduction in volumes that, as described in the report, is directly linked to the global financial and economic crisis. the union has set up the european global adjustment fund to provide additional support to workers who sustain the consequences of major structural changes in world trade patterns or the global financial and economic crisis and to assist their reintegration into the labour market. i support financial assistance to mory-ducros sas workers who have become redundant and hope that deployment of assistance will be dynamic and made available as quickly and efficiently as possible.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on the decision to set up the social protection committee, with the role of strengthening cooperation in the field of social protection, but also to set up a group of senior officials at eu level. it is of the utmost importance that better coordination in the field of employment and social policies is ensured at european union level, while fully respecting national competences. monitoring the social situation and the development of social protection policies in the union, facilitating the exchange of information, experience and good practice between the member states and the commission, and preparing reports or delivering opinions in areas of competence are just some of the functions that the social protection committee is required to undertake.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on the draft council decision establishing the social protection committee and repealing decision 2004/689/ec. such a committee allows the european union to assess social protection measures that are and can be implemented at member state and eu level. a true social europe means more social protection.
in writing. ‒ article 5 of the treaty on the functioning of the european union (tfeu) provides that the union is to take measures to ensure coordination of the employment policies of the member states, with a view to increasing their effectiveness by developing a coordinated strategy for employment. given the increasing number of people being made redundant and the high number of companies facing bankruptcy, it is of the utmost importance that there is a coherent employment policy across the eu. that is why i voted in favour of this resolution setting up the employment committee, a body which will certainly contribute to the success of guaranteeing, coordinating and implementing employment policies at european union level.
in writing. ‒ article 5 of the treaty on functioning of the european union (tfeu) states that the union shall take measures to ensure coordination of the employment policies of the member states to enhance their effectiveness by developing a coordinated strategy for employment and for promoting a skilled, trained and adaptable workforce and labour markets that are responsive to economic change. the proposed council decision aims at establishing an advisory employment committee to promote coordination between member states on employment and labour market policies. i supported this proposal in the plenary session considering the positive outcomes this initiative will have on eu citizens.
in writing. ‒ i voted on the report on the draft council decision setting up the employment committee and repealing decision 2000/98/ec. analysing the employment situation at european level, the solutions developed by the member states and identifying effective and common measures must become a priority for the european union. such a special committee can ensure better cooperation at european level on employment.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the recommendation to amend the multiannual financial framework for the period 2014-2020 so that financial allocations not used in 2014 can be transferred to use for subsequent years. the cohesion fund, the european agricultural fund for rural development and the european maritime and fisheries fund are just some of the axes that will be revised for the transfer of funds for the coming years. the multiannual financial framework (mff) is a multiannual programming structure which translates the political priorities of the union into financial terms over a period of at least five years. it sets annual ceilings for large categories of expenditure. the annual budgetary procedure shall respect those ceilings. the multiannual financial framework ensures budgetary discipline and the predictability of expenditure at eu level.
in writing. ‒ i support the proposal for a council regulation amending the regulation on the multiannual financial framework for the years 2014-2020, as this proposal will have positive consequences on the new cohesion policy, which is essential for the european development and recovery from the economic crisis. the new cohesion policy provides support to new innovative business, supports smes, creates sustainable jobs, improves skills, combats poverty, promotes social inclusion, gives remote regions broadband, tackles the brain drain, improves the environment, promotes energy efficiency and the use of renewable energy resources, builds vital transport links and strengthens efficiency of public administrations. it is therefore important that resources are used in a timely manner and as effectively as possible, to generate growth and jobs. i hope that the swift adoption and implementation of remaining programmes will be carried out soon, that the calculations made by the commission will prove to be realistic and that the increase in the payments will be sufficient.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the recommendation on the proposal for a council regulation amending regulation (eu, euratom) no 1311/2013 establishing the multiannual financial framework for the period 2014-2020. this recommendation provides the legal framework necessary for the implementation of the multiannual financial programmes and cohesion policy. the financial capacity of european programmes is maintained by a transfer of budgetary resources.
in writing. ‒ welcomes the adoption of the european parliament recommendation on the proposal for a council regulation amending regulation (eu, euratom) no 1311/2013 establishing the multiannual financial framework for the period 2014 to 2020. i voted in favour of this recommendation, which concerns the revision of the multiannual financial framework with the aim of ensuring that the unused allocations in 2014 are transferred to the following years, above the corresponding expenditure ceilings. this proposal for a regulation is absolutely necessary in the context of the delayed adoption of the cohesion policy regulations for the period 2014-2020 which has caused delays in the timely adoption of all operational programmes.

in writing.– the number of car accidents is very high and many times a phone call can save lives. i think that the deployment of an emergency call system implanted in the vehicle and based on the 112 emergency number is a very important and concrete achievement for the safety of citizens. about 2 500 lives could be saved every year in europe. in 2013, the commission adopted two proposals to ensure that by october 2015 cars will automatically call emergency services in the event of a serious accident. the ʽecallʼ system automatically dials 112 in the event of a serious crash. however, data protection is a sensitive issue. vehicles should not be traceable and should not be subject to any constant tracking and the minimum set of data sent should include the minimum information.
in writing. road safety is a public health issue. the statistics, especially in states with less developed highway infrastructure, are worrying. in 2013, almost 26 000 people lost their lives in serious road accidents in the eu. the automated emergency system 'ecall' needs the support of the european parliament. preliminary data suggest that the adoption of an automated emergency system in cases where road users involved in accidents are unable to call 112 can save, on average, around 2 500 lives per year. a 10% reduction in the number of victims across the union is a target we must strive for. life comes first and, given that we have the possibility of introducing a mandatory, automated system that leads to saving human lives, the ecall report should have our support.

member of the commission.– madam president, last friday, 24 april, we were commemorating the fact that it was two years since the terrible accident at rana plaza in bangladesh. as we know, 1 100 lives were claimed and over a thousand people were injured. it was a tragedy for everybody who lost their lives, for the families and for those who were injured, and it was a tragedy that could have been prevented. although the garment industry in bangladesh has been very successful over many years, this disaster drew attention to the shaky foundations on which it has been built. it also highlighted the world’s shared responsibility for taking action to redress the situation, given the links between the garment workers in bangladesh and consumers all around the world. and let us not forget that eu citizens are the largest consumers as regards clothes made in bangladesh. through the bangladesh sustainability compact, the eu, the us, the government of bangladesh and the international labour organisation, referred to as the ‘compact partners’, have pledged their engagement to improve labour rights and working conditions in the bangladesh garment and knitwear industry. since the launch of the compact in july 2013, health and safety conditions at the workplace have been improving in the bangladesh garment sector. however, a lot of progress is still needed. these were the conclusions of the compact follow-up meeting between all partners held in october 2014 and of the technical status report that we published last friday. since october 2014, the commission has noted and welcomed the continued progress made by the government of bangladesh to increase capacity and resources for safety inspections on buildings and factories, a responsibility they must fully assume in the long term. but there are outstanding issues and let me highlight them. the first of these is the adoption as a matter of highest priority by the government of bangladesh of the implementing regulations of the labour law. that was decided more than two years ago and it is imperative for the overall improvement of the situation, not least for the newly appointed inspectors in order for them to have clear rules to be able to work effectively. we hear that work is progressing, but i would urge the government of bangladesh to ensure that there are no further delays in adopting the rules and that all stakeholders contribute constructively to the process. it is also important that the implementing regulations address unfair labour practices, including remedies. this will correspond to the government’s commitment to prioritise effective investigation and the prosecution of those involved in unfair labour practices, including anti-union discrimination and reprisals. a matter of equal importance is that we expect the adoption of legislation to ensure that workers in export processing zones enjoy freedom of association and collective bargaining rights. i would also like to emphasise the vital role businesses should play in enabling labour rights and safe working conditions in bangladesh. we have seen an unprecedented engagement by the private sector in all aspects of the accord and the alliance, amounting to more than 250 retailers from 20 countries, and between them they have inspected around 2 500 factories since the launch of the compact. inspection findings and remedial actions are publicly available online together with the summaries of government-led factory inspections. the bangladesh industry association is also playing its role by actively raising awareness among its members of workers’ and trade union rights and the importance of a constructive social dialogue. we commend this engagement by the private sector. it must continue, including through building further on the supply-chain initiatives in line with internationally recognised guidelines and principles on corporate social responsibility. going beyond bangladesh, the commission is actively engaged at multiple levels through the organisation for economic cooperation and development (oecd) and the international labour organisation (ilo) with issues on corporate social responsibility in the garment sector. finally, compensation is one of the burning issues and it was not directly covered by the compact. the commission continues to encourage garment companies and retailers to play their full part in the rana plaza donors trust fund, regardless of whether they produced or sourced from rana plaza. it is important that the experience gained by the government from working with stakeholders on compensation contributes to ensuring that ultimately a sustainable system for insurance and compensation can be established in bangladesh in the future. i thank this house for your strong involvement and support for the actions here and i am looking forward to the debate tonight.
on behalf of the epp group. madam president, two months ago i led a delegation to bangladesh, in dhaka, on behalf of the subcommittee on human rights of the european parliament. the main purpose of the delegation was to understand the extent to which the working conditions of garment workers had improved following the rana plaza tragedy. it must be said that despite progress, the situation of the 4 million workers in this sector, which accounts for 80% of bangladesh's total exports, is a cause for concern. i was able to visit one of the over 4,000 garment factories in bangladesh, and i realized that rana plaza was a serious wake-up call for the safety of the building and the workers, and more attention was being paid to this issue. factories began to have fire safety systems, electrical installations made by engineers, and, above all, to reinforce buildings. it's a little better than it was before april 24, 2013 for the ones that work legally, not for the more than 2,000 who work underground. this is a very sensitive issue, as is the political situation in bangladesh and the deadlock resulting from the confrontation, from the unresolved conflict between the awami league and the bangladesh nationalist party, a conflict that does not allow for an improvement in rights and, in particular, in social rights. in writing.– the agreement this week sends a clear message from the european parliament; we need to limit the use of first-generation biofuels and move towards more sustainable alternatives which put less pressure on the environment, food prices, and food security. using existing agricultural land for first-generation biofuels, and clearing natural carbon sinks such as ancient forests, actually contribute to the environmental problems which biofuels were supposed to help solve. the use of sustainability criteria should drive the development of more advanced biofuels, ones which are fully compatible with environmental objectives and not in direct competition with food crops.
member of the commission.– mr president, we are here today to finalise the last stage of the legislative process of adopting a directive that aims to tackle a very serious and highly visible environmental problem: the overconsumption and littering of lightweight plastic carrier bags. these bags, as was already mentioned, easily escape waste management streams and accumulate in our environment, often in the form of marine litter. once discarded, they can last for hundreds of years, often as harmful microscopic particles that threaten the environment worldwide, especially the marine environment in terms of marine litter. the very high and ever-increasing consumption rates of plastic bags – currently some 100 billion bags per year in the eu alone, and up to 200 bags per person per year – also imply a squandering of resources and have become a symbol of a throw-away society and a symbol of unsustainable lifestyles. lightweight plastic carrier bags that are used once only and then discarded are the example of a ‘linear’ model of dealing with resources. action is needed. we need to tackle the problem of marine pollution, which is to a great extent caused by plastic waste, and we need to save resources and move to a circular economy. clearly, this is a global problem, requiring action beyond the eu, but it is important that we do our part. an early second reading agreement on amending the packaging and packaging waste directive to reduce the use of lightweight plastic carrier bags can be formalised today. looking at the different positions of the co-legislators at the start of the legislative process, it is clear that this has not been an easy task, but thanks to the efforts undertaken by all parties, we now have a compromise on the table. let me particularly express my gratitude to the rapporteur, margarete auken, for her dedicated and thorough work on the commission’s proposal, as well as to the shadow rapporteurs in the committee on the environment, public health and food safety. the commission welcomes the agreement reached by the co-legislators, even though it includes some elements that would, in the commission’s view, have been better addressed in a different, and in a much broader context. nevertheless, this agreement has been possible because we all share the same objective: limiting the consumption and littering of plastic carrier bags. the text presented to you here today will make a real difference in reaching this objective.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the recommendation on the draft council decision authorising member states to become parties, in the interest of the european union, to the international maritime organisation's international convention on standards of training, certification and watchkeeping for fishing vessel personnel. the objective of the convention is to ensure that fishing vessel personnel have the necessary qualifications to mitigate potential risks to the safety of persons and/or property at sea or risks to the marine environment during operations on board seagoing vessels. i believe that maritime training provides greater safety and security in this area. maritime know-how is of strategic importance in maintaining the eu's position as a world leader in maritime affairs.
in writing. ‒ i am in favour of the proposal as it authorises member states to become signatories to the international convention on fishing vessel personnel of the international maritime organization.
in writing. on 7 july 1995, the international maritime organisation (imo) adopted in london the international convention on standards of training, certification and watchkeeping for seafarers on fishing vessels (hereinafter referred to as the 'stcw-f convention'). four member states have ratified this convention: spain, denmark, latvia and lithuania. the european union does not have the competence to ratify the stcw-f convention, only member states can do so. however, member states cannot ratify the convention without the eu's agreement. i voted for this resolution because its text authorises member states to ratify the stcw-f convention.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report as i strongly agree with the need of unified standards for the security of large fishing vessels personnel. adequate verifications should indeed be mandatory on the qualifications and health conditions of these people. it is a dangerous profession and this can both save lives and improve the quality of this field and i welcome the final text adopted by our house.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the draft amending budget for the 2014-2020 multiannual financial framework. the budget is presented together with the parallel commission proposal for the revision of the multiannual financial framework (mff) for the period 2014-2020, in accordance with article 19 of the mff regulation, and essentially reschedules the corresponding commitments for the following years. this project covers all 28 member states and aims to avoid delays in the adoption of programmes and ensure a smooth implementation of programmes supporting growth and employment. it is equally important that payment credits in this context are not modified in any way.
in writing. ‒ i supported this proposal to transfer the bulk of the allocations that were not used in 2014 to 2015, as adopted with unanimity in the committee on budgets.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report on the council position on draft amending budget no 2/2015 of the european union for the financial year 2015, section iii the commission, because its text invokes the need to be able to transfer unused appropriations from the 2014 budget to the budgets of the following years, this measure being vital for european citizens and for the economy of all member states, because in this way it can contribute to job creation and economic growth, two of the major objectives of the eu.
in writing. i voted on the report on the council position on draft amending budget no 2/2015 of the european union for the financial year 2015. i agree with the position expressed in the report on the need for closer monitoring by the commission of budget implementation in order to avoid the accumulation of an increasing volume of unpaid invoices. in the context of the decision to transfer the majority of unused appropriations from the 2014 to the 2015 financial year, i agree with the proposal to the commission to have a flexible approach to deal with possible difficulties resulting from an uneven financial profile, which could lead to unused commitments in the 2014-2020 period.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on the installation of the ecall in-vehicle system. road transport now exceeds 100 million vehicles per year in various member states and is increasing due to the consolidation of the european union. this is why road safety is a matter of major concern throughout the european union and for all its citizens. the purpose of the eu-wide interoperable ecall initiative is to introduce in all vehicles in the eu the minimum functionalities necessary to ensure the proper handling of emergency calls by emergency response services. i believe that action at eu level is needed to ensure interoperability and continuity of service across europe, which is a laudable and auspicious initiative in the current european context.
in writing. ‒ on 13 june 2013, the commission adopted two proposals to ensure that by october 2015 cars will automatically call emergency services in the event of a serious crash. the ecall system automatically dials 112 – europeʼs single emergency number – in the event of a serious accident. this legislative package contained the regulation on the in-vehicle system which establishes the technical requirements for the ec type-approval of vehicles regarding the ecall in-vehicle system on the basis of which the sehnalová report has been drafted. the deployment of a public eu-wide emergency call system embedded in the vehicle and based on the 112 number represents a very important and concrete achievement for the safety of citizens. about 2 500 lives could be saved every year in europe. i therefore voted for adoption of the report.
in writing. ‒ i voted for the regulation on type-approval requirements for the installation of a 112-based ecall system in vehicles so that citizens can benefit from it from 2018. in the eu, 26 000 people die in road accidents every year. improving safety on european roads is a pressing need and requires a system that can reduce the time it takes for emergency services to reach the scene of an accident. ecall is a valuable, free and secure tool for respecting privacy. accident location data should be used for the same objective: halving road deaths over the next 10 years. the negotiations for this regulation clarified the rules according to which the vehicle coordinates are transmitted only when the 112 service is activated. this data is only transmitted to the 112 service and not to other operators. the mandatory nature of ecall for new types of cars is paramount. parliament voted today to introduce this life-saving device which can be compared to the introduction of seat belts and airbags. the commission will continue to monitor the implementation of the new rules and to monitor the implementation of the new rules.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report on the council's first reading position with a view to the adoption of a regulation of the european parliament and of the council concerning type-approval requirements for the installation of a 112-based ecall in-vehicle system and amending directive 2007/46/ec, as i consider that the installation of a 112-based ecall in-vehicle system is highly necessary and very useful for all citizens.
in writing. ‒ reducing the greenhouse gas intensity of fuels used in road transport and non-road mobile machinery by 6% by 2020 is an ambitious target of the european commission. one of the objectives set out in the sixth community environment action programme, established by decision no 1600/2002/ec of 22 july 2002 (4), is to achieve levels of air quality that do not have a significant negative impact on human health and the environment. i voted in favour of this directive because it would further reduce the national permitted levels of emissions of the main pollutants of the member states, as well as the emissions associated with refuelling motor vehicles at petrol stations and would address the sulphur content of fuels.
