in writing. ‒ the fuel quality directive and renewable energy directive (red) aim at limiting the contribution of conventional biofuels towards the attainment of targets in the red, improving greenhouse gas (ghg) performance of biofuel production processes, encouraging greater market penetration by advanced biofuels and reporting the estimated indirect land use change (iluc) emissions. i supported the adoption of the report in the plenary because i believe it is fundamental to move towards advanced biofuels that deliver real benefits for the climate while avoiding competition with food production.
in writing. ‒ one of the objectives of directive 2009/28/ec of the european parliament and of the council is that each member state must ensure that the share of energy from renewable sources used in all means of transport will be at least 10% of the final consumption of energy in the transport sector in that member state by 2020. i voted for this report because the amendments introduced aim to achieve this objective, as well as other important and very necessary objectives, including the encouragement of research and development in the new advanced biofuel production sectors.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report and welcome the work done by the rapporteur, as i believe no effort should be spared in our attempts to improve fuel quality with a view to increasing the use of renewable, green and sustainable energy sources. we could indeed promote even more the development and production of biofuels, and i believe that the short-term costs of implementing directives like this one, of adapting the car manufacturing industry to the new fuels, will be easier to bear than the long-term immense environmental costs associated with pollution and loss of sources for current conventional fuels.
in writing. ‒ finding viable policies to decarbonise the transport system has proved more difficult in practice than we initially estimated, and achieving the targets we have set in this regard will not be possible without the contribution of biofuels. today we voted after two years of negotiations full of syncope and compromise. the final document is not what the european parliament wanted at first reading, but it clarifies some uncertainties and sets a roadmap in quantifying the real impact of iluc on greenhouse gas emission reductions from first generation biofuels. our role is to regulate to the extent that we facilitate a stable and investment-friendly framework that fosters job creation and sustained economic growth. the imposition of a 7% cap on first generation biofuels will allow us to redirect investments to advanced, so-called sustainable biofuels without jeopardising investments already made in the first generation sector. we do not yet have a scientific method for determining the factor - therefore, i believe that the agreement reached on its monitoring and reporting will provide us with the data needed to introduce this factor into the sustainability criterion.
in writing. ‒ reducing the consumption of plastic bags for transport, along with packaging and packaging waste, must be an immediate concern for all those responsible for protecting the environment. given that it can take several hundred years for a plastic packaging to decompose, it is more than worrying that over 8 billion bags become waste in europe every year. i voted in favour of the proposal for a regulation requiring member states to take measures to reduce the consumption of plastic carrier bags of less than 50 microns. however, i think we need to go further and focus on encouraging consumers to reuse plastic carrier bags. moreover, the introduction of standards setting biodegradable properties for carrier bags used on the european market, as well as the setting of quantity limits for carrier bags, would contribute to the decrease in the number of plastic carrier bags.
in writing. ‒ i believe that the obligation on the commission to provide for specific measures on the labelling of biodegradable and compostable plastic carrier bags is an important means of avoiding misleading practices of false labelling of plastic bags, especially in the case of so-called 'oxo-biodegradable' plastic bags.
in writing. ‒ parliament concluded its first reading on 16 april 2014, which was adopted by a wide majority of 543/54/68. it supported binding targets to achieve a 50% reduction in consumption of plastic bags within three years and an 80% reduction within five years as compared to the average eu consumption in 2010. considering the fact that discarded plastic bags cause serious damage to the environment, not to mention the harm being done by marine litter to biodiversity, i strongly support parliamentʼs recommendation. the problem can be easily and efficiently addressed as already proved in some member states; putting a charge on the use of plastic bags is a quick and sustainable way of reducing the problem overnight.
in writing. ‒ the european commission's objective for this directive is to limit negative environmental effects, especially in terms of waste generation, to encourage waste prevention and more efficient use of resources, while limiting negative socioeconomic effects. more specifically, the proposal aims to reduce the consumption of plastic carrier bags with a thickness of less than 50 microns (0.05 millimetres) in the european union. i voted in favour of this report because it meets the objectives of the european commission's proposal, which is essential to improve the environment and the quality of life of citizens.
in writing. ‒ this report is in truth long overdue. i voted in favour because i believe all our voters are tired of seeing trash dumps and landfills full of plastic bags. these items have become ubiquitous in our lives and it is unfortunate. we should actively promote people to reuse bags, to use recyclable and biodegradable materials and to make an effort, over a small immediate personal comfort, for the protection of our environment. i believe any costs associated with this text would be far outweighed by the costs of cleaning and processing the massive amounts of plastic bags in usage today.
in writing. ‒ all the studies carried out by european and global institutions over the last 30 years, unanimously acknowledged in the global work to reduce the widespread use of plastic, show that the environment is irretrievably poisoned by the indiscriminate use of this material. in this context, i welcome the vote in the european parliament plenary today in favour of new legislative proposals to limit plastic bags, considered to be the most widely used and most polluting packaging material, throughout the european union. the legislative changes on the use of plastic bags are in line with all sustainable development programmes adopted both at european level and by the governments of the european union member states.
in writing. i welcome the fact that, after lengthy negotiations between the european parliament and the council, the commission has improved its proposal on reducing the consumption of thin plastic carrier bags by including an obligation for member states. as such, i voted in favour of the recommendation on the council's position at first reading with a view to the adoption of a directive of the european parliament and of the council amending directive 94/62/ec as regards the reduction of the consumption of lightweight plastic carrier bags. in practice, in terms of waste legislation, we will for the first time have eu-wide binding measures on waste generation and management. i believe that romania has a direct interest in the introduction of mandatory measures at eu level that will have positive effects in our waste management system.
in writing. ‒ maritime shipping remains the only means of transportation which is not included in the european union’s action to reduce greenhouse gas emissions. at eu level, the international maritime sector today accounts for around 3% of global greenhouse gas emissions and these are expected to increase significantly in the future. the main objective of this regulation is to establish a european monitoring, reporting and verification (mrv) system for co2 emissions from ships as the first step in a staged approach to reducing these emissions. in order to reduce the related administrative costs while ensuring robust results, simple and lean mrv requirements are proposed. an eu-wide system for the mrv of greenhouse gas emissions from shipping is necessary in order to improve the information about ship efficiency and emissions from the sector, and encourage reducing emissions and fuel consumption.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this resolution on the council's position at first reading with a view to adopting a regulation of the european parliament and of the council on the monitoring, reporting and verification of carbon dioxide emissions from maritime transport and amending directive 2009/16/ec, as it introduces a much-needed system for monitoring, reporting and verifying carbon dioxide emissions from maritime transport.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on amending regulation (ec) no 223/2009 on european statistics in order to strengthen the professional independence of national statistical authorities. recent economic developments have once again demonstrated the need to further strengthen the credibility of statistical authorities. the reliability of statistical data with regard to the technical evaluation criteria is a condition for ensuring the confidence of users, but equally important is the credibility of the institutions producing statistics. in this context, the professional independence of the statistical authorities should receive special attention and be guaranteed by law.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this draft legislative resolution of the european parliament on the council's position at first reading with a view to adopting a regulation of the european parliament and of the council amending regulation (ec) no 223/2009 on european statistics, given the importance and necessity of such european statistics. i would stress that the adoption of the act in line with the council's position is a success.
in writing. ‒ i think the main thrust of the commission's proposal that a management plan for several species in the baltic sea is needed is a correct one.
in writing. ‒ a management plan for the baltic sea cod stocks has been in place since 2007, but the stocks of herring and sprat are not yet subject to a management plan. the current proposal is the first multiannual plan under the reformed common fisheries policy (cfp). it aims to ensure sustainable exploitation of stocks of cod, herring and sprat, and provide stability for fishing opportunities, while ensuring that management is based on the most up-to-date scientific information on interactions within and between the stocks and with other aspects of the ecosystem and environment. this is the first multiannual plan under the reformed cfp which will serve as a model for upcoming multiannual plans. i support the adoption of the report, as it is in line with the objectives of the cfp to ensure environmental, economic and social sustainability and respect the precautionary and ecosystem-based approach to fisheries management.
in writing. ‒ the european union is a contracting party to the united nations convention on the law of the sea of 10 december 1982. the convention provides for obligations to maintain and conserve certain fish species so that they can be exploited at levels that ensure maximum long-term production. i voted for this report on the ep and council regulation because it introduces a series of amendments aimed at restoring, reaching and maintaining the populations of the species concerned above levels which allow maximum sustainable yields for those stocks to be achieved.
in writing. ‒ one of the central objectives of common fisheries policy (cfp) reform is the gradual elimination of discards in eu fisheries through the introduction of a landing obligation. all catches must be brought and retained on board the fishing vessels, recorded, landed and counted against the quotas where applicable, in accordance. the ʽomnibusʼ regulation serves to make the landing obligation operational and to remove any legal and practical impediments to its implementation by removing or amending certain provisions within the current regulations on technical, management and control measures. i voted in favour of the landing obligation, as it provides for the implementation of one of the central objectives of the cfp reform: the elimination of the wasteful practice of discarding. it creates planning and legal certainty for fishermen until new legislation in line with the reformed cfp is in place.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report because it provides for the introduction of a landing obligation for catches of species subject to catch limits rules, as well as for other species subject to the provisions on 'minimum sizes' in the mediterranean sea, landings which aim to phase out discards in all fishing activities in the european union. at the same time, i consider these measures to be essential for the protection of the marine ecosystem.
in writing. ‒ the conclusion of the protocol to the partnership and cooperation agreement establishing a partnership between the european communities and their member states, of the one part, and russia, of the other part, to take account of croatia's accession to the european union is a significant moment for croatia as part of the eu. the protocol includes the republic of croatia as a contracting party to the agreement and represents the eu's commitment to provide the authentic version of the agreement in the new official language of the european union. the partnership and cooperation agreement with the russian federation covers, inter alia, the promotion of trade and investment, including trade in transport services, and establishes a framework for cooperation, which is limited to economic, financial and general technical cooperation, in various sectors. i voted in favour of this report, which represents a normal step in the current context of croatia's full accession to the european union.
in writing. ‒ this is a technical report that takes into account the accession of croatia to the eu and the need to reflect this change in the existing partnership and cooperation agreement with russia.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this draft european parliament legislative resolution on the draft council decision on the conclusion, on behalf of the european union and its member states, of the protocol to the partnership and cooperation agreement establishing a partnership between the european communities and their member states, of the one part, and the russian federation, of the other part, to take account of the accession of the republic of croatia to the european union, given the need and importance of this protocol to the partnership and cooperation agreement.
in writing. ‒ on 19 june 1999, one year after the sorbonne declaration, ministers responsible for higher education in 29 european countries signed the bologna declaration, agreeing on six important common objectives for the coherent and harmonious development of higher education by 2010. the bologna process has brought about profound reforms in higher education for all participating states, marked by changes in higher education legislation and a reconsideration of the basic principles of the educational process for a knowledge-based society. the role of the bologna process underlines once again that education and research are the main pillars of our society in terms of promoting skills development, growth and job creation. i voted in favour of this report because i am convinced that investing in education is essential to combat poverty, social inequalities, social inclusion and unemployment, especially among young people. in this regard, member states are invited to provide more mobility opportunities and to step up the implementation of the mobility 2020 strategy, as well as to take into account the effective promotion of the erasmus+ and horizon 2020 programmes.
in writing. ‒ i welcome the fact that some member states have developed a comprehensive strategy to include students from disadvantaged socioeconomic backgrounds in higher education, thus addressing the problem of the so-called 'social filter', and i hope that it will be an example for all member states.
in writing. ‒ today, ensuring comparability and compatibility in the standards and quality of higher education qualifications, supporting mobility of students and internationalisation, and providing students with a wider and more transparent choice of high-quality educational opportunities are matters of the outmost importance, not only for european students, but also and especially for the recovery of the european economy. these are powerful means to tackle issues like youth unemployment, economic constraints and demographic changes. this is why i support the adoption of this report in the plenary, as i believe that it will boost the bologna process and provide the necessary means to accomplish the fulfilment of its goals.
in writing. ‒ the bologna process has meant profound reforms of higher education for all participating states, marked by changes in legislation and a reconsideration of the basic principles of the educational process. my country signed the bologna declaration in 1999, committing itself to include the objectives set out in it in the priorities of romanian higher education. i voted in favour of this report because its text reiterates the importance of this 'process' in the development of education and learning at eu level, but at the same time involves the entire academic community, the social partners and 'calls for the political commitment and cooperation of the seis ministers in developing a common strategy to achieve the reforms of the bologna process' and, by implication, the education-related objectives set out in strategy 2020.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the resolution on monitoring the implementation of the bologna process, particularly in view of the social dimension of this process. education is one of the areas most affected by the economic difficulties facing the eu. therefore, i believe that a considerable funding effort is required to make the target of 3% of the union's gdp for research and education by 2020 achievable. the fact that one third of european employers are having difficulty recruiting appropriately qualified staff, despite unemployment affecting the younger generation, also obliges member states to streamline education policies in order to bring vocational skills training systems into line with labour market requirements. last but not least, the mutual recognition of professional and academic qualifications can facilitate the movement of labour and the proper integration of european workers. access to education and the promotion of lifelong learning, including through appropriate vocational retraining programmes, can effectively contribute to tackling the economic crisis, inequalities and unemployment and, in the long term, to ensuring a positive momentum for social inclusion and economic growth.
in writing. ‒ european films are economic and cultural assets, making a substantial contribution to the union's economic growth and job creation. the european film fund allocates €2.1 billion annually to support the european audiovisual industry. of this amount, eur 110 million is from the media sub-programme of the creative europe programme. in 2012, some 1 300 films were produced in the eu, compared with over 800 in the us, but only 8% of european films are distributed in cinemas in non-eu countries. the commission will continue to monitor the implementation of the union's policy on the environment and its implementation of the union's policy on the environment, and will continue to monitor the implementation of the union's policy on the environment and its implementation of the union's policy on the environment. in this respect, i welcome this report on european cinema in the digital age, because i believe that the european film forum will open the way for representatives of cinema, member states and european institutions to find appropriate solutions leading to a better distribution of european films.
in writing. ‒ this own-initiative report comes in response to the commission communication on ʽeuropean film in the digital era, bridging cultural diversity and competitivenessʼ. europe’s film industry is diverse and creative, and has a great potential as its film heritage is successful and inspirational worldwide. however, the digital revolution offers new possibilities, as well as posing new challenges. it is therefore essential to adapt to the digital era and use its potential to reach new and wider audiences. the potential of the cultural and creative sectors in europe and in particular of the european film industry is yet to be fully exploited in the promotion of european cultural and linguistic diversity and heritage within and outside europe, as well as the creation of growth and jobs that can also benefit other sectors of the economy, providing europe with a competitive advantage at a global level.
in writing. ‒ promoting european cultures across borders, but also facilitating cultural exchanges, is done through film. the film, an economic and cultural asset, also makes a substantial contribution to the development of the european economy. i voted for this report because, through its text and the amendments tabled, it 'encourages the european film industry to pursue the creation of innovative services, new distribution channels', thus encouraging film distributors to ensure greater visibility and availability of films from all european countries in order to give the widest possible access to them and to the implicit knowledge of the culture and civilization of the european peoples.
in writing. cinematography, part of european culture and civilization, is supported by the eu. the eu allocates €2.1 billion of eu funds to cinema each year to support the european audiovisual industry. in this context, i voted in favour of the report on european cinema in the digital age. welcomes the adoption of the report by mr bogdan wenta, and agrees with his view that, in order to fully exploit its cultural and economic potential, the european film industry must develop in an appropriate environment, stimulated by a stable and adaptable legal framework, which encourages investment and diversity and allows the development of new online services.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on the new eu strategy on forests and the forestry sector because i believe that forests and forestry are a good solution for an additional economic pillar and are also the best guarantors of quality of life, sustainability, jobs and value creation. with over 3.5 million jobs, the forestry sector is the third largest employer in europe, just behind the metal and food industries. over 451 820 forestry enterprises contribute 7% to economic growth and use only 60% of the timber that can be used annually. wood is an important resource with a major economic role for rural areas. the eu strategy aims to further strengthen the social, economic and ecological role of forests and the forestry sector and to put wood at the forefront as a sustainable raw material, considered an important resource for europe.
in writing. ‒ i believe that the eu forest strategy must focus on sustainable management of forests and their multifunctional role from an economic, social and economic perspective and must ensure better coordination and communication of european policies that directly or indirectly target forestry.
in writing. ‒ i welcome the very positive aspects that have been introduced in the report and especially the more holistic approach from the committee on agriculture and rural development on the subject, with more stress on long-term sustainability, resource-efficient use, a multifunctional approach in forest management and future challenges because of wood scarcity and threats from climate change, emphasis on the pan-european forest agreement and an action plan with specific measures and funding. i believe it is important, when dealing with such multidimensional issues, to ensure that we are dealing with them in the most comprehensive way. i appreciate therefore the introduction of very important issues such as employment in the sector and the sustainable use of forest resources. i believe that this report goes in the right direction, by ensuring that people in europe understand better the importance of their forests and will be able to benefit from them in many ways.
in writing. ‒ the forestry sector provides jobs for 3 million european citizens. the report sets out a series of measures that complement the commission's efforts to boost employment and wealth in the european forestry sector in a sustainable way. i voted for this report because the amendments tabled underline the need for 'a specific long-term action plan highlighting the importance of mobilising and using wood sustainably to create added value and jobs in this sector'.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this text as it is a much-needed first step towards a more cohesive approach between eu member states to the preservation, development and sustainable use of their forestry resources. my country, romania, is the country with the richest forests in the eu and i believe they represent a huge economic potential, in terms of sustainable tourism and recreation, of high-quality timber production. more should be done to not only protect but increase europe’s forest, and we must remember that this resource can have a direct impact on other fields as well, including co2 emissions on a continent-wide basis.
in writing. ‒ i voted for the kostinger report on the eu forestry strategy. forests play an important role, both economically and in protecting the environment, by absorbing carbon dioxide. therefore, member states should be encouraged to manage forests sustainably. rural development funds can be used for this and i hope that government and local authorities will show more responsibility when it comes to forest exploitation. i believe that the implementation of the new forestry strategy should compensate for the lack of specific provisions on forestry policy in the eu treaty. it should also ensure coordinated positions between eu and member states' policies on forest-related issues at international level.
in writing. i voted for the report on 'a new eu strategy for forests and the forestry sector'. i welcome the initiative of my colleague elisabeth köstinger to produce a report recommending that the commission strengthen the standing committee on forests, which, in her view, could prevent parallel and divergent approaches at european level to this sector. i believe that the new eu forest strategy must focus on better coordination so that forestry and forests are better positioned in european strategies and enjoy a more coherent approach. i believe that our country has a direct interest in promoting a coherent strategy in this area at european level.
mr president, i support the report on the adoption of the european agenda on security. in fact i think that this agenda – and i am addressing the first vice-president of the commission, mr timmermans – should be more ambitious. i do not understand why we, the european union countries, do not set up a counter-terrorism agency, a european union agency to fight terrorism. we know that member states are currently sharing only a maximum of 50% of the information relating to terrorism. can we afford to continue in this way? can we afford to have more terrorist attacks in europe? it is probably time that we set up together a real counter-terrorism european agency to fight terrorism. we can see that this threat is spreading in europe and we are going to face tremendous situations in the future if we do not increase cooperation to fight terrorism.
the reporter. madam president, we have discussed terrorism in the previous hour and we are all against terrorism. i mean, terrorism is financed by fraud, by organized crime, by corruption and, yes, terrorism is also financed by fraud with european funds. we're talking in the european union about the fraud of our citizens' money of 3 to 5 billion euros a year. it's a huge amount, just in numbers on paper. it's probably much bigger in reality. they steal money for jobs, for youth, for research, for innovation. they're stealing our money. they steal from our lives. poverty is increasing. all this is the consequence of the fact that today, unfortunately, at the level of the european union, we do not have an effective mechanism to combat fraud with european money. the investigation of fraud with european money is now carried out by each member state, not at union level. some member states do it effectively for fraud with funds allocated to their country, but other member states do it not at all or do it very little effectively - very badly, to put it bluntly. this differentiation between the way fraud with european funds is investigated in the member states makes it absolutely necessary to have a single office at european level to investigate fraud with european funds. that is why the european public prosecutor's office is needed. the result will be that fraud with european funds will be investigated faster, better, faster and to a much greater extent, and the recovery of money will obviously mean much more. a lot more money will be put back into the pockets of our citizens. let us not forget that we, all of us here and in the european institutions, are the custodians of our citizens' money. that is what i want the european prosecutor to be. by investigating from start to finish and bringing to justice those who are found guilty or suspected of having stolen european money, the european public prosecutor can guard public money, european money. we need the european public prosecutor's office, which is made up of independent people, of prosecutors specialised in the fight against fraud. the commission will continue to monitor the implementation of the new rules and will continue to monitor the implementation of the new rules. let's make a comparison and see that the only answer is a european anti-fraud office. if we are fighting an organised group of people who are defrauding european funds and they are doing it from several member states, how can we respond other than through a group of prosecutors from all member states, working together, efficiently, flexibly, quickly and annihilating these groups of fraud against european funds. the report shall provide for investigative means. an investigation will always be carried out in any member state, with the authorisation and in accordance with the law of that country and, of course, with respect for the individual rights of suspects.
rapporteur for the opinion of the committee on legal affairs. madam president, first of all i am pleased that this report on the creation of the european public prosecutor's office is to be adopted and i am pleased that i was able to be the rapporteur for the opinion of the committee on legal affairs of the european parliament. i would like to thank my colleagues in the committee for the fact that together we have managed to adopt this report in record time and have thus demonstrated the support of the committee on legal affairs for the creation of this body, which is to fight crime at european level. i note with sadness that three of our ideas were not taken up in the final report. the first concerns the independence of the european prosecutor from political parties and the absence of any link between those appointed to hold these posts and national or european political formations. the second concerns the explicit integration of legal principles such as fairness, justice or the guarantee of equality and freedom of the individual. the third idea is to enhance the role of the european prosecutor in combating and preventing cross-border crime. however, i will vote for this report because i believe that the european public prosecutor's office will help to make the fight against corruption at european level more effective.
the question is "blue cardboard". madam president, i heard what you said, but i must say that in romania and bulgaria, for example, we have set up the cooperation and verification mechanism, and that has helped us to strengthen our justice system. justice has no political colour, just as it has no nationality. do you think that the european judiciary cannot handle things properly? do you think justice has a nationality? i don't think he is! what is your opinion on this subject? do you think that there will be no proper justice at european level?
member of the commission.– madam president, honourable members, thank you for your discussion, for all the opinions, and of course my special thanks to those who expressed support for the proposal to establish the european prosecutor’s office (eppo). i would like to assure you that the fight against corruption and fraud is the highest political priority of the commission and of myself. i am truly convinced that we need an independent eppo which will bring harmonised procedures and ensure the fair investigation of criminal offences infringing the financial interests of the eu; i believe it will bring tangible results. i am convinced that the taxpayers of the eu deserve to have such an institution which will safeguard their money. taking a very conservative estimate, i would say that some eur 1 to 2 billion a year could be secured and brought back to european treasuries and the european budget, or be refunded to the member states, by which i mean used in honest projects in the context of eu structural funds. when we are speaking about such a large amount of money to be secured versus the costs of the european prosecutor’s office, i think we can say there is a good cost-benefit balance in this case. we need the eppo as a specialised institution functioning alongside olaf and eurojust, and mr voss was right when he spoke about the need for a very precise description and plan of the procedures and the cooperation between the eppo, eurojust and olaf because this must operate in a very efficient way. there is still a lot of work to do. we must secure a clear division of competences at the central and national levels, and ensure the transparent selection of people for the positions. we have already introduced the conditions and criteria of integrity, independence and professionalism of the people to be selected. those of you who said that the procedural rights of the criminal procedure of the member states must not be sacrificed, are right. they must also be secured in the eppo procedure. a last comment regarding the yellow cards which the eppo received from several member state parliaments. i do not consider the question of these yellow cards to have been concluded, so i have been addressing all these parliaments, in some cases making a personal visit. i have tried to explain how we can go forward with the proposal, that there are safeguards to ensure that the principle of subsidiarity is not infringed, that a decentralised structure is foreseen and that the jurisdiction of the national courts will be maintained… among many other things. i must say that i have had some quite positive reactions from the members of the national parliaments and i hope that through this enhanced communication we will be able to conclude that there is in fact no breach of subsidiarity. i thank you once again and i would ask you to vote in favour of the eppo in tomorrow’s vote.
the reporter. madam president, that was a very interesting discussion. i'll try to answer some of the questions that have been raised. firstly, i ask rhetorically, because i already have this information, those in the member states or in certain political groups who oppose the european public prosecutor's office: what sums have they recovered through their own investigations in their countries from fraud with european funds? have they recovered much? have they recovered a bit? maybe they really don't want anyone to interfere, they don't want anyone to see if they did a good job or not. this is related to the second thing i want to say, and it's very important: european money, the money of our citizens, is in a common basket. as long as they're together in one basket, they must be protected by all of us. if in one country things are going very well and investigations are being completed and in other countries they are not, you should know that citizens of the countries where things are going well are also being stolen. i would like to give this answer mainly to my colleagues in the netherlands who have invoked this, namely that they do well in their investigations at home. i'm sure you do! except in other countries they don't, and the money is in this common basket. and then a third point: the independence of the prosecutors from politics. i think it was just a speech by mr negrescu to show that he cares about this independence, while at home, now in romania, on the contrary, they vote the opposite in parliament. i want to put it this way: the independence of the european prosecutors, both those in the member states and those in the central office, is clearly ensured from the outset in this report on the european public prosecutor's office. very briefly: four yes, we want to include vat offences and also fraud with european funds in the candidate countries and other countries to which we give money. we must be ambitious to reduce fraud with european funds.
madam president, this regulation aims to achieve two major objectives: firstly, to provide greater protection for investors in mutual funds, which operate on the money market by investing in short-term financial assets, and secondly, to strengthen financial stability by addressing an industry of around 1 000 billion euro. i would like to thank the colleagues who worked on this report because, after a long negotiation, they were able to reach compromise amendments that allow these objectives to be achieved. i would particularly stress the amendments limiting the scope of the concept of the constant value of net assets to those relating to their liquidity, as well as to the prevention of the risk of an unexpected flight of investors, the standards on avoiding risky concentration of the investment portfolio and the necessary transparency.
blue-card question.– these money market funds have been identified as acting as shadow banks and are, therefore, susceptible to different risks. in fact, the liquidity and diversification requirements for these money market funds have been strengthened, as have transparency and reporting requirements. however, they are not overseen like normal banks. do you not think that all these funds should be overseen by the national banks – like all the other banks – with the same requirements?
member of the commission.– madam president, it seems to me there is a very clear linkage between the operation of the markets and small businesses, namely: if you can make them work properly, you can get more money in investment flowing to the small businesses that we all want to see growing in europe. it has been a very interesting debate, if short. my admiration for neena gill has been increased through listening to the divergence of views that we have heard here, articulated very clearly and with equal passion. it confirms in my mind the importance of trying to make progress on the compromise that has been agreed so far. it is also a reflection of the broader challenges we face in looking at financial regulation as to how we can best balance growth and risk mitigation. i am confirmed in my support and admiration for the work that neena gill has done. i will certainly underline to the latvian presidency the importance of making progress with this proposal. we have an opportunity now to get some momentum going, and if we do not take it, i fear that we will find it hard to get it back again. as far as the specific question i was asked about a sunset clause is concerned, it is the case, obviously, that the phasing out of cnav funds was not something that the commission included in its original proposal. the most important issue for us – our bottom line, if you like – is that we get a sufficiently robust regime in place to deal with credit and interest rate risks for all money market funds, including cnavs. if we can get the risk management regime right overall, that would deal with the question of the sunset clause. that is something we will be monitoring closely in the council process, and obviously during the trilogue process that will follow. we need to get a deal on money market funds. it would represent a significant step in moving closer to finalising the post-crisis reform agenda. a positive vote in tomorrow’s plenary would itself be a significant step towards securing that final deal.

question referred under the 'blue card' procedure. you speak very nicely about political parties, as if you are not from a political party. you talk about political groups as if you're not part of a political group. you talk about the money spent by the european institutions as if you don't get your salary from the european parliament. why the criticism? we need to work together so that the european institutions use this money creatively and usefully for citizens. i agree with that! but i don't think we should use populist arguments against democratic principles.
mr president, the epp group supports public-private partnerships. european partnerships have proven to have had remarkable results and have helped to address important requirements of european citizens. the system is a positive one and should be further encouraged. we're discussing today the budget discharges of seven ppe. the court of auditors issued qualified opinions for three of them, imi, eniac and artemis for the third time: 2011, 2012 and 2013. as a result, the committee on budgetary control proposes to postpone the discharge. the epp group supports this delay and calls for the shortcomings identified by the court, in particular those relating to ex-post audits, to be addressed by the autumn of this year. we are also awaiting the commission's reports on the three epps, in view of the unification of artemis with eniac and imi 2. sesar, clean sky and fch received a discharge vote from the committee on budgetary control. information was requested from all epps on the contributions of the partners as well as on the practical results of the work so far. i suggest to the court that a uniform approach be taken to the partners' contributions by mentioning them in all control acts. i hope that the replacement of the iter and f4energy directors will lead to very close collaboration and lead iter towards the achievement of its proposed objectives.
mr president, i thank the rapporteur and the committee for implementing and proposing this project. we are talking about seven million unemployed, we are talking about seven million unemployed young people, we are talking about, basically, seven million destinies that we are deciding today. it's not a small thing! a billion euros for prefinancing projects to combat unemployment is a good measure. it must be supplemented by other measures. i am glad that the european parliament is once again showing that it is moving faster and coming up with solutions to combat unemployment, and coming up with coherent statements and projects. the increase in pre-financing from 1% to 30% is also a positive element. i would like the member states to respond positively to the request of the european parliament and the european commission. in the government of romania and romania i can tell you that there is the necessary support for the implementation of these measures, because romania was, moreover, among the first countries to implement the first pilot projects for the youth guarantee. to make these things a reality, the additional funds must be matched by concrete projects to help young people.
mr president, i wanted to take the floor on this as a member of the committee on budgets. i mean, i'm quite disappointed with this final form of the project, although mr deprez is one of my favourites from the other political groups, because he maintains a number of inequalities and accentuates others. parliament represents the citizens. we fund representation, not bureaucracy! the final report, we have seen, does not take into account the fact that in certain countries the parliament requires meps to be paid a minimum wage. in romania, the maximum salary for local assistants is eur 700, well below the minimum salary in some member states. we limit the number of local assistants even if the constituencies are different. in my case, the constituency is 22 million people. we also remove questions and interpellations as if this mechanism did not exist in all parliaments. i want to tell you that i want my question to be public! perhaps not in all languages, to cut costs, but i would like to see what they are doing in the european parliament, and the declarations, and the other mechanisms that i have at my disposal. democracy costs money. we must not reduce democracy!
question referred under the 'blue card' procedure. i agree with a lot of the things you've said. i think we need to protect those who draw attention to those who evade. my question is: what do you think about people who have evaded and basically point fingers at others who have? you mean we have to protect them, too?
question referred under the 'blue card' procedure. i must say, mr. kamall, that i was surprised by your position, although you started by saying that you have a different life because your family emigrated to england. i want to ask you directly: you said that not everyone, that they can be returned. who determines the right to life of some and the lack of living conditions of others? who to select that yes, has the right man to live no matter on which corner of the world is and who makes this sorting? how do you see this? it seems to me absolutely absurd to say that we give some of it back, we don't give some of it back, and somebody, bureaucratically, decides whether it meets the conditions or it doesn't meet the conditions.
madam president, in this house and in our institutions we have expressed our sorrow too often for stories that keep happening again and again and again without concrete solutions being adopted. we cannot wait until the next tragedy happens; we must act now and act in a concrete manner. i am happy that an extraordinary council meeting was called as well as a foreign affairs and home affairs council, but i am less happy with the outcome. between the outcome of the council and the position of the president of the european commission, jean-claude juncker, i welcome without hesitation the position of president juncker and this is the european way to act. it is time for europe to deserve its nobel prize and to act with a fully strategic and common vision and understanding of the complexity of the problem. firstly, triton must be widened and it has to meet at least the features of the italian mare nostrum operation. secondly, responsibility towards refugees and asylum seekers should be shared among all member states. thirdly, europe in the short term should make sure that mediterranean crossings organised by unscrupulous human smugglers are stopped and that the criminals are brought to justice. but it is obvious that the real problem lies in the crises these people are escaping from: ranging from the conflict in syria, the division in the failing state of libya and the poverty and conflicts in the sahel region.
mr president, the recent drowning of more than 1 000 people in the mediterranean sea sadly highlights yet again europe’s inability to cope with the unprecedented humanitarian crisis in the world. refugees fleeing war or persecution are drowning as europe allocates fewer resources to life-saving missions. letting more people die at sea does not deter others from attempting sea crossings. as a community of values, europe should do more: not just in terms of rescue at sea but also in prevention. one possible way to achieve the latter is to process asylum requests abroad. however, in the long term we need a stronger engagement with countries of origin and a better-targeted development policy addressing the push factors of terrorist conflicts, poverty, systemic corruption and misrule.
in writing.– it is clear that if we do not act now we will bear the responsability before future generations for these inhumane tragedies. we can no longer afford not to tackle this issue seriously: we must implement an effective strategy to save the lives of these people. right now, only those who have money and are strong enough to escape from wars and poverty have a chance to safely reach, illegally, the shores of europe. the weak, the poor, the families with children are left behind in harm’s way. and this is primarily due to our barriers that prevent asylum seekers and refugees from saving their lives in a better world. we must take urgent action to confront these crises and conflicts.
in writing. the tragedies caused by illegal immigration are a reality that the european union is unfortunately facing more and more often and therefore urgently needs to find solutions at community level. the eu needs to use frontex much more effectively. the tripling of the budget for frontex is a positive aspect, but the mandate of frontex must be extended. joint maritime operations poseidon, triton are actions that need to be strengthened and their role needs to be clearly defined in the future agenda on migration. the eu can build a viable european asylum policy by making appropriate use of article 88 tfeu so that the provisions of the dublin convention are functional in all member states. the commission should develop a migration management strategy in its agenda for the next 5 years and respond to the humanitarian crisis triggered by illegal immigration through viable legal and economic immigration policies. europe needs better long-term governance of the development fund, coupled with a consistent european foreign policy. the eu must act at the source: working with the authorities of migrants' countries of origin so that smuggling networks are broken up. saving human lives means stopping ships from leaving the coast.
in writing. humanitarian tragedies in the mediterranean have been at the top of the european political agenda in a dismal succession. the eu is currently overwhelmed by the massive influx of migrants from the coasts of libya and syria. that is why i believe that the common response of the member states must focus on the causes of the refugee flows. first, the rapid and bloody expansion of the islamic state in iraq and syria, and the intensification of instability and conflict in north africa. i do not think that the prospect of a european asylum system and a solidarity mechanism between member states solving the problems of the many asylum seekers is realistic. in this respect, i would like to point out that i do not agree with the european parliament's resolution calling on the european commission to establish a mandatory quota for the distribution of asylum seekers in all member states. by dealing only with the effects, we risk being overwhelmed by the magnitude of the causes. i therefore call for a focus on defining and implementing strategies against the chronic violence and underdevelopment in the countries of origin of migrants. the eu should also step up action against illegal immigration, which is partly controlled by criminal networks of trafficking in human beings, including terrorist groups.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on the presentation by the commission of the consolidated annual accounts of the european union for the financial year 2013, as part of the 2013 discharge procedure. the consolidated annual accounts of the european union for the financial year 2013 have been prepared on the basis of the information provided by the institutions and bodies pursuant to article 148 (2) of the financial regulation applicable to the general budget of the european union, and in accordance with title ix of the financial regulation. the document provides insights into the eu budget mechanism and how the budget was managed in 2013. to this end, it recalls the eu's operational expenditure, covers various headings of the financial framework and takes different forms depending on how the money is paid and managed.
in writing. ‒ whereas the 2013 commission represents the end of a multiannual programming period for which the new commission cannot be held responsible for, the parliament can only recommend that the lessons taught particularly within the discharge procedure and the financial and social crisis are to be learnt. 2013 marks a historical point in terms of impact and change of political and economic challenges, obliging us all to review our priorities and the results achieved. i welcome the progress made and i call the commission as well as the other institutions for a performance orientation, transparency and good governance in europe.
in writing. ‒ the report presented by the european court of auditors regarding the discharge of the european commission's budget for the year 2013 detected an error rate of 4,7%, as compared to 4.8% in 2012. even though the financial year 2013 has been marked by a very high execution rate of the budget, the 4,7% error rate is still too high compared to the recommended threshold of 2%. i would therefore like to stress that from my point of view this proves a lack of commitment to sound financial management. the commission has to solve the problem of the status of the international management group, which received financing of millions of euros from the commission without recourse to any public tendering. in addition, the commission has to set up measures for improving the management of funds in member states, because in 50 cases of structural funds we do not know which budget line applies to which region. i stress the need of a high level of transparency in the commission as a sine-qua-non condition to mitigate risks of conflict of interest.
in writing. ‒ the annual budget of the european union is €145 billion (based on 2015 figures). this amounts to only 1% of the revenues generated annually by the eu economies, although it is a significant amount. each annual budget is part of a seven-year budget cycle known as the 'financial perspective'. the financial perspective is drawn up by the european commission and requires the unanimous approval of the member states and negotiations to be followed by the agreement of the european parliament. after the budget for the following financial year has been established, discharge shall be given for the budget for the following year in respect of the correct use of the funds as provided for by each institution, body or department. i voted in favour of this motion for a resolution on discharge in respect of the implementation of the general budget of the european union for the financial year 2013, section iii commission and executive agencies, given the great importance of informing eu citizens about the use of the eu budget, to which they also contribute by default.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council amending regulation (eu) no 1304/2013 of the european parliament and of the council on the european social fund, as regards an increase in the amount of initial pre-financing granted to operational programmes supporting the youth employment initiative (yei). the yei targets regions where the youth unemployment rate exceeds 25%, thus supporting exclusively young people who are neither in employment nor enrolled in an education or training programme. unfortunately, this initiative was not able to achieve its objective at maximum quotas because it was not used by the member states, one reason being the lack of sufficient pre-financing to initiate the necessary measures. in this respect, i would like to welcome the commission's initiative to release eur 1 billion to ensure the required level of pre-financing. the fight against unemployment and the promotion of youth employment are essential and must be supported all the more as young people represent the future of our society.
in writing. ‒ given the discouraging labour market outlook for young people, i believe that the youth employment initiative is one of the tools through which the objectives of the youth guarantee can be achieved in the areas of europe most affected by youth unemployment.
in writing. ‒ i back the commission proposal to boost the financing of the youth employment initiative. every young person gets a job, an apprenticeship, traineeship or professional training within four months of becoming unemployed. we call on the member states to accelerate their efforts regarding the implementation of the yei. we expect the commission to stick to its promise regarding the immediate transfer of the additional pre-financing to the member states.
in writing. ‒ youth unemployment has been alarmingly high and has not diminished significantly recently. the european union wants to help member states deal with this major problem, which is affecting so many young people. the commission proposal, which would encourage member states to use the additional funds as soon as possible to finance projects in this area, is welcome. i voted in favour of this report.
in writing. ‒ i voted for the youth employment initiative because this report will make a major contribution to meeting the objectives of the youth guarantee in the areas of europe most affected by youth unemployment. the implementation of the youth strategy is a concrete project in all member states, which will improve reforms in education and vocational training and make possible the transition from school to work. this instrument will be used in regions facing an unemployment rate of 25% among young people up to 25 years. the eu has delivered on its promise to young people and has unlocked €1 billion to enable member states to launch the projects they need. it is not about new funds, but about an increase in the prefinancing rate from 1% to 30%. member states will be supported in supplementing the necessary funds allocated to projects that offer young people either a job, a traineeship or vocational training. it remains for the member states to implement this programme urgently to bring young people into the labour market as soon as possible.
in writing. ‒ due to the high level of youth unemployment in the european union, the youth employment initiative was created to provide support to young people who are out of work, education or training in the regions most affected by the crisis. however, the mechanisms made available to member states and potential beneficiaries have identified the problem of implementing operational programmes in the absence of more substantial initial pre-financing. i voted in favour of this proposal, which provides for an increase in the initial pre-financing from 1-1.5% to 30% of the total project cost.
in writing. ‒ i voted today in favour of the report on increasing the amount of initial pre-financing for youth employment programmes, as youth unemployment has reached dramatic levels in recent years. this is a critical situation in which many member states, including romania, find themselves, and the commission's initiative to release €1 billion for youth programmes is commendable. i also support the rapporteur's position that this sum should be made available as soon as possible, given that the outlook for young people is discouraging.
in writing. i voted for the report on the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament on the european social fund, as regards an increase in the amount of initial pre-financing for operational programmes supported by the youth employment initiative. the report also calls for the eu to take action to ensure that the eu's citizens are able to access the internet and to use it to make their own decisions. the unemployment rate among young people has reached a dramatic level in recent years and is continuing to rise. the eu has developed several programmes to help member states combat this scourge, and the release of this amount should help to speed up their implementation.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report which provides for the repeal of eec regulation no 3030/93 in the light of the changes which have taken place over time. this regulation concerns the common arrangements applicable to imports of textile products originating in third countries with which the european community has concluded bilateral agreements, signed protocols or other arrangements. since the only third countries with which the eu has maintained bilateral agreements on imports of certain textile products, namely russia and serbia, are now covered by other agreements, namely russia has acceded to the world trade organisation and the stabilisation and association agreement between serbia and the eu has been concluded, eec regulation no 3030/93 has lost its main purpose. at the same time, this regulation was also used to apply quantitative limits for certain textile products originating in china and later to implement the transitional safeguard mechanism applicable to certain chinese products, which expired on 11 december 2013. in view of these aspects and in order to promote legal certainty, i support the need to repeal council regulation (eec) no 3030/93.
in writing. ‒ on 10 and 11 december 2014, the european economic and social committee delivered a favourable opinion on the text proposed by the european council on the 'proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council on common rules for imports of textile products from certain third countries not covered by bilateral agreements, protocols or other arrangements, or by other specific union import arrangements (recast) com ((2014) 345 final 2014/0177 (cod) ' given that title i of regulation (ec) no 427/20034, and with it the possibility of imposing safeguard measures, expired on 11 december 2013, i voted for this resolution in order to address this legal and procedural vacuum.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council on safeguard measures provided for in the agreement between the european economic community and the kingdom of norway. the adoption of a safeguard measure shall be based on multilaterally agreed rules, taking into account the application of those rules to bilateral relations as they result from internal regulations or specific preferential agreements negotiated to regulate those relations. the adoption of general rules on a bilateral or regional basis shall have particular regard to the procedure to be followed in the event of recourse to safeguard measures. therefore, these safeguard measures are intended to slow down imports in order to remedy and prevent a situation of injury to the eu producers, which is also the case with imports from norway.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the proposal as it fully preserves the content of the act being codified.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council on safeguard measures provided for in the agreement between the european economic community and the kingdom of norway, given the importance of the document for this partnership. i also stress the importance of adopting the text of the european commission's proposal, as adapted, following the recommendations of the consultative working party of the legal services of the european parliament, the council and the commission.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council on certain procedures for implementing the stabilisation and association agreement between the european communities and their member states, of the one part, and the republic of albania, of the other part. i support the importance of the process of economic and political regeneration of the western balkan states, so that they can become members of the european union. stabilisation and association agreements, trade preferences and technical and financial assistance are the three main pillars through which the eu hopes to bring stability to the region. following the signature of the stabilisation agreement and subsequent entry into force of the agreement, albania has made significant progress, leading to the council's decision in june 2014 to consider albania as a candidate country for eu accession.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the proposal as it fully preserves the content of the act being codified.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on the application of the stabilisation and association agreement and the interim agreement on trade and trade-related matters between the ec and bosnia and herzegovina. the recent decision to sign the association agreement with bosnia and herzegovina is a real step forward for that country. both bosnia and herzegovina and the other western balkan countries are exempted from customs duties on all industrial products, all processed agricultural products, agricultural products except beef, fishery products and wines when imported into the eu market under the stabilisation and association agreement (saa). in june 2008, the council concluded an interim agreement on trade and trade-related matters between the european community and bosnia and herzegovina, which provides for the early entry into force of the trade and trade-related provisions of the saa. the implementation of these agreements is important in supporting bosnia and herzegovina's eu accession. however, the progress made by bosnia and herzegovina must also be accompanied by overcoming the precarious economic situation and strong political and ethnic divisions.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report on the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council on certain procedures for applying the stabilisation and association agreement between the european communities and their member states, of the one part, and bosnia and herzegovina, of the other part, and for applying the interim agreement on trade and trade-related matters between the european community, of the one part, and bosnia and herzegovina, of the other part, in view of the importance of the political and economic partnerships that the european union has established with neighbouring countries, as well as with other third countries.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council on certain procedures for implementing the stabilisation and association agreement between the european communities and their member states, of the one part, and the former yugoslav republic of macedonia, of the other part, as this country is the most advanced in terms of alignment with the acquis among the balkan countries that have applied to join the eu. this agreement provides for economic and political cooperation and the establishment of free trade areas with the republic of macedonia and permanent cooperation structures based on common democratic principles, human rights and the rule of law. the effects of the agreement were felt in that 80% of the total foreign direct investment stock came from eu enterprises and trade flows of goods and services with the eu continued to increase. in the nine years since the republic of macedonia became a candidate country for the european union, important progress has been made and the delay in the eu accession process may represent an obstacle to deeper economic integration.
in writing. ‒ i am in favour of the proposal as it is a straightforward codification of existing texts, without any change in their substance.
in writing. ‒ the european union has always placed a strong emphasis on cooperative and good neighbourly relations with all its neighbours. i voted in favour of this report on the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council on certain procedures for implementing the stabilisation and association agreement between the european communities and their member states, of the one part, and the former yugoslav republic of macedonia, of the other part, because it highlights once again the importance of this cooperation.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on the codification of council regulation (ec) no 994/98 of 7 may 1998 on the application of articles 107 and 108 of the treaty on the functioning of the european union to certain categories of horizontal state aid. the proposal provides for the possibility for the ec to declare, by means of block exemption regulations, that certain categories of aid are compatible with the internal market in accordance with article 107 tfeu and are not subject to the notification requirement of article 108 tfeu. these categories include aid to small and medium-sized enterprises, aid for research, development and innovation, environmental protection, infrastructure, employment and training, sport, and aid which complies with the regional aid map approved by the commission for each member state.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the proposal as it fully preserves the content of the act being codified.
in writing. ‒ the treaty on the functioning of the european union (tfeu), as amended by the treaty of lisbon, entered into force on 1 december 2009 with the entry into force of the amending treaty. i voted in favour of this report on the proposal for a council regulation on the application of articles 107 and 108 of the treaty on the functioning of the european union to certain categories of horizontal state aid, given the importance of regulating this mechanism and of strictly complying with both primary and secondary legislation of the european union.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on the codification of regulation (ec) no 659/1999 laying down detailed rules for the application of article 108 of the treaty on the functioning of the european union. the proposal aims to lay down procedural rules on the application of the state aid rules. in accordance with article 108 (3) tfeu, any new aid scheme must be notified to the commission and should not be put into effect before it has been authorised by the commission. the procedure for notified aid provides that any plans to grant new aid are to be notified to the commission in good time by the member state concerned. the commission shall inform the member state concerned without delay of the receipt of a notification. in a notification, the member state concerned must provide all the information necessary to enable the commission to take a decision.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the proposal as it fully preserves the content of the act being codified.
in writing. ‒ the treaty on the functioning of the european union (tfeu) organises the functioning of the union and lays down the areas, limits and conditions for the exercise of its powers. i voted in favour of this report on the proposal for a council regulation laying down detailed rules for the application of article 108 of the treaty on the functioning of the european union, because i consider that strict compliance with the texts of the treaties on which the european union is founded and which govern its functioning is of the utmost importance.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the court of auditors' special reports in the context of the commission's discharge for the financial year 2013. the discharge procedure aims to increase performance by achieving the best possible outcome with union taxpayers' money and to encourage the commission to make more efforts to improve the feedback stage in the evaluation cycle so that lessons learned from the past and recommendations from evaluations contribute as much as possible to the decision-making process, programming and implementation of future eu aid. the court of auditors also notes that budget support remained an important form of aid for the implementation of the union's development policy in 2013, accounting for 27,3% of total commitments. i believe that the court of auditors' reports provide clear and well-founded guidance for the commission, which can lead to improved strategy in the future.
in writing. ‒ the special reports of the court of auditors give in-depth analysis of the delivery of specific funding programme areas and provide considerable detail on the administration of particular policy areas. this complements the horizontal approach of the annual report of the court on the implementation of the eu budget which forms the basis for parliament´s work on discharge for the various institutions. i therefore voted in favour of the adoption of the report in the plenary.
in writing. ‒ the annual budget of the european union is €145 billion (based on 2015 figures). this amounts to only 1% of the revenues generated annually by the eu economies, although it is a significant amount. each annual budget is part of a seven-year budget cycle known as the 'financial perspective'. the financial perspective is drawn up by the european commission and requires the unanimous approval of the member states and negotiations to be followed by the agreement of the european parliament. after the budget for the following financial year has been established, discharge shall be given for the budget for the following year in respect of the correct use of the funds as provided for by each institution, body or department. i voted in favour of this motion for a resolution on the court of auditors' special reports in the context of the commission's discharge for the financial year 2013, given the major importance of informing eu citizens about the use of the eu budget, to which they also contribute by default.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the discharge report for the general budget of the eu - the 8th, 9th and 10th edfs. the document shall include a note to the accounts in which the accounting officer responsible for auditing the edf certifies that these accounts present a true and fair view of the financial position of the european development funds in all material respects. the edf is the main instrument for providing union aid for development cooperation in the african, pacific (acp) and overseas countries and territories (octs) and the caribbean. the 1957 treaty of rome provided for its creation to provide technical and financial assistance, initially only to african countries, which at that time were still colonized and with which some member states had historical links. the report shall transparently present how these resources were used during the financial year 2013.
in writing. ‒ the european development fund is the main eu aid instrument for development cooperation in africa, the caribbean, and pacific countries and the overseas countries and territories aiming at reducing and eventually eradicating poverty - one of the core political priorities shared by the s&d group. we managed to underline the need for including the edf in the general eu budget in order to improve policy coherence and better democratic scrutiny. we also focussed on the need for stronger anti-corruption mechanisms in order to assure better effectiveness of budget support programs. i support the commission's budgetary support approach which places stronger emphasis on accountability and transparency, and i therefore encourage the com to apply systematic risk analysis and risk mitigation strategy in the management of budget support operations. considering the fact that discharge was granted, i supported the adoption of the report in the plenary.

in writing. ‒ i supported the grant of the discharge for european external action service, court of auditors, court of justice, economic and social committee, committee of the regions, european ombudsman and the european data protection supervisor.
in writing. ‒ i fully endorse the proposal of the parliament to postpone the discharge of the council and of the european council for the year 2013. this plenary session was the 5th consecutive session when the european parliament declined to approve the discharge of the budget for these two institutions due to their persistent failure to supply the necessary information about the discharge procedure and their failure to answer parliament's questions. the gentleman’s agreement concluded back in 1970 invoked by the council in support of its actions, is a pathetic argument that proves lack of transparency and accountability towards citizens’ money. even though on the basis of primary legislation - article 319 tfeu- the parliament is vested to only grant discharge to the european commission, according to article 165 of the financial regulation no.966/2012 of the european parliament and of the council of 25.10.2012, the discharge decision of the parliament shall cover the accounts of all the union's revenue and expenditure, including therefore council's expenditure. moreover, council’s refusal to provide information on how its budget has been spent raises by itself question marks on the use of our citizens’ money.

in writing. ‒ i fully support the decision of the european parliament to postpone the discharge of the european institute for innovation and technology (eit) because of insufficient quality of ex - ante and ex - post verifications and because of irregular public procurement procedures. i welcome the fact that this year again the issue of prevention and management of conflict of interest remained high on the agenda and i therefore call for a continuous monitoring during future discharge procedures. in addition, two more issues need to be stressed. first, it is the second consecutive year when the court of auditors did not find any assurance on the legality of eit's grant transactions and secondly, the internal audit function at the agency was vacant for the entire year of 2013; eit has to solve as soon as possible all the problems signalled by the parliament and to follow its recommendations.

in writing. ‒ i fully endorse the decision of european parliament to grant the discharge to the european medicines agency for the year 2013. the agency’s budget implementation rates for the year 2012 were satisfactory. the rate of appropriations carried over was high (27 %), but this was due primarily to the agency’s move to a new location which took place in 2014. the comprehensive conflict of interest policy put into place is an example for other agencies. despite this, there is still place for improvement. the selection board members did not always complete their conflict of interest declarations, or did not do so in a timely manner, and there was no evidence of action taken to address the issues raised by these declarations. the documentation of the selection board’s proceedings was not always adequate and there is no evidence as to how the method for the short-listing of candidates was established and that the questions for the written tests or interviews were set before the examinations, but all in all, the medicine agency performed well.
