madam president, in order to turn europe into a circular economy, boost recycling, secure access to raw materials and create jobs and economic growth, the commission adopted a waste framework directive that sets the recycling targets for the member states. unfortunately, romania has a landfill rate exceeding 90% and is very far from reaching the targets. considering the low rates of compliance with the directive in romania, i would point out that urgent measures need to be taken to put romania on the green map. citizens are willing to participate in the selective collection of packaging if they are properly informed and if there is proper collection infrastructure. penalising waste disposal to landfill through a dumping tax, improving sanitation law and enhancing cooperation between all those involved in recycling systems are steps that need to be taken, and they must be taken into account for the implementation of a much-needed strategic view of romania’s waste management system.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the proposal to open interinstitutional negotiations to amend the school fruit, vegetables and milk aid scheme, as i see a drastic decline in fruit and dairy consumption among young people and the existing aid programmes have not been as successful as hoped. the commission has also identified a number of obstacles to the implementation of the aid schemes, such as cumbersome bureaucracy at member state level and the inability to extend the objectives of the programmes to trainers. we are now facing an avalanche of processed foods and fast food, which has turned young people away from fresh produce. i believe that support schemes should be extended to younger ages because it is essential to train nutritional behaviour from pre-school level. i believe that the aim of the aid schemes should be extended to trainers by allocating a significant percentage to educational measures. information programmes should include trainers and parents. limiting them to the level of educational institutions will not produce the expected results. school programmes should have as their main objective the support of indigenous producers and the promotion of local agricultural potential. i would stress that encouraging local producers contributes to the development of short production chains and promotes the consumption of indigenous products and agricultural products.
in writing. ‒ i think that the unification of the two school fruit and milk programmes and the creation of a common legal framework is welcome, given the situation in the fruit and dairy sectors, which are heavily affected by the russian embargo.
in writing. ‒ this report is fundamental, as it examines the need to continue and strengthen efforts to combat childhood obesity and encourage healthy eating habits early in life. this is a very important issue to tackle, since childhood obesity is increasing across the eu and healthier eating habits need to be encouraged early. schemes for distributing healthy products, and supporting educational measures about their use, must be combined and streamlined to become more effective tools in the work to promote healthier eating among young people. in order to support this programme thoroughly, i reject the idea of introducing cocoa into the list of products. i believe that the use by member states of between 10% and 20% of the fund for educational measures and activities, including farm visits and the distribution of local, regional and national products, such as honey, olive oil, dried fruits and processed fruit and vegetables, is a very positive proposal that needs to be encouraged.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of opening negotiations and the mandate for interinstitutional negotiations on the aid scheme for the supply of fruit and vegetables, bananas and milk to educational establishments. this decision paves the way for a quality-based food program designed to improve the quality of children's nutrition.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of opening interinstitutional negotiations for this aid programme because i strongly believe that it can bring many benefits both for the health of our children and for agriculture in romania. the two programmes, which have been separate until now, for the supply of fruit and vegetables to educational establishments on the one hand and milk on the other, were developed at different times, on different bases, with different budgets, but with the same objectives: to educate children in terms of food by familiarizing them with healthy and fresh products. analyses have shown that the original objectives are still valid, but the programmes suffer from a lack of coordination. in this respect, i support the integration of the two from a legislative and economic point of view as this will mean reducing red tape and unnecessary procedures, thus saving financial resources that can be used within these programmes themselves. the integration of the two is very important for the healthy education of children in romania and across the eu, for their future, and not least for farmers and producers in the member states who support and promote healthy products, including those in romania.
in writing. ‒ i believe that it is good for children to have healthy food as a priority in schools. this is why i support actions such as the 'milk for schools' project in the czech republic. and it is precisely because of this conviction that i could not vote today for the resolution on the aid scheme for the supply of fruit and vegetables, bananas and milk to educational establishments as proposed. the adoption of the amendment, which meant that flavoured milk would not receive aid, would have seriously damaged the czech project 'milk for schoolchildren' mentioned above. the results show that children who take it drink up to eight times as much flavored milk as unflavored milk. the sugar content of flavoured milk is already clearly regulated, but if we do not support flavoured milk, this may mean that children are left with the choice of raw milk, which they do not like so much, and much less healthy but 'good' drinks. then it's obvious that they're going to go for the latter, and the whole milk-promoting system in schools is going to fail.
in writing. ‒ this vote demonstrates the desire of all to continue strengthening programmes on good nutrition in schools. the directive voted today helps to increase the consumption of fresh fruit and vegetables, including bananas, and dairy products among children, and to reduce the number of cases of verified childhood obesity in the member states.
in writing. ‒ i was happy to vote in favour of the commission’s initiative. each year, in a context of increasing rates of child obesity, the school milk scheme and the school fruit and vegetables scheme provide nearly 30 million school children across the eu with much needed healthy food products and help children to develop good eating habits. similarly, at a time of falling fruit and vegetable prices, farmers and rural communities are also guaranteed a secure market for their products. i believe that the merging of the two schemes within a common legal and financial framework would further increase the efficiency and effectiveness of the system and reduce the administrative burden for local administrations in the implementation of the national programmes.
in writing. ‒ healthy food for europe's children must be a top priority for the commission and the member states. childhood obesity is reaching alarming levels and is calling into question the healthy development we all want for european children. nutritional behaviors are acquired from an early age. therefore, the continuation of the fruit and milk supply programme for educational establishments is not only necessary but also mandatory. at the same time, educational programmes for which member states can use between 10% and 20% of the financial allocations can be transformed into activities for children to create healthy lifelong nutrition behaviours. i voted in favour of this proposal for a decision because i consider it important for the united and healthy development of european youth. in addition to the positive features of balanced nutrition, it is also worth highlighting the economic importance that the programme attaches to the development of agricultural production at national and regional level. the european union's contributions under this programme are injected into the national economy and give new opportunities for local producers to develop and consolidate their market position.
on behalf of the s&d group. mr president, based on the idea that the interests of all eu citizens must be protected in the event of major crises that can be triggered by various factors or situations and that can affect agricultural production or distribution at european level, the european commission has this year also put forward a proposal to adjust direct payments to all farmers. the adjustment rate for direct payments is currently 1,39% and it approves payments for amounts above eur 2 000 per farmer. according to the european executive, the adjustment is intended to create a financing reserve of some eur 441 million, compared with eur 433 million in the previous year, which can be used in the event of a crisis in the agricultural sector. depending on the situation, the european commission will be able to make a new proposal to adjust the adjustment rate on 1 december 2015, after reassessing the forecast in october. the european parliament must adopt this proposal within the time limit set by the regulation, i.e. by the end of june, otherwise it is the commission which will be able to decide on the level of this rate. i believe that as representatives of the european citizens we must respect the deadline.
mr president, direct payments are the mechanism absolutely indispensable for sustainable and efficient agriculture. that is why i welcome the commission's concern in general and that of commissioner phil hogan in particular to always refer to the realities on the ground in order to provide the opportunity to take the best measures for the agricultural sector. in this respect, it should be possible for the adjustment rate to apply only to the amount of direct payments for which aid applications were submitted in 2015, without taking into account the moment when the payments to farmers were made, precisely because member states have the possibility to make late payments, after that payment period, within a certain time limit. however, i would like to draw attention again today, with all the responsibility and respect i have for the european institutions, to the unacceptable differences in direct payments between member states, which create major imbalances. never, a subsidy of 150 euros that a romanian farmer receives can not be equal to a subsidy of 700-800 euros that a farmer from another state receives on the same unit of measure, which i find deeply incorrect. the commission must therefore ensure that in future the differences between farmers in the european union are eliminated, ensuring equal treatment, but with the obligation to take account of the particularities of each area, and this as a consequence of belonging to the single european area. last but not least, the commission must remain concerned with the need to ensure a balance between supporting the performance of farmers on the one hand and affordable and accessible food for all the people of the european union and beyond on the other. the embargo imposed on russia, the lack of markets strong enough to absorb all agricultural production at union level, highlights the need for a joint effort by all responsible factors to find viable solutions in crisis situations.
mr president, it is obvious that we need such a crisis tool to use the money in the interests of farmers, but at the same time we must bear in mind the following: it is important to use the money in the right directions to help farmers when they need it. that's why, unfortunately, no one can predict or forecast the onset of a crisis like we had with the russian embargo. that is why i think it is important that the commission, and i have great confidence in commissioner hogan, will set very clear conditions for the beneficiaries of these funds. let us not forget that they are actually the ones who contribute to this reserve fund and, on the other hand, as my other colleagues have said, let us not forget that it is almost impossible to put farmers in competition with each other given the differences in the amount of money they receive. so i stress again that full alignment of direct payments to farmers should be ensured as soon as possible.
mr president, i would like to express my positive vote for the fixing of an adjustment rate for direct payments in 2015. this will provide a reserve that will allow additional support for the agricultural sector in the case of a natural crisis affecting agricultural production or distribution, by applying, at the beginning of each year, a reduction to direct payments with a financial discipline mechanism. even if i truly hope that the crisis reserve will not be needed, i believe that, if such an event happens, it will be an important means for the european agricultural sector, from which we will all benefit. also, i am strongly in favour of very clear conditions being imposed for beneficiaries. i thank the rapporteur and the shadow rapporteurs.

member of the commission.– mr president, the quality and depth of eu-russia relations is a determining factor for the stability and prosperity of our continent. our partnership was severely impacted last year by the illegal annexation of crimea and the destabilisation of donbas. but russia is also an important economic counterpart and an essential partner for the solution of many pressing international problems. this is the backdrop of the report you are debating today. i appreciate your efforts, in particular those of mr landsbergis, which have made this report a very important contribution to the debate on how best to shape relations with russia. let me take up the key political messages in your report. first comes the issue of unity. i fully share your conviction that our russia policy is strong and successful only if it enjoys the unanimous support of all 28 eu member states. the eu must continue acting on the basis of a broad and principled consensus on the ukraine conflict and on its relations with russia. this does not mean reducing our policy to the lowest common denominator. quite the contrary – it means pursuing a comprehensive approach, responding to immediate concerns but with strategic patience and vision. the work of this house is an example of eu unity. i understand that the draft report has been adopted by an overwhelming majority in the committee on foreign affairs (afet). i hope that the plenary vote will also reflect this, in order to send a clear political message about the views of european citizens. second, there is the issue of balance. your report contains strong criticism of moscow’s actions such as the illegal annexation of crimea and sevastopol, its destabilising policy in donbas, the multiplication of hybrid threats throughout europe and the shrinking space for russian civil society and media. at the same time, you are equally strong in stating the eu’s readiness to develop a constructive, predictable and mutually-beneficial relationship with russia. balance is at the core of our approach to the ukraine conflict. on the one hand, we have been firm and decided to adopt sanctions. on the other hand, eu member states and eu institutions are engaged in the search for a political solution to the conflict. work is done in the normandy format and in trilateral talks on trade and energy. the eu provides substantial assistance which is clearly conditional on real reforms in ukraine. these efforts will continue unabated. such a balanced approach should be followed between the eu and russia. dialogue and engagement should go together with resilience and firmness. we cannot turn a blind eye to security risks in sectors like energy, cyber-space, civil aviation or the impact of propaganda on our democracies. we must enhance our capacity for resilience and clearly state our red lines. at the same time, there is an imperative for cooperation based on the inter-dependence and complementarity of our economies, on historical and cultural traditions and on our capacity to make a difference when we act jointly. we should more often exercise our responsibilities as actors in a complex world of global and regional challenges. based on mutual respect, the eu should remain ready to develop a new, positive relationship. thirdly, the commission shares your commitment to a comprehensive approach to our russia policy. as high representative mogherini said in this chamber at the start of her term last autumn, we believe that a successful foreign policy depends on success in internal eu policies fully committed to this principle. the work by high representative mogherini, with commissioners šefčovič and malmström, on the trilateral talks on energy and trade proves we are on the right track. fourth, let me stress the issue of integrity. the eu stands firmly behind democratic values, respect for human rights and a rules-based international order and will continue to do so. these fundamental principles underpin our commitment to the sovereignty and territorial integrity of ukraine. they are the basis for our call on russia to respect its international commitments, be this in the field of governance, security or international trade. we have maintained our support and assistance for civil society organisations and human rights projects in an increasingly challenging environment. despite the deterioration of relations, we will enhance people-to-people contacts in all fields – from education, culture and research to cross-border cooperation. let me finish with a crucial point in your report – perspective. i see that the very first plea you make in your report is for the eu to develop a contingency plan for the short term, as well as a comprehensive plan for long-term relations with russia and with the eu’s east european partners. i share the reasoning behind this call. events in crimea and donbas should not prevent us from taking a broader horizon for identifying the challenges we face and the opportunities to be exploited. eu foreign ministers agreed back in january to continue dialogue with russia at expert level on the resolution of regional conflicts and tackling global challenges. further engagement with russia should be gradual, with russia’s fulfilment of commitments under international law and steps for rebuilding mutual trust. for this to develop, we need a long-term vision – a strategy that we must develop further. to achieve a vision for eu-russia relations that can embrace all scenarios, our reflection should already start now.

answer is "blue cardboard". mr president, i think the only solution we have now is to help the ukrainians fight russia, because it is a war on their soil. we must therefore use all the means at our disposal, at member state and union level, to help these people to defend themselves. this is a right of defence that the english once cherished. now that they are themselves at war with europe, they will invent anything to break this action.

mr president, i would start by saying to the commissioner that we all consider ourselves – except those in flagrant conflict of interest with russia – blacklisted. this is the very moment to say that we have been blacklisted, directly or indirectly, by russia without having violated any norm or any international law. russia has done that. i will now turn to my language, romanian. dialogul a fost și rămâne cuvântul cheie în relația ue-rusia, acesta a fost abordarea generică a uniunii europene cu toți partenerii săi, iar acest raport este un raport cheie într-un moment cheie pentru relațiile noastre cu rusia. pe de o parte observăm, conform celor transmise de misiunea specială de monitorizare a osce și de către nato, suportul militar constant oferit de rusia separatiștilor, iar pe de altă parte continuăm să auzim retorica de negare a implicării rusiei în conflictul din ucraina, ba chiar un interviu scandalos al lui putin care neagă evidențele, spunând că vestul nu ar trebui să se simtă amenințat de către rusia. la toate cele menționate, spuneam, se adaugă lista neagră adoptată săptămâna trecută pe ascuns care arată adevăratele intenții ale rusiei. trebuie să rămânem ancorați în valorile noastre europene și să nu ne abatem de la principiile în care credem cu toții, dar nu putem rămâne indiferenți la astfel de acțiuni provocatoare. personal salut inițiativa președintelui martin schulz de a pune restricții la accesul...(președintele a întrerupt vorbitorului.)
mr president, the actions taken by the russian federation continue to undermine any immediate prospect for reengagement and cooperation on the part of the eu. the russian blacklist of european politicians and officials, including a large number of members of this parliament, adds yet another obstacle to mutual trust and to repeated efforts for a peaceful and sustainable solution to the current crisis. by illegally annexing crimea and waging an armed conflict against ukraine, russia has intentionally chosen not to be a partner. breaching its international commitments including the united nations charter, the helsinki final act, the budapest memorandum and the paris charter, russia has contributed to thousands of deaths in eastern ukraine. yet no opportunities for genuine and constructive dialogue with moscow will be spared. the russian federation is and remains a prerequisite for the de-escalation of the conflict and a political, lasting solution. in the long term, the ultimate objective is and must be that of restoring dialogue and engagement with russia to achieve peace on the european continent.
the right to life, freedom of expression and association, respect for the borders and sovereignty of states, are just some of the principles governing the european union. russia's violation of these values, through actions to annex crimea, destabilise ukraine and the region, was likely to attract a set of measures from the international community aimed at correcting these aberrations. russia must understand that while the european union wants a strategic partnership that pursues common interests, this will not be possible as long as it is a rival to the rule of law, and the minsk agreement, although it was meant to become a reality, is today increasingly being violated. we draw the attention of the russian federation to the fact that, however much the member states may depend on the energy component, they will never accept the violation of the basic principles of security in europe. the european institutions and the member states will remain firm against any aggression that threatens peace and stability in the region.
mr president, to me the most important question in our relations with the russian federation right now is how we move forward in these relations. i would course prefer that we move forward on the basis of common values – but do we share values with a political leadership that invades another country or that pursues an illegal annexation of the territories of another country? i am afraid we do not. in fact i am pretty certain we do not share common values with them. until russia decides to be a trustworthy partner for the free world, i think our number one objective should be to help countries in the eastern neighbourhood which are under pressure from russia. we have to tell the people in these countries that we want these countries to be strong, independent and developed, and the russian federation wants these countries to be weak and controllable so that they can be blackmailed. we should use the financial and institutional means that we have to help these countries develop to build strong and independent institutions at home, and we have to resist the russian propaganda there. we should communicate to the people of these countries what the benefits of cooperation with the eu are for those people.
member of the commission.– mr president, this debate has shown yet again how important russia is for us, in terms of both the risks that moscow’s policy poses and the opportunities that are offered for mutually-beneficial cooperation. we must be fully prepared to face such risks and protect our citizens from hybrid threats. at the same time, we should not lose determination to build on the opportunities and further develop our relations. let me now react to several contributions which we have had. the european union is not being humiliated or allowing anyone to humiliate. we are firm and united on our sanctions. these show clear support for ukraine and at the same time impose a cost on the violation of international law. in reaction to the debate on the blacklist, let me quote high representative/vice-president mogherini: ‘we did protest and will continue to do so in all circumstances.’ unfortunately, federica mogherini cannot be present for this very important debate today on eu relations with russia, as she is currently chairing the eu-celac summit. i will report to her your main messages and i am sure that you will have the opportunity to discuss this important item with her soon. let me thank you for your fruitful exchanges. your report is a timely and strong document. i look forward to its final adoption later this week.

the next item is the joint debate on– the recommendation from the committee on the environment, public health and food safety on the draft council decision on the conclusion, on behalf of the european union, of the doha amendment to the kyoto protocol to the united nations framework convention on climate change and the joint fulfilment of commitments thereunder (10400/2014 – c8-0029/2015 – 2013/0376(nle)) (rapporteur: elisabetta gardini) (a8-0167/2015), and– the recommendation from the committee on the environment, public health and food safety on the draft council decision on the conclusion, on behalf of the european union, of the agreement between the european union and its member states, on the one part, and iceland, on the other part, concerning iceland’s participation in the joint fulfilment of commitments of the european union, its member states and iceland for the second commitment period of the kyoto protocol to the united nations framework convention on climate change (10883/2014 – c8-0088/2015 – 2014/0151(nle)) (rapporteur: giovanni la via) (a8—0166/2015).
i'd like to be clear from the start that we're not in a competition. it's clear that if we treat this debate as a competition and we lose this competition, we all suffer. we all know that the main objective of the kyoto protocol is to reduce greenhouse gas emissions internationally. it represents an important step forward in the fight against global warming, containing binding and quantified targets for limiting and reducing greenhouse gases. given that climate commitments can only benefit us, i welcome the doha amendment which strengthens this commitment period legally under the european union climate and energy package. i believe in the leadership of the european union internationally and i am convinced that the national ratification processes for the adoption of the doha amendment will take place by the end of this year, and that the other signatories to the protocol will try to do the same. all authorities and actors involved must therefore be aware of this, whether they are from the north, east or west of the globe. and there's another concern: the warming effect that occurs in one part of the globe will affect other parts of the globe. it is our duty, all of ours, to leave future generations the right to breathe clean air.
madam president, under the doha agreement we commit to limit our average annual greenhouse gas emissions in the years 2013-2020 to 80% of our 1990 emissions. i am completely in favour of the ratification of the doha amendment to the kyoto protocol as it will send a strong international signal about the efforts and the leadership of the eu and its member states in addressing climate change. i believe we need to increase political momentum towards a strong paris agreement, and this is why i believe that all the other parties to the kyoto protocol should rapidly advance their ratification process. we should call on all these countries to ratify as soon as possible, because this is of tremendous importance to ensure the necessary global response to climate change. a signed agreement will keep us united on the right track, sharing a vision of a climate-safe world with sustainable growth for all.
madam president, although the conclusion of the doha amendment would not bring any change in terms of member states’ co2 reductions and commitments, it would nevertheless give a clear signal, before the paris climate change summit, about europe’s ability to face its responsibilities as a polluter and its commitment to be at the forefront of the fight against climate change. however, as the report rightly points out, we must use all possible political, diplomatic and economic tools at our disposal to take on board the still uncommitted major polluters in the new international agreement in paris this year. in this sense, yesterday’s breakthrough agreement from the g7 summit is an encouraging development. we should do our utmost to use it in the creation of a global climate change action plan that is economically efficient and politically bold and farsighted.
the debate is closed. the vote will take place on wednesday, 10 june 2015 at 12.00. written statements (rule 162)
in writing. i believe that the european union must continue to have a major approach under the kyoto protocol and in this regard i support the adoption of the doha amendment which provides for legally binding commitments to reduce ghg emissions in the period 2013-2020 to 80% of the reference year's emissions. given that romania is the first european country to sign the kyoto protocol, whereby it has undertaken its commitment to support the fight against climate change by reducing greenhouse gas emissions, i believe, as does the rapporteur, that the formal adoption of this amendment is among the priority objectives of the european union, contributing fundamentally to global efforts to address climate change.
the next item is the report by algirdas saudargas, on behalf of the committee on industry, research and energy, on european energy security strategy (2014/2153(ini))(a8-0164/2015).
question referred under the 'blue card' procedure i appreciate my colleague's input, and i appreciate the report, but i have a pointed question. how do you think we will be able to achieve the energy union, how will we be able to get the development gap in energy and transport infrastructure in the member states to be narrowed if the junker investment plan does not take account of social cohesion and geographical criteria, allocating funds on technical criteria?
the energy security strategy must first ensure the negotiation of the purchase of energy resources, in particular gas from russia, with one voice. we should start at regional level, with the assistance of the commission, to create regional energy infrastructure hubs. new gas sources are needed, limiting energy dependence on russia, expanding and strengthening transmission and distribution networks. the energy world involves coordinated governance of the internal market as well as strategic interconnectors, particularly in the western balkans. member states need incentives to develop a diversified energy mix based on indigenous energy sources that meet demand from renewable sources, including hydro, but also from fossil, thermal or nuclear hydrocarbons. a clear coal strategy is needed to ensure energy supply continuity. the black sea region is of geostrategic importance and accelerated cooperation is needed to develop the southern corridor and to provide a link with the caspian sea area, the middle east and central asia, to strengthen security of supply and to eliminate the russian monopoly. the commission should create the conditions for the integration of the offshore potential of the eastern mediterranean, the north sea, the baltic sea and the black sea, which is essential for the development of the european internal energy market. the european union needs to monitor more closely the strategy of the russian monopoly including the geopolitical acquisitions of the energy grid and distribution points and storage facilities. the nabucco project failure should not be forgotten but used as a lesson for the development of new gas transport corridors.
yesterday, ten member states including germany, france, poland and the czech republic signed a joint declaration on the regional initiative to develop a single electricity market, with the aim of strengthening security. it is noted that the formation of the single european electricity market passes through the formation of regional markets as an intermediate stage. i believe that concrete steps must be taken to achieve a single regional electricity market for the member states of southern and eastern europe together with the third countries in the area. this is a way of strengthening energy security. to this end, we need the support of the european commission to develop the necessary physical interconnections, harmonise regulations and transfer energy-efficient technologies.
madam president, allow me to quote a commission report which says there is no diversification or back-up in the event of supply problems, whether for technical or political reasons. you know that russia could cause significant disruption in the eu energy sector, and not only with regard to gas supply but also in relation to nuclear supply and nuclear fuel. as you know very well, there are 18 russian-designed nuclear reactors functioning in european union countries using russian atomic fuel: in finland, bulgaria, the czech republic, slovakia and hungary. this is a subject that has to be addressed quickly by the commission in the future energy security strategy of the european union. it is a subject of tremendous importance for europe’s energy security in the future.
for many countries in central and south-eastern europe, the concept of energy security is essential, both from the point of view of national security and the well-being of citizens. already marked by vulnerability to import dependence, especially from politically unstable regions, these states have seen an escalation of fears in the context of the crisis in ukraine. the crisis has called into question the urgency of progress on: european energy infrastructure, the completion of the internal energy market and the diversification of import sources. despite this context, there are also countries which are making considerable progress towards energy independence on a temporary basis. in the last three months, the moderation in demand for natural gas on the romanian market could be met from domestic production without having to rely on imports. we need more examples of this and i am glad that we have agreed the terms of a european energy security strategy. the creation of the energy union is the only solution to the vulnerabilities that logically derive from regional instability. the energy union can provide member states with a physical and legal framework through which they can cooperate and provide each other with energy resources needed for economic growth and job creation, citizens' welfare, industrial competitiveness and the business environment.
blue-card question.– you said that information has to be available to all relevant authorities. do you believe that access to the system for law—enforcement purposes should be granted, or not?

in writing. ‒ climate change is one of the most important challenges facing humanity and requires a responsible approach and concrete action at global, national and regional levels. rising temperatures, droughts, floods and melting glaciers are increasingly common phenomena that confirm the existence of climate change. the european union has been engaged in the fight against climate change for several years, both internally and internationally, making it one of the eu's priorities. in this context, the 1997 kyoto protocol, which gave the european union and its member states a shared responsibility to meet their collective greenhouse gas (ghg) emissions reduction commitment of 8% compared to 1990 levels in the period 2008-2012. it has been an effective tool used by the eu. in view of the problems of climate change and the steps to be taken to protect the environment, i welcome the wish to establish a second commitment period under the kyoto protocol as this helps to eliminate risks for all present and future people on the planet.
in writing. ‒ i support the adoption of the doha amendment establishing a second commitment period under the kyoto protocol from 1 january 2013 to 31 december 2020, providing for legally binding emission reduction commitments, thus demonstrating that both the european union and the member states are committed to limiting their annual average greenhouse gas (ghg) emissions over the period 2013-2020.
in writing. ‒ under the doha agreement we committed to limiting our average annual greenhouse gas (ghg) emissions in the years 2013 to 2020 to 80% of our 1990 emissions. i am in favour of ratifying the doha amendment to the kyoto protocol as it will send a strong international signal about the efforts and the leadership of the eu and its member states in addressing climate change. i believe we need to increase political momentum towards a strong paris agreement and this is why i believe all the other parties to the kyoto protocol should rapidly advance their ratification process. this ratification is of tremendous importance to ensure the necessary global response to climate change. signing the agreement will keep us united, on the right track, sharing a vision of a climate-safe world with sustainable growth for all.
in writing. ‒ it is important that the ratification decision on the adoption of the doha amendment to the kyoto protocol and the joint fulfilment of commitments by the european union sends an important message at international level. the eu must set a positive example in this respect.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the recommendation on the ratification decision on the conclusion of the doha amendment to the kyoto protocol because the eu has to promptly address the issue of climate change at an international level. a multilateral response to climate change, together with a smart, strategic framework for an energy union are two complementary eu policies. we cannot coherently tackle the issue of energy security and efficiency without taking into account climate change. in addition, the eu and its member states are already implementing a 20% emissions reduction target by 2020, which in fact allows them to agree to implement their commitments for the kyoto protocol. we are witnessing extreme weather events: very high temperatures on the hand, and on the other hand the western antarctic and greenland ice-sheets melting at unprecedented rates. while the oceans are warming and industrial pollution is booming we must not forget that nature takes care of us, so we need to take care of nature as well! protecting our planet and the future of our grandchildren has to be our primary goal.
în scris. ‒ the kyoto protocol to the united nations framework convention on climate change was signed in 1997 setting an internationally binding emission reduction target. i have voted for this report because it will commit the states parties to reducing greenhouse gases and also because it is a valuable part of the momentum for global climate action.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the recommendation on the proposal for a council decision on the conclusion of the agreement between the european union and its member states, of the one part, and iceland, of the other part, on iceland's participation in the joint fulfilment of the commitments of the european union, its member states and iceland for the second commitment period of the kyoto protocol. this agreement lays down the conditions governing iceland's participation in the joint fulfilment of commitments by the union, its member states and iceland. this country participates in the joint fulfilment of commitments on the same basis as eu member states. i believe that iceland's participation in the joint fulfilment of commitments for the second period under the kyoto protocol will have a visible impact and send a strong signal in terms of coordinated european efforts and engagement to address existing climate change issues.
in writing. ‒ i appreciate that iceland, which is not a member state, also supports the adoption of the doha amendment, thus demonstrating its interest in jointly meeting this commitment based on the total greenhouse gas emissions permitted for the period 2013-2020 under the eu climate and energy package.
in writing. ‒ the doha amendment establishes a second commitment period under the kyoto protocol, starting on 1 january 2013 and ending on 31 december 2020, with legally binding emissions-reduction commitments according to which the european union, its member states and iceland are jointly committed to limit their average annual greenhouse gas emissions in the years 2013-2020 to 80% of their base-year (in most cases 1990) emissions. since iceland is not an eu member state, the terms of joint fulfilment concerning its participation had to be laid down in a separate international agreement. the ratification decision on the conclusion of the doha amendment to the kyoto protocol, and the joint fulfilment of the commitments by the european union, will send a strong signal about the efforts and the leadership of the eu and its member states in addressing climate change at international level, and the consent of the european parliament to this agreement is therefore necessary.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the recommendation for a council decision on the accession of croatia to the convention on mutual assistance in criminal matters between the member states of the european union, adopted by the council on 29 may 2000 on the basis of article 34 of the treaty on european union and to the protocol of 16 october 2001 thereto, as the 2012 act concerning the conditions of accession of the republic of croatia to the european union has simplified the accession of this country to the conventions (and protocols) concluded by the member states on the basis of article 34 of the treaty on european union. the convention on mutual assistance in criminal matters between the member states of the european union aims to support and facilitate cooperation between judicial, police and customs authorities in criminal matters. it complements, in particular, the 1959 council of europe convention on mutual legal assistance in criminal matters and its 1978 protocol. such an act is welcome as a spontaneous exchange of information (without prior request) can take place at any time between member states, concerning criminal offences and administrative offences for which the sanctioning or treatment is the responsibility of the receiving authority.
in writing. ‒ this commission recommendation for a council decision will pave the way for croatia to complete its accession to the 2000 convention on mutual assistance in criminal matters (‘the mla convention’), between the member states of the european union, and its protocol. it follows from the 2011 treaty of accession concerning croatia, which lists six conventions and protocols in the area of justice and home affairs to which croatia would accede by way of council decisions. this council decision will make the adjustments to the mla convention which are required by reason of croatia’s accession. i backed this proposal in the plenary.
in writing. ‒ on 30 june, croatia became the 28th member state of the european union. today, i have voted for this report to continue its accession to the conventions and protocols concluded by the other member states of the european union.
in writing. ‒ the general secretariat of the council drew attention to a technical error in the commission recommendation affecting the provision on the date of entry into force of the convention between croatia and the member states. indeed, according to article 1 of the recommendation, the convention enters into force between croatia and the member states for which it is in force on the first day of the first month following the date of adoption of the decision. in accordance with article 3, the decision 'enters into force' on the 20th day following its publication in the official journal. article 3 (5) of the act of accession therefore provides that, to this end, the council is to adopt a decision determining the date on which those conventions enter into force with regard to croatia and the adaptations to be made to them as a result of the accession of the new member state (which would include, in any event, the adoption of the conventions in the croatian language so that those versions are 'equally authentic'). i voted in favour of this recommendation for a council decision because i consider the requirement of publication to be an essential procedural requirement and because the provisions laid down clearly regulate time limits.

in writing. ‒ in the context of recent geopolitical events, the importance of the european union's energy security has become essential. despite significant progress in strengthening it, by increasing the share of renewables and by a general reduction in demand, 53% of the total energy consumption of the european union is covered by imports. the main risks stem from the fact that much of this energy comes from geopolitically unstable areas such as the middle east, russia or the caucasus, and from the fact that many european states continue to be dependent on a single external source of supply, which leads to high costs for citizens and endangers national and european security. i support the idea of creating an energy union, based on the principles of competitiveness and sustainability, in a fully integrated energy market. we need full integration of energy systems to enable the trans-border transport of surplus energy in order to prevent shocks caused by external energy supplies. greater effective solidarity between european states would reduce risks to energy security and help to eliminate a serious vulnerability in the current international context marked by tensions in ukraine, the middle east and the maghreb.

rapporteur.– mr president, after the cold war, the black sea – which was relatively closed before – became, first, a transport route for caspian oil and gas towards the west and, second, a source of energy in itself, forcing both its opening up and its consideration in a larger regional perspective, namely the ‘black sea area’. thus the black sea area has become both economically relevant and politically contested, as witness the geopolitics of the various pipelines crossing it and the efforts by russia and turkey to oppose outside penetration. the breaking up of the former soviet union and the admission of romania and bulgaria to both nato and the eu have markedly transformed the political landscape, specifically compelling the eu to come up with an integrative instrument, namely the black sea synergy, back in 2007. contrary to the bureaucratic view, the initiative has had little impact in terms of fostering a regional common identity among the countries in the area, and consequently on strengthening cooperation between them. in part that was so because almost all the countries involved had more important forms of collaboration with the eu, other than the synergy. however, the relatively reduced efficiency of the initiative is geopolitical. the area was in flux in 2007 and it still is today. after the illegal annexation of crimea by russia, the latter’s destabilisation of eastern ukraine and the practical inclusion of both abkhazia and south ossetia in russia’s military organisation, one could say that the black sea area is moving back to what it looked like two decades ago, with russia attempting to control its northern shores, as the soviet union did 24 years ago. the occupation of crimea and the current efforts to cut two territorial corridors – one from russia towards crimea and another from crimea towards transnistria – are undeniable realities. the siege of mariupol and the destabilisation of odessa are testimony to that. the fact is that, since the illegal annexation, crimea has become a launching pad towards bosnia – and the area around and beyond – due to the transformation of the initially small, defensive russian force stationed in sevastopol into a significant strike force equipped with long-range force-projection systems, quite apart from an aggressive programme of modernisation of the russian black sea fleet. in sum, russia has thus provided itself with a southern kaliningrad in support of its potential expansion. consequently, in the last year-and-a-half the black sea has acquired important military relevance, in addition to its existing economic relevance, which could not leave the eu uninterested, especially when both the eu security and defence strategies are being revised, making all the union’s other interests – environment for instance – inevitably mediated by the long—term militarisation process initiated in the area. therefore, the aim of this report is to increase the eu’s awareness of the complex situation created in the black sea, which could not – and should not – be either ignored or left entirely to nato to deal with. this reality calls for responsible management of the situation in the black sea, but a dialogue with russia – provided it was not misinterpreted by the latter as an encouragement to dare more – should obligatorily be accompanied by the continuation of deterrence as part of a strategic reassurance to the eastern members of both nato and the eu, who have lost faith in russia’s real intentions.

madam president, the illegal annexation of crimea by the russian federation and the military conflict in eastern ukraine has of course completely changed the security balance in the black sea region. in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on the strategic military situation in the black sea basin following the illegal annexation of crimea by russia because i believe that it correctly captures the situation in this region. the report also proposes a set of measures to strengthen the black sea basin region so that aggressions similar to the annexation of crimea are no longer possible. the member states of the european union must remain united in one voice on strengthening the sanctions regime against russia as long as it fails to comply with international law, while expressing readiness to resume talks when the occupied territories are returned to ukraine and international law is respected.
in writing. ‒ considering the recent developments in the military situation in the black sea basin which represent a big challenge to eu security, i welcome more warmly than ever the adoption in the subcommittee on security and defence (sede) of this comprehensive report. i believe that the eu can play a very constructive role and be a very important actor in this region, as this region is for the european union. stability in this region must be our key priority. we must enhance cooperation with nato and with the united states, and the osce should enlarge the scope of its efforts with regard to black sea security, this being fundamental to resolving protracted conflicts in the country.
in writing. – the black sea basin is one of the world’s most strategic regions, with high importance to the european union and its member states, thus ensuring their security and defence. i have voted in favour of this report, which highlights the strategic importance of the black sea basin to my country, romania, and also to the whole european union.
in writing. ‒ in the context of the serious events in ukraine in 2014 and 2015, i voted in favour of the report on the strategic military situation in the black sea basin following the illegal annexation of crimea by russia. due to its neighbourhood, the stability of the black sea region is fundamental to the security of the european union, which is threatened by the illegal annexation of crimea by russia. in addition, he has been involved in the repression of the ukrainian people. in response to this major change in the strategic and security landscape of the black sea, the report recommends maintaining a firm position and continuing communication with russia. however, due to the lack of trust following russia's recent actions, any resumption of cooperation must rely primarily on the firm strategic reassurance offered by nato to its eastern members. secondly, a change in russia's policy towards ukraine, in particular the full and unconditional implementation of the minsk agreements of september 2014 and february 2015 and the return of crimea to ukraine, is very important for the restoration of control of the ukrainian authorities over their territory within the internationally recognised borders.

written explanations of vote
in writing. ‒ the scandal at the fifa board level is seriously damaging the credibility of the world's most famous sports federation. it is sad that on the one hand the athletes promote positive attitudes and the spirit of fair play, and on the other hand the investigations reveal serious acts of corruption and money laundering, undermining the integrity of the federation. i am convinced that the very substantial sums invested in the football industry and the lack of a regulatory authority created the conditions for the emergence of acts of corruption and the creation of a kleptocratic structure that held control of the entire structure of the federation. the resignation of sepp blatter as fifa president does not fully solve the problem, a complete overhaul of the federation's organizational structure is needed. a body to oversee and regulate the activity of sports federations would be a way to stop abuses, and limiting the mandates of those appointed to the management structures would remove the establishment of clans for whom sport is an illicit business. i voted in favour of this resolution because i am convinced that structural reforms are needed at fifa level, both to restore its image and to increase transparency in decision-making.
in writing. ‒ the existence of corruption at the highest levels of the football world – with football now being the ‘world’s game’ – is a proven fact that must be roundly condemned. this endemic corruption not only compromises the quality of play on the field but also reduces fan support for the sport and tarnishes the beauty of the game. fifa is still structured in a way that fosters corruption: it is clear that the decision-making system must be revised. it is time to reform fifa, creating a separate institution that functions with transparency and oversight, and also to deal with the broader problems that the world cup creates in hosting nations, such as the increase in public debt, evictions and the militarisation of public spaces. the recent revelations are very discouraging for the millions of football fans who deserve a clean, transparent sport. but they are also an opportunity to raise the authority of international football governance to the level of the sport it represents.
in writing. – the formation of fifa took place on 21 may 1904 (111 years ago) to oversee international competition. headquartered in zürich, its membership now comprises 209 national associations. fifa is today responsible for both the organisation and the promotion of a number of tournaments, which generate revenue from sponsorship. in 2013 fifa had revenues of over usd 1.3 billion, for a net profit of 72 million, and had cash reserves of over usd 1.4 billion. i voted in favour of this motion for a resolution that opposes the corruption scandal among fifa’s high-level officials and proposes solutions to avoid such situations in the future through more transparency, self-regulation and activity reports.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this joint motion for a resolution on the recent revelations of corruption within fifa, as it expresses the views of a very large number of citizens who are outraged by the systemic extent of corruption within fifa. there has been a lot of talk for a long time, and investigative journalists have pointed out many times, of suspicions of serious corruption within this organization, and it is to be appreciated that a very thorough international investigation has been launched. it is shocking that this organization, which promotes fairness and fair play through the sport it represents, is actually being crushed by a systemic corruption that calls into question many, if not all, of the decisions it has made over the years. unfortunately, this is the result when we talk about huge amounts of money being managed by closed, non-transparent organizations with no independent and permanent oversight. all those who have committed illegalities must pay, and this organization must be rebuilt on a democratic and transparent basis so that these acts are not repeated.

mr president, first of all i would like to thank the rapporteurs of the european parliament who led these negotiations, because it was an extremely difficult task for all those who took part. it was a difficult negotiation, with four committees, with many rapporteurs, and at the same time, on the other side, there was a kind of union between the council and the commission and i hope this will not happen again in the future. i think they have done a very good job, they have managed to mitigate the effects on the two programmes 'connecting facility' and 'horizon 2020' and i think this will be seen in the future. now we have the legal framework. it was a project that had been long overdue. now let us see what the member states are doing, what projects they are presenting and let us hope that all the other eligible entities will present projects that cannot be financed by other means and projects that lead to economic development, to jobs. at the same time, i ask the commission to ensure that in the 2016 budget, in the same negotiation with my colleague mr fernandes, it tries to put money back into the connecting europe facility and horizon 2020. thank you very much.
question asked in accordance with the 'blue card' procedure. mr president, you mentioned in your speech that it would be important to see how we can also provide funds to smes and at the same time you said that you were sure that there would be no political influence. can you explain how you're sure there won't be political influence?
mr president, following the sharp drop of investments in the eu in the aftermath of the financial and economic crisis, the setting up of the european fund for strategic investments could be one of the answers to the provision of stimulus the european economy needs. i am hopeful that through a well-managed fund we can efficiently attract leveraged private investment in order to achieve the goal of creating more than a million new medium- and long-term jobs. the fact that, during the negotiations with the commission and the council, parliament succeeded in minimising the budget cuts in the connecting europe facility and the horizon 2020 programmes is also a great achievement, which ensures that vital financing for energy and transport infrastructures and research and development projects is secured.
in writing. the european union needs additional investment in the real economy over the next three years, and the european fund for strategic investments can and should support higher risk projects that can contribute to job creation and growth in the member states. by maximising the impact of public spending and unlocking the financing of private investment projects, europe can make progress in the member states and in the sectors where job creation and growth are most needed. we can only hope that there will be favourable treatment under the stability and growth pact for national contributions to the european fund for strategic investments, but also that the specificities of the member states will be taken into account.
in writing. this initiative by the european commission is very welcome. this european fund for strategic investments is to finance large-scale projects with high risks that member states do not and will never undertake. at the same time, we must avoid competition between member states. the expertise is totally different, the ability to attract funds and to invest is different. supporting smes is very important, as they can bring great benefits to the eu if they can get off the ground and start the engine of the economy.
in writing. the european parliament and the council have demonstrated that it is possible to set up a european fund outside the union budget - in this case, for strategic investments - using the community method. this success confirms once again that, when there is political will, the european union is able to make progress towards common goals. in this respect, i hope that we can achieve faster the formation of a fiscal capacity at union level, so as to achieve a true economic and monetary union, in line with the principles set out in the recent report of the presidents of the european institutions.
in writing. in the current global economic situation, where the european union is competing with strong states and regional structures, we need to harmonise tax systems to ensure that we all benefit from a coherent and unified environment within the union, offering equal opportunities for development to all member states. solidarity, which must return to the centre of the european institutions' concerns, dictates a clear principle: fiscal fairness. corporations have to give back to the communities that make them exist. we therefore call for greater transparency of tax obligations for large companies. the fight against corporate tax evasion is a fight for our medium and long-term development. europeans deserve to be informed and to have a clear understanding of the profit margins of companies operating in europe. in this way, we can know very clearly what taxes are due in each member state and that those business entities pay taxes where they produce and make a profit. it is essential that there is a balance between member states as regards taxation of multinational companies. this balance is necessary to provide more resources for the sustainable development of the member states and the prosperity of european citizens.
madam president, europe is today in the midst of a crisis of legitimacy, because it is failing to protect its citizens and to ensure equal treatment for all, regardless of country or nationality. this is the situation of european citizens from my country, romania. romanians are underrepresented at the level of european institutions and, more specifically, romania, although the seventh largest state in the european union, ranks only 22nd in terms of representation in senior positions in the european institutions. romanians are also stigmatized by many politicians in europe lately. for example, in austria, the foreign minister decided to ask for a reduction in social rights for romanians living in that country. when, dear members of the european parliament, are we going to call an end to all these abuses? when will we realise that europe means freedoms and rights for all its citizens? if we talk today about the issue of the rights of european romanians, i assure you that if we do not act, we will be talking tomorrow about poles, greeks, spaniards, maybe even germans. we must build a european society for all, and romanians, like all europeans, are full eu members.
madam president, the question of the nationalization of property by the communist authorities in romania has been raised on several occasions, including in the form of a question to the commission. we pointed out that the restitution process in romania had stopped, and in fact, in the case of an important church property, the court decided in favor of re-nationalization, finding the officials guilty of performing their official duties. despite the unacceptable situation, the european institutions did not speak out, did not take account of the commitments made by a member state. on june 11, the united states congressional budget committee unanimously included in the budget of the state department in washington the issue of the return of church property in romania, requesting the treasury to report on this issue within 90 days. so it seems that the united states believes that it is important to uphold human rights and minority rights in an eu member state, while our own institutions are unable to formulate a coherent position and hold accountable commitments in relation to the relevant policy of a member state.
madam president, i believe that fundamental rights and freedoms in a democratic society must be a reality. the european union is considered a community of values based on human dignity, freedom, equality and solidarity. the free movement of workers is provided for in the treaty on european union and in regulation (eu) no 492/2011. however, some member states do not comply with this regulation. as a member of the european parliament, i argue that the european union's regulation needs to be respected and i call on the commission, the council and all european institutions to take the necessary measures to ensure that workers' rights are respected in all member states. i cannot stand by and watch discrimination by some states against citizens of my country and other countries and i demand that freedom of movement be respected. i do not think that some member states should just choose what suits them from a treaty, but they should respect all the regulations of the european institutions if they are members of the european union.
the statements of foreign minister sebastian kurz regarding the allowances granted to romanian children living legally in austria, namely the intention that their payment be made at the level of the amount in romania, demonstrate an unacceptable irresponsibility for a minister of a state that is part of the european union. i'd like to think that it was just a moment of deep intellectual silence from someone with no experience of public office. just as i don't want to believe that romanians are good for those in western europe just to build their houses, clean their garbage or protect their borders. child benefits are not only a right but also an obligation of the state in which their parents live and work legally, and they must be paid equally, regardless of race or nationality. i warn the austrian government, from the rostrum of the european parliament, that, the second after such a decision is taken, i will publicly demand that all companies with austrian capital operating in romania pay taxes and duties to the romanian state, as well as employees, at the level of the amount in austria.
in writing. ‒ i voted for this report in accordance with the resolution and the analysis of the report.
in writing. ‒ i voted for this report in accordance with the resolution and the analysis of the report.
in writing. ‒ in the context of the recent economic and financial crisis, european actors are advocating increased investment in the eu to cover the investment gap generated. this lack of investment has created a downward spiral of reduced spending, rising unemployment and loss of confidence in future progress. the introduction of new incentives to increase investment, backed by guarantees, can increase the confidence of investors, public authorities and the industrial sector. by unlocking new investment, the efsi can become the cornerstone of an investment cycle that creates new jobs and opportunities. these new investments are not only necessary to revitalise the union economy but also to transform it into a sustainable, innovative and circular economy. it is also of particular importance that the efsi reinforces those policies and contributes to their delivery, by also focusing on the transformative investments needed for sustainable and low-carbon transport infrastructure, digital and research infrastructure, renewable energy creation, energy efficiency and energy storage, and the bringing to market of new innovative products, services and technologies.
in writing. ‒ after years of painful austerity and structural reforms, europe is still in a process of recovery, while growth remains sluggish. compared to pre-crisis years, we must realise that we find ourselves in an ʽinvestment holeʼ, as commission president juncker himself put it. investor sentiment remains rather low and our economy needs a rapidly deployable booster. hopefully this will be the role of the famous juncker plan, made fact in the european fund for strategic investments, for which i voted today. of course, parliament left its mark on the original plan. ultimately, this resulted in it having oversight over some of the fund’s governance aspects, project selection has become more transparent and eur 1 billion less will be taken from the eu’s flagship research and infrastructure programmes. all in all, i hope i will not regret having shared in the optimism of the fund’s supporters.
in writing. ‒ the european fund for strategic investments (efsi) was designed to boost the european union's long-term economic growth and competitiveness. i voted in favour of this report on the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council on the european fund for strategic investments and amending regulations (eu) no 1291/2013 and (eu) no 1316/2013 because the final proposal incorporated several amendments that i had initiated to allow access to these funds for all states and beneficiaries.
in writing. ‒ given the s&d contribution to the final form of this programme, i reiterate that we will not agree to a reduction in research funding. horizon 2020 and the connecting europe facility now benefit from a budgetary solution to maintain financial strength and to continue the investments started. we must take into account that european research and innovation programmes must not be a source of emergency funding for other programmes and must remain functional, because they produce jobs and clear results in the economy. the political consensus on a programme that will give us a chance at sustainable development is used to draw attention to the fact that the application of the efsi must be fair to all member states, but especially to regions that have to overcome significant development gaps, both in terms of infrastructure and other socio-economic aspects. i think we must take every opportunity to ensure european solidarity, including economic solidarity. the efsi now represents a chance to develop the eu's border infrastructure, to reduce economic and social disparities in europe and to increase competitiveness in all european regions, including the least prosperous.
in writing. i voted in favour of the report on the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council on the european fund for strategic investments (efsi). i welcome the perspective of the rapporteurs, who pointed out that the efsi should support projects that promote quality job creation, growth and competitiveness in the short, medium and long term, research, early education and training, infrastructure and transition and energy efficiency. the report adopted by the ep also underlines that investments supported by the efsi should contribute to the implementation of existing union programmes and policies and to the achievement of the europe 2020 strategy objectives for smart, sustainable and inclusive growth. the efsi aims to mobilise at least eur 315 billion in private and public investment across the european union. the commission proposal also establishes a european investment advisory hub.
in writing. ‒ the european globalisation adjustment fund (egf) provides support for people who lose their jobs as a result of major structural changes in world trade patterns due to globalisation or the economic and financial crisis. as shadow rapporteur, i voted for this report to amend the regulation for a better implementation of egf projects.
in writing. ‒ globalisation is a complex phenomenon that can sometimes pose a number of problems even for the most developed countries in the world. the changes it implies in labour dynamics may come as a surprise to governments and international institutions. to this end, the european globalisation adjustment fund was set up, which can help some of those who have lost their jobs as a result of the changes brought about by globalisation to reintegrate into the labour market. the budgetary effort of the european union for this programme is not very large, but its effects can be considerable for the achievement of efficient employment of the available workforce. this programme contributes to social cohesion measures within the union, in particular the reintegration of young people, one of the most vulnerable groups, into the labour market. for these reasons, i consider the draft resolution on the mobilisation of the european globalisation adjustment fund to be a useful document for european citizens, which should be supported by the european parliament.
in writing. i voted in favour of the report on the creation of a technical assistance system within the commission for member states that intend to receive funds from the european globalisation adjustment fund (egf). the egf was established to provide additional support for workers whose jobs have been affected by the consequences of major structural changes in international trade practices. the commission proposal concerns the mobilisation of eur 630 000 from the egf reserve for technical assistance at the initiative of the commission. the objective of the technical assistance is to finance monitoring, information activities, to create a knowledge base interface and to provide advice to member states on the use, monitoring and evaluation of the egf. according to the report adopted in the ep, the commission will organise liaison activities between member states through two seminars dedicated to the egf implementing bodies in the member states, which will take place around the same dates and will focus on issues related to the practical implementation of the egf regulation at grassroots level.
in writing. ‒ more than seven years after the start of the crisis, the euro has been supported by measures such as the revision of the stability and growth pact (sgp), the budgetary pact, the creation of a european stability mechanism (esm), the establishment of the banking union and the establishment of the key role of the european central bank (ecb). however, the forecasts of a decrease in the unemployment rate and inflation were not met. in the light of the present situation, a controversy has arisen over the policies adopted in the wake of the crisis, given that the euro area has encountered difficulties vis-à-vis its counterparts. the new provisions have not been sufficient to counteract the cumulative effects at union level on the budgetary position of the member states and have therefore not resolved problems such as the deflationary threat, low economic growth or high unemployment. i voted in favour of the report because i want to see emu working better and a symmetrical approach to contributions to the co-financing of projects under the efsi.
in writing. ‒ since the financial crisis of 2007, the weaknesses of the economic governance framework established for the euro area in 1990 have become apparent, failing to take account of the complexity of the macroeconomic policy challenges for a monetary union. i voted in favour of this report on the evaluation of the economic governance framework for the implementation of new elements with a view to achieving closer coordination, economic convergence and the rationalisation of the european semester.
in writing. ‒ the european union is, from its very origins, a project designed to strengthen solidarity between european states and citizens. the first area where this has been true is the economic sector. today, the european union's economy is one of the best performing in the world, allowing a high standard of living for our citizens. however, the crisis has called into question the viability of our development model, particularly because of the problems faced by some member states. the response mechanisms created at eu level to address these issues suffer from an inherent lack of legitimacy, which can only be remedied through the involvement of the european parliament, the representative forum of european citizens. it is only in this forum that we can decide whether or not the rules by which the economic and monetary union operates can be changed, only here can we choose one model of development or another, a greater or lesser degree of convergence. in the current context, i believe that the solution is to increase european integration and solidarity by achieving a fiscal union, a banking union and the introduction of a european minimum wage. the continuation of the european project can only mean strengthening economic integration, to ensure the prosperity of all our citizens.
mr president, i think that this circus, this attempt to export the circus that the communists are making in greece, must be stopped here in the european parliament. i think we must get back to serious things and stop this attempt to do anything in this parliament. i am therefore against the debates proposed by these communists who have put greece in a terrible situation and who are going to make a mess here.
