in writing. ‒ every crisis is also an opportunity for society to rethink the way it organises production. the green economy is one of the sustainable alternatives for boosting economic growth in the european union. this may also lead to the creation of new jobs for european citizens. in the context of structural changes in the labour market, support is needed for the re-skilling of citizens to acquire the skills needed in the new type of economy. at the same time, this type of economy can be supported by measures to strengthen environmental criteria in public procurement and lower taxes for green businesses. the promotion of the green jobs initiative and the green sme action plan by the european commission over the past year has been an important element in developing this sector, limiting fossil fuel consumption and making it more resource efficient. however, these documents are only the beginning of a coherent investment policy to create sustainable jobs in the green economy and support smes in this sector. the present report is a decisive new step in this direction and its adoption will create the conditions for a positive development towards sustainable economic growth within the union.
in writing. ‒ as global warming and biodiversity loss reach limits beyond which irreversible effects on our societies and the natural environment cannot be avoided, the exploitation of the green economy for jobs is emerging as a source of hope for improving human well-being and social equity. moreover, the development of new technologies, new less polluting sectors, renewable energies and new modes of production can represent a potential for economic growth in europe and worldwide. in this scenario, i consider that the transition to a green economy can have the effect of creating new jobs, as sustainable economic activities involve more labour than those they replace. moreover, waste prevention, ecodesign and reuse could generate net savings of €600 billion or 8% of annual turnover for eu businesses, while reducing annual greenhouse gas emissions by 2-4%. for these reasons, i voted in favour of the report on the green jobs initiative.
mr president, the commission must as a matter of priority set out an ambitious action plan to support developing countries in the fight against tax evasion, in the establishment of fair, balanced and transparent tax systems. information on beneficial owners of companies and other institutions must be made public and in a format accessible to all. we also need an international definition of tax havens. we need sanctions for operators that use these tax havens and the creation of a blacklist of those countries. the commission's revised 2015 tax avoidance plan is good, but member states need to agree on a consolidated, common corporate tax base.
in writing. ‒ domestic resources are and will remain the most important source of finance for developing countries as well as for developed countries. although the level of these resources as a percentage of gdp has increased over the last decade, the average share of taxes and duties in gdp in developing countries is still too low, leading to basic services of far too low quality for their citizens, and to an increasing financial dependence on international aid from the eu and other international donors. the share of taxes and duties in gdp in low-income countries is between 10% and 20%, and in many of these countries it is below 15% (this is generally considered to be the minimum threshold below which governments can finance their basic functions and services). i voted in favour of this report because i believe that the internal tax collection process needs to become more predictable, more transparent, more stable and better managed.
in writing. ‒ trade, the informal nature of the economy, together with political, administrative and economic constraints, are an obstacle to revenue mobilisation, particularly in developing countries. domestic resources are and will remain the most important source of financing for developing countries. the loss of tax revenue can be exacerbated by tax treaties, a key component of international tax law. the oecd-proposed and g20-approved base erosion and profit shifting (beps) action plan seeks to redefine international tax rules in order to combat profit shifting practices and ensure that companies pay taxes where their economic activity takes place and where economic value is created. i voted in favour of the report because i believe that an action plan to combat tax evasion and tax fraud in developing countries is needed.
in writing. ‒ there is a considerable potential to increase tax collection in developing countries, which right now, in comparative prospective, raise substantially less revenues than advanced economies. i strongly believe that domestic resource mobilisation is key to achieve the new sustainable development goals and at a time when oda is not sufficient in that regard. better tax justice will help reduce inequalities and eradicate poverty, while also bringing an end to tax havens for multinational companies, including european companies. i welcome the recommendations included in the report, such as the importance of strengthening financial and technical assistance to developing countries and regional tax administration frameworks; the adoption of strong solutions to enhance transparency and cooperation in the fight against tax dodging, such as an automatic exchange of information mechanism and country-by-country reporting, taking into consideration developing countries’ needs and constraints; the conducting at eu and member states’ level of an impact assessment of tax policies on developing countries; the preservation of source countries’ taxation rights when negotiating tax treaties, and the creation of a truly intergovernmental body where developing countries could participate on an equal footing in the global reform of existing international tax rules. i thank the rapporteur elly schlein and the shadows for the great job done.
in writing. ‒ the commission should take concrete measures to support developing countries and regional tax administration frameworks. listed or unlisted multinational companies of all countries and sectors must adopt country-by-country reporting (cbcr) as a standard. they should publish as part of their annual reporting and on a country-by-country basis for each territory in which they operate. i voted in favour of this report.
in writing. ‒ i have voted for this report that tackles the need for an action plan in the fight against tax avoidance and tax evasion in developing countries.
in writing. ‒ the european union is the most important source of development aid to the world's poorest countries. this is rooted in the principle of solidarity, which is at the foundation of the union and which is also applied in its relations with developing countries. however, development aid often misses its target because of the inconsistency of the tax and tax systems in these countries, which stimulate the underground economy, corruption, tax evasion, organized crime. some states don't even have tax systems, providing tax havens for laundering black money from developed economies or for exploiting their mineral resources. the legitimacy of their governments is very fragile because they don't fulfill this side of the social contract that is supposed to bind them to their citizens and that translates into using public funds to provide public goods and services. in these circumstances, the european union, which has more experience in this field, can help combat tax evasion in developing countries. this would contribute both to the sustainable development of those countries and to combating negative phenomena that feed into the lack of a tax system, such as terrorism, piracy and the illegal trafficking of goods and persons.
in writing. ‒ resource efficiency is of paramount importance in the current european and international context. europe depends on imported resources more than any other region in the world, as over 40% of all materials used in the eu come from imports. increasing the efficiency of resource use by using them in a more coherent way would reduce dependency, both in terms of costs and human security. according to the european commission estimates, an annual increase of 2% in resource productivity by 2030 would create two million new jobs in the eu. i voted in favour of this resolution because i believe that we can increase europe's competitiveness and reindustrialisation and raise living standards only by decoupling economic growth from resource use and thus making the transition to a more circular economy.
in writing. ‒ europe is more dependent on imported resources than any other region in the world, and a move towards a circular economy would reduce this level of resource dependency and raw material costs. in addition, new businesses and jobs would be created in europe, all of which would be a way of increasing resource efficiency. financial statements, accounting rules and integrated reporting should better take into account the systemic risks posed by environmental degradation, overuse of resources and short-term market trends and therefore a new and clear policy framework is needed to enable private and institutional investors to shift their investment paradigm towards sustainable investments. i voted in favour of the report because current policies do not sufficiently focus efforts on this paradigm shift, locking europe into a system where valuable materials, many of them with high environmental and social costs, end up in landfills or incineration.
in writing. ‒ in a circular economy model, existing materials and products are continuously re-used, repaired, re-furbished and recycled, and thus the waste quantities are minimised. moving towards a circular economy is essential to deliver on the resource efficiency agenda, which can bring major economic benefits. the transition to a circular economy requires changes throughout value chains, covering product design, manufacturing, marketing and consumer behaviour, and the involvement of all relevant stakeholders. the committee report as adopted in the envi committee sends an ambitious signal to the commission with the aim of guiding the ongoing work on the new waste package which is expected by the end of 2015. implementing a circular economy model responds to key policy challenges in the eu such as jobs and growth, innovation, the re-industrialisation agenda, and an intelligent use of resources.
in writing. – today’s unsustainable use of resources is both causing environmental damage and posing an economic risk. the global economy uses the equivalent of 1.5 planets’ worth of resources, thus i have voted for this report to improve resource efficiency that will benefit our economy and security.
in writing. ‒ the optimisation of resource management is something i am very much in favour of so i supported this report. there is a wide variety of resources in europe which are either scarce, or not present at all, and what we do have, we certainly need to use better, for a longer term. a circular economy in this sense should be a major medium- to long-term sustainability target for all the member states and the commission, in all available areas. from fisheries to natural resources and manufacturing, from flora and fauna resources, all should be exploited in such a way so as to create even further benefit in the long run. and this is not simply about recycling and the jobs associated with that, but about many other products and their lifespans, their production and post-usage cycles. i believe all national governments should adopt this term for themselves very soon.
in writing. ‒ i voted 'for' because all the studies and expert opinions i have had access to indicate that this legislative package can transform europe's economy into a sustainable system and will lead to new jobs, especially among young people. i also believe that more attention needs to be paid to regions and workforces negatively affected by the transition to a circular economy, such as the approximately 350 000 jobs in europe's mining industry. the european commission needs to work with the social partners to create solidarity mechanisms such as financial compensation, retraining and retraining for this workforce.
in writing. ‒ a transition to a circular economy, with greater emphasis on reuse and recycling, would relieve pressure on finite resources and create opportunities and employment in the expanding reuse and recycling industries. it would also reduce european dependence on imported resources and energy. to bring about the changes in consumption patterns necessary to create a circular economy, significant modifications will need to be made on many levels, including product design, manufacturing, marketing, and consumer behaviour. these changes will need to be encouraged by the right legislative framework. i urge the commission to take note of parliament’s recommendations, especially on the issues of landfill, green public procurement, biomass, and eu financial support for greater resource efficiency.
in writing. ‒ we are on the verge of changing the way we approach the use of natural resources and the traditional economic model. without compromising the living standards and well-being of citizens, we have the opportunity to revolutionise the framework for natural resources policies and support the reindustrialisation of the european union, decoupling it from the irresponsible use of raw materials. the political signal given by the vote on it will create the leverage needed to steer investment towards job creation and the generation of new business models. a resource-efficient economy is a cost-optimized economy, one based on redistribution and solidarity. i welcome proposals to develop indicators on resource use, optimisation of supply chains and prioritisation of waste, which will have a considerable impact on ecodesign. the creation of product passports will increase responsible production by producers and consumer confidence. the industrial symbiosis generated by this communication will contribute to increasing the global competitiveness of our companies and to economic independence from those raw materials that come from high geopolitical risk areas, without which the digital economy loses its momentum.
in writing. ‒ irresponsible use of resources can be a danger to the environment, leading to climate change, decline in biodiversity, loss of diversity and deterioration of ecosystem services. in a context where europe depends on important resources that will be depleted in a relatively short period of time, and where the global economy uses the resources of one and a half planets for the production and absorption of waste, i believe that a swift transition to a circular economy is needed. it is an economic concept closely linked to sustainable development and whose objective is to produce goods and services while limiting the negligent consumption of raw materials, water and energy sources. to avoid an economic and environmental impasse in europe and globally, we need to increase resource efficiency, which means moving away from the current linear economy, perfectly characterised by the phrase 'use-produce-consume-throw-away'. furthermore, they argue that special attention must be paid to spatial planning and transport solutions in order to build a sustainable society.
in writing. ‒ the unfortunate events at chernobyl and fukushima, which claimed thousands of lives and left a black mark on human history, must serve as a reference point for the european union and the entire international spectrum in relation to future action in the event of a nuclear accident or other radiological emergency. the european union has a duty to have and to ensure up-to-date legal instruments, including flexible decision-making procedures adapted to each situation, to deal with post-nuclear-accident-type situations. that is why i voted in favour of this report on the proposal for a council regulation laying down maximum permitted levels of radioactive contamination of food and feed following a nuclear accident or any other radiological emergency, because i believe that the european union must be prepared to prevent such extremely unfortunate situations, which endanger the lives of its citizens.
in writing. ‒ it is absolutely important to have legal instruments that include flexible, incident-specific decision-making procedures to address situations like those that occurred in the wake of the accidents at chernobyl and fukushima. i welcome the inclusion in the report of the referral to the need of consultation with independent experts when reviewing maximum levels. moreover, full information must be made immediately available to the general public. food safety is the ultimate objective of the council regulation: therefore i strongly support that the change of the legal base of the lisbon treaty is appropriate to give the european parliament an appropriate say in the protection of public health, in line with its co-legislative role.
in writing. – i have voted for this report because the european union needs up-to-date legal instruments that include flexible and specific decision-making procedures to address situations like those that occurred in the wake of the accidents at chernobyl and fukushima.
in writing. ‒ i voted against this report as i believe this document did not meet the level of expertise needed for it to pass a plenary vote in the european parliament. it lacked an adequate amount of guarantees supporting its conclusions, the basis of its findings is not clear enough and its opinions are not truly endorsed by many key partners, for example euratom.
in writing. ‒ i fully support the decision of the rapporteur and shadow rapporteurs to change the legal basis to allow for the full involvement of the european parliament in this legislation. it is vital that parliament can exercise its full co-decision powers on an issue which has such great implications for human health. this change in legal basis allows parliament to make important changes to the text which will improve safety standards and increase transparency.
in writing. ‒ nuclear accidents are a danger to the safety and security of european citizens. it is not that long since 1986, when the chernobyl plant created one of the worst nuclear accidents in history, and the echoes of this tragedy must not fade, precisely to help us be better prepared and prevent such situations. the nuclear event response procedures need to be continuously updated. i therefore believe that both prevention measures and response plans in the event of a nuclear event must take into account the long-term effects on food and food safety. the safety of european consumers depends on the prompt application of reaction procedures to any nuclear event, but also on the continuous analysis and assessment of radioactivity levels for food and feed by experts in the field. in the same context, they agree that this analysis should also be carried out for food originating from areas other than the european one, in order to ensure the safety and security of european consumers.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the motion for a resolution on the creation of a capital markets union. to remain competitive and attractive on the international market, the european union needs a deep approach to capital markets and, not least, it needs to take account of developments in capital markets at international level. the european union is also defined by the diversity of member states' business models and financial markets, which can be turned into assets and which deserve to be protected at european level. i believe that through flexible legislation, which takes account of the needs of each member state individually, but also of the european union as a whole, the major obstacles to investment and investors will disappear and the eu will undoubtedly strengthen its position on the international market.
in writing. ‒ i strongly support this report, representing the ep’s input into the green book of the european commission. the capital markets union can play a full part in financing economic recovery in the eu through deepening and broadening eu capital markets, alongside bank finance. i welcome the introduction of our main priorities in the report, which lay at the core of our social-democratic values, namely capital markets to finance long-term investment, the real economy and especially smes. i support the importance of developing the european capital markets to diversify funding and improve access to financing, restoring also the stability of the banking sector. we succeeded in improving the text, by defeating many amendments which aimed at making the cmu a deregulatory agenda for the financial markets; the text now clearly refers to the need for legislative action. in this sense, i am strongly in favour of the review of legislation in order to the ensure highest investor protection standards and the need to address taxation of capital markets because it might represent an obstacle, despite the opportunities offered by a well-designed eu capital market. i would like to thank the rapporteur, and shadow rapporteurs, for their approach.
in writing. – i have voted for this resolution to improve access to capital markets through new sources of funding.
in writing. ‒ i support creating a genuine and truly european capital markets union and this document represents a good step in that direction. europe needs to find more means to ensure a stable and growing economy, with a particular european flavour to it, as the report duly notes. a capital markets union could have a very positive impact on cross-border finance, including on savings or financing, as well as the development of smes and joint ventures. still, it will need adequate studies and proper expertise for its implementation, and we need to ensure a lot more transparency and a level playing field of companies from different member states.
in writing. ‒ the financial trends of the past year have shown that investment in the real economy in europe has relatively declined over several decades, despite a large increase in the size of the european and global financial sector over the same period. in order to improve the efficiency of markets and ensure a fair, adequate and economically sound risk-return relationship in eu capital, a european capital market union is needed. such a union will provide better access for european businesses and smes to financing, increasing and diversifying the sources of funding and making the market more effective both within member states and cross-border. the final text, which i voted in favour of today, includes several of the s&d priorities to achieving our goal. mainly: using capital markets for financing long-term investment and the real economy; making the capital market union a deregulatory agenda for the financial markets; reviewing legislation to ensure highest investor protection standards and addressing taxation of capital markets. a harmonised, pro-european approach that takes into consideration the different economic and cultural composition of the national financial sectors, is a constructive way to address the financial difficulties we are facing today.
in writing. i voted in favour of the resolution on the creation of a capital markets union, considering that it is necessary to improve access to capital markets through new sources of financing. the rapporteur's concern is welcome, as he pointed out in the resolution adopted by the ep plenary that reducing the fragmentation of capital markets could lead to lower capital costs, while improving their distribution, and could thus support the development of enterprises, in particular smes, and job creation in the eu. the resolution stresses that improving financing conditions for businesses in europe must be based on strengthened economic and financial stability, which includes the implementation of reforms in all member states. it is also stated that imperfect capital markets have led to an erroneous assessment of risks and a disconnect between the earnings sought and the actual risks assumed, which has made the markets very unfair to entities such as smes.
in writing. ‒ terrorism, radicalisation, organised and cybercrime are the biggest threats to europe today, endangering citizens' lives by limiting security, fundamental freedoms and human rights. given that the post-cold war world is a globalised one, characterised by a high degree of interdependence, which makes it impossible to avoid affecting other states in one way or another, and also in the context of the current conflict in ukraine, the instability of the european union can be a real issue to alert eu member states to the prospect of strengthening security. i voted in favour of the motion for a resolution on the european agenda on security because i believe that the development of a roadmap in this area will exponentially increase operational cooperation on internal security and protect the fundamental rights and freedoms of european citizens, which cannot be infringed under any circumstances.
in writing. ‒ following the european commission’s communication on the european security agenda for 2015-2020, i support the key priorities formulated by the commission as fundamentals to strengthen member states’ cooperation in tackling security threats and increase the common efforts in the fight against terrorism, organised crime and cybercrime. i consider that, in view of the challenges the european union is currently facing, these are the most serious issues which require coordinated actions at union level in full respect of human rights and citizens’ rights. i strongly welcome the libe resolution to the plenary, which has adopted our s&d line, namely the full compliance with fundamental rights, more transparency, accountability and democratic control, better application and implementation of existing legal instruments, a more joined-up inter-agency and cross-sectoral approach, and a greater link between the internal and external dimensions of security. in line with the resolution, i call on the commission and on the council to establish a roadmap of the agenda’s implementation in which to comply with them.

in writing. ‒ threats to european security have recently diversified and multiplied, taking new forms such as hybrid warfare, asymmetrical conflicts and unconventional weapons. terrorist threats, cybercrime, social tensions and racial violence have also increased. these negative phenomena require a coordinated response from the european union to ensure the security of all member states by adopting common standards in this field. the european commission has identified three key responses to the challenges for 2015-2020: preventing terrorism and countering radicalisation, fighting organised crime and tackling cybercrime. the european parliament, in its turn, must provide solutions to these problems as the representative forum of european citizens. this can identify more nuanced remedies to security threats, such as decision-making transparency, democratic control, information sharing and the use of databases, eliminating the confusion between islam, terrorism and migrants, promoting religious tolerance, supporting the security industry. in this respect, i support the adoption of the resolution on the european agenda on security, which is a necessary document both for the debate in this area and for ensuring the real security of the member states.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the motion for a resolution on the situation in yemen. when it comes to human rights violations, violence and security limitations, it is welcome that the european union intervenes and reaffirms its firm commitment and determination to address the threat posed by extremist and terrorist groups, which in this case endanger the lives of yemeni citizens. the european union advocates the resolution of conflicts through dialogue and negotiation, rather than through acts of violence, abuse and the use of weapons. the current situation in yemen is all the more serious in view of the limited humanitarian and medical assistance that the population urgently needs. the denial of the right to liberty and health care is the worst abuse a citizen can suffer. the situation in yemen should continue to be monitored by the commission, the council and the parliament, as well as by all international bodies with the power to prevent and punish such abuses.
in writing. ‒ the current crisis in yemen is the result of the failure of successive governments to respond to the legitimate aspirations of the yemeni people for democracy, economic and social development, stability and security. all parties to the conflict must agree to a humanitarian pause, especially during the current ramadan, to allow aid to reach the people in need (13 million people in yemen face a food security crisis and over 9 million have little or no access to water). at the same time, this pause is necessary to be used as a first step towards a ceasefire that prepares the ground for a sustainable political solution. it is essential that all parties involved respect their obligations under international humanitarian and human rights law and allow unrestricted access to humanitarian workers so that immediate assistance can be provided to those in need. efforts must be made to resolve differences through dialogue, compromise and power-sharing leading to the formation of a government of national unity with the aim of restoring peace, avoiding economic and financial collapse and addressing the humanitarian crisis.

in writing. ‒ the european union's relationship with its eastern and southern neighbours is an essential component of the union's foreign and security policy. the european neighbourhood policy has been one of the tools for improving the eu's relations with its neighbours, but it has become insufficient in the context of developments in the targeted states. in this regard, the present report proposes a reshaping of the neighbourhood policy to take account of the differences in approach between the southern and eastern sides and to place greater emphasis on supporting democracy, the rule of law, good governance, institutional capacity, ethnic and religious tolerance, strengthening civil society, security cooperation, supporting regional integration, and resolving internal or frozen conflicts. at the same time, countries that so wish can conclude association agreements with the european union and should be able to become candidates for accession to the union provided they fulfil the convergence conditions. realising the full potential of the neighbourhood policy depends, however, on how we succeed in promoting european democratic values in these countries. i believe that this report is a step forward in this direction and deserves to be adopted by the european parliament.

in writing. ‒ the current report intends to set parliament’s position on copyrights, in view of the upcoming commission proposal on the copyright reform, due to be released in the autumn. the text represents several key elements. mainly: 1) restating the principle of territoriality; 2) safeguarding works that are in the public domain, and any digitisation of these works; 3) applying minimum standards across the exceptions and limitations; 4) providing accessibility of exceptions and limitations to people with disabilities; 5) revising the liability of intermediaries; 6) asking for more transparency regarding the private copying levies; 7) calling for a full scientific evaluation by the ipr observatory on national legislations that introduced ancillary rights. the only controversial element in the report was a restriction on the freedom of panorama. upon a mutual agreement between all political groups, the paragraph was deleted from the report and is not mentioned in the voted text. this report provides a balance between ensuring the rights of authors and performers, on the one hand, and access to culture and information on the other. it ensures a good climate for the creative sector and the preservation of the european cultural diversity, therefore i voted in favour of it.
in writing. i voted for the report on the harmonisation of certain aspects of copyright and related rights in the information society because the situation of many industries in this area is quite complicated. welcomes the rapporteur's assessment of the commission's commitment to further develop the eu digital agenda, including the objective of modernising copyright rules. the report also acknowledges the need to review directive 2001/29/ec in order to ensure adequate remuneration of authors, performers and other rightholders and adequate protection of those rights, and to achieve an appropriate balance in the european cultural economy between all stakeholders, namely smes, consumers, users, creators and rightholders, in a digital age that involves a constantly changing and evolving technological environment and generates changes in user behaviour, as well as opportunities and challenges. i have read carefully the views that have been submitted to me in relation to this report and i support the urgent need to review directive 2001/29/ec, given the complexity of the subject.

in writing. ‒ the european endowment for democracy has demonstrated in the current challenging international context that it is successfully fulfilling its objective of promoting and encouraging democratisation and genuine and sustainable democracy in countries in political transition and in societies struggling for democratisation. the edf has made considerable efforts to ensure and accelerate the initiation of a democratic process, bringing justice closer to the citizen. despite its short operating period and limited funds, as well as the inherent problems in assessing the impact of democracy support actions, the edf has followed parliament's recommendations and added value to the current eu support for democracy, helping to reduce political risks in the eu. i voted in favour of the report on the eu's new approach to human rights and democracy assessing the activities of the european endowment for democracy (edf) since its inception and i welcome the work undertaken by this vital eu body.
in writing. ‒ the edf's commitment to freedom of expression and association, freedom of the press, the creation and strengthening of the rule of law, the fight against corruption, social and political pluralism, and to supporting the development of democratic regimes in the eu's eastern and southern neighbourhoods is commendable, with 158 initiatives funded totalling over eur 4.5 million in the eu's southern neighbourhood and over eur 4.4 million in the eastern neighbourhood. in order to sustain and develop the edf's effectiveness, it is essential to ensure long-term, sufficient, stable, transparent and predictable funding. the edf should be actively involved in countries where external support to civil society is severely hampered or where state funding is discriminatory and granted exclusively to certain civil organisations or societies. member states should continue to provide financial assistance to russian civil society and media through the edf, given that recent events such as restrictions on civil society organisations, the crackdown on political opposition and aggressive disinformation campaigns by state-controlled media appear to serve the purpose of creating a highly nationalist political climate marked by anti-democratic rhetoric, repression and hate speech.
in writing. ‒ the european endowment for democracy has shown, after two years’ existence, that it has fulfilled the purpose for which it was created: the promotion of european values of freedom and democracy has achieved very good results. the eed remains an independent private-law foundation that delivers through fast, flexible, bottom up and demand-driven funding. it provides these funds directly to beneficiaries in a financially efficient manner that complements other eu means, doing so with a minimal administrative burden and simple procedures. it is vital, in order to sustain and further develop the effectiveness of the eed, to ensure long-term, sufficient, stable, transparent and predictable funding. i support stronger emphasis on groups that suffer from social exclusion or political marginalisation by supporting, among others, groups such as women’s movements, lgbti human rights activists, emerging political movements, trade unions, bloggers and new media activists.

in writing. ‒ the european union is a champion of democracy, the rule of law and respect for fundamental rights and freedoms in the world. the european endowment for democracy was set up to support these rights in the countries of the eastern or southern neighbourhood, especially where they are threatened by authoritarian systems, economic difficulties, security threats or censorship. with this flexible instrument, the union has been able to support laudable initiatives in favour of freedom of expression and association, freedom of the press, the creation and strengthening of the rule of law, the fight against corruption, and social and political pluralism. by involving more member states, and even external partners, a significant number of initiatives have been funded, but involving more resources and more countries would create even better conditions for supporting the democratisation process in the eu's neighbourhood. the use of new technologies guarantees a greater penetration force of the programme, allowing the support of activists for democracy and freedom of expression. of course, there are many other areas where the fund can help, such as the protection of minorities, the promotion of women, the prevention of social exclusion and support for media activists. however, the results achieved so far are remarkable, which justifies the adoption of this resolution.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the motion for a resolution on the situation in burundi. when it comes to human rights violations, violence and security limitations, it is welcome that the european union intervenes and reaffirms its firm commitment and determination to address the threat posed by extremist and terrorist groups, which in this case endanger the lives of burundian citizens. the european union advocates the resolution of conflicts through dialogue and negotiation, rather than through acts of violence, abuse and the use of weapons. the current situation in burundi is all the more serious in view of the limited humanitarian and medical aid that the population urgently needs. the denial of the right to liberty and health care is the worst abuse a citizen can suffer. the situation in burundi should continue to be monitored by the commission, the council and the parliament, as well as by all international bodies with the power to prevent and punish such abuses.
in writing. ‒ the political impasse in burundi and the deterioration of the security and economic situation have serious consequences for the population and pose risks for the region as a whole, with burundi facing its worst crisis since the 12-year-old ethnic civil war. only through dialogue and consensus, with the involvement of the government of burundi, the opposition and civil society and in accordance with the arusha agreement and the burundian constitution, can a lasting political solution be found in the interests of security and democracy for the burundian people. burundi has also signed and ratified the international covenant on civil and political rights and the african charter on human and peoples' rights and is therefore obliged to respect universal human rights, including freedom of expression. the burundian government must allow for real and open debate without fear of intimidation and refrain from abusing the judicial system to exclude political rivals. the commission has a duty to urgently re-evaluate eu aid with a view to redirecting it, increasing financial support to civil society and focusing on humanitarian aid.

rapporteur.– mr president, please allow me first to thank my colleagues, the shadow rapporteurs, for their work on this file, and the commission and the council for their cooperation. without all the good work and support received, we would not have reached an agreement in june under the latvian presidency, bringing the eu basic regulation into line with the world trade organisation (wto) ruling. in 2009, within the basic regulation, the eu opted for a ban in trade in seal products, with two main exceptions: products from hunts conducted by inuit and other indigenous communities (the ic exception) and products from hunts conducted for the sole purpose of the sustainable management of marine resources on a small scale and non-profit basis (the mrm exception). the aim of this regulation is to ensure that products derived from seals hunted for commercial purposes are no longer found on the eu market. the seal regulation and its implementing act were challenged by canada and norway in the wto. the final rulings of the wto panel and the wto appellate body were adopted on 18 june 2014 by the wto dispute settlement body on 18 june 2014, disapproving of one of the two exceptions, namely the mrm exception. canada and the european union had agreed that the reasonable period of time to implement the recommendations and rulings should be 16 months from the date of adoption. that period expires on 18 october 2015. the european commission did not adopt its proposal for amending the current regulation on trade in seal products until 6 february 2015, bringing the current legislation into line with the wto rulings by renouncing the mrm exception and keeping the reinforced inuit exception. although i very much appreciate that not all meps and member states agree with the deletion of the mrm exception, i am very pleased to announce that the final agreement reached is in line with the wto rulings. as regards the inuit exception, the consolidated text encompasses a new set of criteria under which seal products resulting from hunts conducted by inuit and other indigenous communities could be placed on the market – a clear reference to the needs of such communities to provide food and income to support their life and a sustainable livelihood. we amended the commission’s proposal, taking into consideration in particular the right to self-determination of the inuit and other indigenous communities. the proposal was amended so as to reiterate that seal hunting is an integral part of the culture and identity of the inuit communities, making a major contribution to their subsistence, providing food and income to support their families and small communities, and preserving and continuing the traditional existence of the community and the cultural heritage of bartering. in the report i have proposed a new article, namely 5a, referring to the need for citizens to be properly informed about seal products placed on the eu market which originate in inuit and other indigenous communities, and that those seal products are lawful in origin. last, but not least, as regards article 7 on reporting, the agreed text asks the commission to report by the end of 2019 on the implementation of the new rules, paying particular attention to the impact of those rules on the inuit community. i look forward to hearing what the commission, the council and, of course, my colleagues have to say.
madam president, considering the final rulings in the dispute settlement body of the world trade organisation on 18 june 2014 defining the inuit and mrm exceptions as an arbitrary and unjustifiable discrimination, we have no choice but to adopt an amendment to the current regulation on trade in seal products in order to bring the eu regulation into compliance with the world trade organisation rules. as stated by the world trade organisation, the eu did not address animal welfare in inuit hunts given that the overall objective of the regulation was based on animal welfare concerns, and the ambiguity of some of its conditions could lead to the use of the exception for hunts in ways which should in reality be characterised as primarily undertaken for commercial purposes. i therefore strongly agree on the links made in the proposal between the use of the exception and respect for animal welfare. this provides for a mechanism that could help prevent its misuse.
member of the commission.– madam president, thank you to all those who have participated in this debate. let me once again thank you for being engaged in this process so constructively, despite the sensitivities surrounding the subject, which have been well reflected in most of the points which you raised. the updated regulation aims at ensuring that the fundamental economic and social interests of those communities traditionally engaged in the hunting of seals will not be affected adversely. the hunt, as has been explained, is an integral part of their culture and identity and represents a source of income and, as has already been highlighted by most of the speakers, contributes to their subsistence as well. indeed, the marine resource management exception is not part of the outcome, as it clearly is incompatible with the wto. however, rest assured that we have thoroughly examined each and every proposal that we have received but found no possibility for keeping the exception without running a great risk of wto sanctions because of continued non-compliance. the revised legislation will enable the eu to comply with the wto ruling and provide a non-discriminatory legal framework in line with public moral concerns. so thank you for giving the proposed regulation your support.
rapporteur.– madam president, i can understand that the agreement reached does not completely satisfy some of the nordic and baltic countries, but i do appreciate that they also understand that this agreement is more valuable and should be adopted, especially as we succeeded in having a new set of criteria for the inuit exception and because of the agreed text on article 7 on reporting. i agree with mr bendtsen’s remarks and i truly believe, after the meetings i had with the representatives of the greenland and danish parliament, with the inuit community, different ngos and with the commission itself, that the hunt conducted by inuits and other indigenous communities does not harm or threaten to harm the habitat and health of the seal populations, and there is no chance that it is made primarily for commercial purposes. the inuits hunt because this is their way of supporting their family and their small communities. their livelihood needs are very simple and modest. they have been doing it for hundreds of years as part of their tradition and cultural heritage and they have respect for animal welfare. we have a very fast-track calendar, and without good cooperation we could not have reached an agreement and met the deadlines in order to give the commission time to prepare all the necessary subsequent acts by the october deadline. thank you very much once again. i look forward to the vote tomorrow.

first vice-president of the commission. – madam president, of course the simplification of the common agricultural policy is a way to reduce the number of controls on the spot. simpler rules mean that it is going to be easier to implement them, easier for farmers to work with them and easier for authorities to check up on them. as some of you have said, phil hogan has already started with this simplification exercise and it is well advanced. we have received many contributions from all stakeholders. some changes have already been implemented and the commission will present more proposals in the coming months. however, we do not have to wait for new rules to impact on the number of controls farmers face. the current legislation allows member states with reliable management and control systems to reduce the level of the spot checks. some member states have expressed interest in taking advantage of this possibility. the commission services are working closely with them to ensure all conditions for this reduction are met. of course we want simple rules and better application, but we also have a great responsibility in ensuring that taxpayers’ money is not misappropriated and does not end up where it should not. member states are also encouraged, in the current legislation, to organise their controls in a way that reduces the burden for farmers. let us not forget either that only 5% of farmers are subject to on-the-spot checks for compliance with cap rules. most of the controls they are faced with result from national laws and from cross-compliance requirements, which do not originate from cap legislation. obviously, to most farmers it does not make any difference whether a rule comes from brussels or from their own country: they are faced with rules and they want fewer of them. they are absolutely right. they should be farming and not involved in constant bureaucracy. but we believe that member states could, in so far as possible, try to group their own controls with those resulting from cap obligations, and perhaps they could also learn more from each other than they do today. as i said, controls are, and will remain, necessary. if the eu legislator or the member states has specified a conditional requirement to be respected before aid can be paid, then there needs to be a check that this condition or requirement has been met. the more numerous or complex the requirements, the more numerous or complex the controls. taxpayers have the right to know whether subsidies from the eu budget are being spent according to the rules, and we will therefore not accept any proposal that might compromise the sound financial management of the eu budget. finally, we should ask ourselves whether an error rate of 2% is, per se, the appropriate benchmark for a complex policy such as the cap and, more concretely, rural development. in that context, we should also raise the issue of the acceptable relation between the cost and the benefits of controls. any reflection that does not attempt to tackle this question would really be a missed opportunity. the common agricultural policy is, and will remain, a cornerstone of eu policies. it is in our common interest that this policy be as effective as possible and that it retain the support of farmers and citizens. taxpayers will want to be sure that their money is well spent. i would like to thank mr sarvamaa very much for his report, which will be added to the contributions to the ongoing debate about simplification of the cap.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the draft report on the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council amending regulation (ec) no 1007/2009 on trade in seal products, as it seeks better regulation in this sector. i believe that seal hunting contributes greatly to the subsistence of indigenous communities, as it is one of the few sources of food to which they have access. the report proposal is beneficial to these communities, as it regulates, among other things, the cases in which the european commission may intervene to adopt delegated acts to limit the quantity of products obtained from this hunting that can be placed on the market.
in writing. ‒ considering the final rulings of the dispute settlement body of the wto on 18 june 2014, defining the inuit and mrm exceptions as ‘arbitrary and unjustifiable discrimination’, we have no choice but to adopt an amendment to the current regulation on trade in seal products, in order to bring the eu regulation into compliance with wto rules. as stated by the wto, the eu did not address animal welfare in inuit hunts, given that the overall objective of our regulation was based on animal welfare concerns, and the ambiguity of some of its conditions could lead to a use of the exception for hunts that should in reality be characterised as primarily undertaken for commercial purposes. i therefore strongly agree with the links made in the proposal between use of the exception and respect for animal welfare and it provides for a mechanism that would help prevent its misuse. i support the agreement reached that makes it obligatory on the commission to inform public and private authorities of the impact of this regulation, namely the fact that seal products derived from inuit hunts can be legally sold.
in writing. ‒ i voted for this report that will instate a prohibition on placing seal products on the market.
in writing. ‒ around one third of the world trade in seal products either passes through or ends up on the eu market. to answer animal welfare concerns, the eu banned trade in seal products in 2009. however, it allowed two exceptions for seal products from hunting by inuit and other indigenous communities, and for small-scale hunts to ensure the ‘sustainable management of marine resources’ (mrm exception). in june 2014, a wto ruling challenged these exceptions, arguing that they could have discriminatory effects. as a reaction to that, the commission tabled a proposed update of the eu rules which align them with the wto ruling by renouncing the mrm exception and clarifying the inuit one. the current reports backs the commission report and provides further improvements, asking the commission: 1) to report on the impacts of this regulation, and to assess deletion of the mrm-exception, and 2) to inform the public of the impacts of this regulation, namely the fact that seal products derived from inuit hunts can legally be sold. adoption of this report sets a stronger eu ban on the trade in seal products and helps to ensure fewer seals are hunted for their fur.
in writing. ‒ seal hunting is an integral part of inuit culture. it provides a source of livelihood that fully corresponds to the traditional lifestyle of the community, preserving its identity and thus guaranteeing its perpetuity. i therefore welcome the commission's decision to maintain the ic exception in the context of the amendment of regulation no 1007/2009 on trade in seal products, but to strengthen it by imposing strict conditions. furthermore, i agree with the removal of the exception on products from fishing for the sustainable management of marine resources, as it risks being interpreted broadly and thus leading to abuses. the report is particularly innovative in proposing that consumers be properly informed about the origin of seal products from indigenous communities. furthermore, the report asks the commission to conduct an impact study of the new regulation on the inuit community by the end of 2019. convinced that such strict but highly useful measures would have a positive effect on the inuit community, while ensuring animal welfare, i voted in favour of the report on trade in seal products.
in writing. ‒ we all know that animal cloning is a hazard for animal welfare. it leads to placental and foetal abnormalities resulting in poor welfare for offspring and dams used for cloning, and often substantial pain for the latter. cloning treats animals as commodities, not as sentient beings, and is associated with great animal suffering at all stages of the process. the negative effects of cloning, inter alia on animal welfare and on food security, greatly outweigh any possible positive effects: thus, the use of descendants of clones is simply not acceptable. therefore, i strongly support the prohibition of cloning of animals in the eu and i believe that the use of cloning and the placing on the market of the corresponding products should be prohibited until further scientific progress is made.

in writing. ‒ the european convention on human rights was, until the treaty of lisbon, the legal basis for respect for human rights in the european union, but since the entry into force of this treaty, the charter of fundamental rights has been given the same value as the other treaties, which means that states are obliged to give priority to respect for human rights. i believe that this report on the situation of fundamental rights in the european union is a way for the european union to become even more involved in the internal affairs of states, since i believe that each state is capable of defending human rights within its own borders. moreover, this report makes the border between the european union and the council of europe, the specialised human rights organisation, increasingly blurred. in my view, the european union should focus more on other areas, such as economic stability, which is often the cause of many violations of fundamental rights. moreover, it should pay close attention to the refugee crisis, which could lead to increased violations of fundamental rights. i therefore voted against the report on the situation of fundamental rights in the eu.
in writing. ‒ the practice of public hearings of commissioners-designate is a very useful exercise for potential members of the european commission, but especially for the interested public. even though these public hearings are not provided for in the treaty, they were conducted in a democratic and efficient manner. these have developed over the last 20 years at the insistence of the european parliament, which has asked candidate european commissioners to present their agendas to the commission and the committees corresponding to their portfolio before parliament gives its vote of confidence to the commission. in this context, although the opinions of the committees on individual commissioners have no legal significance, they are taken into account, so that when they have issued negative opinions, they have had the effect of changing the composition of the commission or redistributing portfolios. i voted in favour of the report on the procedures and practices relating to the hearing of commissioners, as the results have shown that this process reflects the political balance at commission level. moreover, the media showed a strong interest, not only through traditional channels but also through social media platforms, which resulted in hundreds of thousands of european citizens being informed about eu-level decision-making processes.
in writing. ‒ i welcome this report, which clarifies the procedures and practices for future commissioner hearings. in particular, i agree on the idea that a deadline should be fixed for member states to put forward candidates and allow time for the allocation of portfolios and hearings; that each member state should put forward a female candidate and male candidate on equal footing for consideration; that each questionnaire will have the right to an immediate follow-up question; that the legal affairs committee needs to clarify the rules about how to manage commission's declaration of interest.
in writing. ‒ i have voted for this report that will better regulate the commissioner hearings, a practice developed over the past 20 years at the insistence of the european parliament.
in writing. ‒ the public hearings of prospective members of the european commission is a democratic exercise which provides the parliament and the public an opportunity to discover the personalities, the approach and the priorities of each candidate. the process produces political clarifications and commitments, adjustments to portfolios, and further clarity on the relationships between the vice—presidents and other commissioners. nevertheless, there is always room for improvement, and few propositions are outlined by the current report. for example, the report asks for a fixed deadline for member states to put forward candidates and allow time for the allocation of portfolios and hearings. it also asks the ep legal affairs committee to clarify the rules on how to manage designate commissioners’ declaration of interest and scope of application, to also include cover financial interests of family members. lastly, a recommendation which i particularly support, is the need to put forward at least two candidates, a male and a female, on an equal footing for consideration by the president-elect. drawing the lessons of this period, i welcome this report that clarifies the procedures and practices for future commissioner hearings, while providing inputs on how to improve the process.
some information and communications technologies produced in europe are sold and may be used in third countries by persons who are engaged in the mass collection of personal data for the purpose of unlawfully locating and eavesdropping on persons. it is very serious what is happening and that is why we must prohibit european companies from selling such technologies to people who are using them precisely to plan attacks against us. in this context, i ask the european commission to remove such companies from public tenders and also, when it comes to requests for aid to third countries, not to grant aid to those countries where human rights are trampled on and where there are groups of people or individuals who use technologies bought from us precisely for the destruction, location and identification of people and the destruction, i repeat, of democracy.
in writing. ‒ the internet has become a public space and also a developed single market, based on the free flow of information and access to information technology. in the 21st century, the internet is a revolution in the possibilities it offers for exchanging data, information or knowledge of any kind. at the same time, human rights and fundamental freedoms are universal and must be defended worldwide, regardless of the form in which they are expressed. the commission should be able to assess the compatibility of the measures with the internal market in accordance with article 108 (3) tfeu. the report also calls for clauses to be included in all agreements with third countries explicitly referring to the promotion, safeguarding and respect of digital freedom, uncensored and unrestricted access to the internet, the right to life and data protection. i voted in favour of the report because, in addition to the above, it draws attention to the development of icts in conflict zones for better security and respect for human rights.
in writing. ‒ given that technological systems can be misused as tools for human rights violations through censorship, surveillance, unauthorised access to devices, jamming, interception, tracking and tracing of information and people, it is important to implement conditions, benchmarks and reporting procedures to ensure that eu financial and technical support for the development of new technologies in third countries is not used in a way that violates human rights. the commission has a duty to pay particular attention to human rights issues in procurement processes for technological equipment, especially in countries with unsafe practices in this area.
in writing. ‒ if conducted outside an adequate legal framework surveillance of communications, as such, interferes with the rights to privacy and expression. security measures, including counter-terrorism measures, cannot be used as pretext for violations of the right of the privacy and for clamping down on the legitimate activities of human rights defenders, journalists and political activists. on the contrary, respect for fundamental rights is an essential element in successful counter-terrorism policies, including the use of digital surveillance technologies.
in writing. ‒ i have voted for this report that will assess human rights impact and will make recommendations for adjustments that will increase the protection of human rights.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report because i believe that fundamental human rights and freedoms are universal and must be defended worldwide, and in this respect the eu can and must lead by example. as the document adopted today states, technological developments and internet access have become indispensable to the lives of as many people as possible, and their use in an ethical manner, with full respect for the rights of those who access them, is essential for the eu, but also for third countries with which the eu has bilateral relations. there is a well-founded fear that insufficient regulation of the use of new communications technologies may, in some states, lead to human rights violations such as surveillance, interference or interception of citizens without a warrant from an independent judge. it is one of the reasons why i voted today in favour of this report, which condemns the misuse of technology and which tilts the balance towards the need to respect human freedoms and rights.
in writing. ‒ technology, particularly the new media, has two coins. it can be used as a tool for exercising the freedom of expression. however, it can also be used for violating human rights, particularly with regards to privacy and surveillance. with this current report, the parliament aims to address the use of technology in human rights violations. the position expressed in this report underlines that the surveillance of communications, if conducted outside an adequate legal framework, interferes with the rights to privacy and expression. the report requests coherence between the eu’s external actions and internal policies related to icts, in order to promote democratic oversight of security and intelligence services, and ensure european technologies do not contribute to human right violations in third countries. equally important, the report also notes the fact that security measures are increasingly used as pretext for violating the right to privacy and cracking on legitimate activities of human rights defenders, journalists and political activists. i strongly believe that technology should serve the voice of the people, not act against them. as a prominent human rights defender the eu has the responsibility to ensure our technologies protect and promote human rights, not the other way around, particularly in third countries.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report in support of one of the most necessary common policies of the european union, namely the common agricultural policy. as the common agricultural policy has become an extremely complex and bureaucratic instrument in recent years as a result of several reforms, there has been a series of debates in which it has been shown that european farmers are facing difficulties and the number of errors on the ground has increased. in order to respond to these concerns and to continue to meet the objectives originally set, the report voted on today is beneficial. the document proposes to reduce the administrative burden and to ensure a supplementary, qualitative and well-structured financial control, instead of multiplying the number of checks. simplification and rationalisation of the cap are key to involving as many people as possible in agriculture, to keeping them and to professionalising them, with the ultimate aim of ensuring quality and affordable agricultural products at member state level.
mr president, despite the lack of clear and uniform criteria to define ‘family business’ across europe, and their vast heterogeneity in terms of incorporation form and size, there are various common traits which set them apart, such as a flexible decision-making process, a high degree of creativity and innovation, a longer-term view on investment, and high involvement and responsibility towards their business, customers, employees and their local community. it is because of such assets that they play a pivotal role in the regional and national economies and account for more than half of jobs in the private sector in europe. however, various studies conducted recently show that they also face similar difficulties in terms of access to finance, taxation, a stifling regulatory framework, and the challenge of attracting the right people with the right skills. coming from a region whose economy is overwhelmingly based on family companies i can only salute the drafting of this report and stress the importance for the european union of taking supportive measures in their regard.
in writing. ‒ the financial and economic crisis has had significant consequences. there are still some 25 million unemployed across the european union, and the number of young unemployed under 25 is over 5 million. in this context, promoting jobs, growth and investment is the number one priority of the political guidelines for the current european commission, as presented at the beginning of its mandate in the summer of 2014. in this context, family businesses can play a decisive role in overcoming the financial and economic crisis and in revitalizing the economy, and the conclusions reached by the european commission's expert group in its 2009 report highlighted that over 60% of eu businesses are family businesses, providing around 40-50% of private sector jobs. i voted in favour of the report on family businesses in europe because they have a longer-term vision than those not run by their owners, while also ensuring that future generations also achieve good economic performance.
in writing. ‒ family businesses make a key contribution to the success of vocational training reforms and to the growth of apprenticeships. in this context, i believe that, in the long term, functional vocational training systems can help to combat skills shortages and youth unemployment, and i believe that member states and the commission should promote the exchange of good practice on how vocational training systems can provide family businesses with the best environment for investing in apprentices.
in writing. ‒ family businesses play a significant role for the economic growth and social development, by decreasing the unemployment rate, and for very much needed investments in human capital. thanks to their transnational dimension and their multi-generational character, they reinforce the stability of the economy. and since not all 28 eu member states have specific structures to serve their needs, i welcome the initiative to better adjust eu legislation to the reality, assisting the family businesses to benefit from funding programmes and from reduction in red tape (excessive regulation). we indeed require more data, facts and figures from the member states to better understand their challenges. in respect to the importance of this group of entrepreneurs, we need to provide support where it is needed, by determining if the proposed changes to eu law have effects on family businesses and, if so, to identify them.
in writing. ‒ more than 60% of all enterprises in the european union are family-run, and they account for about 40-50% of jobs in the private sector. i have voted for this report that will conduct an impact assessment on family businesses that play such an important role in our economy.
in writing. ‒ i supported this report because i believe that family businesses play a significant role in driving the european union's economy. a number of reports have shown that small family businesses have contributed to the recovery of the european economy and have played an important role in promoting economic growth and social development, reducing unemployment, especially among young people, and investing in human capital. today's report presents the problems and difficulties specific to these small firms, referring in particular to the inequalities between them, and i believe that the problem exists in all european states, including romania. in this respect, as the report proposes, member states and regional and local authorities should stimulate and strengthen entrepreneurship, simplify and de-bureaucratize the work of european businesses, provide tax incentives for businesses and other compensation to help women and men working as employees, as self-employed workers or as managers of family businesses to reconcile family life with professional life, creating an environment conducive to economic performance.
in writing. ‒ family run businesses provide a significant financial contribution to the eu’s economy. it is estimated that over 60% of all enterprises in the eu are family-run, accounting for about 40-50% of jobs in the private sector. the current report aims to draw attention to this important group of entrepreneurs by exploring ways to foster their economic contribution while addressing some of the challenges this group is facing. one of the main challenges the report presents is the lack of a formal definition to ‘family business’. with over 90 definitions used by the different member states, some family businesses find themselves struggling with red tape and restrictions on access to funding. moreover, in the absence of data, facts and figures on the activity of family businesses in the different member states we are unable to design policies that could better assess the challenges family businesses are facing, or exchange best case practices. by aiming to tackle these issues, this report sets in place the right conditions for the succession of family business in europe. its adoption in plenary demonstrate the parliament's commitment and support to this important business community.
in writing. ‒ in the context of a slow recovery of the european labour market after a long economic and social crisis, i believe that the role of the european union is to actively support and facilitate the creation and development of family businesses. family businesses account for 85% of all european enterprises, providing 60% of private sector jobs. moreover, as this report shows, they contribute substantially to the sustainable development of the european economy and to reducing unemployment, especially among young people. given the importance of these family businesses, i believe it is more than necessary for the european union to find sustainable solutions to the administrative, financial and fiscal obstacles faced by family businesses. in my view, the commission should call on the member states to review their tax policy, given that inheritance and gift taxes are often far too high, often leading to the disappearance of family businesses. the right to property, enshrined in the eu charter of fundamental rights, must be fully protected. for these reasons, i voted in favour of the report on family businesses in europe.
in writing. ‒ family businesses play a very important role in the european economy, but unfortunately, political actors pay them little attention. over 60% of enterprises in the european union are family businesses, providing around 40-50% of private sector jobs. although the european commission established a definition of small and medium-sized enterprises (smes) in 2003, the same cannot be said for family businesses. in 2009, a group of experts from the european commission tried to follow this example and establish a definition that is not legally binding and does not apply in some member states. therefore, it is not possible to collect comparable data from eu member states to draw attention to the situation, needs and outstanding economic performance of family businesses. the european parliament resolution draws attention to the need for a european definition and proposes, inter alia, the creation of a single window for enterprises, which would serve as a european contact point for family enterprises and family business interest groups and provide assistance on specific issues, in particular on european legislation and access to eu funding.
