in writing. ‒ our cultural heritage represents a rich and diverse mosaic of our inheritance from previous generations and our legacy for those to come. it is an important resource for economic growth, employment and social cohesion, offering the potential to revitalise urban and rural areas and promote sustainable tourism. to better preserve, foster and realise the potential of our european heritage, we need an integrated and coordinated approach to culture heritage based on improved coordination and communication between different policy areas, better access to information and increased funding opportunities through eu programmes (i:e. erasmus, european capitals of culture). the report also recommends designating 2018 as the european year on culture heritage. while i support this initiative, i also believe we must see cultural heritage in a broader context, particularly with regards to tourism. as the two themes go hand-in-hand a european year on cultural heritage and tourism will surely raise awareness to europe’s touristic, historical and cultural diversity. nonetheless, i support the elements in this report and view its adoption as a way forward in the promotion of an integrated policy, one that not only preserves our heritage but also realizes its potential as a source of sustainable jobs and growth.
in writing. ‒ europe's cultural heritage is our common heritage, the legacy that previous generations of europeans have left us and that we, in turn, will leave to future generations. it is a valuable resource for economic growth and job creation and a factor of social cohesion. our cultural heritage and the way we preserve it therefore determine europe's place in the world and the attraction that this continent has for those who live, reside or travel here. cultural heritage may face more challenges than other sectors to which more importance is attached. although there are many opportunities for european funding for these sectors, information is often not always passed on to beneficiaries. in this context, this report proposes the creation of an eu-wide cultural heritage portal that would collect information from all eu funding programmes. furthermore, this report supports the digitisation of cultural heritage as a way to protect our past and as a tool that can offer many opportunities for research and, by implication, economic development. i therefore voted in favour of the report 'on an integrated approach to european cultural heritage'.
in writing. ‒ in july 2014, the european commission presented a communication entitled 'on an integrated approach to european cultural heritage'. this document presents the union's approach to heritage in different policy areas and outlines the tools available at eu level that complement national and regional programmes to help protect and enhance the intrinsic and social value of europe's cultural heritage. the aim of the communication is to help member states and stakeholders make the most of the considerable support available under eu instruments and to move towards a more integrated approach at national and eu level, ultimately turning europe into a laboratory for heritage-based innovation. the european parliament resolution underlines the need for an integrated approach to european cultural heritage, which will lead to the enhancement and promotion of this heritage, and proposes, inter alia, the creation of a single european portal to include information from all eu programmes for the financing of european cultural heritage. i voted in favour of this resolution.
in writing. i come from transylvania, a region that boasts a rich cultural heritage that fully reflects the multiculturalism of life here and that we have a duty to protect. this is just one of the reasons why i welcome the approach of my colleague, mr mircea diaconu, in his report on european cultural heritage. we voted for the report on an integrated approach to cultural heritage, which is comprehensive and inclusive. i appreciate that the report also highlights the importance of the sme sector in this area.
mr president, right2water is the first citizens' initiative to have gathered almost two million signatures from european citizens. i am very pleased that it has also succeeded in passing the legislative conditions imposed by the treaty. what do people ask of us? the people who voted for us want to be heard, it's natural to do that and to want that and to demand the right to clean water. i therefore ask the european commission to respect the wishes of almost two million people and to come up with a draft directive recognising the human right to water and fully integrating universal access to water and sanitation into union policies. it should also be remembered that member states have very important obligations themselves: they must require water suppliers to indicate the physico-chemical characteristics of the water on water bills, to approve urban planning plans that have been drawn up in relation to the water resources of the places concerned and also to develop immediate actions for the sanitation of toxic substances in drinking water and their removal.
in writing. ‒ currently, 748 million people lack sustainable access to safe drinking water and one third of the world's population lacks access to basic sanitation. this is regrettable and illustrates the polarity between the regions. drinking water must be made available to all european citizens. water and its treatment must be a priority for the eu. i voted in favour of the report entitled 'monitoring the european citizens' initiative right2water' because access to water must be a fundamental human right and the eu institutions and member states must take all necessary measures to ensure that all citizens have access to water and sanitation services.
in writing. ‒ i believe that member states and local and regional authorities must move towards a genuine social agreement on water, with the aim of guaranteeing the availability, stability and safe management of the resource, in particular by adopting policies such as the establishment of water solidarity funds and other social action mechanisms, to support people who cannot afford access to water supply and sanitation services, so as to meet the requirements of security of supply and not to jeopardise the human right to water. i believe that all member states must introduce social action mechanisms, such as those already in place in some countries of the union, to ensure the supply of drinking water to citizens who are facing real difficulties.
in writing. ‒ it is highly disappointing that the response given by the commission is insufficient, does not address in a proper manner the issues raised by the european citizens initiative organisers and does not present fresh ideas and measures that may help to achieve the goals. i therefore welcome the fact that the report addresses in detail the demands presented by the organisers of the eci right2water. in particular, i agree on the idea that the european commission should propose legislation implementing the human right to water and sanitation as recognised by the united nations. water is a basic human right and should be accessible and affordable to all. i believe that eu should remain neutral in relation to national decisions governing the ownership regime of water undertakings and thus by no means to promote their privatisation. we must push for a full integration of universal access to water and sanitation in the eu development policies.
in writing. ‒ i have voted for this report, which has as its main objectives to ensure that all citizens enjoy the right to water and sanitation and to make sure that water supply and water resources will not be subject to internal market rules.
in writing. ‒ clean water is one of the most basic factors that contribute to our way of living. therefore it is not surprising that the european citizen’s initiative (eci) right2water received over 1.6 million verified signatures, making it the first successful eci. what is surprising, however, is the commission’s response to the right2water eci. although the commission made few important statements following the adoption of right2water, like recognizing that water is not a commercial product, the commission failed to address the demands made by the signatories of the eci and commit to legislation which would recognise the right to water as a human right. acting this way, the commission undermined not only the right to water, but the eci mechanism as a whole. on this background, the current report addresses in more details the demands presented by the organizers of right2water. mainly it calls on the commission to propose legislation that will recognize the right to water and sanitation as a human right. i believe water must be made accessible and affordable to all. the current report backs this notion and brings back to the discussion on the right2water. my hope is that the commission will not fail us the second time around.
in writing. ‒ the citizens' initiative 'right to water' is the first successful example of this democratic mechanism. the aim of this initiative is to ensure that european union governments provide all its citizens with safe drinking water and adequate sanitation and that these services are not subject to common market rules. access to water should, in my view, be a constitutional right guaranteed to everyone; therefore, water and sanitation should be excluded from any trade agreements the european union is considering. water is a cause of inequality and social exclusion, it is a right closely linked to the right to the highest standard of physical and mental health, as well as to the right to life and human dignity. for example, in romania, at the end of 2013, 1,3% of urban and 28,3% of rural localities in romania did not have water distribution networks. in these circumstances, i believe that viable and rapid solutions are needed to ensure this right for citizens, both romanian and european, and therefore i voted in favour of the citizens' initiative 'right to water'.
in writing. i voted for the report on the actions taken as a result of the european citizens' initiative (ice) right to water - right2water - even though there are many statements, findings and proposals in it with which i do not agree. i voted for this report for two reasons. first, the eci is a very valuable instrument of participatory democracy that can have a significant impact on bringing eu citizens closer to the european institutions and increasing their trust in legislative procedures. 1.9 million eu citizens have expressed their support for the right2water initiative, and the voice of these citizens is forcing us to respond in concrete ways. secondly, the un recognises the right of every citizen to water and sanitation, and the eu must be at the forefront of this global movement. it seems paradoxical to me that in the eu of the 21st century, there are over a million citizens who do not have access to water and almost 10 million europeans who do not have access to sanitation. i voted first on the alternative motion by the ppe and the ecr and i regret that this much more balanced position than that of the rapporteur, mr boylan, was not successful in the plenary.

proposed four years ago in the white paper on transport. we have negotiated an ambitious agenda to bring about structural changes in this system and to create a truly single european transport area. this space will have to accommodate an increasing demand for mobility and meet the needs of passengers, goods and services in the 21st century. for that reason, i brought back and put the passenger at the center of the discussion. i believe that we need to raise the quality of work in all transport sectors by setting minimum standards first. in the labour market, we must seize the opportunity to apply the principle of equal opportunities and make this field much more attractive to women. a transport system of the future can only be one without barriers of any kind and using all modes of transport in a sustainable way. that means we need both physical infrastructure and digital infrastructure. all our efforts must be focused on connecting border areas and peripheral regions with the other regions of the union so that passengers, goods and services can move freely and efficiently. infrastructure investments in these areas are considered to have a significant impact on territorial cohesion and the elimination of disparities in infrastructure development between eastern and western europe. the increased urbanization brings into question the need to improve and increase the capacity of public transport. urban centres are also the places where we face the negative effects of transport on a daily basis, whether in the form of carbon emissions or air quality or traffic congestion. integrated mobility services and real-time information provision will bring us closer to the goal of transitioning to sustainable transport modes. transport is a driving force of the european union, essential for the development of related industries such as tourism, on which the existence of connections between the infrastructure network, the efficiency of mobility, but also the quality of services for passengers depend.

in writing. ‒ i support the call to all members of the wto to try to find a solution without delay for implementing the bali package in all its aspects, including the reduction of trade-distorting subsidies, so that the dda can be concluded for the tenth wto ministerial conference. implementation of the agreement, in particular by developing countries, will result in the standardisation and simplification of trade-related procedures. moreover, the agreement can provide new opportunities to expand the use of innovative technologies and electronic systems, including electronic payment systems, national trade portals and one-stop shops.
in writing. ‒ i voted for this report that will amend the marrakesh agreement and should increase trade flows, expand duty collection revenue as a result of higher trade volume and better detection of fraud, and improve the efficiency of customs administrations.
in writing. ‒ the european union is one of the main supporters of free trade worldwide. this is manifested by the constant attitude to finance development and facilitate international trade. in this regard, supporting the amendment of the marrakesh agreement, which underpins the world trade organisation, is a further contribution to strengthening fair trade relations at the planetary level. the amendment primarily aims at changing the treatment of developing and least developed countries by establishing differentiation from other countries in the implementation of wto rules and providing technical assistance for the compatibility of customs systems. the amendments involve the reduction and transparency of customs procedures, increased security and lower trade costs for the benefit of consumers. the development of the private sector of free enterprises, in particular those involved in small and medium-sized enterprises, will also be supported. reforming the world trading system through these changes represents a new opportunity for developing and underdeveloped countries. the eu must stand in solidarity with these countries and with the idea of fair free trade. these measures are in the interest of european citizens, who deserve to benefit from the best value for money. i therefore believe that the present document should be adopted, as it constitutes an important step forward in this area.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the recommendation on the draft council decision authorising the kingdom of belgium and the republic of poland to ratify the budapest convention on the contract for the carriage of goods by inland waterways (cmni) and the republic of austria to accede to it. both the accession of belgium and poland and the ratification of this convention by austria provide a much better regulated framework for the transport of goods by inland waterway. the participation of these countries in the convention benefits citizens as well as businesses and will contribute to the implementation of this legal instrument alongside the 11 other member states that are already parties to the convention.
in writing. ‒ the budapest convention is thus an agreement falling partly under exclusive european union competence. however, the convention does not provide for the possibility for the union to become a party. nevertheless, member states cannot ratify or accede to it without an authorisation by the union (article 2(1) tfeu). in this case, the union’s exclusive competence is limited to a single provision, and an authorisation given to individual member states would not have a negative effect on the implementation of the union’s external policy on judicial cooperation in civil and commercial matters. i therefore voted in favour of the report.
in writing. ‒ inland waterways are a strategic asset of the european union, both economically and socially. they allow the interconnection of member states using the natural courses of major rivers or the connecting man-made canals built over time. it is a less polluting mode of transport, but also more advantageous in terms of price. for these reasons, this type of transport should be supported at european union level. the budapest convention on the contract for the carriage of goods by inland waterways, adopted in 2001, regulates the commercial exploitation of inland waterways, establishing uniform standards and harmonising national rules already in place in the 11 eu member states that are signatories to the convention. the accession of austria, belgium and poland to this convention is a real gain, as it ensures the completion of the common shipping space, facilitating commercial shipping activity. the european union has the competence to approve the accession of new member states to the convention. i therefore believe that we must support this formal approach to strengthening the union's inland waterway network, which is an important asset for ensuring the coherence of the european common market.
in writing. ‒ hundreds of migrants are now choosing to leave their home countries to start a new life in europe. one of the causes of this impressive influx is the humanitarian crisis in syria, and we can see the effects of this in the considerable number of migrants arriving on european soil. since the beginning of the year, some 500 000 people have arrived in the eu. the countries most affected by this crisis are primarily greece and italy, which are a gateway to europe for the refugee wave, with 249,855 arriving in greece and 119,500 in italy since the beginning of 2015. i voted against the amendment on compulsory quotas because i believe that account should be taken of the ability of states to provide decent conditions for immigrants, but i voted in favour of the report on provisional measures in the field of international protection for the benefit of italy and greece as a whole, because we must show solidarity both with these two countries which are no longer able to cope with the situation and with immigrants who want a new life. but i would stress once again the need to concentrate all efforts on the countries of origin of migrants in order to eliminate the causes of this phenomenon.
in writing. ‒ i strongly support a credible and substantial eu-wide compulsory resettlement scheme, including a binding quota for distribution, accompanied by a compulsory scheme for the relocation of recognised refugees within the european union. the provisional emergency measures foreseen in the report will set up a fair and equitable relocation mechanism, will relieve the significant asylum pressure from italy and greece, by relocating an important number of applicants in clear need of international protection who have arrived in the territory of italy and greece. however, this is only a first step towards the creation of a long-term solution to the migrant emergency. any proposal for a permanent emergency relocation mechanism must be based on a more substantial contribution to solidarity and responsibility-sharing among member states, including a significant increase in the number of available relocation places to adapt to rapidly changing migratory flows and trends. i really hope that member states will show more solidarity between them and we will be capable of creating a truly european asylum system.
in writing. ‒ the last few months have seen an exponential increase in migration from conflict zones in the eu's neighbourhood to member states. beyond the populist polemics that mark the public space in the member states, the problem will continue to exist; this is why an eu-wide solution is needed. the first arrival countries (mainly italy and greece) are under enormous pressure, which requires action in solidarity with the other member states. refugees must be redistributed according to a jointly negotiated and agreed scheme, according to the possibilities available in each country of the union. refusing to take in refugees is clearly a violation of the principles on which the european union was founded and cannot be accepted. what is essential, however, is that the rights of each person are respected and that redistribution is not affected by discrimination on arbitrary grounds. at the same time, it is the right of every refugee to express his or her consent to be resettled in one or another member state; so i think the focus should be on what refugees want and less on what some european politicians want.
in writing. i voted against the report on the proposal for a council decision establishing provisional measures in the area of international protection for the benefit of italy and greece. i believe that solidarity action by member states is crucial in formulating a concrete and sustainable response to the refugee crisis. this response must contain concrete elements, some of which are urgent and others of which constitute a medium- and long-term response. as for the central and eastern european states, i believe that the most appropriate measure for their involvement in the european refugee placement system is that based on voluntary quotas taken in the emergency relocation process. this is the official position of the visegrad group countries and of my country, romania. european support is needed to strengthen the capacity of these member states to participate in the future implementation of the common european asylum and refugee policy.
mr president, european policies have a direct impact on urban development and national urban policies. the objectives of the member states shall be linked to smart, green, sustainable and diverse economic growth. obviously, in diversity and tolerance of each other. with these ambitions, european urban policies need to be strengthened. improving the urban dimension of these european union policies would simplify and allocate european funds at local level so that decisions are taken by local communities. i therefore support the association of functional cities and urban areas with the whole cycle of european urban policies. functional urban areas, cities, member states, the commission need to cooperate to improve these urban policies in a concrete way and according to the wishes of local communities, because the people there know best what they want. let's be the citizens of today for the cities of tomorrow.
in writing. ‒ the european urban agenda sets a coherent framework for eu urban policies by adapting sectoral policies to urban development needs, responding to urban challenges and at the same time contributing to strengthening territorial cooperation. cities are real engines of economic development, providing growth and jobs, and acting as catalytic centers for creativity and innovation. at the same time, urban areas face numerous economic, social and environmental challenges to which the european urban agenda can offer concrete solutions. the objectives of the agenda shall focus on specific priorities that have the capacity to deliver measurable results in the development of smart cities and the low-carbon economy and that are conducive to social inclusion. better coordination of european urban development policies and the necessary coherence shall be achieved through measures of simplification, efficiency and harmonisation and by facilitating the widest possible access to a harmonised knowledge base. the financing measures available through the structural and investment funds and through existing financial instruments are an essential support for the development of urban areas. given that almost 70% of european citizens live in urban areas, i believe that cities are and must remain the main beneficiaries of investment through cohesion policy.
in writing. ‒ i believe that european union policies must support functional cities and urban areas to express and realise their full potential as engines of economic growth, employment, social inclusion and sustainable development. i believe that these functional cities and urban areas need to be more closely associated with the whole european policy cycle.
in writing. ‒ today, more and more people are living in cities, in europe and worldwide. this trend is being hastened most of all by population growth and new technology. i support the call by the rapporteur on the commission to develop a new multi-level governance model combining formal governmental structures with informal structures which take into account new digital communication possibilities and network activities. the new model should guarantee an exchange of information both horizontally and vertically and should improve citizen participation and democratic legitimacy. another objective of the report is to simplify eu law in the interest of efficient urban development policy, in order to facilitate implementation and reduce costs. i therefore voted in favour of the report.
in writing. ‒ i believe that towns, cities and functional urban areas should be fully supported by eu policies and should be more closely associated with the european policymaking cycle. also, subnational governments should be involved in the policy process and development strategies.
in writing. ‒ i have voted for this report that will examine the urban policy challenges for eu policy makers and to devise guidelines and boundaries for a future sustainable eu urban development policy.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report because i believe that directing eu policies towards the urban dimension of eu policies is an option adapted to the reality of our times. taking into account that in 2014 half of the world's population and 72% of europe's population lived in urban areas, and that by 2050 nearly 80% of the world's population is estimated to live in urban areas, it is clear that we are looking at a population that is deeply committed to participatory democracy, development and economic development, but that requires an adequate supply of jobs. in this respect, i believe that the inclusion of a common european urban agenda that would promote in particular the development of governance solutions capable of meeting the challenges and objectives of sustainable development and favourable to the economic and social inclusion of urban areas is beneficial for the eu, and i am thinking in particular of romania, a country that is changing demographically and urbanistically at a higher speed. i also welcome the report's proposal to take account of the local territorial specificities of each member state in view of urban size and economic growth, an approach which should be applied in as many european policies as possible.
in writing. ‒ urban areas are where most of the eu's population lives and are the main engines of the member states' economies. their development has been based almost exclusively, up to now, on the interest of local and national authorities, in accordance with a limited interpretation of the principle of subsidiarity. however, the implementation of european policies has a direct effect on cities, especially in the field of regional development. in this context, the need for a european policy for urban centres has become apparent, in order to enable cities to meet the challenges posed by the process of globalisation, technological progress and urban development. this can be the result of better coordination, both horizontally between the various european sectors and initiatives and vertically, with a view to optimising the various administrative levels. in this respect, the proposal to appoint an eu special representative for urban areas is a commendable initiative that can give the necessary impetus to the process of deepening cooperation. the development of this european policy can contribute to the achievement of the europe 2020 objectives, in particular with regard to social inclusion, demographic change and sustainable development. for these reasons, i believe that the adoption of this report is timely for the development of our cities.
in writing. ‒ cities and functional urban areas are the key economic pillars and job-creating engines of the european union. although the european commission published a communication on the union's urban agenda in 1997, the role of european cities in the eu policy-making process is still under discussion. the eu has no explicit competences in the field of urban development, but a wide range of legislative initiatives have a direct or indirect impact on cities and functional urban areas. the resolution adopted by the european parliament calls for the swift adoption of an eu urban agenda that is consistent with the eu's objectives and strategies, in particular the europe 2020 strategy. this will certainly lead to better policy coordination and better integration of urban development objectives across as many policy areas as possible.

mr president, we are living in difficult times and in difficult times we must be creative and innovative. for me the social— and solidarity—based economy is one such measure. it now provides employment for more than 14 million people in the eu and between just 2009 and 2013 created 1.3 million new jobs. maybe for some this is not much, but if we are smart enough we should capitalise on the huge potential here, considering their diversity, the services they provide and the methods that they use. since they often employ the socially excluded and many young people, their capacity to enhance cohesion within communities by creating jobs and minimising social inequalities should be duly taken into consideration. unfortunately, up to now only a few countries already have in place national legislation concerning the social and solidarity based economy. the commission should be tougher in this direction. other member states should follow this example and i am glad to say that my own country, romania, is close to adopting it. at the same time, appropriate support should be provided for the establishment and development of small and medium—sized enterprises, the backbone of our economy. we cannot ask for new jobs and quality jobs without helping those who can provide them by creating the proper environment.
mr president, the 23 million unemployed people in europe are the result not only of the economic crisis of the past years, but also the result of structural shortcomings within eu labour markets. we have to tackle these if we are to create more employment in europe in the years to come. therefore i advocate three solutions: firstly, facilities for labour mobility, secondly, an improved entrepreneurial environment and, thirdly, a better way of matching the education system and employers’ needs, mainly through vocational education. on the first point, labour mobility: nowadays citizens have to move to where the jobs are. therefore, cities need to provide enough affordable housing for people from rural areas who need a second house in the city for working days during the week. a further point on labour mobility: we talk a lot about people moving between eu member states, but we also need to talk more about people moving within an eu member state. there are still significant discrepancies between regions in terms of employment opportunities within a country. i therefore call on the commission to establish a catalogue of best practices to stimulate mobility within a member state and to share these experiences with member states which still have work to do on labour mobility. secondly, on improving the entrepreneurial environment, we all know the erasmus for young entrepreneurs programme established by the commission. it is a good programme, which i fully support, but it needs to be complemented by a similar programme at national level. the erasmus for young entrepreneurs programme obliges you to move from your home country to another country to undertake a traineeship paid by the commission with an already established entrepreneur. it is a good programme and i give it my full support, but member states should also launch and publicly finance such programmes at national level in order to stimulate mobility within the member states. the commission could assist, based on its experience with erasmus for young entrepreneurs at european level.
mr president, unemployment continues to be one of the main challenges in the european union, especially among young people. the unemployment rate is still alarming, as are the significant differences of unemployment rates between member states. i agree on the emphasis given to the need to achieve a competitive labour market, to the implementation of reforms that can increase labour market and personal career flexibility, and to the better matching of skills and jobs, including stronger synergies between education systems and labour markets. the issue of skills mismatches, however, should not hide the real problems of the labour markets, the need to fight precarious employment and social inequalities, to invest in human capital in order to prepare the labour markets for the future, and to foster a comprehensive approach regarding labour mobility based on the free movement of citizens and workers and the principle of equal pay for equal work.

in writing. ‒ the economic crisis has had a negative impact on the economic, social and territorial cohesion of the union and has slowed down the objective of reducing disparities between regions, so that at the beginning of the new programming period, progress has been particularly slow. some member states are facing serious problems due to a lack of administrative capacity and bureaucratic overload, reflected in the low implementation of funded projects and the poor absorption performance of community support, so that the risk of funds being disbursed at the end of the programming period cannot be avoided. structural reforms are required in member states which had a particularly low absorption rate at the end of the previous period in order to avoid similar scenarios in the future. the efficiency of cohesion policy lies in the ability to adapt and flexibly adapt its instruments to local and regional specificities, but also in the ability of regions to turn them into development opportunities. the commission should take into account all economic and social aspects arising from the suspension of commitments or payments pursuant to article 23 (15) of the common provisions regulation. i therefore consider that suspension of payments should be avoided where minor errors are found.
in writing. ‒ cohesion policy is the european union's main instrument, aimed at reducing economic, social and territorial disparities in european regions, boosting their competitiveness, combating climate change and energy dependence, and at the same time contributing to the achievement of the europe 2020 objectives. i consider that, despite the difficulties faced by some member states and regions in co-financing them, cohesion policy investments have significantly mitigated the negative effects of the economic and financial crisis and contributed to ensuring stability within regions by securing funding flows in a period when national and regional public and private investments have sharply decreased, with cohesion policy funds representing 21% of public investments across the union and 57% in cohesion fund beneficiary countries overall.
in writing. ‒ during the recent crisis and austerity conditions, cohesion investments gave stability to the regions by ensuring the flow of funding when national public and private investments declined. during the 2014-2020 financing programming, in areas such as innovation, digital and low carbon economy, employment and smes, clearly showed potential for creating sustainable jobs, especially for youth. i agree with the rapporteur on the fact that a late start of the current cohesion policy cycle and backlog in payments are not acceptable. moreover, we must improve administrative capacity of public authorities, especially at regional and local level and increase cooperation with all stakeholders.
in writing. ‒ every three years the european commission presents a cohesion report on the progress made towards achieving economic, social and territorial cohesion. the report underlines that the potential for creating sustainable jobs, especially for youth, is promising taken into account the investments during the 2014-2020 financing programming (in areas such as innovation, employment and smes). the report pays special attention to the future of cohesion policy after 2020. however, an analysis of the 2007—2013 period is necessary.
in writing. ‒ i have voted for this report that includes new measures to increase effectiveness and result orientation, thematic concentration in particular on innovation, the digital and low carbon economy, education and sme support.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report in support of one of the most important policies of the european union, namely cohesion policy, which aims to reduce regional disparities, promote economic, social and territorial cohesion between the regions of the member states and support job creation. it is clear that ensuring a stable fiscal and economic environment (as well as an effective institutional, administrative and regulatory environment) guarantees the effectiveness of cohesion policy. in this respect, as the document suggests, member states should regularly hold high-level political debates in national parliaments on the effectiveness, efficiency and timely implementation of the funds, and on the contribution of cohesion policy to the achievement of the objectives pursued. cohesion policy must be the fundamental instrument for maintaining the level of investment in the different member states and i am convinced that the objectives and means proposed will ensure that my country, romania, also benefits from fair treatment.
in writing. ‒ the economic, social and territorial cohesion of the union is one of the strategic objectives of the european project. the european institutions have invested and are investing considerable sums of money in its implementation, even under the austerity regime imposed by the recent economic crisis. the main areas of this investment in the current multiannual framework (2014-2020) are innovation, the digital and low-carbon economy, the creation of new sustainable jobs (especially for young people), and small and medium-sized enterprises. however, there are also problems with late payments, the limited administrative capacity of public authorities at local and regional level or insufficient cross-border cooperation. in the long term, a serious debate on the issue is needed, especially on cohesion policy beyond 2020, incorporating the lessons of the last multiannual frameworks, both in terms of the positive aspects and the shortcomings. the present document is only a step in this important process, the very purpose of which is to defend the interest of the european citizen. it must therefore be supported in order to give further impetus to the european union's cohesion policy and the coordinated economic development of the member states.
in writing. i voted in favour of the own-initiative report on 'investing for jobs and growth: promoting economic, social and territorial cohesion in the european union' by my colleague tamás deutsch. i welcome his initiative in producing this report, all the more so as the decisive role of eu cohesion policy in reducing regional disparities, promoting economic, social and territorial cohesion between the regions of the member states and supporting job creation is undeniable. cohesion policy is the main instrument for investment in the real economy across the union and is a proven tool for growth and job creation in the eu, with a budget of over eur 350 billion by 2020. i welcome the fact that the rapporteur has called on the ec to pay particular attention to the situation of minority groups across the union, as they face various forms of social exclusion and are therefore more likely to be affected by structural unemployment. the same report also highlights the key role played by smes in the context of job creation and highlights their potential to promote smart growth.
in writing. ‒ it is clear that older people should not be a burden on society. in this regard, capacity building is necessary to promote their active participation in society. unfortunately, there are large differences between regions in how older people are engaged in society, which must be changed through social protection, support infrastructure and budgetary resources. better targeted and more effective active ageing strategies are needed to ensure social inclusion, active participation and well-being of all generations. i voted in favour of the report on the implementation, results and overall assessment of the european year of active ageing and solidarity between generations (2012) because older people must be given the opportunity to play an important role in society and the promotion of active ageing must remain a priority for the eu.
in writing. ‒ i regret that older people are still often exposed to age discrimination, stereotypes and barriers and therefore believe that member states must implement the equal treatment directive in relation to employment and occupation without delay and in a fair manner.
in writing. ‒ active ageing policies shouldn't be considered only as an instrument to maintain the employability of older workers, but as an opportunity for older citizens to enhance the positive role they play in the society. i support the idea stated in the report that linking the retirement age only to life expectancy fails to take account of the importance of labour market trends and is therefore not the only instrument to tackle the challenge of an ageing society; instead, through their employment protection legislation and systems of wage formation member states should support the recruitment of older workers especially before their statutory retirement age, as unemployment would have further negative effects on their retirement income, and ensure sustainable social protection systems.
in writing. ‒ i believe that eu is facing unprecedented demographic, social and structural changes that have to be addressed immediately. the commission should study the worrying problem of unemployment among people over the age of 50 and the rising level of long-term unemployment. i voted in favour of this report.
in writing. ‒ i have voted for this report that will raise general awareness of the value of active ageing and its various dimensions, stimulate debate, to exchange information and to develop mutual learning, offer a framework for commitment and concrete action and promote activities which will help to combat age discrimination, to overcome age-related stereotypes and to remove barriers.
in writing. ‒ i supported this report because i believe that encouraging active ageing is one of the eu's biggest challenges at the moment. we are all facing unprecedented demographic, social and structural changes that need to be addressed without delay; as the general ageing of the population is accompanied by a decline in the birth rate. to address these issues, i believe it is essential for romania and the rest of the european countries that the state promotes and strengthens, through social security systems, public infrastructure (care units, day centres and home care) available to older people. as the report also states, member states need to improve the allocation of funds for active ageing and ensure that this segment absorbs european funds efficiently. the social role of older people is crucial for any society, and sharing values and experience with the new generations will undoubtedly ensure the evolution and coherence of the european project.
in writing. ‒ the european union faces unprecedented demographic changes, inter alia due to an ageing society, a declining working age population and a rising level of demographic dependency. these negative demographic trends are also coupled with social changes in family structures, such as the rise in single-adult households and the decreasing number of multi-generational family households. the european year for active ageing and solidarity between generations was a much-needed initiative to raise awareness concerning these challenges, but also to start exploring the opportunities lying in the silver economy. as the example of several member states shows, there is a lot that public authorities, healthcare systems and even private companies can do to allow aging people to live dignified, useful and healthy lives and to be full members of our society.
in writing. ‒ 2012 has been designated as the 'european year of active ageing and solidarity between generations'. this was not by chance, as there has been a general trend towards an ageing population at union level for some time, which poses a challenge to european demographic policies. beyond viewing ageing as an exit from the labour force, the process must not lead to the marginalisation of this growing group within society. on the contrary, we need to think of new ways in which older people can be involved in society beyond a certain age, which is formally considered to be the limit of active life. their experience is a significant resource for the development of our societies. on the other hand, if we think about the labour market, it too will have to undergo changes in form and content to keep up with the new trend. it is therefore necessary to protect employees in old age and to prevent them from becoming unemployed, which can affect their pension levels and living standards. for these reasons, this document is a useful tool for the future demographic policies of the union.
in writing. ‒ the transport sector is a major force in the european economy, generating 10 million jobs. to remain a leader in generating growth as well as jobs, a number of important measures need to be taken at eu level. in this respect, a change of paradigms in transport policy is needed, precisely to meet the challenges of the future. at the same time, complementary measures are needed at national, regional and local levels of government, as well as at the level of citizens and the sector. the objective of reducing europe's dependence on oil imports and of reducing carbon emissions from transport by up to 60% by 2015 is extremely ambitious and can only be achieved through a well-defined set of interventions. i voted in favour of the report on the implementation of the 2011 transport white paper: assessment of the state of play and the way forward to achieve sustainable mobility as it is necessary to transform the european transport system and to create well-founded policies for the sustainable development of this sector.
in writing. ‒ through the adoption of this report, we will provide current and future generations with access to safe, secure, reliable and affordable mobility resources to meet their needs, while minimising undesirable impacts such as congestion, accidents, air and noise pollution, and climate change effects. i strongly support the inclusion, in the report of important social aspect in all modes of transport such as ensuring equal and fair treatment, good and safe working environment, promoting high quality jobs and working conditions for transport workers and ensuring fair and undistorted competition between transport operators. i welcome the introduction of measures for doubling public transport use in urban areas by 2030; the inclusion of measures for safety, usage in urban areas, elderly or disabled people and cyclist and the shift towards a more sustainable transport mode, less polluting and most energy-efficient mode of transport. these steps are of fundamental importance in the path to define a long-term strategy that would help the eu transport system achieve the overall goal of the common transport policy.
in writing. ‒ i have voted for this report that reiterates the european parliament’s support for the effective implementation of the white paper on transport.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on the implementation of the 2011 white paper on transport because, in my view, this is an objective that calls into question the achievements to date, but also the remaining objectives in this vital area for the european union. the commission's mid-term evaluation of the implementation of the 2011 white paper on transport is key to creating a clear perspective on our evolution and progress to date. we need to know very precisely which of these goals have been achieved, which are to be achieved and which are those that we will not achieve at the current rate. this evaluation, as the report also underlines, must provide concrete solutions to achieve all the objectives, must make efficient use of resources and, last but not least, keep pace with new developments in the eu, without setting targets lower than those of 2011. i believe that the document brings useful assessments and analyses to the eu and to transport policies, which are so important for our societies and for the economic development of european states.
in writing. i voted for the report on the implementation of the 2011 transport white paper: assessment of the current situation and the way forward to achieve sustainable mobility. i welcome the rapporteur's view that the completion of the trans-european transport network remains one of the preconditions for a more sustainable, efficient and continuous multimodal transport system and for a more balanced distribution of freight and passengers between modes of transport. i agree that the selection of projects eligible for eu funding should focus on the new core network corridors, on creating missing connections, in particular in cross-border segments, on removing bottlenecks, on upgrading existing infrastructure, on innovative transport solutions, on interoperability and on creating multimodal terminals and urban nodes.
in writing. ‒ gender equality is one of the principles promoted by the european union, aiming to eliminate all forms of discrimination against women and to reduce gender segregation in the scientific and academic community in the eu, as it is of the utmost importance to ensure that women and men enjoy equal treatment, have the same rights and obligations and work opportunities, and that their contribution to society is valued and respected equally. despite recent positive developments, member states still face a low presence of women in the highest academic and decision-making positions in scientific institutions and universities, which confirms the existence of bias-based barriers that prevent women from accessing leadership positions. according to statistics, even though 59% of higher education graduates in the european union are women, only 18% of them are university professors, and women are underrepresented in science, engineering, management and leadership. i voted in favour of this motion for a resolution because i believe that immediate action is needed to remove the cultural and institutional barriers that favour the presence of gender segregation in the scientific and academic environment and to encourage equal and non-discriminatory treatment in the hope of boosting research activities.
in writing. ‒ in europe, according to the latest available statistics, the research workforce is ageing. there is therefore an urgent need to make attractive careers in science available to young people, especially women, as science plays a key role in the european economy and science needs as many women researchers as possible who can develop exploratory research, thus contributing to the achievement of the objectives of the 2020 strategy. one of the main objectives of the strategy is the careers of women. i believe that there is a need for better systematisation of the available data on the gender breakdown and monitoring of the position of women scientists at member state level in order to promote gender equality in all public and private research institutions and i also believe that there is a need for more flexibility in terms of working conditions for both female and male researchers, to allow them to reconcile professional and family life and to eliminate the pay gap between male and female researchers with a view to respecting gender equality. last but not least, i believe that member states should, through the levers available, strive for a better gender balance in the bodies responsible for the recruitment and promotion of researchers.
in writing. ‒ gender equality is a fundamental principle of the european union, a basic precondition for the full enjoyment of human rights by women and girls and is essential for their empowerment and the achievement of a sustainable and inclusive society. unequal access for women to research positions, funding and publishing still persists, including an unadjusted gender pay gap in the area of science and academia. i believe that we must be keen in pointing out and defeat by all means the low presence of women in the highest academic and decision-making positions in scientific institutions and universities, which indicates the existence of a glass ceiling, an invisible barriers based on prejudices which stand in the way of women accessing positions of responsibility. we have to fight all forms of direct or indirect discrimination against women; otherwise, horizon 2020 will not be achieved.

in writing. ‒ i voted for this report because i have always considered that equal opportunities for women and men is a proof of our status as a civilized nation, it is a result of all the lessons that history has taught us, that discrimination creates unforgettable social dramas. i worked in the last term on the parliamentary committee on women's rights and gender equality and i was always close to the problems that still face many women, not only in my country. i think this report rightly highlights a serious problem, the discrimination against women in academia and science, where all the data shows that they are underrepresented and underpaid. by my vote today, i want to join those who are calling on the commission and the member states to apply all european legislation in this area in good faith and/or to change it if it is not effective.
in writing. ‒ i am particularly pleased with the initiative to promote the empowerment of women in science. at european level, it is felt that, due to the existence of prejudices and stereotypes against them, women are still underrepresented in the academic sphere. the european union's commitment to human rights requires us to uphold our existing legal provisions and, where necessary, to introduce new ones to achieve gender equality. for example, research shows that women are particularly disadvantaged by both being considered less promising male candidates for jobs requiring mathematical skills. although my country is one of the most positive in this field, it also needs programmes that encourage women to pursue scientific careers, while at the same time promoting family values. in this sense, i believe that the commission and the member states should develop programmes to ensure that the necessary enabling environment is created for women's academic careers, taking into account the role of women in the family.
in writing. ‒ the european union has come a long way towards adopting an appropriate legislative framework to support gender equality. at present, the legal provisions in the member states in this respect are among the most advanced in the world. however, in practice, in many member states, the situation of women is still precarious, affected by the persistence of prejudice and stereotypes. a special case is that of women involved in science and academia: their share is alarmingly low, at only 18% of university professors and 10% of rectors. in order to correct this flagrant imbalance, the european institutions must apply gender policies more vigorously, in order to strive as much as possible for the equality of the status of women with that of men, both through educational policies, promotion programmes and non-discriminatory practices, and through the introduction of mandatory quotas in scientific and academic institutions in the member states, by ensuring a balance between personal and career life. these measures may be promoted, inter alia, through horizon 2020. it is important that those measures are implemented in concrete terms and evaluated accordingly. this document is a step in that direction.
in writing. we voted on the report on the careers of women in science and academia and the glass ceilings encountered. i agree with the rapporteur's request that the commission and the member states review existing legal provisions to implement them properly and, if necessary, revise them to ensure that equal treatment between women and men is respected. the commission and the member states are also invited to ensure compliance with the principle of non-discrimination, recognised in the treaty of lisbon as an objective of the european union, in all types of employment contracts or funding, and to respect the legal right to equal pay for equal work, for all components of remuneration awarded to men and women, including grants and scholarships, by ensuring, for example, pay transparency.

in writing. ‒ the member states of the european free trade association and the european union have established an agreement establishing equal conditions and non-differentiated treatment, thus contributing to the expansion of the european single market. the agreement of 21 june 1999 between the european community and the swiss confederation provides for the free movement of persons, the recognition of professional qualifications, lays down the basis for mutual recognition in the field of conformity assessment and establishes a framework for the application of public procurement contracts. the eu and switzerland have long-standing close economic relations, which have been factors of growth and stability. however, the implementation of the initiative 'against mass immigration' casts doubt on switzerland's continued compliance with the agreements in force, and the outcome of this decision may have a major impact on economic relations. given that cross-border professional mobility is a key factor in strengthening the internal market, i consider that switzerland should respect the conditions of reciprocity set out in the agreements in force. i voted in favour of this resolution because i am convinced that any damage to the free movement of persons within the european area means a review of the eu-switzerland agreements.
in writing. ‒ the eea agreement is a key factor for economic growth and the most far-reaching, comprehensive instrument to extend the single market to third countries; taking into account the internal developments in the eu, it has proven to be a solid, efficient and well-functioning agreement ensuring the integrity of the single market also in the long term. the obstacles to cross-border professional mobility have to be removed in order to deepen the internal market. cooperation under the agreement on mutual recognition in relation to conformity assessment is satisfactory, but the functioning of the agreement could be substantially improved if switzerland were to pledge to update it consistently in line with developments in eu law.

in writing. ‒ the european economic area (eea) is the opportunity offered by the european union to develop cooperation in an institutionalised manner with the member states of the european free trade association (efta). three of these, iceland, liechtenstein and norway, have become full members of this continental economic structure, supporting the development of european economic relations on the basis of a common market. in the case of switzerland, non-participation in the eea has been compensated over the last two decades by the signature of over one hundred sectoral agreements. a number of obstacles relating to labour market access, disaster prevention, energy policy and free movement still need to be overcome in order to achieve legislative harmonisation between the eu and efta states. the many problems persist in relation to switzerland, which has chosen, through referendums, not to cooperate with the eu in a number of important areas, such as education, free movement, transport and agriculture. from this point of view, there is clearly a need for more cooperation and negotiations to overcome the existing deadlocks, rather than populist manipulation of sensitive issues. for these reasons, i support the adoption of this document, which is an important step towards strengthening the european economic area.

in agriculture. i think we all regret the crisis we are in now, and the last farmers' demonstration in brussels gave a strong signal that this situation must end. the commission has also proposed that the european parliament should be consulted on the future of the milk sector. here we are five months later, and we're still talking about the negative impact of the russian embargo. in brussels, german, french and belgian farmers who had been favoured by the commission and the court next door were able to take part in the debate and to demonstrate against the crisis in the milk, pigmeat, beef and cereals sectors caused by the drought. not all european farmers could do this. from romania only a few representatives could be present but, in no case, could they bring a tractor, they would not in front of the parliament, young farmers informed the citizens about the situation in the milk sector and gave a simple example: the production cost is 0.40 cents per litre, the farmer price is 0.25 and in the supermarket, for citizens, 0.50. if this situation continues, we will be helplessly watching the collapse of the most important agricultural sectors, at least in eastern europe. thank you. in writing. ‒ since the adoption of the convention in 1930, the international labour conference has called on member states to eliminate the use of forced labour as soon as possible and to criminalise any such practice. yet, more than 80 years later, the international labour organization (ilo) estimates that at least 20.9 million people are victims of forced labour worldwide. this protocol aims to address all implementation gaps and to make progress in the prevention of trafficking in human beings for the purpose of labour exploitation, as well as issues related to the protection and compensation of victims of forced labour. in this context, ilo member states should develop a well-defined policy and action plan at national level and take measures to implement the provisions of the protocol. i voted in favour of the council's proposal to ratify the 2014 protocol to the 1930 international labour organisation forced labour convention as it concerns fundamental rights, victims and combating trafficking and is an important step towards guaranteeing the rights of victims of crime across europe.
in writing. ‒ one of the eight fundamental ilo conventions, which defines the fundamental international labour standards, is the labour convention, adopted in 1930 and considered as an instrument for the protection of human rights. the ilo estimates that worldwide, some 20.9 million people are victims of forced labor. i support the ratification in the interest of the eu by member states of the 2014 protocol to the 1930 ilo labour convention. i consider it a priority to address implementation gaps and to make progress in the prevention of trafficking in human beings for the purpose of labour exploitation, as well as in the protection and compensation of victims of forced labour.
in writing. ‒ i believe that, under the protocol, ilo member states must develop policies and a national action plan for the effective and sustained suppression of forced labour and take measures to implement the provisions of the protocol, consulting both employers' and workers' organisations. i believe that we must consider the protection of migrant workers against potentially abusive and fraudulent recruitment and placement practices and we must fight to eradicate the root causes that cause the increased risks of forced labour.
in writing. ‒ this report represents parliament’s position on a draft council decision authorising member states to ratify the protocol of 2014 to the forced labour convention of the international labour organisation. articles 1-4 of the protocol touch on matters relating to judicial cooperation in criminal matters and thus require the eu to authorise member states to ratify it. as this is an international convention which seeks to enhance the protection of workers and tackle forced or compulsory labour, it is something which i fully and wholeheartedly support. the report simply confirms parliament’s consent for the draft decision and has been adopted in the committee on civil liberties, justice and home affairs (libe) with the unanimous vote of those members present. i voted in favour of the report.
in writing. ‒ the international labour organization estimates that 20.9 million people are victims of forced labour globally. forced labor is considered one of the most profitable criminal activities in the world. this report shall address the ratification of the forced labour convention as regards aspects related to judicial cooperation in criminal matters. this is one of the eight core ilo conventions for which the european parliament's opinion is required. i voted for this report because harmonising international labour standards is a tool for protecting human rights and reducing the risk of impunity. the protocol aims at concrete measures: the development of a national policy and action plan for the effective and sustained abolition of forced labour. even if ratification of this protocol is voluntary, the protection of the fundamental rights of these people is a permanent responsibility for each of us.
in writing. ‒ i voted for this recommendation for a protocol that seeks to address the gaps in implementation and to make progress on preventing trafficking for labour exploitation as well as protecting and compensating victims of forced labour.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report because i believe it is absolutely necessary that those elements of the 1930 international labour organisation forced labour convention which are lacking be completed and adapted to the new social and economic realities. forced labour is unfortunately still present in our societies, including in developed, civilized and free states, where it takes on new forms. however, this forced labour is most often associated with trafficking in human beings and organised crime and is cross-border in nature. the fight against forced labor, against slavery is part of our civilization, because we are committed to defending and fighting for the rights and freedoms of people. this report, which supports the adoption by member states of the new protocol to the convention, is an important step in the fight against the practices that lead to forced labour and thus provides means to help people in such situations to overcome them and start a new life.
in writing. ‒ eighty-five years after the signature of the forced labour convention almost 900 000 people in the european union are still being coerced by their recruiters or employers to work against their free will. women are especially vulnerable in this regard, half of women in forced labour being sexually exploited. with physical violence replaced by more elusive coercive measures, like the retention of identity documents or threats of denunciation to immigration authorities, such dreadful practices are even more difficult to detect and, as a consequence, successful prosecutions remain rare. therefore i do hope that today’s consent by parliament for authorising member states to ratify the new protocol will endow the responsible authorities with the 21st century means to fight against this terrible form of human rights violation.
in writing. ‒ the ratification of the 2014 protocol to the labour convention is an important step in the fight against trafficking in human beings and in guaranteeing the rights of victims of this crime in europe. the labour convention, the protocol to which we are referring, defines international labour standards and serves as an instrument for the protection of fundamental human rights. despite the adoption of this convention by the member states of the international labour organisation, 20.9 million people are still victims of forced labour worldwide. i voted to ratify the protocol because we need a policy and action plan at the level of each member state to eliminate forced labour practices. i expect that, for more effective implementation, the provisions of the protocol will be discussed with employers' and workers' organisations at a later stage. unfortunately, we currently lack a mechanism for educating and informing people about the prevention of forced labour. the most vulnerable are migrant workers, by nature of abusive and fraudulent recruitment and placement practices. this protocol will enable us to identify, release and provide assistance and support to victims, including by not prosecuting them for the illegal activities they were forced to engage in.
in writing. ‒ the international labour organisation convention on the abolition of forced labour was adopted as early as 1930, but despite this, according to the ilo, 21 million people are currently victims of forced labour, generating an illegal profit of $150 million in the private economy every year. forced labour is a truly global problem, affecting all regions and countries of the world, whether industrialized or developing, rich or poor. forced labor is the opposite of decent work, violating all of its fundamental norms. in this regard, the 2014 additional protocol to the forced labour convention is a binding legal instrument, which aims to strengthen prevention, protection and compensation measures, as well as to redouble efforts towards the elimination of contemporary forms of slavery. by ratifying this protocol, states undertake to ensure that all victims have access to all possible remedies and that the competent authorities have the right not to prosecute victims for illegal activities they have been forced to perform. the ratification of this protocol is therefore an important step in the fight against slavery. i therefore voted in favour of ratifying the 2014 protocol on forced labour.

in writing. ‒ the beginning of 2015 was a very difficult time for bulgaria and greece. both snow and flooding led to total direct damage of eur 243 305 million for bulgaria and eur 395 878 million for greece. the events in these two countries are considered to be a major natural disaster. as regards bulgaria, the south-east region was the most severely affected, with over 300 buildings flooded in just one city. the commission also found that the average annual rainfall in the union was between 0,9 and 0,9 mm. as regards greece, the agricultural sector has been the most affected. some 17,500 ha of land was flooded and agricultural infrastructure, warehouses and crops were destroyed. 150 km of roads were damaged or destroyed, and water and sanitation infrastructure was damaged in 17 settlements. the profound impact of these disasters on the two countries and the high level of damage led me to vote in favour of the allocation of eur 16 274 765 for the two countries and, implicitly, in favour of the report on the mobilisation of the solidarity fund in the case of bulgaria and greece.
