in writing. ‒ the geographical indication serves to identify a product originating in a country, region or locality, where a quality, reputation or other characteristic of the product is linked to its geographical origin. however, non-agricultural products do not currently benefit from unitary geographical indication protection at eu level, beyond national provisions. at present, there are no rules at european level to protect the names of these industrial and craft products. in view of this, 15 member states have so far established mechanisms for the protection of geographical indications for non-agricultural products. but this protection is reduced, as geographical indications (gi) are protected either by the establishment of the offence of fraud, by trademark law or by specific gi provisions. i voted in favour of the own-initiative report on the possibility of extending the protection of european union geographical indications to non-agricultural products, as there is an urgent need to create a single system of protection of geographical indications throughout the european union, these products being part of the cultural, social and economic heritage of a given place and being evidence of the breadth of european know-how and cultural heritage, representing a history that benefits from specific knowledge of certain european areas.
in writing. ‒ given that geographical indications have a huge economic potential and that their adequate protection can bring important benefits, in particular to smes and european regions, i believe that such protection promotes and facilitates access to the common market, but also to markets outside the union, for european handicraft products, which are the fruit of traditional knowledge and skills, which contribute to the preservation of valuable know-how, characteristic of entire social and local communities, and which also represent a significant component of the european historical, cultural, economic and social heritage.
in writing. ‒ i believe it is very important for the commission to come up with a proposal for a unified system of geographical indication protection of non-agricultural products, proposing a system which would permit co-existence of already established rights but with the possibility of european-wide registration and uniform protection and guarantees. this system of protection by geographical indications would have very positive effects on traditional arts and crafts and would solve problems arising from the current fragmentation of legal protection. i strongly support the adoption of this report in this plenary session. creation of a system of protection of non-agricultural products is very much needed in this sector.
in writing. ‒ this report aims to put pressure on the european commission to come up with a proposal for a unified system of protection of geographical indications for non-agricultural products, based on the one already existing for agricultural products. the report proposes a system that would allow the co-existence of already established rights and offers the possibility of european registration and uniform protection and guarantees. i voted in favour of this report.
in writing. ‒ i have voted for this report that will enable a eu geographical indication (gi) protection instrument at european level, as part of a broader strategy for promoting high-quality eu products, based on a stronger commitment from the eu institutions to treat manufacturing and craft industries as a driving force for growth and the completion of the single market, thus enhancing the prestige of locally based manufacturing and handicraft production, supporting local economic development and employment in the areas concerned, boosting tourism, and strengthening consumer confidence.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report because european consumers are increasingly interested in product safety, the origin of products, their authenticity and their production methods, and not just in agricultural products. i believe that the measure to give european citizens the right and the possibility to be able to identify the origin and quality of any product is justified. as we are facing important trade negotiations with the united states of america and the national laws in force protecting non-agricultural products establish different levels of protection in the member states, i believe that it is indispensable to create a single system of protection throughout the european union. the protection of geographical indications of non-agricultural products is important for consumers, but at the same time it can contribute to the preservation of europe's local and regional traditions, values which are part of the european cultural and artistic heritage.
in writing. ‒ i am convinced that the application of geographical indications of origin should be extended to non-agricultural products, since these too contribute to enhancing the attractiveness of a region, to preserving the uniqueness of local identities and thus to having a positive impact on tourism, culture, employment and trade. it is very important that the commission takes account of the needs of producers when developing the rules, by not imposing excessive bureaucratic requirements and by keeping the costs of the procedure low. this is also important because we are basically talking about small producers, small entrepreneurs, who - mainly in the new member states of the european union - have to bear a significant administrative cost of a few hundred euros. i would like to emphasise that the text is very correct in referring to the 'language of the place of origin' in relation to the brand/logo, since it is the language of the community in the region, and thus the traditional name of the product may be the dominant one, rather than the official language of the member state.
in writing. ‒ the outstanding quality and reputation of products from traditional regions of the european union are reflected in what we call geographical indications of these products. the know-how and traditional techniques applied during their manufacture are part of the cultural heritage of the european union. through the existence of geographical indications, traditional high-quality agricultural products from european member states have contributed to the overall attractiveness of their regions. at the same time, these products have been shown to maintain local identities and promote the diversity of places, with a complete economic impact and immeasurable benefits for the tourism sector, culture, employment and trade. i voted in favour of this report, which calls on the commission to come forward with a proposal for a single, harmonised system of protection of geographical indications for non-agricultural products on the basis of the existing system for agricultural products. i hope that in this way we can encourage entrepreneurship at local and regional level and help to promote activities directly linked to local realities. geographical indications for non-agricultural products have a huge economic potential and their adequate protection can bring important benefits to smes and european regions.
in writing. ‒ within the european union there are many non-agricultural products that come from the traditions of each member state and have become an important part of their local and regional culture. the reputation and authenticity of these products make them highly sought after and, in this respect, they can be subject to counterfeiting, which can be detrimental to consumers and producers. there is a need to develop a single system of protection of geographical indications at european level, as different levels of protection exist in the member states, which is a problem for their effective protection. a strategy is needed at european level to promote these high-quality products. this can lead to an increase in the prestige of manufactured and craft products in europe's regions and thus to stimulate the local economy by creating new jobs in these sectors, encouraging tourism and increasing consumer confidence. this strategy can promote the development of small enterprises, which produce about 80% of traditional local products, through more efficient sales methods and closer cooperation within this unitary system at european level. i therefore voted in favour of the report on the possibility of extending the protection of eu geographical indications to non-agricultural products.

in writing. ‒ in the field of development cooperation, the european union's main objective is to combat poverty. it is not only a moral obligation but also a contribution to building a more stable, prosperous and equitable world. under the treaty on the functioning of the european union, the eu ensures coherence between its various policies and actions and takes account of development cooperation in implementing policies that may affect developing countries. in this regard, i believe that strengthening the role of local authorities in development cooperation in these countries will enable the tasks undertaken by the european parliament in its resolution of 13 june 2013 on the millennium development goals to be fulfilled. the eu can support this process by effectively participating in the development planning, implementation and financial aid flows to local authorities in these countries. i therefore support the adoption of the report on the role of local authorities in developing countries in development cooperation.

in writing. ‒ be it in developed or developing countries, it can be witnessed that decentralised governance is the most efficient way of public administration: being closer to citizens, local authorities have better knowledge of the local cultures and local needs and can more efficiently deal with problems at source. this has to be recognized in our development policy as well: the eu should promote the political, administrative and financial autonomy of local authorities in partner countries and thus work in favour of democratically legitimate, accountable and representative forms of governance. of course, decentralisation alone is not a quick fix to every problem a society faces but, if it is appropriately implemented, it can strongly contribute to human development.
in writing. ‒ the role of local authorities is undoubtedly to represent the state institutionally at local government level. local authorities thus contribute to the creation of democracy at the core of society and to sustainable territorial development based on the active participation of the local population in political decisions. the definition, organisation and achievement of development objectives are part of the state's portfolio of activities in the territory. and while the fundamental role of local government is most evident in developed countries, it becomes fundamental in developing countries with unstable governance and vulnerable populations. i voted in favour of political dialogue through this report. the new global sustainable development framework must provide opportunities for civil society, local authorities and national parliaments to get involved. more autonomy for local authorities will mean much fairer, more transparent and more accountable governance. the objectives and challenges of the post-2015 global development agenda require strong partnerships with civil society, and their success will depend exclusively on action at the local level.

mr president, the abolition of the death penalty in all countries of the world is one of the main objectives of the european union's human rights policy. the death penalty is clearly incompatible with humanity and human dignity, and studies and research have shown that it does not deter violent crime. the european union is the largest donor of funds to the efforts of civil society organisations worldwide to abolish the death penalty. we are the first to adopt rules that prohibit trade in goods used for capital punishment, as well as torture and ill-treatment, and the provision of technical assistance related to such goods used in this abhorrent practice. we, the european union, have a duty to encourage consistent and constructive dialogue, to raise public awareness through education and information campaigns, to persuade countries that use the death penalty to abolish it or at least to introduce a moratorium as a first step in this direction.

member of the commission.– mr president, every day citizens and businesses conclude cross-border transactions or enter into cross-border civil-legal relations benefiting from the european single market. but things may go wrong. products may be faulty or services may not be delivered. in such situations people need to be able to assert and enforce their rights. the european small claims procedure offers a uniform procedure to enforce rights in a cheaper and faster way. the current system has been operational for five years. we have assessed it and identified its shortcomings. now is the time for improvement. i would like to thank ms geringer de oedenberg, the rapporteur, as well as all the shadow rapporteurs for their cooperation on this dossier. it was not easy to come to a meaningful compromise so speedily. the commission’s objective was to modernise the small claims procedure. we proposed extending its application to claims of up to eur 10 000, paying close attention in particular to the needs of small and medium-sized enterprises. the final compromise sets the limit at eur 5 000. currently it is only eur 2 000, so this is a significant improvement. i know that some of you would have welcomed it if employees’ claims could have been included in the scope of the regulation. we agreed that we would come back to this issue in the future after having analysed the practical needs in this respect. the overarching priority for the commission in these negotiations has been to improve effective access to justice for more eu citizens. the level of court fees plays a key role in this regard. citizens must not be discouraged from effectively enforcing their rights. the prohibition of disproportionate court fees, which is included in the compromise text, is a step forward. we will monitor its implementation and application in the interest of citizens. more generally, the commission will support the practical application of the revised regulation through awareness raising and the wide dissemination of information.

in writing. ‒ the success of tunisia’s transition to democracy will depend on its future economic and social development. tunisia has significant long-term growth potential. the implementation of the expected reforms, combined with existing assets such as its human resources and open economy, will unleash this potential, thereby boosting its economy in a more sustainable and inclusive manner. over recent years, the tunisian economy has deteriorated markedly, both domestically and in the international arena, especially in terms of its trade with europe, which remains its main partner. in light of this, it is vital for the tunisian issue to become an eu priority, with the eu making concrete economic and investment commitments aimed at supporting the country’s fragile transition to democracy, while being mindful of the fact that the success of the tunisian experiment is in the interests of the entire region and the eu. i therefore voted in favour of the report.

in writing. ‒ the arab spring was a historic event of extraordinary magnitude, which changed the evolution of societies in the islamic world of the near east. tunisia was the first country where this mobilization of the population in support of democratization and modernization was manifest. however, the transition from an authoritarian society to a democratic and pluralistic system is a complex and difficult process that cannot be achieved in such a short time. at the same time, the challenges facing tunisia's young democracy are multiplying. economic and social difficulties are exacerbated by the intensification of the phenomenon of islamic fundamentalism and its corollary, the phenomenon of terrorism. the recent terrorist attacks in tunisia demonstrate the vulnerability of the transitioning society to the adversaries of the open society. the european union is tunisia's main neighbour and trading partner. in this respect, the union has an important responsibility for the development of tunisia's young democracy. one of the tools through which the eu can make a real difference is economic cooperation. this requires the adoption of the agreement for tunisia's participation in european programmes. the more we speed up this process, the more tunisian citizens will feel the benefits of the development of democracy in their country and the less the dangers of terrorism and sectarian conflict.
in writing. ‒ since march 1998, there has been a euro-mediterranean agreement establishing an association between the european communities and their member states and the republic of tunisia. this agreement aims to develop a strengthened dialogue on political and security matters, economic, financial and trade cooperation, and to promote social, cultural and educational cooperation. the events of recent years in tunisia, in particular the arab spring, have marked the country's passage into a new stage of its development on its way to democracy. however, the increasingly fragile economic situation, in particular due to the deterioration of trade with the eu, tunisia's main trading partner, with 75% of its exports and imports, is hindering its democratic development. in this context, tunisia needs the union's support for better economic development, ensuring a triumph of democracy, to the benefit of both the mena region and the eu. furthermore, at the social level, there is a need to strengthen cooperation in the field of education, training and youth training, which is an important pillar of the democratic revolution in tunisia. i therefore voted in favour of the protocol to the euro-mediterranean agreement on the general principles for the participation of tunisia in union programmes.
mr president, i voted in favour of this regulation. as a former minister of justice of the czech republic, i know how big a problem it is to resolve cross-border disputes. many eu citizens and businesses are afraid to enter into such disputes because they are objectively longer, more costly than purely domestic disputes. it is therefore good that the european union is trying to remove these barriers, so to speak, to judicial cooperation, judicial integration, and is adopting such a regulation, which may lead to the use of videoconferencing in cross-border disputes in the future for the examination of witnesses, to the electronic delivery of individual files to the courts, to the harmonisation of the level of court fees, to the setting of certain limits and thus to the reduction of the costs of the disputes in question. i think this is very important for the future, because non-communicative justice is one of the barriers to the internal market of the european union.
mr president, we have two regulations - one from 2006 and one from 2007 - which regulate shorter procedures, specifically for small claims and those relating to the european summary procedure. all of this is to help people, to help business people, small businesses and medium businesses so that the whole judicial process goes faster. we live and work in different countries in the european union and as such, the legal procedures must be adopted. but now we need to go further and change these regulations, with the following objectives: we need to increase the amount for small payment claims to eur 5 000; furthermore, electronic means of communication, of notification must be used by the courts; also, in certain cases, when possible, the judges should use teleconferencing; the administration of evidence, likewise, should be possible to do remotely and by teleconference; judicial fees should be paid by remote means. all of this will improve life and business.
in writing. ‒ the establishment of the european small claims procedure is an important step forward from the procedures existing under the laws of the member states. i believe this report will simplify and speed-up cross-border small claims litigation in civil and commercial matters and will cut costs. i welcome the inclusion in the report of the point that ensures that the judgement given by the european small claims procedure will be recognised and enforceable in another member state without the need for a declaration of enforceability and without any possibility of opposing its recognition. increasing the threshold to eur 5 000, with a 5-year review clause in order to see whether a further increase is possible, is one of the better aspects of the report as it will make the escp more accessible and therefore more used. finally i find it very positive that court fees will be proportionate to the claim and that assistance for the use of procedure will be free of charge.
in writing. ‒ i have voted for this report that will better regulate the european small claims procedure and raise the threshold for small claims which fall under the european small claims procedure.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this text as it is indeed needed to speed up cross-border small claims judicial procedures in the eu. a large part of the union economy relies on trans-border commerce and interaction and therefore it is understandable that litigation will occur. for the actors, knowing that in cases of litigation it takes a long time to solve the matter and the cost might vary greatly between member states, this could actually be a deterrent from risking cross-border ventures of various kinds. also, as this affects mostly smes, the backbone of a prosperous economy, finally addressing these issues and creating a regulation across all the eu can be very beneficial.
in writing. ‒ one of the main gains of the consolidation of the european union and the single economic market has been the removal of all obstacles to european free trade. this complex process can involve multiple issues, giving rise to litigation over small amounts. the recovery of those damages may raise additional problems for small producers or smes, which do not have the resources to pursue a transnational litigation. to that end, regulation (ec) no 861/2007 established european procedures for small claims and regulation (ec) no 1896/2006 established a european order for payment procedure. these documents needed a revision in order to streamline procedures, which is done through this document. thus, a limit of eur 5 000 for claims by natural persons and eur 10 000 for legal persons, with the possibility of revision after a period of 5 years, is established; the use of means of distance communication and videoconferencing for judicial hearings is encouraged, as well as the inclusion of labour claims in claims and an adjustment of judicial fees in relation to the amount of damage. all these changes are likely to contribute to making clear progress in this area.
mr president, air pollution remains the main environmental factor causing disease in the european union. we have medium combustion plants that are used to generate electricity, heat and cool in the domestic sector, supply heat for industrial processes and are a major source of sulphur dioxide, nitrogen oxides and particulate matter emissions. we have about 150 000 such installations in the european union which are not subject to environmental legislation. the report that we voted on today brings all these procedures up to the standards we have adopted in the european union and puts them in the same category, so as to prevent them from continuing to pollute the air we breathe and, in effect, to reduce the cause of disease for those living in these conditions. the commission should also assess, by 31 december 2016, the minimum energy efficiency standards for environmental combustion plants in accordance with available techniques.
in writing. ‒ according to the commission's impact study, air pollution leads to over 400 000 premature deaths a year and medical costs of up to €940 billion. it also contributes to significant environmental degradation, with 62% of the eu area exposed to eutrophication and economic damage such as €15 billion in lost working days, €4 billion in medical costs, €3 billion in lost harvests and €1 billion in damage to buildings. this proposal for a directive is welcome in the context that reducing emissions from medium combustion plants could help to meet eu objectives in areas such as climate and energy, reduce greenhouse gas emissions, while improving energy efficiency and promoting renewable energies. i voted in favour of the proposal for a directive of the european parliament and of the council on the limitation of emissions of certain pollutants into the air from medium combustion plants because i believe that by acting now and closing the current legislative gap, clear signals can be sent in terms of investments and stimulating research and innovation in breakthrough technologies.
in writing. ‒ air pollution remains a real cross-border problem, with many member states importing a considerable part of their air pollution from neighbouring countries. there is currently no eu-wide regulation on the level of emissions of air pollutants from medium combustion plants (installations with a rated thermal input between 1 and 50 mw). i support action at eu level to establish a coherent and ambitious regulatory framework and to tackle emissions effectively.
in writing. ‒ i agree with the rapporteur's position that the proposed amendments improve the possibility of realistic implementation of this directive so that it can become an important tool for improving air quality in the european union without imposing unjustified burdens on society and the economy.
in writing. ‒ i believe that measures to tackle air pollution at the source are indispensable and therefore i strongly support the adoption and strict implementation of the directive on medium combustion plants. medium combustion plants are one of the most important sources of emissions and a very serious threat to health and the environment. i congratulate my colleagues for being very ambitious in setting these targets, for granting a limited number of derogations and for deciding short compliance timelines for existing plants. hopefully member states will be as proactive on the matter and make efforts towards cooperation with the commission by providing correct and punctual data from medium combustion plants, and will assess the need for stricter emission values in areas that still do not comply with eu air quality standards.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report. the action programme which will run up to 2020 sets the framework for a review of eu air quality. it aims to lower the potential risks to human health and the environment by laying down rules to control and reduce emissions of sulphur dioxide, nitrogen oxides and particulate matter into the air.
in writing. ‒ i voted for this report that will establish an emission limit value for medium combustion plants, engines and gas turbines.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this resolution as i believe clean and healthy breathable air is crucial for the health of our citizens and there is nothing we should prioritise more. the emissions from combustion plants are obviously a main source of pollution and this text does an important job in calling for tighter regulation, with more control over the permits and functioning of these plants, but also envisaging a reduction in emissions in the next period. and this i believe is the key – not to preserve the current status quo when it comes to air pollution and emissions, but to strive for a reduction in the future, for a better air quality and for greener alternatives for energy production.
in writing. ‒ air pollution is one of the key environmental problems facing our societies today. lack of proper air quality can cause many long-term health problems for us and our children. in this context, it is necessary to adopt a unified european union approach to reducing carbon dioxide emissions overall. this document represents an important step towards limiting these pollutant emissions (sulphur dioxide, nitrogen oxides and particulate matter) by establishing clear rules on pollution from medium combustion plant activities. the regulations complement existing european legislation on internal combustion plants of large companies and small plants. in general, these measures contribute to the implementation of the union's climate change policies. of course, the application of these measures will require a transitional period for those installations to be adapted to the new environmental standards. the transition period may vary depending on the size and profile of the installations, the impact on the population. however, in the end, these measures will contribute to improving the living conditions of all union citizens.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on the proposal for a directive of the european parliament and of the council on the limitation of emissions of certain pollutants into the air from medium combustion plants. according to the impact assessment carried out by the commission, air pollution is estimated to lead to over 400 000 premature deaths per year and to health costs of up to eur 940 billion; it also contributes to significant environmental degradation. the report shows that reducing emissions from medium combustion plants can contribute to meeting the union's climate and energy objectives. i welcome the approach of the rapporteur, who in his proposal has taken account of the special situation of the sme sector. given that 75% of medium combustion plants are operated by smes, the report states, great care must be taken to avoid imposing an excessive administrative burden on them.
in writing. ‒ the report on caseins and caseinates intended for human consumption proposes the approximation of the laws of the member states on caseins and caseinates intended for human consumption, the need arising from the requirements to adapt the compositional requirements for edible caseins to the international standard. thus, international standards require the setting of the parameters related to the maximum moisture content of edible casein at 12% (instead of 10% as before) and the maximum milk fat content of edible acid casein at 2% (instead of 2,25%). the importance of these standards is reflected in the context of general food law, which provides for the free movement of healthy foodstuffs which make a significant contribution to the quality of life of citizens. to this end, it will ensure that consumers are informed about the food they consume, including provisions on the labelling of casein and caseinates intended for human consumption. i voted in favour of this report because i believe that health and food safety must be given due importance so that union citizens can enjoy a healthy life, conducive to harmonious development and in line with international standards.
in writing. ‒ i support the rapporteur's position, in particular for aligning the composition requirements for edible caseins with those imposed by the codex alimentarius, thus ensuring a level playing field for all food business operators on the world market.
in writing. ‒ i strongly support the introduction, in the commission proposal, of the provision of sufficient information in business to business relations in order to ensure the presence and accuracy of food information for the final consumer; the updating of the definition of ‘casein’, in line with the international food standards as defined by the fao and who; the introduction of a specific label for caseinates exceeding the minimum compositional requirements of milk protein. moreover, i welcome the proposal that the power to adopt delegated acts should not be conferred on the commission for an unlimited period of time, but rather for five years, thus increasing the monitoring capability of the co-legislators of the adoption of delegated acts by the commission. finally, i approve of the proposal to set an ambitious yet realistic date for the implementation of this directive in the member states (12 months after the entry into force of this directive).
in writing. ‒ i have voted for this report that will instate provisions on the labelling of caseins and caseinates intended for human consumption. in case the mandatory information laid out therein does not appear on the packages, containers or labels, such products may not be placed on the market as edible caseins or caseinates or used for the preparation of foodstuffs.
in writing. ‒ food security for european citizens is one of the principles underlying the powers conferred on the european parliament by the treaty of lisbon in the field of food. in accordance with this principle, we, the european parliamentarians, are responsible for regulating the processing rules of food intended for consumption by the citizens of the member states. caseins and caseinates are components obtained from the processing of milk, representing the main protein intake of dairy products. this process is the exploitation of an agricultural product which is very important for farmers in our countries. at the same time, however, we must take account of food safety, so as not to endanger the health of the population. this implies an update of directive 83/417/eec to take into account the relevant codex n290 standard and the world health organisation rules, which require a higher mandatory minimum amount of that protein in dairy products placed on the european market. in this context, the adoption of the current document is a win for ensuring better quality of dairy products for european consumers, which is why i support its adoption.
in writing. ‒ the report on the proposal for a regulation on the financial rules applicable to the general budget of the union introduces new rules on public procurement and the conclusion of concession contracts with the european institutions. there are three main directions pursued in this report that i was referring to: alignment with the directives which will introduce clarifications on how contracting authorities can contribute to environmental protection and the promotion of sustainable development, obtaining an economically advantageous offer and imposing certain labels and/or using appropriate award methods. the report also addresses rules on the exclusion of economic operators in order to protect the financial interests of the union. this will create a database that will centrally store exclusion cases to ensure the detection and prevention of potential risk factors, and subsequently make public the information on excluded operators. with regard to public procurement by the union, it is intended that electronic procurement contributes to a more efficient use of public funds and to improving access to public contracts for all economic operators. i voted in favour of the report on the financial rules applicable to the general budget of the european union as it ensures the effective, transparent and appropriate use of funds, which is one of the union's main concerns.

the next item on the agenda is the debate on seven motions for resolutions on the situation in thailand (2015/2875 ((rsp)).
on behalf of the ppe group. madam president, the political situation in thailand is at an impasse. on the one hand we have a military regime which has seized power by force and which wishes to maintain itself as long as possible, and on the other hand we have social tensions which are the result of a hardening of the existing regime, particularly in the area of freedom of expression. the european union has long enjoyed strong political, economic and cultural relations with thailand. our role now is to support a democratic transition in the country and to push the military junta to speed up the electoral calendar. the prime minister has announced that the constitution drafting process will take 20 months, which would postpone the elections until june 2017. this timetable is not an acceptable solution for the people, who want to see the return of a legitimate civilian government as soon as possible. the recent appointment by the government of a new constitution drafting committee and the release of several journalists are also to be welcomed. these are positive signs, but much remains to be done. only by holding free and fair elections will the thai government regain the trust and respect of the people.
it is clear that the ep parliamentary group and the whole european union are looking forward to the normalisation of thai politics: we want civilian rule to replace military rule through free and democratic elections, and that the process of drafting a new constitution is completed as soon as possible and a basic law based on equality, freedom and the rule of law is adopted. i think the european union has the opportunity to support this process, because the biggest working capital investor in asean member states is europe. we have more investment in the region than the united states and japan combined! and as a trading partner, only china is ahead of us. of course, respect for human rights, including the rights of national minorities, is an essential part of economic, political and cultural development. this is often forgotten even by some eu member states within the union, including their own member states.
madam president, considering the deteriorating situation of human rights and freedoms in thailand, as evidenced by the severe censorship of tv channels and community radio situations, the arbitrary detaining of people and the arrest of 14 activists from the neo-democracy movement, i support the call on the thai military authorities to lift repressive restrictions on the right to liberty and the peaceful exercise of other human rights, in particular those relevant to peaceful involvement in political activities. concerning the situation of the workers’ rights defender, andy hall, who is facing seven years in prison and a multi-million-dollar fine for defamation after contributing to a report alleging labour abuses by a thai pineapple wholesaler, i welcome the call in this resolution for the dismissal of all charges against him, since his actions, as a human rights defender, were directed at exposing instances of human trafficking and improving the legal situation of migrant workers in thailand.
madam president, i want to join in what has been said here. i want to thank the authors of this motion, i want to thank all of you who have come forward and clearly condemned the violence that is taking place in nigeria. the numbers here have been falling, and i don't need to repeat them, over two million internal refugees in this country, thousands of murdered women, children, but also ordinary civilians. more than ten million children in nigeria are out of school, the highest number of out-of-school children in the world per capita. i think that this is a subject that needs to be debated, not underestimated just because it does not directly concern us, as the problems of the middle east do. i think the european commission should be very active here. i call on the commissioner to try to be a leader in getting humanitarian aid to this territory, to the children and women living and displaced in this area. the money that the donors promised needs to be delivered, and unfortunately, it's not today. we need to talk to the president.
madam president, throughout nigeria insecurity caused by the conflict between the terror group boko haram, military forces and civilian self-defence has escalated into a worsening humanitarian crisis. the latest spate of attacks has uprooted 500 000 children, bringing the total number of displaced children in north—east nigeria and neighbouring chad and niger to 1.4 million. these children are at risk of being trapped in a cycle of violence, separated from their families, exposed to exploitation and recruited by armed groups, despite a commitment by the commission to provide additional funds to boost urgent humanitarian aid to the region. i would like to express my concern at the funding gap between commitments and actual payments for unicef operations. it is essential that we contribute to bringing to an end the violence of boko haram as soon as possible, re-establish stability and security across the whole country and address the root causes of terrorism and illegal migration.
in writing. ‒ the report on the proposal for a directive of the european parliament and of the council on payment services in the internal market brings new regulations in line with technical innovation and the rapid growth of electronic payments and the emergence of new types of payment services on the market. thus, significant progress has been made in the integration of retail payments in the union, in particular in the context of union legislation on payments. developments in payment services in the internal market have given rise to important regulatory challenges. for example, important segments of the payment services market, in particular card payments, on the internet, from mobile devices, become fragmented along national borders. the lack of a clear legislative framework to regulate this issue has led to legal uncertainty, the emergence of potential security risks in the payment chain and a lack of consumer protection in certain areas, which is why i voted in favour of the report on the proposal for a directive of the european parliament and of the council on payment services in the internal market.
in writing. ‒ i believe that the continued development of an integrated internal market for secure electronic payments is crucial to support the union's economic growth and to ensure that consumers, merchants and businesses can fully enjoy the variety and transparency of payment services to benefit fully from the internal market.
in writing. ‒ i congratulate the rapporteur for his work on the consensual outcome of the report. i would congratulate him especially for ensuring the development of new practices and new players in payment services in response to the challenges the current framework faces, while ensuring safety and transparency for consumers. transparency of payment services is a key element in terms of guaranteeing that consumers benefit fully from the internal market, and strengthening trust in a harmonised payments market. the payments institutions’ access to accounts maintained with a credit institution will allow the unrestricted and efficient provision of payment services. lastly, consumer protection is a shared competence of the eu and member states and, especially in the field of financial services, it falls within the broader aim of protecting economic interests. therefore, i support the elements added to strengthen the provision for consumer protection, such as the unconditional right to reimbursement, better protection in relation to transactions and in the framework contract between a consumer and a payment services provider.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report. it will allow the development of new practices and new players in payment services while, at the same time, ensuring safety and transparency for consumers.
in writing. ‒ i voted for this report which will improve the effectiveness of the european parliament and council directives on payment services in the internal market.
in writing. ‒ the european union's single market economy can only function when there is an optimal circulation of money for the purchase and sale of goods and services between citizens and traders in the member states. in this respect, payment services are a key element that can have a significant impact on the economic development of member states. the european commission issued the first directive to regulate this area in 2007, but in the meantime, important progress has been made which requires its revision. the use of third parties to provide those payment services provides greater transparency and security for consumers. the new document provides more protection against erroneous payments, for the protection of invoice payments and for the protection of consumer rights. it also regulates surcharges on transactions based on certain payment instruments, in particular on bank cards, with a view to establishing limits at least at the level of interchange fees within the union. i believe that this document brings important changes to the regulation of payment services, which are in support of european citizens and the development of the union economy.
in writing. ‒ i believe, considering the large number of petitions received by the ep denouncing abusive terms in mortgage contracts and risky financial instruments in spain, that it is very appropriate to request the commission to make effective enquiries as to whether there have been violations of fundamental rights and infringements of european legislation. we must be straightforward and take the lead in order to put an end to bank-related infringements of eu consumer-rights law in spain. the situation there is critical: since 2008, more than 700 000 people have completely or partially lost their savings and nearly 400 000 have been evicted from their homes. the spanish government should act as soon as possible to put an end to this situation, and should put forward initiatives to stop it happening in the future.
in writing. ‒ i voted for this resolution, which will initiate new legislation to harmonise mortgage contract terms and debt settlement procedures with a view to reinforcing consumer protection across the eu.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this resolution because i believe it is unacceptable for financial institutions to deceive or not to inform customers about all aspects of the loans, deposits or financial investments they encourage them to make. many people in spain, but also in romania and other eu member states, have found themselves in desperate situations, losing their homes and their life savings. unfortunately, this has often been the case because people have not been fully informed or, in the case of investments, have not been made aware of the real risk they are taking. of course, eu law provides for a number of measures and regulations which, if properly and fully implemented, would drastically reduce or eliminate such cases. however, the reality is that these people have been misled and the authorities in the member states, together with all eu institutions, need to improve the legislation, fully enforce it and ensure that such abusive practices and conditions and false or incomplete promotion will not be repeated in the future.
in writing. ‒ petitions are a very important tool through which the european parliament keeps in touch with the citizens it directly represents and with the problems they face. the interest of the citizen as a consumer must be a priority in all the measures we take. one such case is the legislation governing mortgage lending in the member states. citizens are now telling us that there is a problem in spain with incomplete information for mortgage-backed loans, which is leading to the eviction of tens of thousands of people who have put their trust in this type of credit instrument, presented in an overly favourable light by certain banks. the problem is also found in other countries affected by austerity policies that have been implemented without an assessment of the social impact they may have. it is our duty to correct these shortcomings and to come to the aid of citizens who have resorted to this type of credit without bad faith, but who have ended up in dramatic situations. we must be aware that for many of our citizens, we may represent the last chance they have for a normal life.
mr president, i supported this motion because i believe that the european union, as an international institution, must defend human rights in the world. we are constantly debating the human rights violations in the world, so we must also be the ones who will fight against the death penalty. in short, there are still fifty-eight countries that have the death penalty, and in some states it is carried out in a very barbaric way. i want to mention china, i want to mention iran, i want to mention saudi arabia, these are countries where the death penalty is clearly abused, and we also debated in the bloc this morning about how a young dissident should be brutally executed, murdered in saudi arabia. we must therefore fight against this and try to promote the prohibition of this punishment in all international forums and, on the contrary, insist and say that the adequate punishment for the most serious crimes is life imprisonment.
i'm against the death penalty. in 2014, 2,500 people died as a result of the death penalty. every day there are people sentenced to death for crimes under the common law or for exercising their freedom, and i'm talking about the case of the protesters, the case of those who participate in the protests, in particular, for example, the case of the minor ali mohammed al-nimr in saudi arabia, who participated in the protests and was killed. not many months ago, saudi arabia employed executioners to behead prisoners or amputate limbs (legs or hands) of those convicted of lesser crimes. question: are we all in 2015 or just some of us?
in writing. ‒ as the world day against the death penalty on 10 october 2015 focuses on raising awareness of the use of the death penalty for drug-related offences, i consider that this is incompatible with the values of respect for human dignity, freedom, democracy, equality, the rule of law and respect for human rights on which the union is founded, and that any member state reintroducing the death penalty would thus be in breach of the treaties and the eu charter of fundamental rights.
in writing. ‒ i am very concerned by the fact that, in opposition to the general trend of recent decades, an increasing number of countries have enacted laws permitting the death penalty for drug related offences. i therefore strongly support the call on the commission to mainstream the campaign to abolish the death penalty in eu foreign policy and external relations; and to have talks with third countries that are responsible for a significant rise in the number of executions or for re-starting executions. the death penalty is the ultimate cruel, inhuman and degrading punishment, which violates the right to life, as enshrined in the universal declaration of human rights, and it is an act of torture unacceptable to states that respect human rights. we need to stick to our strong position against the death penalty, seeking the establishment of a universal moratorium with a view to the global abolition of capital punishment, as a key objective of the union’s human rights policy.
in writing. ‒ i strongly support the abolition of the death penalty and salute the eu’s paramount aim on this matter – universal abolition. i am also deeply concerned about the number of death sentences delivered in recent months and i believe that such practices violate international human rights standards. furthermore, it is clear that the death penalty is at odds with the values upon which the eu was founded. the commission should pay attention in relation to aid and political support flowing towards countries that do not make progress towards abolishing the death penalty.
in writing. ‒ i voted for this resolution that reiterates the long-standing opposition of the european union to the death penalty in all cases and under all circumstances, and emphasises once again that the abolition of the death penalty contributes to the enhancement of human dignity.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this resolution as it comes at a critical time in the world. instead of the human rights situation improving, it seems to be deteriorating worldwide. more and more executions take place in asia, and also in iran and saudi arabia. the penalty is also applied in the usa and japan and i consider this method of punishment to be barbaric and outdated, no longer in line with modern standards and respect for human rights. in particular, the barbaric and even arbitrary way the death penalty is being used in some countries, including in south-east asia, coupled with the serious doubts we have over the stability and independence of the judiciaries in these countries, the almost inexistent appeal recourses for people on trial and the low standards of professionalism employed by some of their law enforcement agencies lead to the unavoidable conclusion that innocents are being executed under the guise of a legal death penalty. death penalty as a practice should be outlawed everywhere in the world immediately!
in writing. ‒ the death penalty is one of the vestiges of humanity's long-gone eras that still persists in some parts of the world. it is an outdated legal tool designed for a type of society based on fear and terror of death by unnatural means. meanwhile, humanity has progressed to a stage that presupposes a society based on rational arguments and legal instruments designed to ensure the reintegration of troubled individuals into society. in this regard, the european union must send a clear message to other partners and international actors that it does not agree with the continuation of this practice and become a model for states in other parts of the world in the humane resolution of the problem of legal punishment of criminals, including drug traffickers. in this context, it should be noted that the focus should not be on the removal of the individual, for whose education the state and society have invested significant resources, but on the correction of the behaviour in question and the constructive reintegration of individuals into society, through unrestricted access to retraining courses and personal rehabilitation within society. such an approach is much more advantageous for all of us and for the world in which we live.
in writing. ‒ the european union maintains a firm opposition to the death penalty on principle and its abolition is one of the high priorities of eu human rights policy. the european union is the main institutional actor in the fight to abolish it. the death penalty is a cruel and inhuman punishment, with ample evidence demonstrating that it has no deterrent effect on crime. its abolition is essential for the protection of human dignity, freedom, democracy and the rule of law on the one hand, and for the development of human rights on the other. despite the many texts adopted at european and international level in recent years, there was an increase of 23% in 2014 compared to the previous year, with 2466 people sentenced in 55 countries. the eu therefore reaffirms its concern about the use of the death penalty, in particular by minors and persons with mental disabilities, and calls for a definitive end to these practices, which constitute a serious violation of international human rights law. in view of the increasing use of this sanction, as well as the wishes of other countries to reintroduce it in their national systems, i support the european parliament's resolution on the death penalty.

in writing. ‒ poor implementation of eu laws, deficiencies in inspections and gaps in relevant eu legislation are issues that, if not addressed effectively, can lead to a situation similar to the one exposed by the red mud disaster in hungary and in some neighbouring countries. it seems that, even now, hungary and other member states with similar mining plants are not correctly implementing eu laws; that legislation needs to be reinforced and properly applied; and that nothing is being learned from the disasters of the past. i therefore strongly support the call for greater emphasis on disaster prevention through research and development into the treatment of hazardous waste, and for more stringent environmental inspections. the commission and the member states must step up efforts to improve, and ensure the proper implementation of, all eu legislation governing the extractive waste industry so as to avoid a repeat of such an environmental and human disaster. let us protect the environment more effectively. let us fight pollution. let us fight climate change!
in writing. ‒ we must avoid a repeat of such environmental and human disasters. the resolution clearly stipulates that member states with similar mining plants are not correctly implementing eu laws. the legislation needs to be reinforced and properly applied.
in writing. ‒ i voted for this resolution, which will further elaborate the concept of an eu-wide industrial-disaster risk-sharing facility, with full observance of the polluter-pays principle, to cover possible costs beyond a high level of mandatory financial security.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this resolution today because i believe that a repeat of an accident similar to the one in 2010 in hungary, in which a very large amount of red mud was spilled, flooding several villages, killing 10 people and polluting very large areas of land, including protected areas, must be prevented by all possible means. of course, subsequent investigations have found a lack or poor application of eu law and a weak control and inspection system. unfortunately, this is not unusual in other member states where there are such deposits of red mud or other dangerous chemicals. it is imperative that eu legislation in this area be reviewed and completed to close gaps. at the same time, without accountability and punishment of the polluter and without full enforcement of the law, such cases will unfortunately be repeated.
in writing. ‒ the protection of the environment is one of the basic principles of the european union institutions. this implies a great responsibility for all economic operators in the territory of the member states to manage their activity in such a way as not to cause damage to the natural environment. mining activities involve quite high risks of destruction of the places where the extractive procedures take place, as confirmed by the tragic event that took place in hungary five years ago. to avoid such events in the future, european legislation has been amended to focus on the preventive and anticipatory side. however, the adoption of legislation is not enough to guarantee greater safety for citizens and the environment. member states need to implement the legal provisions in practice and ensure through repeated checks that those hazards have been eliminated. otherwise, we risk facing new accidents and disasters that endanger human lives and irreparably destroy the environment. for these reasons, the adoption of this resolution is necessary, which sends an alarm to authorities at all levels to take appropriate measures to avoid such regrettable events.
in writing. ‒ as the european union has committed itself to promoting gender equality and ensuring that gender is mainstreamed in all its actions, i believe it is important to deliver on measures to strengthen women's leadership and participation and women's rights organisations in the public and private spheres.
in writing. ‒ considering the importance of empowering women, not only as a self-standing human rights issue but also as a precondition for achieving post-2015 sustainable development goals, i believe that the 2017 mid-term review of the development cooperation instrument presents a good opportunity to assess the impact of dci-financed programmes on women and girls and to make reallocations if necessary. two of the millennium development goals explicitly address women’s rights: namely the promotion of gender equality and the empowerment of women; and the improvement of maternal health. they remain, unfortunately, largely unachieved. moreover, the progress towards gender equality and women’s empowerment has been slow and uneven in many countries. the conclusions of the evaluation of the gender action plan 2010-2015 show the clear need for a step-change in eu action on gender equality and women’s empowerment and the fact that we need a renewed political commitment by the european external action service and the commission to improve performance. i therefore strongly support the call to put in place measures that will strengthen leadership and participation by women and women’s rights organisations in both the public and private spheres.
in writing. ‒ i voted for this resolution that will renew the eu plan of action on gender equality and women’s empowerment in development and will focus on all aspects of eu external policy – development cooperation, humanitarian aid, trade, human rights and foreign affairs, migration and asylum – in line with the ‘policy coherence for development’ principle, which should apply to developing, neighbourhood and enlargement countries alike.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report because i have known about the issue of discrimination and abuse against women since the last mandate, when i was a member of the femm committee (committee on women's rights and gender equality). i believe that the european union must respond with one voice to a problem that still exists in many of our societies. since one in three women worldwide is at risk of experiencing violence (physical, sexual), discrimination and coercion at some point in her life, we need a common european action plan on promoting women and gender equality. to address this issue, i believe it is paramount for romania and the rest of the european countries that the state promotes, facilitates and strengthens girls' access to all levels of education. the report also states that member states should strengthen women's legal rights and access to justice through gender-sensitive legal reform. the role of women is crucial in any society and is one of the keys to economic and social development at european level.
in writing. ‒ the european union is the world's leading provider of development aid. however, the resources allocated by the european institutions to this area do not always reach the groups that need them most, for more or less objective reasons. one such case is that of women around the world who do not enjoy equal status with men. thus, globally, women represent the category most exposed to negative phenomena such as poverty, illiteracy, domestic violence, discrimination, undeclared work. attempts to change this situation through development aid are hampered either by the ignorance of national authorities or by the persistence of attitudes based on traditional stereotypes among the citizens of the respective states. in this regard, it is necessary to make more clear that eu development aid is conditional on compliance in practice with un gender equality criteria. only in this way will the countries concerned understand that they must apply these criteria in order to be eligible for union aid and will conditions be created that are favourable to improving the situation of women everywhere. the present resolution is a first step towards changing these imbalances.
the report highlights the lack of work-family balance as one factor in women's disadvantaged labour market position. the text very rightly underlines that the tension between family and professional life contributes to the postponement of childbearing and low fertility rates in most member states. i think that without raising the fertility rate, our societies are going to be on a very unhealthy path, and so this is going to be one of the key issues for the next few decades. and the increase in the desire to have children is certainly linked among many other factors to the inflexibility of jobs and the discrimination against mothers with small children. we still have a lot of work to do in these areas, but i certainly welcome the report's finding that it may be necessary to exclude women with one or more children from the method of calculating the wage gap. this indicator would thus indeed reflect the wage gap resulting from discrimination.
in writing. ‒ equal treatment between women and men is one of the european union's main concerns. the principle of equal pay for work of equal value has been enshrined in the treaties from the outset, but even up to now, it has not been possible to reduce the pay gap, with the average wage gap being 16.4%. slow progress was also made in the employment rate: the employment rate for men was 69.4% in the eu, compared with 58.8% for women. the report on equal opportunities and treatment for men and women in employment proposes to promote this principle on the basis of both moral and economic benefits. gender equality at work benefits the economy and society at large, as reducing the gender pay gap contributes to poverty reduction and income growth. i voted in favour of this report because i firmly believe that economic recovery, competitiveness and growth are desirable and can be achieved through equal pay and equal treatment for women and men.
in writing. ‒ despite the existence of the 2006 directive 2006/54/ec on equality between women and men in the labour market, pay gaps still persist and are even increasing. equal pay for equal work is a right principle that must also work in gender equality and must be evaluated by all employers, and for that we need better legislation.
in writing. ‒ the fact that progress towards gender equality in pay has proven totally insufficient in many eu countries, even though eu measures have been transposed into national laws, leads to a very uneven situation. we must make absolutely sure that unequal pay practices are discouraged and we must promote wage transparency, as requested by trade unions and gender equality bodies. i support the request to introduce mandatory pay audits for companies listed on the stock exchanges, except smes, and to introduce sanctions to exclude companies which fail to meet their responsibilities with regard to gender equality from the public procurement of goods and services from the eu budget. and i welcome the reversal of the burden of proof – a fundamental concept introduced by the report that makes sure the employer would have to prove that any difference in treatment was not based on discrimination.
in writing. ‒ i support the case law of the court of justice of the european union regarding the principle of equal pay that must be observed in respect of each of the elements of remuneration granted to men and women. also, i am a firm believer that empowering women and girls through education is an essential element in promoting equal treatment and equal opportunities in employment.
in writing. - i voted for this report. there are a number of substantial issues that remain unresolved in the area of equal opportunities in the labour market. in 2008 and 2012, the european parliament adopted important resolutions on equal pay for women and men. i, for my part, stressed the importance of non-discriminatory treatment of women in terms of access to education, information and a balanced working life. although many member states have harmonised their national legislation with the relevant provisions of european union law, this transposition is insufficient to ensure respect for certain fundamental rights. the principle of equal pay for equal work or work of equal value, enshrined in article 141 of the treaty and confirmed by the settled caselaw of the court of justice, is also infringed. we need to ensure that we have fair and uniform labour evaluation, that the principle of equal treatment applies to pension schemes, that effective monitoring systems are in place. in addition, access to legal aid is fundamental for victims of discrimination of any kind. if we want a europe where equal opportunities are not just a slogan, we need to generate the legislative framework to make this possible.
in writing. ‒ i voted for this report that reiterates the need for clear, harmonised definitions – to facilitate eu-level comparison – of terms such as gender pay gap, gender pension gap, remuneration, direct and indirect pay discrimination, and, especially, work treated as ‘equal’ and work of the same value. a clear and harmonised job classification system and greater wage transparency will improve access to justice.
in writing. ‒ as a member of the femm committee (committee on women's rights and gender equality) in the last mandate, i supported this report because i believe that this problem still exists in many of our societies, including romania, and the european union needs to have a common vision in this context. as the employment rate is generally lower for women than for men and equal treatment between women and men is one of the fundamental principles of european union law, we need common european legislation on equal opportunities in employment. as stated in the document adopted today, member states must actively pursue gender mainstreaming in the budget in order to promote and improve the situation of women in the labour market. it should also address the gender pay gap by taking appropriate measures to reduce the gap, which is a direct consequence of the gender gap. the potential of women, which is an under-exploited source of economic growth at european level, must not be forgotten.
