question asked in accordance with the 'blue card' procedure. madam president, your speech made it clear that national governments should do more. i've seen the same thing from other colleagues. i ask you: do you not think that the governments and, by implication, the citizens of our countries should know very clearly what the comprehensive programme devised by the european union is, from stopping the case to ensuring the security of europe's borders?
madam president, with an estimated 200 million people in the world forced to leave their homes because of natural disasters in the last five years alone, it is highly likely that climate change could soon become the biggest source of population displacement and that it would have a disproportionately higher impact on less-developed states. the costs of inaction are enormous and the preventive measures of today are far less costly than the adaptation costs needed tomorrow. succeeding in reaching an agreement at the paris conference is not the end of the line, but rather the start of a long period of transformation and adaptation. therefore, in order to ensure that this agreement will have the strongest possible impact in the long term, we have to make sure that the targets are ambitious and binding enough, and that the agreement is underpinned by strong rules on transparency in reporting, monitoring and verification.
in writing. in the not too distant future, the world risks facing new challenges if appropriate action is not taken, and one of the problems will be a fierce competition for resources, generated by climate change. this competition also risks increasing the risk of displacement of the population, both within national borders and across borders. according to a 2014 unep report on climate change adaptation gaps, developing countries will need to double or even triple their climate change adaptation budgets from previous estimates of usd 70-100 billion per year by 2050. particular attention should be paid to reducing deforestation and forest degradation, which are responsible for 20% of global greenhouse gas emissions, and to meeting commitments to restore 350 million hectares of forest, which would reduce co2 emissions by 4,5-8,8 billion tonnes per year by 2030.
in writing. i support the idea that eu member states should increase investment in public research in the energy sector to help create generations of low-carbon technologies. stimulating innovation can also generate economic growth. that's why we need more political signals on this. we are all invited to join our efforts to combat climate change. in the last 10 years, more than 150 million people have been forced to flee their homes due to natural disasters, creating a new category of refugees, climate refugees, who, although not legally recognized, do exist. in the current context, which puts us in the difficult position of managing war refugees, it is more than necessary to pay particular attention to combating climate change, so that we do not have to manage climate refugees as well. climate change is a threat to global stability and security in all respects. i want to emphasize that the lack of real action on climate change will affect all regions of the world differently, from economic, environmental and social losses to loss of human lives.
member of the commission, on behalf of the vice-president of the commission/high representative of the union for foreign affairs and security policy.– madam president, let me thank you for this opportunity to discuss today the situation in ukraine with the european parliament. much attention has been given to other pressing problems lately, but ukraine remains a top priority for the eu. we must not underestimate what is at stake. first and foremost, it is human lives. the latest numbers are appalling: almost 8 000 people killed, 1.5 million displaced, and another 1.1 million have left the country since the start of the conflict. secondly, basic principles of international law have been challenged: territorial integrity, sovereignty and the inviolability of borders – cornerstones of the european security order. crimea and sevastopol have been illegally annexed by the russian federation. i want to thank the european parliament and its members for keeping ukraine high on the agenda. the interparliamentary meetings, the recently—signed memorandum of understanding between the european parliament and the rada on parliamentary support and capacity building, and recent visits to ukraine by the committee on legal affairs, the committee on international trade, the subcommittee on human rights and the committee on foreign affairs are just a few examples. in less than two weeks, some of you will travel to ukraine to monitor the local elections – another opportunity for the ukrainian people to exercise their democratic rights. all of this strengthens eu-ukraine relations. your role cannot be overestimated. the european parliament ratified the association agreement a bit more than a year ago, paving the way towards an era of new opportunities for citizens in ukraine, based on its political association and economic integration with the european union. during the last plenary debate on ukraine in february, you discussed at length the normandy format and the minsk agreements. high representative/vice—president mogherini stressed then that the diplomatic efforts led by germany and france are genuinely european, and that we must remain united in our support of the normandy format and the trilateral contact group in order to achieve results. a lot has happened since then. during spring and summer, the situation on the ground deteriorated. nevertheless, ukraine adopted decentralisation-related amendments to the constitution at first reading, including a provision enabling special arrangements for self-government in certain areas of the donetsk and luhansk regions, in line with the minsk agreements. since 1 september – following intense diplomatic efforts – the ceasefire, which was first agreed in september 2014, is at last being largely respected. two weeks ago, an agreement was reached on the withdrawal of tanks and smaller weapons, implementation of which has already begun. the eu-supported organisation for security and cooperation in europe (osce) special monitoring mission is growing further to its full strength of 1 000 monitors on the ground to cope with all new tasks of verification and monitoring. we know, however, that it is not only the number of monitors but also, and above all, their full access to the territory which can make a real difference. that is why we strongly emphasise the need for it. demining along both sides of the line of contact has started. the normandy summit of 2 october 2015 gave further impetus to the political process, and the separatist so-called ‘elections’ in luhansk and donetsk – which would have violated the minsk agreements – have now been deferred. does this mean that the conflict is almost over? clearly not. cases of shooting and shelling still take place; people continue to die. internally displaced persons are unable to return to their homes. the modalities of the local elections according to osce standards still need to be fixed under ukrainian law. the special arrangement for self-government has to be agreed and an amnesty implemented. there should be no russian forces on ukrainian soil. ukraine should regain control over the 450-kilometre-long segment of its border that it has been forced to abandon. nevertheless, what we have now is a process that is moving in the right direction, albeit slowly and sometimes hesitantly. this is no small thing. the joint support of eu institutions and member states for this process has certainly contributed substantially. the eu will continue to support the process, including through financial and in-kind contributions to the osce special monitoring mission. also, the eu and its member states have contributed over eur 242 million in humanitarian and recovery aid, including eur 42 million provided by the commission to all affected populations, including refugees in russia and belarus. in parallel, the commission is engaging in trilateral talks on energy and on implementation of the deep and comprehensive free trade area. they are ensuring that gas supplies to and through ukraine remain uninterrupted during the winter season. they are also addressing russia’s concerns about the deep and comprehensive free trade area without amending or delaying the implementation of the agreement from 1 january onwards. eu relations with ukraine are developing dynamically despite the difficult realities of the conflict which its authorities and, above all, its people have to face. our goal remains to help them create a well-functioning state and a successful economy. just a few examples: the support group for ukraine continues to focus eu advice, technical assistance and financial resources on the ukrainian reform process; over six billion of the original eur 11 billion support package announced by the eu in march 2014 has already been mobilised to launch the reforms that will secure the future. the eu advisory mission to ukraine is doing important work to assist security-sector reforms. its mandate is currently under review to further streamline its activities toward ukraine’s most immediate needs. on visa liberalisation, we are moving towards the goal of visa-free travel for ukrainian citizens to the eu, an important step to enhance people-to-people contacts. further progress is needed, notably in the fight against corruption. to sum up, we have reason to be cautiously optimistic about progress on the diplomatic track if we remain united, and we will continue to support ukraine on its path to becoming a prosperous country. these are our joint objectives, and i look forward to working towards them together.
on behalf of the epp group. madam president, since the last debate we had on ukraine, there has been some progress. the first is, of course, the agreements on the withdrawal of several categories of weapons. that has brought a security boost and we have to acknowledge that. on the other hand, we have, of course, following the meeting that the commissioner mentioned, an important political agreement to cancel the elections scheduled for 18 october. holding this election would have greatly complicated the situation in the eastern territories. i think that in this context we should welcome the implementation, even if delayed, of the minsk agreements, while being aware, however, that the end of 2015 is a failure. the date will probably have to be extended in 2016. on the other hand, it should be noted that from a political point of view, kiev's trust in the moscow authorities has not increased. the messages that our friends, poroshenko and the others, are sending are not encouraging. that's why i think local elections are an important test; a test for central authorities, of course, but also an opportunity to show democratic commitment. i am glad that we will have a european parliament mission there and i think we do not need to talk at this moment about lifting sanctions.
despite our efforts, the european union's efforts, even more than a year after the ratification of the association agreement between the european union and ukraine, the situation in the area remains frozen. the situation is having a significant economic and political impact on eastern europe and i believe that the union's efforts to bring the situation to a final settlement must be stepped up. it is true that european diplomacy in general has made significant strides towards bringing ukraine onto the european path. from viktor yanukovych's political statements in 2011, when he told both the russian federation and the european union that "i am convinced that ukraine will be a member of the european union in about ten years", to the latest success of the negotiations between the european union and the russian federation, which last week led to the postponement of the 2016 elections that were to be held in the separatist republics of eastern ukraine, huge steps have been taken, indeed. still, it's not enough! as a representative of romania, a country in ukraine's neighbourhood, i believe that the short respite given by the postponement of elections in the separatist provinces must be used to the maximum to prevent the outbreak of a new conflict in this region. in practice, the holding and ratification of elections in the separatist provinces will also mean the de facto confirmation of the independence of these provinces from ukraine and will be the moment when conflict tensions will erupt. this is the moment when the european union should do everything in its power to prevent it, because if this frozen conflict re-emerges, this area of europe will become a hotbed of instability for many years to come, with incalculable consequences for the economies of the neighbouring eu member states.
madam president, as russia apparently cannot handle two conflicts at the same time, and the new priority is saving assad’s regime, it has decided finally to allow for the implementation of the minsk ii agreement – most probably in the hope that by starting to comply, sanctions would not be renewed at the end of the year. certainly, those sanctions are technically tied to the implementation of the minsk ii agreement, but one should not lose sight of the bigger strategic picture. that picture indicates not a change of heart on the part of russia, and even less a change in behaviour, but rather a shift of focus from eastern europe – with the exception of a moldova rocked by the demonstration of pro-moscow forces – to the middle east. as russia is simply demonstrating that it is acting strategically in geopolitical terms, the west’s response should be in similar terms.

in writing. ‒ the visa information system report established the vis as a system for the exchange of visa data between member states. the purpose of establishing this system is to improve the methods of implementing the common visa policy and to contribute to strengthening internal security and the fight against terrorism under clearly defined and supervised conditions. this initiative is thus a key point in the european union's policies for establishing an area of justice, freedom and security. another argument in favour of this system is the need for the competent services to have the most comprehensive and up-to-date information in their fields of competence in the fight against terrorism and other serious crime. it is therefore important to designate the competent authorities of the member states which are authorised to access the vis for specific purposes to prevent, detect and investigate terrorist offences. i voted in favour of this report because i believe it is essential to have clear policies that contribute to strengthening internal security and the fight against terrorism.
in writing. ‒ i agree with the rapporteur's position on access to the visa information system (vis) for consultation by the designated authorities of the member states and by europol for the purpose of preventing, detecting and investigating terrorist offences and other serious criminal offences.
in writing. ‒ this report represents the european parliament’s position on a draft council implementing decision which determines the date (1 september 2013) from which designated authorities and europol have access to the visa information system (vis) in accordance with council decision 2008/633/jha. this is the council’s second attempt to fix the date of effect of the council decision. its first attempt to fix the date of effect was successfully challenged by the european parliament before the court of justice of the european union because the council had failed to consult the parliament before adopting its implementing decision. the report itself is uncontroversial as the implementing decision merely confirms legally the date from which the member states’ designated authorities and europol have access to the vis under certain conditions, that access having already been established in the vis regulation and council decision 2008/633/jha. i therefore voted in favour of the report.
in writing. ‒ i support the council’s draft regarding the consultation of the vis by authorities of member states and by europol in order to prevent and counter terrorist offences and other serious criminal offences.
in writing. ‒ the visa information system (vis) allows schengen states to exchange visa data. it consists of a central it system and of a communication infrastructure that links this central system to national systems. i have voted for this report that has for its purpose to facilitate the checking and the issuance of visas, the fight against abuses, the protection of travellers, support with asylum applications and the enhancing of security.
in writing. ‒ this report represents the european parliament’s position on a draft council implementing decision which determines 1 september 2013, as the date from which designated authorities and europol have access to the visa information system (vis) in accordance with council decision 2008/633/jha. even though the council decision from 2008, laid down in articles 5 and 6, sets out the conditions under which the designated authorities in the member states and europol were entitled to have access to the vis, the exact date of effect of that decision was dependent on the full implementation of vis regulation (ec) 767/2008. as all the necessary procedures have now been complied with, it has become possible to fix the date of from which the member states’ designated authorities and europol have access to the vis under certain conditions. the current report, which i voted in favour of, legally confirms the chosen date of 1 september 2013.

in writing. ‒ climate change is currently a global threat that requires urgent attention, with irreversible potential for human societies and the biosphere. in this context, there is an urgent need to address this issue at international level. moreover, the seriousness of the threats posed by climate change should be a major concern, especially as the planet is far from limiting global warming to below 2 degrees celsius relative to pre-industrial levels. governments must take concrete and binding action to combat climate change and work towards a highly ambitious and legally binding agreement in paris in 2015. i voted in favour of the report on a new international paris agreement on climate change because the paris conference is not just a test meeting, but a decision meeting, and this conference symbolizes a decisive step in the negotiation of a new global climate agreement, which will enter into force in 2020.
in writing. ‒ the scenario of a race to the bottom for the most basic resources could become a reality in the near future, unless we implement concrete policies to combat climate change. i welcome the idea of a new international agreement on climate change, which would become effective and immediately applicable by reducing greenhouse gas emissions and keeping the temperature rise below 2°c. the imposition of emission restrictions on pollutants on states that did not have the same economic start as those that went through the industrial revolution is a constantly debated topic. but how much progress can we make if we don't have the resources and the environment to grow the economy? the answer can only be found in a circular and sustainable economy, as we have a moral duty to keep the planet functional for future generations. i believe that global solidarity is needed to achieve a new agreement on climate change and to take over the decisions taken without delay. i therefore support the pargneaux report on the proposed international paris agreement on climate change.
in writing. ‒ i believe that the european union must continue and intensify its diplomatic efforts to better understand the positions of partner countries, to encourage them to pursue ambitious policies to combat climate change and to build alliances in support of this ambition.
in writing. ‒ we are all aware of the fact that climate change is a reality: around the world, the impacts of climate change are accelerating, and the most vulnerable countries are already paying the higher price. last september, the conclusions of the intergovernmental panel on climate change were published, and the debate about the human influence on the climate is now over: we are responsible for warming the earth. luckily, next november is rapidly approaching. we have never had a better opportunity than the upcoming cop21 to tackle the tremendous danger of climate change. this is the greatest challenge that we must face: we must face it with the greatest ambition. next november, in paris, not only the european citizens, but more than 7 billion people will ask us to be brave and our choices to be bold. they will ask us to go beyond our differences and our doubts, and to chart a new course together. much has to be done in paris, but if we are able to make the climate agreement a reality, our generation will not be remembered as the one that destroyed the world, but as the one who finally came to respect it.
in writing. ‒ getting off coal as a source of electricity by 2030 would help to limit global warming considerably. however, the targets for the phase-out of coal are too steep and member states whose industries rely heavily on coal production will suffer both economically and in terms of employment. a programme of phasing out both fossil fuels and coal as a source of electricity should be initiated, along with a re-engineering to reduce emissions. in addition, there is no flexibility for member states to determine their own combination of different types of energy according to specific conditions.
in writing. ‒ the threats induced by climate change are serious and we must be concerned that the world is far from being on track to limit global warming. a stable climate system is important for food security, energy production, water and sanitation, and the preservation of biodiversity and terrestrial and marine ecosystems.

member of the commission.– mr president, i am here on behalf of my colleague, commissioner kristalina georgieva. the commission takes note of the proposal submitted by the committee on budgetary control to the plenary to grant discharge to the joint technology initiative on embedded computing systems (the artemis joint undertaking) and the joint technology initiative on nanoelectronics (eniac), the european institute of innovation and technology (eit), and to refuse discharge to the council for the financial year 2013. the commission is happy to note that parliament’s committee on budgetary control agrees that the ecsel joint undertaking (ju), which is the successor of artemis and eniac, has implemented actions to address the remarks of the budgetary authorities, and that it therefore proposes to grant discharge for the year 2013. eniac and artemis have convincingly demonstrated that public-private partnerships, using a tripartite model that pools together member state and eu funding with industrial investments, deliver important results such as leading edge low-power electronic chips and worldwide standards for software platforms for cars. these give industry in europe a clear competitive advantage and increase its capacity to grow, as was illustrated by the high industrial investment in these partnerships. both initiatives have had a very high leverage factor – every euro from the public side has resulted in an investment of at least eur 3 by industry in the two initiatives. eniac and artemis therefore provide a unique opportunity and an effective means for industry, member states and the eu to closely cooperate across europe. this creates a critical mass for electronic components and systems that is of vital importance for the digital future of europe. the initiatives have financed more than 3 000 of europe’s best engineers and researchers in the field every year. their work helps sustain at least 80 000 jobs in europe per year. in the horizon 2020 framework programme, eniac ju and artemis ju are merged in a new ju on electronic components and systems for european leadership (ecsel). in ecsel a structural solution is found for verifications and ex-post audits of new expenditure. in the draft resolution, the commission is asked to carry out an evaluation to assess the activities of eniac and artemis to be considered for the 2014 discharge exercise. the commission intends to reconcile this request with the ecsel regulation. the ecsel regulation provides that the commission will conduct an interim evaluation of ecsel that will include the final evaluation of eniac and artemis by 30 june 2017. to conduct separate evaluations on the very same projects would put a considerable administrative burden on the beneficiaries and the commission. finally, i would like to reiterate that the commission will provide advice and full support to ecsel in its continued efforts to address the concerns of the european parliament. the european institute of innovation and technology (eit) has made significant improvements in the areas identified in the april parliament decision. on the legality and regularity of its transactions, the eit has reformed its audit methodologies, the eit knowledge and innovation community grant guidelines and procurement capacities and procedures. as a result, the combined error rate for the 2014 grants is only 0.9%. the eit has also taken extensive measures to improve its planning and monitoring. finally, we would like to note that the winner of this year’s eit change award, mr govinda upadhyay, was selected as a finalist in the forbes’ 30 under 30 social entrepreneurs competition. this is precisely the kind of impact that the eit was designed to create. as for discharge to the council, the commission regrets that a suitable solution has not been found between the two arms of the budgetary authority in this dispute lasting now for six years. the commission considers that the institutions should cooperate for a smoother functioning of this procedure. the commission hopes that this issue will be solved in a suitable manner for both institutions.

madam president, there are many people who try to hide income for which they have not paid taxes or do not want to pay taxes in the future. that's what tax evasion is. it is estimated that at european level, one trillion euros are lost in this way. under the agreement signed this year, as of 2018, the european union and switzerland will automatically exchange information on the financial accounts of their residents. the information exchanged shall include revenue, interest, dividends, account balances and proceeds from the sale of financial assets. this report proposes concrete measures to combat tax evasion, in particular by natural and legal persons domiciled in the european union, with the participation of financial institutions established in third countries. the report suggests mandatory disclosure of the full name and registration code. this leads to absolute transparency and reduces the risk of tax fraud or evasion.
in writing. ‒ the eu-switzerland agreement on the automatic exchange of information on financial accounts was signed on 27 may 2015. this agreement plays a very important role at european level, because it improves cooperation in the tax field and brings the rules into compliance at international level. this agreement will be implemented from 2018 and seeks switzerland to apply enhanced measures equivalent to the eu directive and to comply with the automatic exchange of financial account information promoted by the 2014 global standards of the organisation for economic cooperation and development. by agreement, the financial administrations of the member states and switzerland will be able to correctly identify the taxpayers concerned and administer and enforce national tax laws. i voted in favour of this report because it is a mechanism to combat tax fraud and tax evasion which affects the economy of the european union and beyond.
in writing. ‒ i welcome the agreement signed on 27 may 2015 between the european union and switzerland on the automatic exchange of financial account information, which will improve international tax cooperation and compliance. switzerland is a key player and the agreement is a significant step in our efforts to clamp down on tax fraud and tax evasion. i believe that the automatic exchange on the financial accounts between the eu and switzerland, starting from 2018, will address situations where a taxpayer seeks to hide capital representing income or assets for which taxes have not been paid. also, i think it is very important that the agreement gives the ability to tax administrations in the member states and in switzerland to identify correctly the taxpayers concerned, as well as to administer and enforce their tax laws in cross-border situations. at the same time, i hope this will help authorities to better assess the likelihood of tax evasion being committed and, in some cases, stop unnecessary investigations.

in writing. ‒ the european union and switzerland signed an agreement on 27 may 2015 on the automatic exchange of financial account information, aimed at improving international tax cooperation and compliance. i voted for this report that will ensure that switzerland applies strengthened measures that are equivalent to the eu directive as upgraded in march 2014 and that it complies with the automatic exchange of financial account information promoted by the 2014 oecd global standards.
in writing. ‒ in order to effectively fight against fraud, tax avoidance and tax evasion, and to correctly limit those who would avoid paying the legal and proper taxes on their income, this report suggests a number of measures that i agree are necessary. it would extend to switzerland the strengthened measures to prevent fraudulent activities that are already applied in the eu, and would allow an automatic exchange of financial account information to prevent persons based in the eu from hiding their capital in the financial institutions of switzerland, exploiting its status as a non-member state. the oecd global standards that apply to this kind of information exchange would be respected in these cases, protecting the privacy of individuals who are adequately complying with union tax laws. additionally, this report provides a framework for preventing the use of non-member state financial institutions by eu-based persons and companies to avoid paying the appropriate taxes, which will need to be addressed in many countries, not only switzerland. again, i reiterate that steps need to be taken to continue to fight tax evasion and tax avoidance, and this report offers viable solutions.
in writing. ‒ the automatic exchange of information on financial accounts is a very important measure in the fight against tax evasion and a factor in increasing tax transparency. in this regard, since march 2015, there has been an ambitious proposal to establish an automatic exchange of financial account information between all member states of the european union, and in may 2015 an agreement was signed to this effect with switzerland, with the objective of improving tax cooperation and compliance. the commission notes that the swiss authorities have not provided any evidence that the taxpayer has not paid tax on the amount of the taxable income. the kofod report therefore intends to make certain improvements to this agreement in order to ensure maximum efficiency of this agreement. in this context, the report proposes: an unconditional exchange of information, the removal of the condition of exchange of information based on prior approval of the competent authorities, a quarterly frequency of exchanges. i therefore voted in favour of the kofod report on the automatic exchange of information on financial accounts between the eu and switzerland.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on the repeal of the savings tax directive because i believe that we need to have a tax economy that is as transparent and clear as possible. fair taxation is desired, both at european and international level. to achieve a healthy economy, we need sustainable economic growth, decreased inflation and poverty, both nationally and internationally, but these things can only be achieved through a simple, transparent and effective mechanism. the 2003 directive concerns the taxation of savings, requires the reporting of income in the form of interest on debt and applies to a large number of separate bilateral agreements between eu member states and overseas territories. this directive entered into force in 2005. the commission notes that the commission has not provided any evidence that the measure is compatible with the internal market. following the discussions, the commission proposed to repeal the 2003 directive so that member states avoid the inconvenience of dual data collection and reporting systems.
in writing. ‒ i support the need for the european executive to take the necessary measures to respect the time needed to review bilateral agreements between the eu and the five european non-eu countries (swiss confederation, principality of liechtenstein, republic of san marino, principality of monaco and principality of andorra) as well as with each of the member states and the 12 dependent or associated territories in order to avoid the emergence of loopholes for cross-border tax fraud and evasion or other inadvertencies in the transition to the new automatic exchange of information standard. i consider the role of parliament to be essential in the effort to reduce any possible loss of tax revenue by member states across the union.
in writing. ‒ i welcome the proposal to repeal the eu savings tax directive 2003/48/ec as we need to make sure that there is only one applicable standard for automatic exchange of information within the eu and to avoid any overlap between the savings directive and the amending directive on administrative cooperation that may result from their different approaches. whilst i support the repeal, i remain concerned about the potential for creation of loopholes if the separate bilateral agreements between the european union and five european countries that are not member states of the union (switzerland, liechtenstein, san marino, monaco and andorra) are not rapidly concluded. therefore, i consider it important that the commission report on the results of the repeal and on any potential loopholes that may arise, ensuring with all means that such loopholes are closed.
in writing. ‒ in 2003 the eu savings tax directive was adopted as a measure to ensure that tax is paid on the interest of savings, and the provisions became applicable in 2005. in the meantime the 2011 directive on administrative cooperation was revised to align it with the oecd’s global standard on automatic exchange of financial account information in tax matters and was adopted in 2014. i voted for this report that will repeal the 2003 savings tax directive so that member states do not have to apply the provisions in both directives, avoiding the inconvenience of double systems of collecting and reporting of data.
in writing. ‒ the directive on administrative cooperation that has been proposed by the commission seeks to update and simplify the taxation procedures that were applied according to the 2003 savings directive, a necessary process that has my support. part of this simplification involves fully repealing the prior legislation, as the contents have been renegotiated. if it is not repealed, there will be a period of double legislation. the commission should always seek to avoid such unnecessary and repetitive legislation, but in doing so there is a possibility of taxation loopholes opening up for this short period. this report proposes amendments that would ensure that the commission is closely monitoring the situation and reporting, under deadline, to the parliament and council on their findings. ultimately, i am in favour of legislation that seeks to limit burdensome bureaucracy, and this report does that while also respecting the important democratic role that the parliament plays in legislative decisions.
in writing. ‒ the 2003 eu savings tax directive was designed to ensure that tax is paid on the interest of savings. the directive was applied among eu countries and in separate agreements between eu countries and 12 overseas, and five non-eu european countries (switzerland, andorra, liechtenstein, monaco and san marino.) in 2014 the agreement was revised in order to tighten loopholes and align the directive with the oecd’s global standard. as part of its march 2015 tax transparency package, the commission proposed to repeal the 2003 savings tax directive, to enable member states to avoid the inconvenience of double systems of collecting and reporting of data. nevertheless, the repealing of an existing directive must take into consideration the need to uphold fair taxation across the eu. the current text gives consent to the proposed repeal, while asking the commission to monitor possible loopholes, use legislative proposals if needed to address them, and report back to the ep. i believe this report, which i voted in favour of, will address and reduce the risk of potential loss of tax revenue to member states across the eu.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the authorised exchange of data on dactyloscopic data from sweden because cross-border cooperation is very beneficial for the member states and is also beneficial for protecting national legislation and helps to eradicate terrorism as well as strengthening the rule of law. the commission decision implementing decision 2008/615/jha provides that the automatic exchange of data is to be carried out on the basis of an evaluation report based on a pilot test, a questionnaire drawn up by the working group and an evaluation visit, which is to be carried out by the audit. sweden has taken all the necessary steps, i.e. it has applied the data protection questionnaire and the questionnaire on the exchange of dactyloscopic data.
in writing. ‒ considering the need to step up cross-border cooperation, particularly in combating terrorism and cross-border crime, and to strengthen cross-border law-enforcement cooperation in the eu, i voted in favour of the report.
in writing. ‒ a vote adding sweden to the legal architecture of europe allowing the fighting of terrorism and organised crime while fully respecting human rights and the rule of law.
in writing. ‒ i voted for this report that will implement the council’s decision on the launch of automated data exchange with regard to dactyloscopic data in sweden.
in writing. ‒ ensuring the security of european citizens is one of the essential tasks of the european institutions. in order to achieve this, all necessary measures must be taken to avoid the risks inherent in the free movement of persons within the single european area enshrined in the schengen convention. at the same time, however, those measures must not lead to a restriction of the rights and freedoms of individuals, but must be implemented in full respect of european values. fingerprinting of persons entering the european area is one of those preventive measures necessary to ensure european security. although its application involves procedures more characteristic of the prevention of national and crossborder crime, its concrete results are likely to strengthen the database needed to prevent dangerous persons, for example terrorists, from gaining access to the european area. this does not, of course, preclude the entry of individuals who are not in the existing database, but it is a first step in prevention work. sweden is one of the countries affected by the phenomenon of extra-european migration which has intensified in recent months. in this context, closer cooperation with the other member states is needed to avoid the penetration of elements hostile to european values and of a terrorist nature.
in writing. ‒ the european parliament legislative resolution refers to the draft council implementing decision on the launch of automated data exchange with regard to dactyloscopic data in sweden. automated access to dactyloscopic data (fingerprints, latent fingerprints, etc.) is regulated in council decision 2008/615/jha on the stepping up of cross-border cooperation, particularly in the fight against terrorism and cross-border crime. the aim of this decision is to accelerate crossborder police and judicial cooperation between european union countries in criminal matters by improving the exchange of information between authorities with responsibilities for crime prevention and investigation. the launch of automated data exchange with regard to dactyloscopic data may only take place after the implementation of the general provisions on the protection of personal data in the national legislation of the member states. the verification of compliance with this condition shall be carried out on the basis of an evaluation report based on a questionnaire, an evaluation visit and a pilot test. those criteria have been successfully fulfilled by sweden, and the council has therefore given a favourable opinion to that country to receive and supply personal data for the purpose of automated searching of dactyloscopic data. by means of the legislative resolution, parliament approved this council decision.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the authorised exchange of data on dactyloscopic data from belgium because cross-border cooperation is very beneficial for protecting national legislation and helps both to eradicate terrorism and to strengthen the rule of law. the commission decision implementing decision 2008/615/jha provides that the automatic exchange of data is to be carried out on the basis of an evaluation report based on a pilot test, a questionnaire drawn up by the working group and an evaluation visit, which is to be carried out by the audit. belgium has taken all the necessary steps; it has thus applied the data protection questionnaire and the questionnaire on the exchange of dactyloscopic data and has carried out a pilot test together with france and luxembourg which was conclusive.
in writing. ‒ considering the need to step up cross-border cooperation, particularly in combating terrorism and cross-border crime, and to strengthen cross-border law-enforcement cooperation in the eu, i voted in favour of the report.

in writing. ‒ i voted for this report that will implement the council’s decision on the launch of automated data exchange with regard to dactyloscopic data in belgium.
in writing. ‒ the adoption of the schengen convention was one of the main achievements of the european integration process. ensuring freedom of movement at the level of the european union, including for nationals of the member states, is a sure win. however, the application of the provisions of the convention to the movement of persons, including third-country nationals, may raise a number of problems for ensuring european security. it is therefore necessary to take preventive measures, including fingerprinting and the exchange of such data between member states. the application of that measure must respect the rights and freedoms of citizens which are at the heart of the european construction. the admission of belgium to the list of member states which have adopted these measures is likely to contribute to the strengthening of european security. this is all the more so as belgium hosts the main european institutions, making a vital contribution to the smooth running of our work as members of the european parliament. for these reasons, i consider that the adoption of the present document is imperative and constitutes a step forward in strengthening european security.

in writing. ‒ the extension of the schengen convention to the member states of central and eastern europe was an important moment in the consolidation of european integration. the achievement of free movement within the european union is one of the key achievements of the european integration process. free movement of persons has enabled our citizens to move without restriction beyond the borders of their own countries and without being stopped by the borders of member countries. however, this freedom also entails a number of risks in terms of the movement of third-country nationals or immigrants from neighbouring countries, as has become apparent in recent times. for these reasons, the creation of a dactyloscopic database containing the fingerprints of those entering the european area has become an imperative measure. poland's joining the group of member states already applying these measures is an important step, extending the european security area to a significant part of central europe. therefore, the approval of this document is necessary to prevent the entry into the european area of individuals who may prove to be real threats to our citizens.

in writing. ‒ the considerable efforts made over the years in the union to strengthen the right to information of its citizens are steps that need to be supported by legislation in all areas of service provision. all the more reason to speak of transparency and fair information in the provision of services by private individuals to private individuals, since in this equation those who need protection are the recipients of services, and the union must provide them with an optimal framework in which to exercise their right to free movement, guaranteed by the eu treaties. i support the commission's position on how this framework for the operation of travel services will be secured and aligned with democratic norms, to protect those who use the services. i voted in favour of establishing fair trading practices by creating a legal framework whereby entities marketing their online services do not offer additional services in a hidden, unclear or ambiguous manner, such as by concealing the option not to book other additional services. i believe that only in this way can we speak of an effective right to information and of real transparency in the provision of services.
in writing. ‒ i support the draft legislative resolution of the ep on the council's first reading position with a view to adopting a directive of the european parliament and of the council on package travel and associated travel services, amending regulation (ec) no 2006/2004 and directive 2011/83/eu of the european parliament and of the council and repealing council directive 90/314/eec (09173/3/2015 c8-0281/2015 2013/0246 (cod)). the amendment to the regulation aims to modernise the rules on package travel, to include personalised combinations of travel services, in particular those purchased online, with the aim of increasing legal certainty and transparency for both travellers and businesses. another benefit is to reduce the harm to consumers by granting additional rights to terminate a contract and to establish stricter rules on price increases, while ensuring fairer competition between tourism businesses.
in writing. ‒ in a europe of free movement of citizens, guaranteeing their right to be well informed about the services they can benefit from while travelling in europe and beyond is necessary and beneficial for all parties. in addition, travellers should have access to adequate means of redress in the event of problems arising during the period of use of the services concerned, whether it is the journey as such or a stay, in particular in the case of services purchased on the internet.
in writing. ‒ the package travel proposal represents a positive solution for consumers and businesses. i strongly support more effective rules on insolvency protection for travellers in case of the trader’s insolvency; stricter liability of traders in case of underperformance of the package; improved pre-contractual information requirements and termination rights; and better protection in cases where the traveller’s return is impossible because of unavoidable and extraordinary circumstances. i believe that the compromise reached after a difficult negotiation regarding definitions of linked travel arrangements and travel packages represents a satisfactory result. it is very important that the definition of linked travel arrangements has been widened in order to ensure adequate protection for travellers. moreover, i welcome the obtaining by the european parliament of an appropriate review process by 2018 of these definitions by the european commission, accompanied if necessary by legislative proposals, in order to verify ‘whether an adjustment or broadening of the definition of travel packages is appropriate’.
in writing. ‒ i voted for this recommendation that will revise the commission staff working document entitled ‘guidance on the implementation/application of directive 2005/29/ec on unfair commercial practices’. the commission will inform parliament on how its views have been taken into account when the revised guidance is adopted.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this package as i believe it is in the interests of all europeans to have a streamlined, modern and secure legislation on travel packages and arrangements. tourism is one of the most stable and important sectors of the economy in all of the eu. tourist numbers are only increasing across the board and revenues made from this industry are helping to keep tens of thousands of families financed. as more and more packages are trans-border, as more intra-union and external travellers want to see more, to travel more, we need to have a full set of regulations that allow agencies, travel operators, transport companies and the tourists themselves a full range of options and modern terminology, protect their rights, ensure compensation and security and boost this sector of the economy. i believe this document makes an important step in this direction so i voted in its favour!
in writing. ‒ the communications sector has been a challenge for the european union in its efforts to create a common trading area and to give its citizens equal rights as consumers and beneficiaries of services. it is inconceivable in this century that european regulations do not include policies for standardising telephone and internet services, which are the most common means of communication between citizens of the union. i support these policies which provide for ensuring access to the open internet for all citizens and the elimination of all roaming charges on public mobile networks. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to cover the whole of the eu, including the eu's maritime borders, and to extend the scope of the directive to cover the whole of the eu's maritime borders. i voted in favour of achieving such objectives, considering that a transit framework needs to be created, and that this is achieved precisely by introducing harmonised rules guaranteeing access to the open internet, the protection of users' rights and the elimination of roaming surcharges.
in writing. ‒ given the importance of the implementation of the european single market for the deep development of all member states, i believe that the achievement of a european single market for electronic communications is in line with the principles of the union. in accordance with article 3 of the treaty on european union, the union is to establish an internal market. it works for the sustainable development of europe, based on balanced economic growth and price stability, a highly competitive social market economy aiming at full employment and social progress, and a high level of environmental protection and improvement. one of the essential things provided for in this article is the promotion of scientific and technical progress. i believe that this promotion can only be achieved in the context of a universal service within the eu that gives the same rights to users of communications telephony and the internet. i therefore support the second reading of the report on the single european electronic communications market.
in writing. ‒ i strongly support the long awaited abolition of roaming surcharges and the safeguards for net neutrality in eu law. this agreement will finally allow european customers to replicate their average mobile domestic consumption while periodically travelling in the union. this is the end of a long battle that we started many years ago to end eu roaming charges, to break the logic of artificial borders for mobile communications inside the european union, and to guarantee net neutrality by ensuring a strong open internet with non-discriminatory traffic, transparency and clear end-user rights. the result of our commitment is that mobile phone retail roaming surcharges for calls, sms and data within the eu will be abolished by 15 june 2017, provided that the wholesale prices review will be applicable on this date, and that the freedom and the right of european citizens to access or distribute internet content will no longer depend on the rules of the country in which they live.
in writing. ‒ i voted for a piece of legislation that will finally put an end to roaming charges and promote the principle of net neutrality in the rules that guide the management of internet traffic. it is a significant package that brings more freedom to european citizens. firstly, starting from 15 june 2017 we will be free to use our mobile phone anywhere in europe just as much as we do in our home country. secondly, it is about freedom to access legal internet content without discrimination and therefore keeping our internet open. this is an important step forward for our digital union.
in writing. ‒ i have voted for this recommendation that will introduce harmonised rules to safeguard open internet access, to protect users’ rights and to end roaming charges.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of a regulation on the regulation of the single telecoms market. this agreement marks the end of a long battle to end eu roaming charges, break the logic of artificial borders for mobile communications within the european union and guarantee network neutrality by ensuring a strong open internet with non-discriminatory traffic, transparency and clear rights for end-users. the surcharge for intra-eu roaming calls, sms and data will be eliminated by 15 june 2017, after a transition period from april 2016 to june 2017. as s&d coordinator for the itre commission i support the adoption of this regulation which is for the benefit of european citizens.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this text, despite the fact that it is far from perfect. yet i believe that the key provisions contained in here are not something we can afford to postpone for much longer. it is true that the successive negotiations on this have managed to both water down some of the important proposals concerning consumer protection and digital rights as well as to lessen the accuracy of the text. at the same time, even in its current state, the council position does indeed respect the key issue of a free internet, data roaming and the creation of a true european single digital and telecommunications market.
in writing. ‒ the right to physical and mental integrity is effectively guaranteed to every citizen of the union, but in order to be consistent and to continue the fight against torture and other inhuman punishment and treatment in practice throughout the world, we must ensure that the states with which the union cooperates also respect these democratic principles. this amendment to the regulation ensures our consistency as institutions of this union and our willingness to continue the fight by introducing controls at the eu's external borders, precisely to prevent the export of possible items with potentially lethal and inhumane uses. i voted in favour of the report on both the prohibition of trade in 'single-use' goods and related technical assistance intended for torture and execution and an authorisation system for 'multi-purpose' goods that could be used for torture and executions by lethal injection. i am confident that there will continue to be the closest possible collaboration between all the committees involved in strengthening regulation (ec) no 1236/2005, so that the eu's objectives of protecting human dignity and life, enshrined in both the lisbon treaty and the charter of fundamental rights of the european union, are also achieved and respected beyond its borders.
in writing. ‒ in the context of a european single market and the globalisation of trade transactions, which are becoming increasingly complex, eu controls on the trade in instruments of torture are proving to be extremely important. on the other hand, the european parliament's efforts to prevent torture contribute primarily to the protection of human rights. the role of the member states is also vital, with a need to monitor the implementation of member states' commitments and their reporting and information exchange obligations. i believe that it is necessary to ensure the consistency of eu export controls so that products do not suffer from a duplication of controls, but the checks and, if necessary, the sanctions, must be effectively complied with.
in writing. ‒ i fully support the revision of this regulation which aims to contribute to the elimination of the death penalty worldwide and prevent torture through eu-wide controls on exports of torture goods and drugs used for lethal injection. the revision includes adding export licencing controls for lethal drugs and prohibiting trade in new items which have become regularly used for torture by certain regimes such as spiked batons, electric shock sleeves and cuffs for example. the so call ‘catch all clause’ will make it boundary for customs authorities to seize any good, whether listed in the regulation annexes or not, if there are reasonable grounds to believe that its final use will be for the purpose of torture. finally, i welcome the establishment of a union general export authorisation for countries that have undertaken firm international commitments and the use of urgency procedure to amend the lists of banned/controlled items, which will allow the eu to react more quickly to emerging trends and human rights crackdowns in the future.
in writing. ‒ i welcome the revision of the eu ‘anti-torture regulation’ which will make it more effective in preventing export of goods which could be used for torture, death penalty and other inhuman treatments. i support the extension of the scope of the regulation so as to include services related to the export of ‘torture goods’ such as marketing, transport, insurance and financial services; the ban of transit of ‘torture-goods’ via the eu and the introduction of a ‘catch-all’ clause which would impose authorisation requirements for other goods not included in the relevant annexes to the regulation but whose use could be suspicious. a more effective anti-torture regulation will not only better reflect the eu values as embedded in the eu charter of fundamental rights but will also enable us to more coherently export such values to the rest of the world.
in writing. ‒ i have voted for this report, which will contribute to the long—standing eu policy of eliminating the death penalty worldwide and of preventing torture. it will achieve these goals by combining prohibitions with licensing requirements for trade in listed goods.

in writing. ‒ this report is asking to revise the current regulation, aiming to contribute to the efforts to eliminate death penalty worldwide and prevent torture through eu-wide controls on exports of torture goods and drugs, which are used for lethal injection. this revision includes adding export licencing controls for lethal drugs and prohibiting trade in new items which have become regularly used for torture by certain regimes, such as: spiked batons, electric shock sleeves and cuffs, to name few examples. i welcome the enlarged scope of the report that expends the list of medical products from being used for capital punishment by lethal injection. i also welcome the establishment of a union general export authorisation for countries that have undertaken an urgency procedure to amend the lists of banned, or controlled items, which will allow the eu to react more quickly to emerging trends and human rights crackdowns in the future. the eu has been advocating the elimination of the death penalty around the world for many years. this report, which i voted in favour of, represents a very positive step in our efforts to achieve this goal.
in writing. ‒ the abolition of the death penalty and of inhuman and degrading treatment is one of the priorities of the eu's human rights policy. regulation (ec) no 1236/2005 lays down community rules governing trade with third countries in goods which could be used for capital punishment, torture and other inhuman or degrading treatment or punishment, and technical assistance for the use of such goods. the review of eu controls on trade in torture equipment has been long overdue, and the updates of the checklists are steps in the right direction. the european parliament report supports the revision of regulation (ec) no 1236/2005, stressing the importance of the strictest possible controls on those goods and products that could be used for torture or capital punishment. this review will allow us to ensure that there is protection of the right to life and prevention of torture. at the same time, we will be able to know whether products are used for legitimate purposes or for other purposes, such as medical. i voted in favour of this resolution.
in writing. ‒ the european parliament's draft legislative resolution on the mandatory automatic exchange of information in tax matters envisages establishing the scope and conditions for the mandatory automatic exchange of information on cross-border tax rulings. the issue of tax fraud and evasion has always been a challenge for the european union, and joint action aimed at effective communication between member states on their tax decisions is needed. at present, administrative cooperation in the field of taxation is deficient, with member states neglecting the responsibility for transmitting tax decisions, which has a negative impact on the union's fight against tax fraud. i believe that transparency in the tax decisions taken by member states should guide the fight against tax evasion, and that a permanent, prompt and transparent exchange of information between member states is necessary, which is why i voted in favour of the draft legislative resolution on the mandatory automatic exchange of information in tax matters, considering it appropriate in view of the current challenges.
in writing. ‒ i support the rapporteur's proposal for an efficient exchange of information and efficient processing of tax information between member states, but there are still a number of important practical difficulties, such as the discretion of the issuing member state to decide which other member states should be informed. in addition, the monitoring system is not sufficiently efficient, which makes it more difficult for the commission to identify any breach of the requirement to exchange information on advance cross-border rulings and advance pricing arrangements.
in writing. ‒ i would like to congratulate the rapporteur on the proposal for a council directive amending directive 2011/16/eu as regards mandatory automatic exchange of information in the field of taxation. the challenges posed by cross-border tax avoidance, aggressive tax planning and harmful tax competition should be indeed one of the eus concerns. therefore, i strongly support the call to increase transparency and to fight against all the earlier mentioned challenges by extending the scope of the directive to all tax rulings and not just to the cross border ones. in order to increase effectiveness, the commission shall develop a secure central directory where information to be communicated in the framework of this directive must be recorded in order to satisfy the automatic and mandatory exchange of information. in case of member states non-compliance, i welcome the proposal to introduce sanctions and establish penalties for refusal or omission of information exchange. also, in order to increase the directive’s efficiency, i believe that the publication of a summary containing the main tax rulings exchanged is necessary.
in writing. ‒ yet another vote completing the legal architecture of europe allowing the disciplining of financial transactions and limiting the scope for tax evasion and fraud.
in writing. ‒ the challenge posed by cross-border tax avoidance, aggressive tax planning and harmful tax competition has increased considerably and has become a major focus of concern within the union and at global level. i have voted for this report that will introduce a new article into the existing directive, setting out the scope and conditions for the mandatory automatic exchange of information on types of cross-border tax rulings and transfer pricing arrangements.
in writing. ‒ to combat tax evasion and tax avoidance, in light of the fact that legal personalities can take advantage of differences in tax rates and tax bases in different member states, it is necessary that the member states work together and share information. the commission has proposed that any rulings that relate to cross-border transactions must be securely shared among the member states, so that exploitation or other negative effects can be more easily discovered and prevented. cross-border rulings that have occurred in the last 10 years should also be shared, so that any recent indiscretions can be duly handled. this proposal is an excellent start to limiting the manipulation of tax laws, and takes great strides to improve transparency and communication between member-states. though there are further strides still to be taken in the fight against fraud and tax evasion, this is a definite step in the right direction for the european union, a step that will benefit the tax revenue of each individual member state.
in writing. ‒ increasing transparency and fighting against aggressive tax planning is one of the issues the parliament has taken the lead on. the current legal framework (directive 2011/16/eu), gives member states the discretion to decide whether a tax ruling might be relevant to another eu country. this creates a situation where a member state can issue tax rulings without being aware to other tax rulings issued elsewhere in the eu, which may impact their own tax bases. moreover, as the information exchanged between the member states is very limited and not mandatory, we are falling short from creating a more transparent and responsible tax regime. amending this current legal framework will increase required transparency. the current report supports the commission's proposal, which sets the scope and conditions for mandatory automatic exchange of information on types of cross-border tax rulings and transfer pricing arrangements. the parliament calls to extend the scope of the directive to all rulings, exchange all valid tax rulings already before the entry into force of the directive, and introduce sanctions in case of non-compliance. the adoption of this report will prevent companies from exploiting loop holes to artificially reduce their tax contribution, therefore i voted in favour of it.
in writing. ‒ the proposal for a council directive amending directive 2011/16/eu as regards the mandatory automatic exchange of information in tax matters provides that all tax rulings of a member state which have a cross-border dimension are to be made available to the other member states through an automatic exchange of information. the european parliament's report supports the commission's proposal, introducing a number of improvements in terms of the scope of mandatory exchange of information, the way decisions are communicated and transparency towards citizens. the european parliament wants to send a clear message by voting in favour of transparency, clarity and fair tax competition in the european union.
in writing. ‒ the budgetary report for the financial year 2013 of the artemis joint undertaking shall exhaustively present its financial situation as at 31 december 2013, presenting both the results of its operations and its cash flows, in accordance with the provisions of its financial rules. however, i cannot but be concerned by the court of auditors' reservations on the legality and regularity of the subsidiary operations to the annual accounts, given that the joint undertaking has failed to assess whether the ex post audit strategy is a sufficiently valid instrument to ensure the legality and regularity of the underlying operations. in response to the court of auditors' concerns, the joint undertaking submitted an action plan setting out measures to address the identified deficiencies, which is why i voted in favour of the discharge report on the implementation of the artemis joint undertaking's budget for the financial year 2013, believing that these deficiencies will be addressed as a result of the action plan.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the discharge of the artemis joint undertaking for the financial year 2013. following a consensual compromise between the political groups, the agreement was voted by a large majority.
in writing. ‒ i have voted for his report that will further support artemis joint undertaking (‘the joint undertaking’) which was initially set up in december 2007 for a period of 10 years to define and implement a ‘research agenda’ for the development of key technologies for embedded computing systems across different application areas in order to strengthen union competitiveness and sustainability and to allow for the emergence of new markets and societal applications.
in writing. ‒ the artemis joint undertaking was set up in 2007 for a period of 10 years to define and implement a 'research agenda' for the development of key technologies for integrated information systems in different application sectors. the objective of artemis is to strengthen competitiveness and sustainability within the union and to facilitate the emergence of new markets and applications in society. in 2014, artemis and the eniac joint undertaking merged to create the electronic components and systems for european leadership (ecsel) joint technology initiative, which will continue for 10 years. the total financial contributions from the artemis member states should be at least 1,8 times the union financial contribution and the in-kind contribution of the research and development organisations participating in projects during the lifetime of the joint undertaking should be equal to or higher than the contribution of the public authorities. as vice-chair of the committee on budgetary control and as s&d coordinator for the committee on industry, research and energy, i am in favour of granting discharge to the artemis joint undertaking in respect of the implementation of the budget for the financial year 2013.
in writing. ‒ this report recommends granting discharge to the director of the artemis joint undertaking for the financial year 2013. with this text, the parliament recognizes that the artemis ju has taken the necessary steps requested to redress the shortcomings the parliament committee on budgetary control (cont) identified, particular, the fact that artemis ju failed to respect the 2014 recommendations of the discharge authority, by not adopting a comprehensive policy for the prevention and management of conflict of interests. however, following the revised report submitted by the director of artemis to cont, on june 2015, the committee decided that improvements have been made, i.e. in the ex post audits and audit strategies, the progress in managing the assurances provided by national funding authorities as well as on development of new methodology for residual error rate estimation. i agree with the committee’s decision to grant discharge to artemis, and therefore i voted in favour of the report in plenary.
in writing. ‒ the budget report for the financial year 2013 of the european institute of innovation and technology (eit) shall present in a comprehensive manner the financial situation of the eit up to 31 december 2013, showing both the results of its operations and its cash flows, in accordance with the provisions of its financial rules. following the court of auditors' report, reasonable assurances were obtained regarding the reliability of the institute's annual accounts, but, similar to the situation of the artemis joint undertaking, sufficient audit evidence regarding the legality and regularity of the underlying transactions could not be obtained. however, the european institute of innovation and technology provided enhanced guidance to the certification auditors in june 2013, also providing guidance to the knowledge and innovation communities, the beneficiaries of the institute's grants. as a result, there is an improvement in the level of insurance obtained. i conclude by pointing out that the institute's efforts during the financial year 2013 resulted in a budget execution rate of 96,97% and that the execution rate of payments in respect of payment appropriations was 96,86%, which is why i voted in favour of the discharge report for the implementation of the budget of the european institute of innovation and technology for the financial year 2013.
in writing. ‒ the european institute of innovation and technology (eit) has a vital importance in terms of delivering the goals of the eu’s policies to promote technology and innovation. eit management has shown a clear improvement in their shortcomings. this report aims at redressing the identified shortcomings in the discharge to the director of the eit for the financial year 2013. i welcome the many improvements of the eit’s report that make it possible for us to endorse the discharge, such as the newly introduced complementary ex-ante verifications for grant expenditure, which added a second layer of assurance on the legality and regularity of grant transactions; the redesigned procurement procedures since 2013 with a proactive approach towards the detection of errors; the obtainment of the audit certificates on the costs of eit’s beneficiaries; and the review of the portfolio of beneficiaries’ complementary activities.
in writing. ‒ i have voted for this report on the 2013 discharge of the european institute of innovation and technology that starting from 2014 uses the same audit certificate methodology as all other programmes under the horizon 2020 framework programme.
in writing. ‒ this report recommends granting discharge to the director of the european institute of innovation and technology (eit) for the financial year 2013. with this text, the parliament recognises that the eit has taken the necessary steps requested to redress the shortcomings the parliament committee on budgetary control (cont) identified related to the combined error rate on the audit issues and material procurement errors between 2% and 3% of total 2013 expenditure, which is above the materiality threshold of 2%, the insufficient quality of ex ante and ex post verifications as well as irregular public procurement procedures. however, following the progress report published by the eit on 29 july, 2015, the committee decided that improvements have been made, i.e. newly introduced complementary ex-ante verifications for grant expenditure, redesigned procurement procedures since 2013 with a proactive approach towards the detection of errors; improved the planning and monitoring procedures related to the budget implementation which include a more rigorous assessment of activities, increased absorption capacity of the first-wave beneficiaries and introduction of additional second wave beneficiaries. the eit management has shown the clear improvement in the shortcomings identified by cont, therefore i voted in line with cont's decision to grant discharge to eit for 2013.
