in writing. ‒ i have voted for this report on the 2013 discharge of the european union’s general budget.
in writing. ‒ the discharge report of the european council and council in the financial year 2013 repeats similar trends from past years, regarding the budgetary transparency of the council. since 2009, the council refused to provide information on its dealing with finances, particularly on its increasing underspending and carry—overs of commitments in their 2013 budget. the current report reminds the council that all institutions are fully part of the follow-up process to the observations made by parliament in the discharge exercise, and that all eu institutions should cooperate to ensure the smooth functioning of the discharge procedure. it further emphasises the parliament’s prerogative to grant discharge to each heading of the budget individually in order to maintain transparency and democratic accountability towards taxpayers. lastly, the report insists that the expenditure of the council must be scrutinised in the same way as that of other institutions and that the fundamental elements of such scrutiny have been laid down in its discharge resolutions of the past years. i believe it is unacceptable for the council to conduct itself in such matter, particularly in the post lisbon treaty, when the parliament's powers have increased. this is why i voted against granting discharge to the council in 2013.
in writing. ‒ the ebola outbreak first appeared in sierra leone, liberia and guinea, the most affected countries, where life expectancy is less than 60 years, schooling rarely exceeds three years and about 80% of the population lives in extreme poverty. these indicators show the vulnerability of the populations in these states who cannot get through this crisis on their own. the european parliament has the task of overseeing the executive, acting as legislator and providing political impetus as a world leader in development. it also has a special responsibility in promoting the right to universal access to health care. the current ebola crisis has highlighted the structural weaknesses that persist in some countries, but at the same time it underlines the need for eu leaders to meet their targets of allocating at least 20% of public aid to the development of basic social sectors, giving priority in particular to health. that is why i voted in favour of the report, wanting to show solidarity with the states affected by this devastating virus.
in writing. ‒ the ebola crisis was possible due to shortcomings in the health systems of the affected countries, and has therefore both highlighted the structural problems that are still to be found in a number of countries and served as a reminder to eu leaders of the need for them to stay true to their goal of allocating at least 20% of official assistance to the development of basic social services, giving priority to healthcare. in the future, we must make sure that our investments are carefully planned and are targeting the real needs. we need to start discussing the ways in which the best use can be made of the humanitarian organisations’ capabilities in the future. moreover, it will be vital for the three countries to receive aid with a view to kick-starting their economies. all actors involved must demonstrate the vision and assume their responsibilities in the next months, even though ebola faded from the news headlines a long while ago.
in writing. ‒ since march 2014, sierra leone, liberia and guinea have been in the grip of the worst ever ebola crisis. i have voted for this report that will press ahead with its efforts to stop the development of this epidemic.
in writing. ‒ it is estimated that the latest ebola outbreak claimed the lives of at least 11 312 people and infected over 28 457 persons. liberia, sierra leone and guinea suffered the most from the crisis. but that, unfortunately, is not surprising. these three countries are at the bottom of the undp human development index. moreover, they are home to some of the worst-funded education and healthcare systems in the world, making the scale of the ebola epidemic a real challenge. the current report highlights the role of the eu, as a world leader on development, when it comes to promoting the right to universal healthcare. it emphasizes the eu’s leading role in providing development aid to these countries, in order to help revive their economy and support the development of basic social services - with healthcare as a priority. although ebola faded from the news headlines a long while ago, this current report, which i voted in favour of, highlights the structural problems that are still found in a number of countries and the responsibilities that still need to be fulfilled in the post-ebola period.
in writing. ‒ in 2014, west africa experienced the largest ebola outbreak in history, affecting over 20 000 people mainly in guinea, liberia and sierra leone, before spreading to other continents where isolated cases were reported. this ebola crisis has highlighted the shortcomings of health systems, especially in these countries, which do not have enough resources to have a robust and effective health system. moreover, this crisis has led to increased political instability and social and economic tensions in the affected countries. the efforts of the eu and other international actors involved in this crisis have led to progress at european and international level, but have not been sufficient to eradicate the ebola epidemic once and for all. in this context, a european strategy is needed to improve coordination and cooperation between eu countries in the fight against this epidemic, to increase protection at european level, and to support developing countries in their efforts to build up effective health systems. i therefore voted in favour of the goerens report on the ebola crisis and the long-term lessons.
in writing. ‒ i support the rapporteur's proposal for the commission to present a new design of the current type-approval regime to ensure, on the one hand, that type-approvals and certificates of conformity issued by the competent national authorities can be independently verified and re-evaluated by the commission, where appropriate, with a view to ensuring a level playing field at eu level, and, on the other hand, that eu regulations are effectively implemented and deficiencies in the implementing measures are corrected without the necessary increase in administrative burden.
in writing. ‒ such frauds as the one exposed by the volkswagen scandal are truly unacceptable: an action against health and the environment that can neither be tolerated nor forgiven. while we were investing a huge amount of money in technological development for a low carbon footprint we were neither improving nor harmonising our emissions testing adequately to safeguard us from being fooled by these cheaters. it is absolutely necessary for the commission to investigate any kind of manipulation in this sector, to standardise emission testing at the level of the 28 member states, to cooperate with nation states to improve their monitoring capacity, and to make all possible efforts to avoid this kind of situation in the future.
in writing. ‒ i fully supported a resolution that denounces an outright breach of eu environmental regulations and the manipulation of millions of consumers. the volkswagen scandal signals the need for a tighter approach to implementing car emissions regulations in europe. such fraudulent behaviour puts at risk global confidence in the product of an industry that provides europe with countless jobs in times of still-sluggish economic growth. the answer for more competitiveness must lie in more innovation, not in deceiving consumers.
in writing. ‒ i have voted for this resolution that will establish a committee of inquiry to investigate the respective responsibility of the commission and of member state authorities for the failure to ensure the proper implementation and enforcement of the relevant eu law on emission measurements in the automotive sector.
in writing. ‒ the automotive industry is one of the main drivers of growth and innovation and contributes to employment in a significant number of member states. if decisive action is not taken, this scandal risks undermining the reputation and competitiveness of the entire eu automotive sector. we call on the commission and the member states to immediately launch an investigation into the use of handling devices (in relation to both the emission limit values and the advertised co2 level in g/km) for a wide range of vehicle makes and models. the survey should be carried out on the basis of data collected and transmitted by the approval authorities of the member states for vehicles on the market, using real-world driving tests. member states and the commission need to restore consumer confidence quickly through concrete measures. we therefore call on the commission to come forward with a legislative proposal for an eu-wide collective action mechanism so that consumers can have recourse to collective actions. we urge companies to take full responsibility for their actions, stressing that employees do not have to pay the price for the manipulation of emissions measurement devices. as s&d coordinator for the committee on industry, research and energy, i voted in favour of the resolution on emission measurement in the motor vehicle sector.
in writing. ‒ the deliberate cheating of tests and sale of vast numbers of vehicles making false claims about their performance has left consumers’ confidence in the car industry badly damaged. the commission should look seriously at a robust, centralised test procedure which creates a level playing field for car manufacturers, ensures proper implementation of pollution laws, and restores consumers’ confidence in this industry.
in writing. ‒ the recent emissions scandal not only highlights the need for robust rules on competition among car manufacturers but, more importantly, it makes the case for the eu to update its testing procedures. tests carried out by the eu's joint research centre (jrc) and other independent ngos clearly point to weaknesses in the current procedures. according to the jrc, real-world nitrogen oxides (nox) emissions of diesel passenger cars exceed two to five times the regulatory standards. considerable discrepancies exist between type-approval and on-road co2 emissions as well. this gap is due to the current eu test procedures, which do not use normal driving conditions and allow for undue ‘testing optimisation’ – a form of cheating all manufacturers resort to. if we do not urgently adopt a real-life emissions test cycle for all major pollutants, not only will we keep denying our citizens their right to be adequately informed, but we will also work against our goals on the protection of public health and the environment.
in writing. dieselgate, which began in early october, is forcing us to discuss an issue that has long been on the public agenda but has been ignored. i voted for the european parliament resolution following the debate on the falsification of car emissions tests by a car manufacturer. although the problem is limited to one player in this market, consumer confidence has been severely affected and is spilling over to the whole industry. technologies like diesel are now under public scrutiny, though the problem is unethical business practices. parliament urges the implementation of a new testing protocol, the so-called wltp, in 2017. the wltp is a necessary step to ensure that the consumption and emissions figures produced are representative for a given category of motor vehicles. the same should apply to compliance checks carried out by independent bodies. if they differ from those of the certification authorities of the member states, car manufacturers should be required to change their declared figures. but most importantly, we need to have a european certification authority. this ensures that certification procedures and standards are applied in the same way in all member states.
in writing. we welcome the adoption of the commission's work programme and look forward to concrete proposals for the implementation of the digital single market strategy so that it becomes fully operational. as regards energy, i would stress that the energy union must have at its core an efficient and functioning internal energy market, which ensures economic growth, jobs, affordable and competitive prices for individual and industrial consumers, and the protection of vulnerable consumers. the european commission and the council will set the governance framework after 2020 and must ensure that all legislative proposals forming part of the energy union follow the ordinary legislative procedure, thus fully involving the european parliament. the commission should present an annual report on the implementation of the energy union, including details on the implementation of energy legislation. i regret that the commission has not so far come forward with any proposal for a harmonised scheme for the compensation of indirect carbon emissions, which is now left to the member states. it would also be important to have a european action plan on energy poverty.

in writing. the commission proposal is not clear at all and thus jeopardises the proper functioning of the internal market. the commission is to present a new proposal to allow member states to restrict the use of genetically modified food and feed on their territory. the current proposal not only lacks an impact study, but also fails to meet mr juncker's original commitment to review the existing procedural rules for the authorisation of gmos so that the commission is no longer able to authorise gmos when a clear majority opposes it. the commission should propose a revision of the rules for the authorisation of gmos in europe to reflect the position of eu citizens. it should no longer be possible to authorise new gmos for cultivation or import into the union until this promise is fulfilled.
rapporteur for the opinion of the committee on agriculture and rural development. mr president, first of all i would like to congratulate the rapporteur and the shadow rapporteurs on their efforts to reach an agreement on novel foods. the simplification and improvements to the current text, by means of generic authorisation, shortening the authorisation period and facilitating the addition to the list of novel foods of products considered traditional in third countries, are welcomed. but at the same time, i want to reiterate that food innovation must be encouraged, but not at the expense of safety and health. i am also glad that this dossier has been dealt with separately from the one on cloning, but i hope that at the same time the commission and the council will find a way to address parliament's requests for the proper regulation of food from cloned animals. i do not want this agreement on novel foods to lead to the hesitation and even the abandonment of specific regulation of food derived from cloned animals.
in writing. i believe that there is an absolute need for transparent and clear legislation on novel foods. the free movement of novel foods which are safe for the health of consumers is an essential aspect of the progress of the european market. i am not against novel foods which have the capacity to provide a high level of protection of the health of the population, especially children, but i would like to point out the need to implement eu legislation on these foods which, in my view, must comply with stricter rules than classical or traditional foods. i welcome eu legislation on novel foods or foods produced using new technologies and production processes. the eu has a moral and legal obligation to establish clear information rules whereby food manufacturers inform consumers as thoroughly as possible about the technologies used and the origin of the raw materials used to obtain these novel foods.
in writing. ‒ the eu general budget for the financial year 2016 proposes to reduce the amount to be reallocated from a number of budget lines under horizon 2020 and the connecting europe facility. the result will be an increase of eur 153 million in commitment appropriations for horizon 2020 and eur 150 million in appropriations for the connecting europe facility. in the current context, account must be taken of a financial effort to address the shortcomings of the european union's economy, but also of the challenges it faces: migration and the refugee crisis, the actions to be taken on the farmer crisis, job growth, the key role played by micro-enterprises and smes, but also the commitment to reduce the outstanding payment arrears for the 2007-2013 cohesion programmes to around eur 2 billion by the end of 2016. i voted in favour of this proposal because it increases funding on lines such as: migration and asylum, erasmus plus, boosting innovation for smes, the eu's smart external borders, programmes that lay the foundations for a prosperous european union with the lowest unemployment rate.

in writing. ‒ i support the introduction of the review clause and of gender balance, and the increase in the number of judges in the general court to 28. it is absolutely necessary to ensure the functioning of the european judiciary. member states could not agree on criteria as simple as merit: they insisted on their national interests. this comes at a high price for citizens, but the price for a dysfunctional judiciary would even be higher. therefore we should accept their agreement, but insist on overcoming discrimination: it is about time that both genders were equally represented in european courts.
in writing. ‒ i voted against the doubling of the number of judges at the general court of the european union because, in reality, this measure is not necessary, as it seems to be the wish of some member states. do we really want trials to be faster and more efficient? the solution is to hire more referees and clerks in the judges' offices, because they're the ones who do the research and documentation for the judges' decisions. the numbers don't lie. the hiring of more secretaries in 2014 halved the processing time of one case. why, then, do we need to double the number of judges and not hire more secretaries? the president of the general court also requested the council to increase the number of auxiliary staff in december 2014. i ask that the allegations of possible secret correspondence between the president of parliament and the president of the court of justice and the other allegations mentioned in the letter received by all meps from a group of university professors be investigated.
in writing. ‒ in 2011, the court of justice of the european union (cjeu) launched a legislative initiative to change its status to allow the appointment of 12 more judges to the general court. i voted for this proposal, which will increase the number of judges at the cjeu.
in writing. ‒ i voted against this report, even though the coordinator of this dossier is a colleague from the alde group and the committee on fisheries, because i do not consider it necessary to increase the number of judges in the court of justice of the eu. the justification given, that of increased responsibilities and therefore increased workload for judges, was not a reasonable one in my view, given that each judge has less than 60 cases per year to judge. the court of justice has also established that the principle of proportionality is not infringed by the principle of proportionality. in these circumstances, i believe that the number of auxiliary staff should have been increased, because they are the ones who will actually have an increased workload.
in writing. ‒ in order to ensure the most comprehensive legislative framework for fisheries, the european parliament and the council agreed to transpose into union law a series of recommendations made by the general fisheries commission for the mediterranean (gfcm agreement). this agreement provides for an appropriate framework for multilateral cooperation to promote the development, conservation, rational management and optimal use of living marine resources in the mediterranean and black seas at levels considered to be sustainable and with a low risk of depletion. the gfcm recommendations provide for a number of measures to improve the existing framework, including measures on the sustainable exploitation of red coral in the commission's area of competence, measures to reduce incidental catches of seabirds, sea turtles, monk seals and cetaceans in fisheries in the gfcm agreement area, and measures to ensure a high level of protection against shark and catfish fishing. i voted in favour of the recommendation on amending regulation (eu) no 1343/2011 on certain provisions relating to fishing in the gfcm agreement area as these regulations are to provide the fisheries sector with a consolidated regulatory framework geared to all sectors of activity.
in writing. ‒ regulation (eu) no 1343/2011 had to be amended to incorporate conservation and control measures adopted by the general fisheries commission for the mediterranean (gfcm). measures include provisions for the sustainable exploitation of red coral, the mitigation of incidental captures of seabirds, sea turtles, monk seals and cetaceans, the protection of sharks and rays, and the extension of some technical measures to the black sea as well as management measures for fisheries exploiting small pelagic stocks in the adriatic sea.
in writing. ‒ i voted for this report, which will provide an appropriate framework for multilateral cooperation to promote the development, conservation, rational management and best utilisation of living marine resources in the mediterranean and the black sea at levels which are considered sustainable and at low risk of collapse.
in writing. ‒ i voted today in favour of my colleague's report in the committee on fisheries because it is a good report that has been negotiated with council representatives for a long time and i have therefore had the opportunity to support my amendments during the procedure. the final form of these negotiations, the document voted on today, is one that meets the needs of the general fisheries commission for the mediterranean for the conduct of its work. it is also very important that this document also contains an exceptional derogation for romania regarding the use of trawls and seines in the black sea fishing activities, which would have had a major negative impact on the romanian industry. this derogation was possible because the main reasons why the use of trawls and seines should be restricted, although they apply to the mediterranean sea, do not apply to the black sea.
in writing. ‒ fishing in the mediterranean is one of the european union's major economic activities. regulation of this activity constitutes the main task of the general fisheries commission for the mediterranean, as laid down in the agreement adopted in 2011. these regulations now need to be amended to incorporate a number of measures to conserve and control marine habitats, including the protection of certain species of birds, turtles, seals, cetaceans and sharks. specifically, the use of trawls and seines in the black sea fisheries, which is included in the tasks of the general commission, the minimum basal diameter of colonies, fishing gear and devices, and the harvesting of red coral are concerned. however, the text adopted by the commission also accepted a number of derogations concerning trawling for a limited number of vessels and the use of remotely controlled underwater vehicles in the coastal areas of the black sea, unlike the mediterranean sea, where this is not allowed. however, these derogations will not act as a precedent for other situations and will be closely monitored by the general commission. the present amendment is a necessary measure to update the regulations in this area.
in writing. ‒ on 22 april 2015, the commission presented, together with the communication on 'review of the decision-making process on genetically modified organisms', a proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council amending regulation (ec) no 1829/2003 as regards the possibility for member states to restrict or prohibit the use of genetically modified food and feed on their territory after such products have been authorised - opt-out - (com2015) 177). in view of the absence of an impact study, the feasibility of the proposal, and the fact that it is contrary to the 'transparency' and 'better regulation' commitments undertaken by the new commission, and taking into account the long-term consequences of the proposal for the functioning of the internal market for food and feed and the competitiveness of the union agricultural sector, i support the rejection of the commission's proposal.
in writing. ‒ it is well known that the use of genetically modified organisms has always been controversial, with the european union having very strict rules and complex authorisation procedures for their cultivation and marketing. i welcome the fact that, as of april 2015, member states can decide whether to allow gmos to be grown on their territory.
in writing. ‒ we must ensure that clear and unambiguous rules are set to provide legal certainty for member states which want to restrict the use of gm food and feed in order to respond to the concerns raised by citizens. the commission proposal is not acceptable, especially considering the non-existence of an impact assessment, the incompatibility of member state opt-out measures with internal market and wto rules, the failure to ensure legal certainty, and the weak prospects for the proposal actually being implemented. citizens’ concerns about gmos have to be taken into account today, as our main priority in this matter is the health and safety of european citizens. it must be up to the citizens to choose europe’s future food and agricultural model and to refuse gmos if they do not wish to have them on their table.
in writing. ‒ a clear vote upholding the european single market and the principles of rules-based international trade.
in writing. ‒ i voted for this report which rejects the commission’s proposal that member states wishing lawfully to restrict or prohibit the use of gm food and feed on their territory must provide ‘compelling reasons’.
in writing. ‒ i voted to reject the commission proposal because it does not review or improve the gmo authorisation process, in fact it leaves it completely unchanged. the entire gmo system in the eu needs a thorough review. the existing system is not transparent and does not reflect the concerns that many citizens have in relation to gm products and their potential effects on human health and the environment. the commission must honour its commitment to look again, in depth, at the gmo regime at eu level and propose changes which reflect citizens’ concerns.
in writing. ‒ the use of genetically modified organisms in the diet of the population has been a subject of intense and controversial debate from the outset. beyond the arguments of the proponents and opponents of this type of food, the decisions we take as representatives of european citizens must take into account their interests. the commission's proposal to amend the 2003 regulation in this area concerns the possibility for member states to restrict or even prohibit the use of genetically modified food and feed on their territory, provided that an eu-wide authorisation system is maintained. the application of these amendments would, however, create legal uncertainty as regards the practical application of the measures proposed by the commission, would fragment the internal market and distort competition, would contravene the principles of good governance and transparency and could limit the free movement of goods within the eu. in this context, it is clear that we need an impact assessment of these measures, but above all a series of scientific opinions from the european food safety authority, assessing the risks to human health, animal health and environmental protection. i consider the position of the committee on the environment, public health and food safety to be well founded and support the adoption of the report, in the sense of rejecting the commission's proposal.
in writing. ‒ the la via report is built against the european commission's proposal on the possibility for member states to restrict or prohibit the use of genetically modified food and feed on their territory. this commission proposal follows the pattern of a recent amendment allowing states to ban the cultivation of eu-approved gmos on their territory, but not their marketing. member states could thus restrict or prohibit, under certain conditions, the use of genetically modified food and feed on their territory after such products have been authorised. this commission proposal is, first of all, flawed, as there is no preventive study showing the real implications for the functioning of the internal market, in which controls have been removed, and for the competitiveness of agriculture in the eu, which is heavily dependent on protein supplements from genetically modified organisms. in this respect, we could be seeing a regression in the single market by reintroducing controls between member states that accept and those that do not accept the marketing of such products. i therefore voted in favour of the la via report, which recommends rejecting the proposal for national bans on gmos.
in writing. ‒ the food sector is one of the most productive in the european union. this productivity must take into account first consumer safety and then profitability. in this regard, the amendment of the novel food report is intended to provide consumer safety by subjecting novel foods to a safety assessment and authorisation before being placed on the eu market. innovation is also attractive, but consumers demand that food products be safe to eat, they demand to be informed about how they were produced, but also about their benefits. the innovation is accepted only if it provides consumer confidence. i voted in favour of the report on the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council on novel foods because a robust legislative framework is needed for the approval of novel foods to ensure compatibility in terms of safety, benefits for the consumer, as well as environmental, social and ethical concerns.
in writing. ‒ eu rules on novel foods were established with the entry into force of regulation (ec) no 258/1997 of the ep and of the council and commission regulation (ec) no 1852/2001. in view of the scientific and technological progress made in the food industry in recent years, it is natural that legislation should reflect the new realities in this sector in the eu internal market. the definition of a novel food, the rationalisation of the authorisation procedure and the data protection provisions are the main concerns. i support the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council on novel foods (2013/0435 ((cod)) as i believe that stakeholders need an efficient procedure that provides certainty and adequate protection for products.
in writing. ‒ i believe that the new rules will subject food to safety assessment and authorisation through a fully harmonised procedure at eu level. the european food safety authority (efsa) should carry out an assessment in all cases where a food may affect human health.
in writing. ‒ i strongly believe that we must ensure food safety, protect public health and secure the functioning of the internal market for food, while supporting innovation in the food sector. streamlining the authorisation procedure, improving its efficiency and transparency must be our priority. i support the clarification of the definition of a novel food and of new technologies which have an impact on food production, as well as the introduction of a faster and more proportionate safety assessment for traditional foods from third countries having a history of safe food use. however, implementing acts for the authorisation procedure for a novel food give parliament absolutely no political control over what kind of novel food is being authorised; the list of categories of novel foods is non-exhaustive and can cover any new food that falls under the scope; and no transitional measures regarding the food derived from the descendants of cloned animal are included – thus leaving a legal gap until new legislation is in place. i am therefore not fully satisfied with the final text of the regulation.
in writing. ‒ i abstained in the vote on the proposal for a regulation on novel foods.
in writing. ‒ i voted against this report because i believe that it, like the commission's proposal, although it seeks to simplify the certification procedures for novel foods to be placed on the eu market, could endanger the health of citizens. the commission has very correctly identified since 2008 the need for new eu-wide rules for the authorisation of novel foods and the need to facilitate the procedures in this case, but i believe that centralising this decision and eliminating individual authorisations in favour of a generic authorisation system essentially means that in certain cases there will be products that will be authorised without being individually assessed. this, in my view, represents a real danger to the health of eu citizens because certain products that affect human health could be authorised. or, if we are talking about centralised authorisation, it means that there will be no further filters to identify these products, but they will be directly part of the citizens' diet.
in writing. ‒ novel foods are a separate category within the food industry in the eu member states. it arose as a result of the need to regulate the technological processing of food for sale on the consumer market. the progress made in processing technology since the first regulation in 1997 makes it necessary to review european legislation in this area. the new regulation proposed by the council provides a number of benefits, such as establishing a single, centralised and harmonised procedure at european level for the authorisation of novel foods, data protection and legal certainty for companies submitting authorisation applications, reducing the administrative burden for small and medium-sized enterprises, adapting to new techniques and creating a favourable framework for innovation in the agri-food sector. at the same time, the new regulation excludes aspects related to cloning, which are the subject of other legislative proposals, and provides for a separate simplified procedure for the placing on the market of traditional foods from third countries. in order to ensure the protection of public health, the opinion of the european food safety authority becomes essential, which is an important step forward. however, it may be useful to include the european parliament institutionally in this decision-making process.
in writing. ‒ novel foods are foods that were not commonly used in human nutrition in the european union before 15 may 1997, such as: foods with a new or intentionally modified primary molecular structure, foods containing, consisting of, or produced from plants, foods containing, consisting of, or produced from micro-organisms, fungi or algae, etc. they were introduced by a regulation in 1997. the nicholson report proposes to revise this regulation, as several new food products and food ingredients have since been developed due to scientific and technological progress. it also proposes new rules on the safety assessment and authorisation of novel foods through a fully harmonised eu procedure and, to this end, the european food safety authority should carry out an assessment of foodstuffs that may affect human health. in addition to establishing a single centralised and harmonised eu-wide procedure for the authorisation of novel foods, this report introduces certain measures to reduce the administrative burden for small and medium-sized enterprises and at the same time creates a favourable framework for innovation in the agri-food sector. i therefore support the nicholson report on novel foods.

in writing. ‒ i would like to stress the importance for romania of the proposal for a revised national emission reduction commitments directive, in terms of its impact on many industrial sectors: energy, industry, transport, residential and agriculture. as a general position, i agree that measures to address dangerous pollutants covering all sectors are urgently needed but we need to ensure that the proposed measures will not lead, in the end, to increased costs in economic terms and will not impose undue administrative burden for the government and private sector. the proposal for new national emission reduction commitments applicable for 2020 and 2030 specifically implies for romania the following reduction compared to emissions in 2005: 93% for sulphur dioxide, 67% for nitrogen oxides, 64% for volatile organic compounds, 24% for ammonia, 65% for particulate matter pm2.5; and 26% for methane. these reductions will require additional efforts and costs, to prevent and control emissions, which could affect economic competitiveness. i consider that the objectives for 2030 should better reflect national emission projections, or alternatively that they should be proposed as indicative targets.

in writing. ‒ i decided to vote against this report because i believe that it started from a commission proposal on reducing air pollutants in the eu, which is a topic that needs to be debated and for which viable solutions need to be found in order to meet the objectives, but, through the additions to this initial proposal, it also involved small and medium-sized farming. the addition of provisions on emissions of harmful gases from animal husbandry, with the express designation of small and medium-sized farming, implies costs and obligations for farmers at or below the threshold of profitability. such a provision for farmers and livestock breeders in romania, no matter how large or small, would entail additional costs that would be difficult to bear and would involve the bankruptcy of many. in these circumstances, i felt obliged towards the citizens of romania to vote against this report.
in writing. ‒ this directive on the reduction of national emissions aims to improve air quality, and that will undoubtedly have a positive impact on health. however, headline targets mean nothing if they cannot be implemented or if doing so leads to extensive job losses and increased inequality. ambitious targets must be achievable for all member states and should not represent a disproportionate burden for countries with fewer resources. we must strive to adopt legislation which brings environmental, health, societal and economic benefits.
in writing. ‒ economic development, with its ramifications in increased transport, industrial activity and urbanisation, brings with it a number of negative effects on the health of european citizens. the european commission has dedicated a policy to the objective of improving europe's poor air quality, the instrument of which involves capping member states' total annual emissions for sulphur dioxide (so2), nitrogen oxides (nox), ammonia (nh3) and non-methane volatile organic compounds (vocs). in the central and eastern european member states where indigenous solid fuel is used in the energy mix, the reduction of pollutants such as sulphur dioxide and particulate matter is proving to be much more difficult than in other cases. despite this, the states in question are signatories to the gothenburg protocol, which governs air quality control and protection measures. however, the implementation of the measures proposed in this report by reducing certain air pollutants leads to excessive costs and creates a disproportionate administrative burden on key sectors such as industry, energy, transport and housing. while the european commission's proposal provides for a set of limits on the pollutants that can be imposed, the european parliament's report is very ambitious, based on theoretical assumptions and projections.
in writing. ‒ the opportunity for citizens to express themselves through legislative initiatives is an important step in ensuring the legitimacy and strengthening of participatory democracy at european union level. this is an indisputable fact and it is necessary that the institutions responsible contribute to the smooth running of the procedures so that this democratic instrument can function. taking into account that only three initiatives out of 51 calls for initiatives have been admissible since 2012, this tool needs to be simple, clear, easy to use and widely disseminated. i voted in favour of the report on the european citizens' initiative because i believe it is essential that european citizens can contribute to the exercise of the union's legislative powers and be directly involved in the initiation of legislative proposals.
in writing. ‒ the citizens' initiative is an essential means of linking european citizens to the union's institutions and an effective instrument of democratic participation, because it helps to formulate citizens' aspirations with a view to calling for eu action. in order to enable citizens to contribute to the exercise of the union's legislative powers and to be directly involved in the initiation of legislative proposals, it is necessary that they are familiar with this instrument. it is also why i support the rapporteur's proposal to organise information and promotion campaigns. i also consider it essential to support the media and use all public communication channels to raise public awareness of citizens' initiatives, to take the necessary measures to ensure their transparency and to facilitate communication on current initiatives, for example by creating applications that provide information, send notifications and offer the possibility of online sign-up. it should also be borne in mind that youth civic engagement is fundamental to the future of all democracies, and we need to draw on national experiences of citizens' initiatives which are true models of success.
in writing. ‒ the european citizens’ initiative (eci) is a unique and innovative agenda-setting tool for participatory democracy in the european union, allowing citizens to play an active part in projects and processes that affect them. citizens should be able to participate actively in the further development of the european integration process. i therefore strongly support the implementation of the eci, which will make it possible to ask the commission to submit a proposal on matters on which citizens consider that a legislative act is necessary to implement the treaties – one of eu’s priority objectives being to strengthen the democratic legitimacy of its institutions. action of this kind should be encouraged and supported by all available means, and deficits in this respect need to be tackled in order to make the eci as effective as possible.
in writing. ‒ the european citizens' initiative is a tool for mobilising at european level and for exemplifying transnational participatory democracy. citizens of the member states shall have the right of legislative initiative for projects and processes which concern them directly. of all the requests to launch a european citizens' initiative, only three were considered admissible, which shows that there is still much room for improvement. here are a few examples: - organisers must be given as comprehensive information as possible on the legal eligibility criteria, deadlines and procedures; - the commission must explain in detail the reasons for rejecting a citizens' legislative initiative and the relevant legal considerations must, in the name of transparency, be made public in full; - simplification of the use of the online signature collection application; - the it tools used for the eci should also be made available to the regions, in order to involve citizens more closely in public affairs; this tool needs to be simple, clear, easy to use and widely promoted, precisely because it allows people to call for eu action to fulfil their aspirations.
in writing. ‒ the european citizens’ initiative (eci) has its origins in the constitutional convention on the future of europe and was designed as an instrument giving european citizens the opportunity to participate in launching legislative initiatives. i voted for this report, which will improve the functioning of the eci, make it more user-friendly and eliminate some of the obstacles that have proved a source of difficulty for eci organisers.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on the european citizens' initiative because i share the rapporteur's view of its importance in the eu's democratic process. this initiative gives eu citizens the opportunity to ask the brussels institutions to take action on issues they identify. there has been much talk, and rightly so, of a lack of democracy and transparency in the decision-making process in the eu institutions. i believe that this instrument will improve the democratic process in the eu institutions and bring to the table those issues that citizens face but that the commission or parliament are unaware of. i also hope that future evaluations and any changes to this initiative will focus on improving the process and making it as easy as possible to access, as european citizens need a quick and easy way to make their voices heard in the eu institutions. i therefore encourage romanian citizens to use this initiative and to actively engage in the process of identifying eu problems.
in writing. ‒ when the treaty of lisbon gave european citizens the opportunity to take a legislative initiative to the european commission, many of us felt that we had taken europe one step closer to the citizens. that is why i find it outrageous and a mockery of the six million citizens who have participated in the initiatives so far, that out of 51 applications, only three have been declared admissible and 20 have already been rejected. this is a message to citizens not to interfere in the commission's work and citizens are getting the message, as the number of initiatives is clearly on a downward trend. it is not possible to constantly claim that citizens misunderstand european law and the role of the commission when they are looking for solutions to the most important questions affecting their lives. by doing so, the commission only reinforces the view that the european institutions are incapable of finding answers to citizens' problems. i consider the way in which the commission has dealt with the european citizens' initiative to date to be extremely damaging for participatory democracy and for the perception of the european union, and i therefore support the report by mr schöpflin, which could help to improve the regulation.
in writing. ‒ the eci is one of the most powerful tools for direct democracy that the lisbon treaty provided our citizens. since the entry into force of the eci, 51 initiatives have been submitted, resulting in the participation of more than 6 million people. while this is encouraging, in reality, of the 51 initiatives submitted in the past three years only three were deemed admissible. yet not a single initiative was followed up by legislation. the low success rates are linked to a number of problems regarding 1) the information provided to eci organisers, 2) the software offered by the ec for collecting signatures online, and 3) problems related to the public awareness of the eci. the current report, which i voted in favour of, provides us with the opportunity to address ongoing issues. it calls on the commission to increase transparency to the eci, on both the national and the european levels. it further asks the commission to provide appropriate guidelines, and legal guidance, to eci organizers. lastly, as a young mep i welcome the report’s recommendation to lower the age of participation in member states from 18 to 16. this recommendation will surely help us to draw young people’s interest and participation in this democratic exercise.
in writing. ‒ the european citizens' initiative is an innovation of the lisbon treaty, which gives the right of political initiative to citizens, subject to certain conditions. citizens can thus invite the commission to submit new proposals for legal acts in areas of eu competence, thus directly participating in european policy-making. however, despite this reforming law it introduces, the european citizens' initiative has been facing a number of technical and organisational problems since its introduction on 1 april 2012. thus, in the three years of its existence, 51 initiatives were submitted to the commission, of which only one was accepted. in addition to requiring at least one million supporters from at least one quarter of the member states, organisers of a european citizens' initiative face complex and discouraging procedures and the commission can reject such a request without any particular reason. a reform of this participatory democracy mechanism is therefore needed to meet its ultimate objective, namely to put citizens on an equal footing with the european parliament and the council of the eu before the commission. i therefore voted in favour of the schöpflin report on the european citizens' initiative.
in writing. the eci was seen as a triumph of the lisbon treaty because it opened up the chance for european citizens to become initiators of legislation and active participants in european policy-making. three years after its entry into force, this instrument is disappointing. the bureaucratic, lawyer-like approach of the ec risks producing the opposite effect, contributing to the alienation of citizens from europe. the ep has played an important role in promoting eci legislation, and now, once again, the ep is taking the initiative to change the regulation. the eu must become a political construct and therefore open to the ideas and proposals of its citizens. this imperative must be understood by eu bureaucrats, but also by member states who must facilitate the whole eci procedure, rather than adding additional administrative hurdles. i voted for the schöpflin report, which contains clear proposals for improving the eci regulation. the amendment proposal that the ec has to submit to the ep and the council must demonstrate an understanding that the eu is at a crossroads. either we learn to listen to the voice of our citizens and then we will succeed, or we continue to distance ourselves from european citizens and are thus doomed to failure.
in writing. ‒ the adriatic and ionian region is an area with considerable socioeconomic differences between the eu member states and the other third countries. the eu strategy for the region, eusair, is thus a way of creating a balance of prosperity and sustainable development between the countries in the region, whether eu member states, candidate countries or 'potential candidate countries'. an evaluation carried out by the european commission in 2013 of the previous strategies, namely the eu strategy for the baltic sea region (eusbsr) and the eu strategy for the danube region (eusdr), showed that they led to increased cooperation and thus to the emergence of hundreds of new projects and networks in the danube and baltic sea region. these examples provide a strong argument for supporting a similar strategy in the adriatic and ionian sea region. i voted in favour of the report on the eu strategy for the adriatic and ionian region because this area has vast potential, which can only be unlocked by joint and coordinated efforts by all the countries in the region.
in writing. ‒ representing the eu's third macro-regional strategy, eusair includes 8 countries, eu member states and non-eu member states, and covers over 70 million inhabitants. the region has been affected over time by events with major negative impact on the region. we hope that such macro-regions will be models of good practice and success at european level, because they can benefit all their citizens and contribute to economic recovery and sustainable development through policy harmonisation and investment reorientation. on the other hand, local and regional authorities are the main actors in the area and only through effective collaboration and joint efforts can the adriatic and ionian sea region strategy be a success.
in writing. ‒ the adriatic-ionian region faces a common set of challenges, ranging from difficult political and economic circumstances, due to past historical events, to big socio-economic disparities between different countries and regions. significant infrastructure deficits exist, and there is inadequate interconnection of electricity grids. ecosystems are threatened by increased human exploitation of marine and coastal ecosystems. natural and man-made hazards are apparent. furthermore, administrative and institutional capacities at national, regional and local level need to be reinforced. i support the implementation of the eu strategy on adriatic and ionian region, as it is fundamental for blue growth, for connecting europe, for environmental quality and sustainable and competitive tourism. we should focus on the weak pillars of this strategy and make sure that it provides a comprehensive framework for a coherent macro-regional strategy, as well as an action plan for cooperation between the participating eu and third countries.
in writing. ‒ the european council of december 2012 invited the commission to present a new eu strategy for the adriatic and ionian region (eusair) before the end of 2014. i voted for this report, which will implement eusair, following the model of the eu strategy for the baltic sea region.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on the eu strategy for the adriatic and ionian region because i consider it to be a report which brings important additions to the commission's proposal. i had the opportunity to be the rapporteur on this file in the committee on fisheries and i am familiar with the report written by my colleagues in the committee on regional development. i am pleased to note that the final report of the committee on regional development also contains the suggestions made by myself and my colleagues in the opinion report of the committee on fisheries, as the adriatic and ionian sea region is a special case in terms of pollution and available marine resources. it's a complex strategy for many reasons, but i think the main reason is that it affects both eu member states and non-member states, which don't always have the same laws or standards as ours. i believe that this report complements in essential respects the strategy proposed by the commission and i look forward to seeing the results it will produce.
in writing. ‒ the european union is a project in which the member states have placed all their hopes when they chose to become part of this continental entity governed by rules and principles. for the member countries of central and eastern europe, gaining this status was synonymous with obtaining a huge chance to develop and reach the socio-economic level of the west of the continent. eu cohesion policy is the guarantee of community assistance to reduce development gaps between regions. this is also the case for the western balkan candidate countries. the accession of croatia in 2013 is clear evidence of the eu's interest in this region. however, in order to properly manage the development gaps with the other regions of the union, a separate strategy for the area is needed, as embodied in the eu strategy for the adriatic and ionian region. the strategy will contribute to progress in identified priority areas such as the interconnection of electricity grids, the protection of marine ecosystems, the building of local administrative capacity or the development of sustainable tourism. i think it would be useful to draw up a similar strategy for the black sea region, to take account of the development of the regions in this eu border area.
in writing. ‒ the europe 2020 objectives require a detailed analysis in the mid-term review process so that their achievement takes account of the reality on the ground as much as possible. we note that some changes have occurred in the implementation of cohesion policy, due to the new global challenges we are facing and which are influencing the objectives of the strategy. the ambitious targets set in the 2020 strategy must contain concrete and easily achievable objectives and to achieve the desired result, measures such as: increasing the accountability and participation of partners, by improving transparency and involving authorities at several levels in the process of developing, implementing and evaluating the strategy. the unsatisfactory results on the ground show that the lack of administrative capacity is causing serious delays in the implementation of the set objectives. the establishment of the structural reform support service is a key boost for many member states facing dysfunctions in the implementation of the structural funds. e. i voted in favour of this report because the operational role of the support instrument is to improve the spending of eu funds by providing technical assistance to member states for a more effective implementation of structural reforms, taking into account the specific recommendations of each member state. ̆ the country.
in writing. ‒ i support the report on cohesion policy and the review of europe 2020, as cohesion policy is the key instrument for the implementation of europe 2020. it is the eu's main investment, growth and development policy, set in line with the europe 2020 strategy's objectives for smart, sustainable and inclusive growth, and aims to reduce disparities between regions and promote convergence. i should mention that after the 2008 crisis, cohesion policy became the only financial resource for development policy in some member states or regions. this shows that, thanks to the cohesion policy, some investments have continued despite the drastic decrease in public funding.
in writing. ‒ in this period of economic crisis, the only source of investment for many eu countries has been and remains cohesion policy. it is a considerable support for eu countries in implementing the 2020 strategy. however, it should be borne in mind that the european parliament has an important role in overseeing the implementation of the europe 2020 strategy and cohesion policy, which is why i consider it useful to involve the legislative forum in the evaluation of policies included in the strategy, as well as in the monitoring process to identify cases of combining funding from different existing european funds. on the other hand, a consistent and continuous evaluation process is needed, allowing for a regular analysis of the progress made towards the europe 2020 targets, but also for the launching of appropriate proposals for the achievement of the objectives, where appropriate, and recommendations for the post-2020 cohesion policy. it must remain one of the eu's main investment tools for growth, job creation and climate protection, while ensuring balanced and harmonious development across the eu as a catalyst for change and a driver of prosperity.
in writing. ‒ to achieve its objective of smart, sustainable and inclusive growth for europe, the 2020 strategy correctly relies on five headline targets: employment; research and development; climate and energy; education; and the fight against poverty and social exclusion, translated by each member state into national targets. halfway to the 2020 deadline, however, the delivery of the jobs and growth objectives is still mixed, and much more needs to be done in order to achieve these goals, especially on the social aspects of the strategy. i believe that if the union wants to make progress with regard to the social and employment targets laid down in the europe 2020 strategy, the commission should come forward with an ambitious social agenda and complement the european monetary union with a strong social dimension.
in writing. ‒ i have voted for this report that will provide an eu-wide public consultation gathering the views of all interested parties on how to develop the europe 2020 strategy over the next five years.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this own-initiative report because it underlines both the importance of cohesion policy in the 2007-13 budgetary period and its importance for the 2014-2020 budget. in this context, given that many countries have used these european funds to make investments and thus reduce the impact of the economic crisis, i believe that these funds will remain in the next period the main source of investment and development for countries such as romania. the revision of the europe 2020 strategy, as the rapporteur also states, is necessary because it was negotiated and approved in a different economic and development period to today's, so that the current strategy is not fully compatible with the realities of cohesion policy.
in writing. ‒ as the eu’s main instrument for economic growth and job creation, cohesion policy is best placed to help achieve the europe 2020 strategy for smart, sustainable and inclusive growth. it can achieve this through its substantive budget and through its decades-long experience. unfortunately, not all member states can easily succeed in making use of the opportunities offered by the policy. this is the case of my country, which barely used 65% of the budget put at its disposal in the last programming period. therefore i can only hope, just as the report emphasizes, that the stronger link between structural and investment funds and the european semester process, the setting-up of the task force for better implementation of eu funds and the establishment of the ‘structural reform support service’ will ensure that no more opportunities for development and social cohesion are wasted in any of the member states.
in writing. ‒ the eu's cohesion policy presupposes solidarity between member states to level the playing field of their regions. this objective is consistent with the eu's europe 2020 strategy, which focuses on increasing employment, increasing investment in research and development, digitising the economy, reducing emissions, energy efficiency, reducing school dropouts, reducing poverty. however, in the context of the financial and economic crisis of recent years, the implementation of the strategy has been affected, in particular as regards funding, which is only available through the european structural and investment funds. the creation of the european fund for strategic investments has provided a new breathing space in this regard. however, a segmentation of the strategy is required to adapt it to the specificities of each region of the union. only in this way will investments be directed to the areas of real deficit, involving the optimal decision-making levels. such a debate can provide the framework for a new cohesion policy that is in sync with the multiannual financial framework and that truly meets the needs of citizens in the various parts of the european union.
in writing. i voted for the report on cohesion policy and the revision of the europe 2020 strategy. i agree with the rapporteur that cohesion policy makes a significant contribution to achieving the europe 2020 objectives of smart, sustainable and inclusive growth. i welcome the fact that the report calls, taking into account the delays and time constraints that have occurred at the beginning of the current programming period, for a comprehensive discussion on the future of eu cohesion policy after 2020 to be organised in a timely manner and aligned with the revised long-term strategy for the eu and the new mff.
in writing. ‒ cohesion policy is a policy based on the provisions of the treaty on the functioning of the european union and is an expression of european solidarity, aimed at strengthening economic, social and territorial cohesion. at the same time, cohesion policy aims to reduce the gaps between regions, while also trying to promote socio-economic development in the most balanced and harmonious way possible. as there was a majority concerned that the practical implications of the rescheduling and suspension of the european structural and investment funds were being discussed, this report attempted to strike a balance between different views on the macroeconomic conditionality mechanism from the perspective of its application as a last resort within the system. i voted in favour of the report on the european structural and investment funds and good economic governance: guidelines for the application of article 23 of the common provisions regulation because the european parliament must guarantee the democracy of the application of the provisions on macroeconomic conditionality, and moreover, a constant exchange of reliable information between all stakeholders and full transparency at every stage of the process.
in writing. ‒ i believe that the active role of the european parliament in the application and monitoring of article 23 must be highlighted and supported by transparent collaboration and effective exchange of information throughout the process. on the other hand, better institutional coordination between all administrations, together with simple and transparent reprogramming processes, are essential to achieving the objectives of cohesion policy, given its role in maintaining investment in europe's regions.
in writing. ‒ the provisions regarding measures between effectiveness of the esi funds and sound economic governance – the so called macro-economic conditionality – was a very controversial aspect of the common provisions regulation (cpr) during the last ep legislative term, which s&d and most of the political groups rejected. however, the adopted cpr contain provisions (art. 23) on sound economic governance. many safeguards were obtained by the ep to make sure that this provision is only used as a ‘last resort’ measure. in the current programming period cohesion policy is closely linked with the goals of eu 2020 strategy and economic governance mechanisms. partnership agreements and operational programmes for 2014-2020 should already be in line with eu macro-economic goals, making a (frequent) reprogramming unnecessary. any reprogramming, if needed, should be kept as simple and transparent as possible. regional and local authorities should not be punished, through reprogramming or suspension of funding, as a result of macroeconomic ‘failings’ of a national government. a balance should be kept between the need for effective economic governance and cohesion policy goals.
in writing. ‒ reprogramming or suspending the structural and investment funds under article 23 of the common provisions regulation should only be used in exceptional circumstances. it is a sanctioning measure and for this reason we need such decisions to be carefully evaluated and explained in a transparent manner. cohesion policy is an essential tool in maintaining investment in europe's regions. as the commission also states, reprogramming should only take place in cases where it is very clear that it has a greater impact than the existing allocation of funds. romania is one of the countries for which absorption of structural funds is an important objective. at the end of this year we will no longer have access to unused money from the 2007-2013 programming period. part of the failure is related to the mechanisms of economic governance, but part of it is certainly reflected in the bureaucratic red tape and the changing of the rules during the game. that is why, when we discuss sanctions, i think we have to do so in the light of the multiannual and long-term nature of the programmes and objectives of the funds, adapting them to the socioeconomic conditions of each country. responsible solidarity, that is my message.
in writing. ‒ i have voted for this report that will ensure that the main objective of cohesion is not affected and will gather and analyse data on the interactions between european economic governance processes and the aims and results of cohesion policy.
in writing. ‒ i think this report is a useful one because it highlights the importance of the structural and investment funds for the economies of many member states, but at the same time it draws attention to the need for good governance in order for these funds to bring the maximum benefits. it is also very important to understand that certain economic governance mechanisms, while relevant for macroeconomic stability, may impede the achievement of the esi funds' objectives. it is also important that measures taken at both eu and member state level provide for long-term stability and clarity, as most projects financed by these funds span long periods of time and can be easily affected by economic decisions of the moment. in this context, i considered that this report is coherent and useful for the debate on the 2014-2020 budget.
in writing. ‒ although the link between the european structural and investment funds (esi funds) and the european semester in the common provisions regulation (cpr) might seem controversial, there is evidence that sound economic governance can increase the impact of investment in economic development and job creation. if we add to this the low level of implementation of country specific recommendations, the need for such a correlation seems all the more useful. however, i agree with the view from the report that, given the long-term nature of the challenges that esi funds are intended to solve in member states, reprogramming or suspension under article 23 of the cpr should only be used in exceptional situations. i therefore welcome the cautious approach from the commission’s communication and hope that such reprogramming will be kept to the minimum necessary.
in writing. ‒ the european structural and investment funds are the key instrument for implementing the european union's cohesion policy. the funds will help to reduce the development gap between the regions of the member states and create the framework for the joint development of the european construction at socioeconomic level. however, one of the conditions for the allocation of these funds remains the need for good economic governance, which implies compliance by the state concerned with certain basic rules, generally laid down in the stability and growth pact. those rules concern certain criteria of institutional coordination, transparency and accountability. otherwise, the suspension of payments to the state concerned may be decided by the council on a proposal from the commission. however, the economic difficulties faced by a number of member states in recent years require a more careful application of these regulations, as in many cases those who suffer are those who need assistance the most. those measures must be applied in such a way as not to undermine the objective of cohesion policies. in this respect, the european parliament, as the direct representative of the citizens, should have a stronger say in assessing the compliance of member states with the economic conditions.
in writing. i voted in favour of the report on the european structural and investment funds and good economic governance: guidelines for the application of article 23 of the common provisions regulation. the rapporteur's concern regarding article 23 of the said regulation, which introduces macroeconomic conditionality, which should be removed, is welcomed. i agree with his approach that article 23 of the regulation should not create financial uncertainty and instability, aggravating an already precarious situation, especially in disadvantaged regions or in those most affected by the crisis. i also support his view that the situation where local or regional entities can be sanctioned with the reprogramming or suspension of funds, deteriorating their economic and social situation, due to macroeconomic failures at other levels of administration, should be rejected.

madam president, the ruling of 6 october of the court of justice striking down the commission’s adequacy decision on the us safe harbour agreement confirms the longstanding doubts on the level of protection provided by this instrument. the decision was to be expected as the 2013 espionage revelations had already exposed the uselessness of the agreement’s provisions in view of the citizen surveillance programme’s massive scale. as stated by the court, permitting public authorities to have access on a generalised basis to the content of electronic communications compromises the essence of the fundamental right to privacy, while the lack of provisions on the right of citizens to complain about their data compromises the essence of the right to effective judicial protection. against the backdrop of the recent invalidation of the data retention directive, this new ruling calls for urgent action to strike the right balance between security measures and the protection of fundamental rights. considering, on the one hand, the european conviction that security measures must be pursued under the rule of law and, on the other hand, the vital importance of eu-us counter-terrorism cooperation for both partners, it is of extreme importance that we swiftly take steps to establish common standards in the field of data protection.

member of the commission.– madam president, members of parliament, i would like to thank you and in particular the rapporteur, ms de monte, for this excellent report. i fully share your views on the importance of the eu tourism sector. the travel and tourism sector makes a very substantial contribution to european economies. in 2014 its direct, indirect and induced impacts supported 33.5 million jobs. moreover, in the same period it also contributed more than eur 1.3 trillion to the economy, making up almost 10% of total european gdp. by 2025 the travel and tourism sector's total economic contribution is expected to grow to 38 million jobs and eur 2.1 trillion. in addition, travel and tourism is key to the recovery of those countries that have been hit hardest by recession and the euro zone crisis. 20% of employees in the european tourism industry are aged below 25. tourism is therefore an important entry point to the labour market. tourism has also significant spill—over benefits for the cultural and creative industries, including fashion and high-end products – agrifoods, transport, construction, shipbuilding or retail. therefore tourism has a huge potential to generate economic growth and create jobs. but although europe is still the number one destination, we should not rest on our laurels. we have to address important challenges – competition from emerging destinations is increasing. in 2000 the eu had 51% of the worldʼs tourism market; today we are below 40% and forecasts indicate a further drop to 31% by 2030. to attract new investment and ensure faster growth, we must increase the number of travellers from key markets such as china, india or the us. for this to happen, we need to strengthen our promotional activities. in doing so, we should consider that 99% of the tourist sector is made up of smes and 90% of them have fewer than 10 employees. it is important that we improve the business environment, not least by ensuring a well—functioning single market for services. the commission adopted the new single market strategy just two days ago. we have to fully capitalise on the potential offered by this strategy, ensuring effective enforcement of single market principles and rules, extending also to tourism services. we must continue to work on the issue of over—regulation and cut down red tape where possible. at the same time we must ensure that the principles of the small business act are fully implemented in the tourism sector. we should also follow market trends and enable the development of new innovative business models and take on board the advantages of the digital revolution. especially in this case digitalisation will be a key driver of the sector’s competitiveness. we must help tourism-related smes to seize the opportunities offered by the digital revolution. we wish to embrace the opportunities created by the sharing economy, including for the eu tourism industry. at the same time, we must create a level playing field for all actors and make sure that public and consumer interests are properly reflected. to compete with new emerging destinations were must invest in high-quality offerings and improve infrastructure, resource efficiency and skills. to that end it is essential to ensure better access to finance. there is a serious mismatch between the demand for and the supply of skilled labour in the sector. erasmus+ and the european social fund play a key role in the upgrading of skills, including digital skills, as well as in training and workforce mobility. we have helped to define tourism qualifications and developed a skill passport to help match businesses with job-seekers. we are also promoting high-quality cross-border traineeships and the smooth entry into the labour market for young professionals through a digital platform. there is a strong added value in promotion activities carried out jointly with public and private stakeholders. american and asian tourists want to come to europe and visit more than one country. we should preserve, and capitalise on, our unique cultural and natural heritage and diversity. we should invest more in joint promotion in close collaboration with member states, regions and the industry.
