member of the commission.– madam president, honourable members, allow me to address you for the fourth time today with an equally important topic. the commission considers that satellite-based technology for global flight tracking is a positive development. in the aftermath of the june 2009 accident involving air france flight 447, europe launched extensive work on options both for tracking aircraft and for localising an airplane in distress. the disappearance of malaysia airlines flight 370 in march 2014 has contributed to fast-tracking of the regulatory process at eu level. a committee opinion delivered on 9 july 2015 endorsed the commission’s proposal to amend commission regulation (eu) no 965/2012 regarding requirements for flight records, underwater locating devices and aircraft tracking systems. both in terms of legislation and research our work is performance—based. this means that it does not favour any specific commercial or technical solution as long as the technology used by operators is fit for the desired purpose. our rules will both provide the necessary flexibility and accommodate a number of technical options – existing ones as well as future ones such as galileo search and rescue and/or satellite-based ads, type b. such rules, supported by the member states, would be based on the following three principles: first, the requirements must be technologically neutral and performance based. they will be defined to ensure that large public transport aircraft automatically transmit sufficient trajectory information regularly and accurately enough for search and rescue and investigation purposes. second, provided that the relevant equipment can be operated safely, the requirement should specify that it should have a backup power supply and it should not be possible to disable the flight tracking functions. this apparently occurred during the malaysia airlines flight. third, the requirements must allow air carriers and aircraft manufacturers to opt for the most cost-efficient solutions. the text of the commission proposal has already been submitted to the european parliament and council for scrutiny. on that basis, comprehensive legislation should be adopted and published before the end of the year. the international civil aviation organisation (icao) is also updating international rules accordingly. furthermore, we are working actively to provide passengers with internet connections, both terrestrial and satellite solutions. such systems can support advanced data communication between air and ground. this will eventually make it possible for flights to be fully monitored in real time from the ground. to return to the subject of space—based atsb technology, although this remains an interesting option, the commission would like to underline that it is one of several possible solutions. the commission has set out various options in a technical working paper provided to icao. concerning the commission’s position at the world radio communication conference, the european union as such does not have voting rights in the itu. on monday, 26 october the council adopted conclusions for the world radio communication conference, but this topic is not addressed. we therefore welcome the european parliament resolution and we will work together with member states at the world radio communication conference to ensure that it is coherently supported during the negotiations. to sum up, the commission supported the protection of ads type b at the world radio communication conference and consequently in the itu radio regulation. we also know that during the preparations for the world radio communications conference member states signalled their support for allocation for satellite reception of automatic dependent surveillance broadcast atsb emissions from aircraft limited to messages transmitted in accordance with icao standards. that will conclude my report.
on behalf of the epp group. madam president, i regret to have to mention two sad events, two air accidents, one in the atlantic and the other in the pacific. one of the planes has been located after years of searching, the other has not been found yet. the reason is the lack of a system to ensure a global and permanent tracking of flights, the positioning of aircraft is possible only in 30% of the airspace. oceans and part of africa are not covered due to lack of technical possibilities and lack of land equipment. a poor and expensive system is used which records a relatively accurate position of aircraft at long intervals and results in inefficient use of airspace. we have a technical solution that can provide global coverage, ads-b, a system that is already used on the ground and may be used in the future on satellite systems. the modifications to the flight apparatus are minimal. a frequency band allocation is needed, which is being done by the international telecommunications organization within the framework of the world radiocommunication conference. the conference will take place in november 2015. the next one's in four years. it is obvious that this allocation must be made this year so as not to lose another four years. the use of the new system brings a significant increase in safety in air transport, a highly effective tool for rescue operations, as well as an optimisation of flights in general and especially trans-oceanic flights. the commission has also received comments from the air safety committee and the air safety committee of the european union. we welcome the commission's position and ask it to make the necessary efforts with the member states to support this position in the international conference.

in writing. ‒ the european police college (cepol) is the agency responsible for law enforcement training. although cepol’s budget is about eur 8.5 million, the institution contributes to training police enforcement personnel in skills that are needed for meeting future challenges and safeguarding the security of our citizens the current proposed regulation aligns cepol with the lisbon treaty, by modernising its legal basis and entrusting cepol with the implementation of the principles of the new law enforcement training scheme. this procedure would enable cepol to effectively implement the law enforcement training scheme and to serve the broader european law enforcement community, and at the same time deliver its contribution to the construction of a genuine european law enforcement culture. now, more than ever, we need skilled police enforcement to counter the growing threat of terrorism, transnational and organised crime, and other security challenges. for this reason i voted in favour of this current report.
in writing. ‒ the proposal for a regulation establishing the european union agency for law enforcement training (cepol) provides a legal framework for a new cepol with broader objectives and a more modern governance model, which repeals and replaces cepol as established by council decision 2005/681/jha. the european police college (cepol) is the agency responsible for law enforcement training, with its courses taking place in all member states of the union, mainly provided by a network of training colleges belonging to the national police. the proposed regulation provides for the extension of cepol's mandate to enable it to conduct and coordinate learning activities for law enforcement personnel of all ranks, as well as for customs and other relevant categories of officials dealing with cross-border issues. cepol's objectives are also updated and clarified so that the agency addresses specific thematic areas in criminal or police matters where eu-level training can bring added value over national levels. i voted in favour of this report.

member of the commission.– mr president, let me start by saying that i am really pleased that we are here today in order to discuss the upcoming aviation strategy for europe. i really welcome the interest members have put in this topic and i am pleased to see that our views and assessments converge in many aspects. as you know, aviation is a strong driver of economic growth, jobs, trade and mobility. that is why a strong and competitive european aviation sector plays such a crucial role for the eu economy in delivering on the core priorities of the commission. europe must maintain its leadership position, in the interests of its citizens and its businesses. the commission warmly welcomes the support for this approach in parliament’s draft resolution and the emphasis put on the aeronautics industry as a major contributor to eu growth and jobs, and on innovation as a prerequisite of a competitive and sustainable aviation sector. we fully agree with the call for a long-term strategy for europe’s aviation sector. therefore, the upcoming commission initiative on an aviation strategy for europe, to be adopted on 2 december, will stand as our contribution to help shape the future of the eu aviation system in a comprehensive, holistic manner. regarding members’ specific demands, and considering that our work is still ongoing, please allow me to highlight several points. first, in relation to the global perspective, the global aviation market is changing – it is reshaping. we should not be afraid of that but should engage and play a major role in shaping this new world. in this context, i agree with members that it is essential for eu aviation to be well equipped to compete with strong players in the global marketplace. we face new and relentless competition from regions such as asia and the middle east. i just came back from the middle east today and i can only confirm that. by pursuing an ambitious external aviation policy, the eu could greatly contribute to that, notably through negotiating comprehensive eu-level air transport agreements with key third partners. in particular, market access should be based on a regulatory framework which promotes eu values and standards, enables reciprocal opportunities and prevents distortions. i welcome the call for measures which can effectively address distortive market behaviour in international aviation, which is why the commission is currently considering new measures to address unfair commercial practices from third countries and third country operators. second, the internal market. from an internal market perspective, we see that, whilst some airlines continue to struggle with problems, other airlines are doing quite well. similarly, whilst large airports are profitable, smaller airports struggle to make money. so, despite the industry performing well compared to other world regions, overall financial performance unfortunately remains mixed. against this background, we have taken a close look at the eu’s regulatory environment. we know that further improvements are necessary to make the sector more efficient, provide stability to investors, encourage new research, innovation and technical solutions, and ensure safety is maintained to its current high level. third, easa. i am confident that the proposal to revise the easa basic regulation will allow easa to continue its good work while adapting to the evolving needs of citizens, industry and regulators. the main objectives will be to introduce new mechanisms for more efficient safety oversight and new methods for more risk-based, proportionate and performance-based rule making. within this revision, we intend to lay down the basic legal framework for the safe development of all drone operations in europe, in proportion to the risk. i would like to congratulate parliament on its work on its report on drones. the fourth issue: social matters. there are many social matters that need to be addressed to ensure competitive and sustainable growth in aviation. i fully agree that we must maintain leadership in aviation, including through a highly-educated, qualified and experienced workforce. at the same time, new businesses and employment models have emerged; their consequences on employment should be looked at closely. an active and comprehensive social dialogue is therefore really essential in this regard. fifth: improvements and innovation. we welcome the highlighting of the importance of implementing the single european sky. ses2+ is an important enabler for modernisation of air traffic management and also ensures better safety oversight of air navigation services. furthermore, it allows for improved capacity and environmental performance, less congestion and delays for passengers, and reduced costs for the aviation value network. regarding sesar, we now have a coherent project, governed by a strong legal framework, driven by innovative partnerships and supported by union incentives, that is capable of deploying innovative air traffic management concepts in a coordinated manner. therefore, we agree and share parliament’s desire to implement sesar as quickly as possible. for this reason, i can only echo the dissatisfaction with the legislative files on aviation that are still pending – the slots directive, single european sky 2+ and passenger rights. parliament’s political support is highly welcomed. the sixth topic: the environment. we must deal with the environmental impact of an ever—expanding sector. i am confident that innovation and technical solutions can contribute to a reduced carbon footprint for aviation. i witnessed this myself at the recent paris and dubai air shows. the technology is here to serve. at the same time, the eu has put in place powerful regulatory tools to address co2 emissions. in icao, we need to play a critical role towards developing a global solution. we will do everything to enable this to happen. i believe that by working together we can ensure a strong european aviation sector, and i look forward to hearing members’ views on this.

in writing. ‒ one of the european union's strong concerns has been to facilitate cooperation and communication between member states' institutions, which has been reflected in a number of programmes, one of which is the inter-administration data exchange programme, which aims to exchange data between member states' administrations and between administrations and the eu institutions (ida), launched as early as 1995. with the evolution of technology and the growing expectations of civil society, the interoperability solutions programme for european public administrations (isa, followed by isa 2) was initiated, which focuses on the needs and dynamics of businesses and citizens precisely so that administrations respond effectively and promptly to citizens' needs. the isa 2 programme on interoperability solutions for european public administrations is the basis for modernising public administrations in europe, improving the quality of public services, creating a competitive environment for businesses and at the same time improving the quality of life of the population, which is why i voted in favour of the report on interoperability solutions as a means of modernising the public sector.
in writing. ‒ i believe that interoperability in data protection and closer cross-border cooperation should highlight a substantial potential for improving the efficiency of public services in the member states which, if fully exploited, could contribute to the achievement of the objectives of the european semester. i support the rapporteur's position and therefore believe it is important to introduce specific references to the union acquis on data protection, as the current proposal of the european commission does not sufficiently address this issue.
in writing. ‒ isa is the latest programme in a long line of commission programmes that support the interconnection, digitisation and collaboration of public administrations since the 1990s. the current programme, isa, will end this year and has supported the development of egovernment solutions that are today operational in public administrations across the eu. the new programme, isa, will build on the success of its predecessor. it will ensure seamless electronic cross-border or cross-sector interaction between european public administrations in areas such as government, health, invoicing and procurement. isa² will support the development of interoperable digital solutions which will be available to all interested public administrations on european, national and regional level, free of charge. this will lead to a harmonised interoperability landscape in europe, saving time and costs, and contribute to the modernisation of european public administrations and to the creation of a digital single market. i welcome the introduction in the programme of new priorities such as greater involvement of citizens and businesses, additional safeguards concerning data protection, a stronger emphasis on the reuse and sharing of references and solutions, enhanced cooperation between member states to fight the digital divide, develop creation of user communities and exchange of good practice.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report because the isa2 is the latest in a long line of commission programmes that support the interconnection, digitisation and collaboration of public administrations. moreover, it will ensure seamless electronic cross-border or cross-sector interaction between european public administrations in areas such as government, health, invoicing and procurement. i hope that the isa2 programme will build on the success of its predecessor and will lead to a harmonised interoperability landscape, saving time and costs.
in writing. ‒ an efficient public administration is key to a successful citizen-state relationship. the eu’s aim is to enable the free movement of its citizens, goods and services, and therefore it is important not to burden this movement with unnecessary bureaucracy. if national public administrations could function more like a network, thus collaborating and sharing information, it could save everyone time and money. this piece of legislation puts in place a programme to facilitate digital cross-border and cross-sector information exchange between our public administrations, thus enhancing this network functionality. such an initiative can only increase the quality of the services provided by public administrations in the eu and therefore it has my full support.
in writing. ‒ the programme on interoperability solutions for european public administrations, businesses and citizens was launched in 1995. i have voted for this report that will help public administrations in europe to modernise in order to address overall economic competitiveness and people’s quality of life.
in writing. ‒ isa 2 is the latest commission programme supporting the interconnection, digitalisation and collaboration of public administrations. the current programme will end this year and has supported the development of egovernment solutions that are now operational in public administrations across the union. the new isa 2 programme will ensure cross-border or cross-sectoral electronic interaction between european public administrations in areas such as governance, health, billing and public procurement. isa 2 will support the development of interoperable digital solutions available free of charge to all interested public administrations at european, national and regional level. this will contribute to the modernisation of european public administrations and the creation of a digital single market. the new isa 2 programme is planned to run from 2016 to 2020 with a budget of approximately eur 131 million. as itre s&d coordinator, i welcome the introduction of new priorities into the programme such as greater involvement of citizens and businesses, additional safeguards on data protection, a strong focus on re-use and exchange of references and solutions, enhanced cooperation between member states to tackle the digital divide and to develop user communities and exchange of good practices.
in writing. ‒ in a european union, public administration serves the european citizen at all levels. given the right of our citizens to travel freely within the union and to reside in any member state, public administration services must also remain efficient and respond to the needs of european citizens. to this end, a number of programmes have been launched on interoperability solutions for european public administration, and the report we voted on today focuses on isa2, a welcome continuation of the ida, idabc and isa programmes. in particular, the commission will support the development of a european e-government platform for the promotion of e-government in the union. cross-border electronic barriers are still a cause of fragmentation in the union and prevent the creation of common services in the interest of european citizens. the key element in this context is interoperability in data protection and cross-border cooperation, the contribution of which to the successful implementation of the policies is essential. the isa2 programme brings us closer to the objective of modernising public administration and adapting it to a highly mobile, informed and digital society.
in writing. ‒ the political representation of seats in the european parliament is not determined by a single european election, but by the 28 national elections in the 28 member states of the european union of the national mandate quotas. even if the harmonisation of electoral rules is not an end in itself, european citizens must exercise their right to vote under comparable conditions, respecting democratic principles. the first direct elections to the european parliament (ep) took place in 1979, and the provisions governing european elections have evolved, but not as substantially as the ep would have liked. however, the maastricht treaty gave the ep the right to give its opinion on the council's decision in respect of the uniform procedure, which gives european citizens the right to vote and stand as candidates in their member state of residence, whatever that may be. i spoke in favour of the legislative initiative on the reform of the european union electoral legislation, as it reflects the objective of strengthening the democratic dimension of european elections, strengthens eu citizenship, leads to a better functioning of the european parliament, but also to the governance of the union.
in writing. ‒ i believe that the reform of the parliament's electoral procedure should aim to strengthen the democratic and transnational dimension of european elections and the democratic legitimacy of the decision-making process within the union, to give consistency to the concept of citizenship of the union, to increase the legitimacy of the european parliament's work and to reinforce the principles of electoral equality and equal opportunities, to increase the effectiveness of the system applied in the conduct of european elections and to bring members of the european parliament closer to their constituents, especially the youngest among them. i support the idea that the list of candidates for the european parliament elections should ensure gender equality.

in writing. ‒ the proposals by parliament to reform the electoral law of the european union bring important changes that will stimulate political debate across europe. firstly, the report brings more visibility to the european parties, given that national parties will need to indicate clearly their affiliation to the european ones on the ballot papers and on posters and other campaign materials. the report also creates a clear link between the elections and the future european commission because it states that the nominations for commission president will be announced by all european political parties prior to the elections. i voted for this report because it also seeks to increase the participation rate at european elections by suggesting the introduction of electronic and internet voting options as well as postal voting.

in writing. ‒ the elections to the european parliament are governed to a great extent by national rules. as a result, election campaigns are often dominated by national topics and led by national political actors. reforming the electoral law will make elections to the european parliament more european, in both form and substance, by promoting electoral equality between eu citizens across the eu and improving parliament’s functioning and the eu’s governance. the current report represents parliament’s aim of obtaining such an eu‐wide electoral procedure. the provisions in the report ask for a common deadline of 12 weeks before the vote for the establishment of electoral lists, and nomination of lead candidates; gender balance on electoral lists; higher visibility of national parties’ affiliation to european political parties on ballot papers; and a minimum threshold of between 3 and 5%. while i support the reform of the law, i believe it must exclude any attempts to introduce transnational lists. electing members on transitional lists means these members have no concrete constituencies. that raises concerns as to the democratic accountability of these members towards their voters. yet i voted for the report, as i believe that reforming the law will lead to more transparent, visible and democratic elections.

in writing. ‒ the problem of achieving legislative clarity and coherence is one faced by all systems, from national to international. of course, within the union, its strictness is felt both from the perspective of the member states and the beneficiaries, the former because they need to harmonise their national legislation within the union framework, and the latter to benefit from union provisions, transparency or, better, to know their rights as citizens of the union. achieving this legislative coherence requires not only that we are very careful when drafting laws, but also that we monitor their development and implementation, and that we review and optimise procedures. the commission has undertaken these objectives in line with its commitments under the interinstitutional agreement on better law-making and its policy on regulatory adequacy and will continue to implement them by identifying transitional acts that have already achieved their purpose or whose content has already been taken over by other acts. i voted in favour of repealing this series of acts which have been identified as obsolete because their maintenance would only mislead member states and citizens.
in writing. ‒ in the context of the expiry of the transitional period set out in protocol 36 on transitional provisions, annexed to the treaties, the commission has performed an assessment of the schengen acquis and of the legal instruments in the field of police cooperation and judicial cooperation in criminal matters. a number of acts have been identified as obsolete because their content has been taken up by subsequent acts or because they are temporary in nature. in the inter-institutional agreement of 16 december 2003 the european parliament, the council and the commission agreed on reducing the volume of, and simplifying, union law, including by repealing obsolete acts. on the basis of its screening and in line with the commitments in the inter-institutional agreement on better law-making and its policy on regulatory fitness, the commission submitted a proposal to repeal as obsolete the following acts:- 11 decisions of the schengen executive committee because their content had been taken up in subsequent acts, and- council regulation (ec) no 189/2008 of 18 february 2008 on the testing of the second generation schengen information system (sis ii), the legal effect of which was exhausted once the sis ii became operational on 9 april 2013.

in writing. ‒ with the aim of making the application of european law more efficient and transparent, the european commission has proposed to reassess the need for certain legislative acts at a certain time. the report we voted on today concerns the withdrawal from the schengen acquis of 11 acts in the field of police and judicial cooperation, which are considered to be obsolete because of their temporary nature or because their objectives have been taken over by their successors. the repeal of these acts cannot be achieved at the level of each member state, which is why the measure will be implemented at the level of the union. i believe that the withdrawal of obsolete legislation can only make the application of legislation in the member states more effective, which is why i voted in favour of this report.
in writing. ‒ european union legislation includes a number of acts that are no longer applied. those acts are no longer relevant because of their temporary nature or because their content has been taken over by subsequent acts. in order to improve transparency and to provide greater legal certainty for european citizens, such acts are withdrawn from the union legislative acquis. in view of this and taking into account the expiry of the transitional period provided for in protocol no 36 annexed to the treaties, the commission has carried out an evaluation of the schengen acquis. following this assessment, the commission proposed the repeal of 11 decisions of the schengen executive committee and of the regulation on the testing of the second generation schengen information system (sis ii), which had exhausted its legal effects by the time sis ii became operational on 9 april 2013. the decisions of the executive committee concerned, inter alia, visa policy, the exchange of statistical information, the application of stamps on passports, the fight against illegal immigration, the fight against illegal immigration. the legislative resolution of the european parliament supports the repeal of these obsolete acts. i voted in favour of this resolution.
in writing. ‒ in the context of the increasingly intensive exercise of citizens' right to free movement, it is becoming a reality that many of the acts that may fall within the criminal sphere may occur partially in the territory of several member states, which makes the judicial cooperation of these states necessary for the discovery of the facts and the persons involved, the administration of evidence and other aspects of the imposition of sanctions. the importance of this communication and cooperation of the authorities of all member states has been demonstrated in the course of the conclusion of several union acts and commitments, and the efforts of the commission, the council and the european parliament have also had an impact on citizens, who are safer wherever they are in the union. i welcome this initiative to reduce over-legislation and the burden on the legislative system, given the uncertainty that such legislative stains can create if they are maintained. in accordance with article 288 tfeu, regulations are binding in their entirety and directly applicable in all member states, thus better serving the purpose of the proposal, which is to repeal acts deemed to be obsolete. that is why i voted in favour of this report.
in writing. ‒ in the context of the expiry of the transitional period set out in protocol 36 on transitional provisions annexed to the treaties, the commission has performed an assessment of the schengen acquis and of the legal instruments in the field of police cooperation and judicial cooperation in criminal matters. a number of acts have been identified as obsolete because their content has been taken up by subsequent acts or because they are of a temporary nature. in the inter-institutional agreement of 16 december 2003 parliament, the council and the commission agreed on reducing the volume of, and simplifying, union law, including by means of repealing obsolete acts. on the basis of its screening and in line with the commitments in the inter-institutional agreement on better law-making and the its policy on regulatory fitness, the commission submitted a proposal to repeal as obsolete decisions of the executive committee sch/com-ex (93) 14 (combating drug trafficking) and (98) 52 (police handbook), declaration of the executive committee sch/com—ex (97) decl. 13 rev 2 (abduction of minors) and council decision 2008/173/jha of 18 february 2018 on the tests of the second generation schengen information system (sis ii).

in writing. ‒ the european commission regularly carries out a screening of the legislative acquis to identify acts that could be repealed in view of the expiry of the transition period provided for in the treaties. those acts are no longer relevant because of their temporary nature or because their content has been taken over by subsequent acts. in order to improve transparency and to provide greater legal certainty for european citizens, such acts are withdrawn from the union legislative acquis. following this assessment, the european commission has submitted a proposal to repeal 7 council joint actions, the content of which has been taken up in subsequent acts, and council act 1999/c 26/07 laying down the staff regulations of europol staff. the european parliament resolution supports the repeal of these obsolete acts and also proposes the repeal of two other acts which have become obsolete, namely the convention on the withdrawal of the right to drive motor vehicles and the council framework decision on the european evidence warrant for the purpose of obtaining objects, documents and data for use in criminal proceedings. i voted in favour of this resolution.
in writing. ‒ the proposal for a decision on accession to the extended commission of the convention for the conservation of southern bluefin tuna (ccsbt) aims to approve the exchange of letters between the union and the ccsbt so that the eu can become a full member, given that the european union has been a cooperating non-contracting party since 2006. the union has actively contributed to the sustainable and sound management of marine resources and to combating illegal, unreported and unregulated fishing, pursuing a policy of cooperation with all regional fisheries management organisations (rfmo). these organisations are set up by states concerned by fisheries in certain areas and have both an advisory and an administrative role, with competence in the technical field and in the area of control obligations. thus, only countries can accede to the ccsbt convention. as a result, the union, although playing an active role in regional tuna management organisations, is excluded from membership. i voted in favour of this report because i believe that the active involvement of the union in the management of regional fisheries organisations must be embodied in the granting of full rights.
in writing. ‒ the proposal concerns authorisation of the exchange of letters between the eu and the extended commission of the convention for the conservation of southern bluefin tuna, (ccsbt). the signing of this instrument of international law will allow the eu to become a full member of the ccsbt extended commission, having enjoyed cooperating non-member status since 2006. the european union, in accordance with its commitments under the united nations convention on the law of the sea of 10 december 1982 relating to the conservation and management of straddling fish stocks and highly migratory fish stocks, has been cooperating very actively with all regional fisheries organisations in a bid to contribute to the rational and sustainable management of marine resources and combat illegal, unreported and unregulated fishing. i voted in favour of this report that will allow full participation in the work of the ccsbt.
in writing. ‒ the commission for the conservation of southern bluefin tuna (ccsbt) is a regional fisheries management organisation (rfmo) responsible for the management of southern bluefin tuna wherever it is to be found. the convention for the conservation of southern bluefin tuna entered into force on 20 may 1994. the european union has been a cooperating non-member of the ccsbt extended commission since 2006. i voted for this report which will allow the eu to become a full member.
in writing. ‒ i support this report in my vote today, as it supports the council's decision to authorise the exchange of official letters between the eu and the commission for the conservation of southern bluefin tuna, with a view to the eu's membership of this regional organisation. it is in the interest of the eu to become part of this organisation, given that vessels flying the flag of member states fish in the waters concerned, which also involves incidental catches of bluefin tuna. this is also in line with the eu's objectives to protect and sustainably manage fish stocks.
in writing. ‒ tuna fishing is closely monitored by certain regional tuna management organisations. the european union has pursued a very active policy of cooperation with all regional fisheries management organisations, in line with the commitments it has undertaken under the provisions of the united nations convention on the law of the sea of 10 december 1982, with regard to the conservation and management of anadromous and highly migratory fish stocks. the ultimate objective is the rational and sustainable management of marine resources and, not least, the fight against illegal, unreported and unregulated fishing. the european union plays an active role in six of these organisations. the signature of the convention for the conservation of southern bluefin tuna (ccsbt), an instrument of international law, will give the union full membership, although the union, through the european commission, has been cooperating with the ccsbt since 2006.
in writing. ‒ the european parliament's draft legislative resolution on insurance intermediation aims to reform directive 2002/92/ec by harmonising national provisions in the insurance distribution sector with a view to applying the same level of consumer protection. insurance and reinsurance intermediaries play a key role in the distribution of insurance and reinsurance products within the union. thus, given that insurance products may be distributed by different categories of persons or institutions such as agents, insurance brokers and agents, insurance undertakings, travel agents and car rental companies, it is necessary that all such persons or institutions should be covered by this directive in order to ensure equal treatment between agents and consumer protection. the proposed directive aims to create the same level of consumer protection regardless of the distribution channels, while ensuring a level playing field between distributors. given that there are still considerable differences between the provisions of national law which prevent access to and the pursuit of insurance and reinsurance distribution activities in the internal market, the draft legislative resolution is appropriate in strengthening the internal market for insurance intermediation, which is why i voted in favour of this report.
in writing. ‒ i welcome the supplementary report by werner langen, whom i would like to congratulate on the outcome of the directive’s recast. i also welcome the outcome of the negotiations with the council to broaden the scope of the directive, to strengthen rules on transparency and to align the rules regarding investment products with the markets in financial instruments directive (mifid). i believe it will improve the way insurance products are sold and the level of protection for consumers and retails investors. and these outcomes are achievable only through greater transparency on price and costs, the prevention of conflicts of interest, and better information and advice when selling products. i strongly support the reinforcement of the ‘tying practices’ rules, so that when insurance products are offered with another good or service, consumer will have the option of buying the main good without insurance. sanctions and reporting infractions are also important: member states have to ensure, when transposing the directive, that their competent authority will impose administrative sanctions and other measures applicable to all infringements of the national provisions, and take all necessary measure to ensure that they are implemented.
in writing. ‒ i voted for this report, which is the only eu legislation that regulates the point of sale for insurance products so as to ensure the rights of the consumer. the revised directive seeks to improve regulation in the retail insurance market in an efficient manner. it aims to ensure a level playing field for all those involved in the selling of insurance products and to improve policyholder protection.
in writing. ‒ the supplementary report on the insurance intermediation directive clarifies a number of clauses, seeks to harmonise national provisions in the insurance distribution sector and updates the text of the directive to take account of new trends in the internal insurance market. insurance and reinsurance intermediaries are the main actors in the distribution of insurance and reinsurance products on the european union market. insurance may be distributed by natural or legal persons such as agents, brokers and insurance agents, banks, insurance companies, travel agents and car rental companies. the objective of the directive remains the same: equal treatment of insurance distributors and consumer protection, regardless of the distribution channel for insurance products. in order to achieve that objective, the european insurance and occupational pensions authority should establish, publish and regularly update a database with each insurance and reinsurance intermediary operating in the internal market. in parallel, member states should establish a single information point for citizens, providing them with access to this register or database.
mr president, i supported this report because i consider the growing phenomenon of child poverty in europe to be a major problem. in the last five years, more than 1.6 million children have been affected by child poverty in the european union, and as this trend is growing and negative, it is necessary that we, here at the european union level, address this problem and seek solutions. as a right-wing politician, i support the restrictive fiscal policies of individual nation-states in an effort to keep budgets balanced. on the other hand, it should be said that austerity measures should not affect children and should not increase their poverty, should not affect their social security and access to the school education system, because in the future we are creating the problem of an uneducated and socially weak generation, which can be a major problem for europe and also in the context of internal security.
mr president, your children are the citizens of the europe of tomorrow. the increasing number of children living in poverty and persistent extreme poverty is one of the most pressing challenges facing europe today. alarmingly, in 21st-century europe, malnourished children are on the rise, and diseases long thought to be conquered have resurfaced. it is sobering and beyond the immediate problem that in many member states the risk of child poverty also exists in families with high work intensity. the commission should define a roadmap to overcome these challenges, make the fight against child poverty and increasing school drop-out a priority in the governance of the european semester and the europe 2020 strategy, and set targets for reducing child poverty and social exclusion within the same strategy. this time, i would like to draw the attention of all member states to the importance of combating child poverty, which is the key to the future of our continent.

in writing. ‒ eu funds can be a powerful lever to alleviate inequalities and improve the lives of people in marginalised communities. i fully back the call in this report to ensure that marginalised communities are better served by accountable and transparent use of eu funds. the commission should look closely at how marginalised communities can be identified and defined so that funding can be properly directed on the basis of clearly established guidance. we must make all the necessary efforts to combat discrimination and social exclusion and ensure that marginalised groups are integrated into a diverse, tolerant and fair society. this will bring benefits to all.
in writing. ‒ cohesion policy is the most effective instrument for economic, social and territorial consolidation. experience in managing social disparities shows that we need action at european level in reducing and eradicating poverty and exclusion, preventing segregation and promoting equal access and opportunities for all citizens, including the most marginalised groups. in complementing action taken at union level, i believe that multi-level governance and coordination play a key role in the preparation and implementation of programmes for the integration of marginalised communities. women from marginalized communities are most at risk. in addition to low employment rates, they face multiple and severe discrimination. another issue that the report considers is the need for a definition of marginalized communities. why do i think this is necessary? member states must retain the responsibility to develop their own national indicators on the basis of which to develop a definition, but i believe that we need a set of guidelines from the commission to harmonise the process.
in writing. ‒ the concept of 'marginalized communities' refers to various groups and individuals in society, such as minorities, roma, people with disabilities, people living below the poverty line or at risk of poverty, migrants, refugees and socially excluded groups. the economic crisis and the budget cuts it has caused have repeatedly generated serious budgetary problems for municipalities and have led, in the member states, to the aggravation of existing problems such as unemployment, lack of social security and lack of public health services. moreover, this has led to a decrease or even a lack of actions related to marginalised groups aimed at improving their integration. the report highlights the need to mobilise cohesion policy funds to improve living conditions and facilitate access for marginalised communities to education, housing, healthcare, employment, childcare and social services. furthermore, the need for a long-term perspective is highlighted in order to be effective, as well as the mobilisation of mechanisms to guarantee the impact on target groups and to address the problem of exclusion and marginalisation. i therefore voted in favour of the report on cohesion policy and marginalised communities.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report regarding the eu cohesion policy and marginalised communities. the crisis has had a direct negative impact on members of marginalised communities in the eu, in addition also many municipalities in the member states still continue to face severe budgetary constraints which prevented them from dealing adequately with marginalisation in society. the main responsibility for changing the situation of marginalised communities lies with the member states, but also the eu cohesion policy can play a powerful role in providing an integrated approach to tackling all the different forms of discrimination that marginalised communities face. using eu funds for the inclusion of marginalised communities can become a great opportunity for promoting and supporting greater cohesion in european societies.
in writing. ‒ the future of the european union is linked to peace, security, development and the human rights situation in the world, and the need for cooperation with the un is clear. the challenges facing the eu require global solutions, and global problems necessarily require european action. due to the close correlation between the principles and objectives of the european union's foreign policy, as enshrined in article 21 of the treaty on european union, and those of the un, and the fact that article 21 of the teu explicitly requires respect for the principles of the un charter and international law, the future of both organisations is intrinsically linked and their smooth functioning also depends on how they manage their cooperation and actions. given that the eu is already actively involved, under the auspices of the un, in promoting peace, security and progress, it is necessary to strengthen the role of the union and its member states in the un on all areas of external concern, including crisis management, atrocity prevention, strengthening the rule of law, humanitarian crises and humanitarian aid. the eu cannot tackle these threats alone, but needs the support of international partners, which is why i voted in favour of this report, considering eu-un cooperation to be fundamental.
in writing. ‒ the eu needs global partners to achieve its foreign policy objectives, particularly in areas such as peace and security, organised crime, terrorism, regional conflicts, failed states and the proliferation of weapons of mass destruction. article 21 (1) teu states that the eu and its member states share the values and principles of the un charter. the eu security environment is increasingly volatile due to the high number of security challenges. conflicts such as those in ukraine, syria, iraq, the rise of the terrorist organisation isis, the crisis in libya and the terrorist threat in africa (sahel, libya and the horn of africa) pose serious threats that require global responses. i support the ep's motion for a resolution on the eu's role in the un. i believe that in pursuing its foreign policy objectives (in line with the treaty), it is important for the eu to work towards strengthening global governance within the un system and increasing its influence within the un system, all in the context of the eu's commitment to actively support a comprehensive reform of the un system in order to strengthen its legitimacy, transparency, regional representation, accountability and effectiveness in responding to today's complex and multidimensional challenges.
in writing. ‒ i fully support the initiative to persuade the european union to support a woman for the post of un secretary-general, which provides that the eu will support a woman in the next election for the post of un secretary-general. in this way, we could witness a world first, by electing a woman to a position of global prestige and significance.
in writing. ‒ today we are called to face unforeseen, dramatic events that are already changing the world forever. the number of humanitarian emergencies has never been higher and the refugee crisis represents the ultimate test for the cohesion of the european union. in order to deal effectively and successfully with these transnational issues, it is fundamental that we strengthen cooperation with the un institutions, making sure that our values are promoted, our ambitions are commonly shared and our engagements are mutually respected. we should therefore push for the establishment of a high-level dialogue on the implementation of the sustainable development goals. in order to achieve them, further cooperation is required in the areas of education, health, climate action, food and nutrition, water, sanitation and hygiene, child protection, gender equality, social inclusion, humanitarian aid, migration, human rights, non-discrimination on all ground, good governance and democracy building. in particular, i would like to underline that one of our main priorities should be the protection of children and of women, whose protection is crucial for the achievement of sustainable and equitable development for all.
in writing. ‒ i support the reform of the un as a means of strengthening the efficiency of the organisation. the eu must play an active role within the organisation, project its values and contribute to providing global solutions to global problems.
in writing. ‒ i have voted for this report that should improve the eu’s prosperity, better protect its security and ensure that its governments comply with global rules, not only to safeguard europe’s prosperity and security but also with the intention of spreading respect for democracy, human rights, and the rule of law.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report as it highlights some major points concerning the current nature of the united nations organisation which i think, if reformed, would be beneficial to the eu in particular and the whole world in general. the fact that, taken together, the union is a major economic, political and military actor in the world, with two nuclear powers, a large population and immense political power, reflects, i believe, the outdated nature of the un security council. the un needs a deep and comprehensive reform, streamlining the unsc, but also the rules of the unga, the coordination between its bodies, more tools for its key tasks (for example preventing genocides) and better accountability and transparency of its institutions to its members. the eu needs to be an integral part of this reform, if not an outright leader.
in writing. ‒ the eu and its member states are collectively the single largest financial contributor to the un system, with contributions amounting to 35% of the un regular budget, and 36.8% of the un peacekeeping budgets. moreover, the eu and its member states provide about half of all the voluntary contributions to un funds and programmes. based on these figures i believe that the eu needs to play a prominent role in reforming the un system to make it more democratic, efficient and transparent. i welcome the proposals in the current text. i particularly support the call to reform the un security system with the objective of granting the eu a permanent seat. that will give the eu the opportunity to play an active role within the un in a way that reflects our soft power. i also welcome the support of my colleagues for my initiative to promote gender equality within the un system, by asking the eu to support a female candidate for the role of the un secretary general in the upcoming elections. this comprehensive text will help us define the role that the eu can play, by leading a systematic reform of the un system. therefore i voted in favour of it.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on the eu's role in the un, as the un is the world's leading organisation for improving global governance and the best framework for promoting eu values and interests. the principles and objectives of the european union's foreign policy are closely linked to those of the un, and are founded on respect for the principles of the un charter and international law. in an increasingly volatile environment, the eu faces a number of security challenges, such as the conflicts in eastern ukraine, syria and iraq, the rise of the terrorist organisation isis and the terrorist threat in africa, and global responses are needed, as the eu cannot address these threats on its own, but needs the support of international partners. to better contribute to its foreign policy objectives, the eu must therefore work to strengthen global governance within the un system and increase its influence and that of its member states within this system. in this regard, the report underlines the need for a comprehensive reform of the un system, with the aim of strengthening the eu's legitimacy, accountability and effectiveness in this framework.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on the role of the eu within the un. in this report, parliament recalls that the eu and its member states share the values and principles of the un charter (as stated in article 21(1) teu) and have a crucial role in promoting those principles as well as the goals of the un, through the external action of the union. parliament welcomes the fact that the eu and its member states play an active part and contribute to the work of the un system in different ways and formats. the report recalls the eu’s commitment to actively support a comprehensive reform of the un system in order to strengthen its legitimacy, its regional representation, and its transparency, accountability and effectiveness.

on behalf of the alde group.– mr president, colleagues, a healthy, functional society needs healthy people. employees working in a safe and healthy environment will enjoy not only their lives but also their work, and thus they will be more productive. therefore, investing in safety and health at the workplace is a win-win situation for both the employers and the employees. to achieve this we need clear and simple legislation and its enforcement. today we have 24 directives which regulate this subject, yet the number of accidents and work-related diseases is extremely high. this discrepancy is mostly the result of red tape inherent in a heavy, overlapping and burdening legislation. it is undeniable that there are many work-related risks, both traditional and emerging, but i strongly believe that the focus should not be on adding new pieces of legislation to the pile of existing ones, thereby overloading the employers and resulting in the end in a very low level of compliance. 85% of european jobs are created by smes, yet they are the most encumbered by the legislation as it is today. compliance requires allocation of resources, financial expertise and time—wise ones while trying to stay competitive and generate jobs. this status quo is counterproductive. our emphasis as legislators should be on elaborating a simplified and efficient framework that is easy to understand and implement, that does not necessarily involve great financial costs for employers, and that is ultimately beneficial for employees, the economy and society as a whole. in writing. according to european statistics, more than 4 000 workers die each year in accidents at work and the number of fatal occupational diseases is over 150 000 per year. in the current context it is essential for europe to promote a safe and healthy working environment for all workers throughout the entire working life cycle. we must not forget that the european labour market is changing. the number of precarious jobs is increasing, as is the number of women in these jobs. in addition, new forms of employment are emerging and new technologies have brought with them new challenges in terms of occupational safety. all these require viable solutions and an appropriate process for collecting comparable data on occupational diseases and exposures, precisely to identify best prevention practices. the economic costs of accidents at work and occupational diseases are significant and the particular complexity of many new and emerging risks requires immediate action at eu level.

in writing. ‒ i have stated my support for the report on the mobilisation of the eu solidarity fund (eusf): payment of advances in the 2016 budget as any instrument that can contribute quickly, efficiently and flexibly to resolving emergencies should be encouraged. the aim of the solidarity fund is to enable the eu to respond to emergencies caused by major natural disasters and to show solidarity with the regions of europe affected by a disaster. the fund may provide financial assistance to member states and countries at the stage of negotiations for accession to the union in the event of a 'major natural disaster', that is to say, if the total direct damage caused by the disaster exceeds eur 3 billion in 2011 prices or 0,6% of the gni of the country concerned, whichever is the lower. we must be aware that the solidarity fund is not just a form of eu financial assistance, but also an important means of conveying a clear political message of solidarity, providing much-needed support to the affected citizens.
in writing. ‒ the european union solidarity fund (eusf) was set up to enable the union to respond to emergency situations caused by major natural disasters and to express european solidarity to disaster-stricken regions within europe. the fund can provide financial aid to member states and countries involved in accession negotiations in the event of a ‘major natural disaster’, i.e. where total direct damage caused by the disaster exceeds eur 3 billion in 2011 prices or 0.6% of the country’s gni, whichever is the lower. it can also be mobilised in the event of a regional disaster. the current proposal for a decision of the european parliament and of the council is not linked to a specific disaster. instead, it aims at entering into the general budget of the union for 2016 the amount of eur 50 million in commitment and payment appropriations for the payment of advances in a timely and efficient way in the event of a disaster occurring next year. the eusf is not simply another form of eu financial support, but that it also contributes to sending a clear political message of solidarity, while providing much-needed assistance to affected citizens. a prompt response capacity, including through the payment of an advance, will help the union achieve these objectives.

in writing. ‒ the use of bis (2-ethylhexyl) phthalate (dehp) may lead to undesirable effects with respect to the endocrine system of at least one animal species. this substance is of major concern because the serious effects lead to problems of human health. given the unfavourable effects on both animals and humans, i believe that urgent action is needed to unlock this situation. financial interests cannot be the only ones pursuing it, given that while the committee for risk assessment (cer) has recognised the endocrine-disrupting effects of dehp, the committee for socio-economic analysis (case) considers that the economic benefits of using this substance outweigh the risks to human health. i voted in favour of this report because i believe that we have a responsibility to the european public to protect our citizens and the environment from hazards such as hazardous chemicals.
in writing. ‒ given that bis (2-ethylhexyl) phthalate (dehp) is a known toxic substance, classified by reach as a toxic substance of very high concern, affecting scientifically proven reproduction and the endocrine system in the environment. the applicants did not fulfil the conditions for authorisation as they did not demonstrate that all risks in the procedures applied are adequately controllable. they also failed to demonstrate that the socioeconomic benefits of processing this substance would outweigh the risks of dehp and that there are no suitable alternatives. there are much safer alternatives on the european market in terms of substances, materials, processes and technologies used. what i think we need to take seriously is innovation and the principles of the circular economy. i therefore supported the objection to the authorisation of bis ((2-ethylhexyl) phthalate.
in writing. ‒ dehp is as a substance of very high concern and, already in 2000, it was included in annex 1 setting out the candidate list of 553 substances under category i of chemicals that showed evidence of endocrine disrupting activity in at least one species using intact animals. on 12 december 2014, the member state committee (msc) unanimously agreed to the identification of dehp as a substance giving rise to an equivalent level of concern due to its endocrine disrupting properties in the environment(6); the msc unanimously acknowledged that, in the case of dehp, there is scientific evidence on endocrine disrupting activity and on the causal link between this activity and adverse effects on human health. i therefore supported the call on the commission to withdraw its draft implementing decision and to submit a new draft rejecting the applications for authorisation for the formulation of recycled soft pvc containing dehp.

in writing. ‒ european integration is a complex process in full swing. a key component of this, in addition to the political and monetary component, is the fiscal dimension. the member states' charging systems are still too different to have a coherent system at union level. this creates gaps in development and living standards between member states. for these reasons, there is a need for greater harmonisation of tax policies at european level. this process is not possible without monitoring in each member state by independent and impartial actors whose work must not be affected by the interests of the state actors concerned. following the monitoring, recommendations will be issued with a view to establishing a minimum and a maximum level of taxation at eu level. at the same time, a comprehensive database of 'tax havens' will be established and the fight against intra-community tax evasion will be regulated more effectively. states or commercial operators that fail to comply with these regulations will have to bear the consequences and pay the penalties set by the european institutions. this will generate new revenue for the union which can be used for the development of the member states.

mr president, raising labour standards and the level of occupational health and safety is not just in the interest of workers but also in the interest of companies’ productivity and competitiveness, the sustainability of social security systems and of society at large. we need clear and efficient rules in the field of health and safety at work and rigorous application regardless of the size of employers. this does not preclude however, taking into account the specific situation and needs of micro and small enterprises and the provision of special assistance to them in the implantation of health and safety legislation. i also strongly agree with the call from the report that we should step up our measures against undeclared work, as it is undeclared workers that are most exposed to work-related accidents.
in writing. ‒ based on one of the european union's objectives that all workers have the right to the highest level of protection of health and safety at work, we need to focus our attention on the need to promote a safe and healthy working environment for workers throughout the entire working life cycle. i believe that more investment is needed in risk prevention policies and in promoting, developing and supporting a culture of prevention in relation to health and safety at work. this prevention, together with increased attention to the cumulative effects of occupational risks, creates added value for workers and for society as a whole. given that risks to workers' health and safety are largely similar across the union, the eu has a role to play in helping member states to tackle risks effectively and to ensure a level playing field across the eu. i voted in favour of the report on the eu strategic framework on health and safety at work 2014-2020 because this framework is a concrete means of providing workers with safer working conditions.
in writing. ‒ i believe that ensuring a level playing field throughout the eu and eliminating unfair competition and social dumping is crucial and i believe that labour inspectorates play a key role in ensuring that workers' rights to a safe and healthy working environment are respected and in providing advice and guidance to employers, especially smes and micro-enterprises. i also believe that member states should be encouraged to comply with the ilo standards and guidelines on labour inspection, to ensure sufficient staff and resources in labour inspectorates and to improve training for labour inspectors, as recommended by the european economic and social committee.
in writing. ‒ considering that every year more than 4 000 workers die due to accidents at work and the number of fatal work-related diseases amounts to more than 150 000 on an annual basis, an eu strategic framework on health and safety at work is very much needed. the framework will allow the identification of many important challenges facing european employees and employers, but it still lacks, however, an ambitious agenda for concrete legislative proposals to improve the situation of workers with regard to existing and new and emerging risks as well as work-related diseases. i welcome the call for the commission to revise directive 2004/37/ec, adding more binding exposure limit values on the basis of scientific evidence; the call for a proposal for a comprehensive legal instrument on musculoskeletal disorders; the call for the development and implementation of a programme for systematic monitoring, managing and support for workers affected by psychological risks. the financial and economic crisis should not be used as an excuse to undermine occupational risk prevention policies as this approach is neither acceptable nor effective. nor should alleged administrative simplifications lead to lower health and safety standards for workers.
in writing. ‒ the financial crisis should not be used as an excuse to undermine workplace risk prevention policies. the commission and the member states should improve the collection of reliable data on occupational diseases, exposures and risks across all sectors. the commission must put forward concrete legislative proposals on health and safety at work and thus transform its 'strategic framework' into a real strategy.
in writing. ‒ every year more than 4 000 workers die due to accidents at work and the number of fatal work-related diseases amounts to more than 150 000 every single year. good health is a fundamental right in europe and even though considerable progress has been made in the area of occupational health and safety throughout the years, major risks to workers’ health and safety continue to exist. i voted for this report that will improve the health and safety situation of workers and ensure a level playing field for businesses.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report because it gives a very accurate analysis of the health and safety needs at work in the eu. the commission's strategy in this area, coordinated with national strategies, should ensure a high standard of health and safety at work for european citizens. it is a right that citizens have, but also an obligation on the part of employers, whether private or public, to ensure this standard. unfortunately, in the context of the economic crisis, many companies, but also the public sector, have had drastic cost reductions and layoffs. this has often led to situations where the workload has become larger and in some cases more dangerous for the remaining employees, which has endangered and endangers both the safety and health of people. the commission and the member states must work together to find a common approach to this problem and i am referring in particular to the implementation of effective strategies to ensure a standard level of occupational safety and health, with clear sanctions for those who do not comply with this standard.
in writing. the incidence of accidents at work and deaths from occupational diseases has reached alarming levels. for these reasons, more effective regulation of safety and health risks at work is needed. regulations should aim at limiting exposure to carcinogens and mutagens, avoiding the development of locomotor deficiencies and psychological risks from stress and avoiding exposure to asbestos. at the same time, the involvement of the social partners and social dialogue at all levels is required to achieve adequate protection of workers' safety and health, regardless of the size of the employer, the type of activity, the member state or the type of contract. the financial and economic crisis and the administrative simplifications (refit) should not be used as an excuse to lower safety and health standards for workers. a separate chapter is devoted to the challenges and risks facing women in the workplace. they must be vigorously combated, as must the incidence of violence against women in the workplace. the implementation of high european standards of worker protection can help to improve the situation internationally by including these requirements in all eu trade agreements with third parties. for these reasons, i support this laudable initiative.
in writing. ‒ the economic crisis has led to increased job insecurity and reduced earnings for businesses, especially smes, and this should not lead to a loss of focus on the importance of health and safety at work. improving occupational health and safety across europe can contribute to economic recovery and to achieving the europe 2020 targets of reaching an employment rate of 75% among the population aged 20-64. health and safety at work is a fundamental interest of society and an investment that has a positive effect on the productivity and competitiveness of enterprises and also improves the sustainability of social security systems. cancer is the leading cause of mortality from working conditions, followed by cardiovascular and respiratory diseases, while occupational accidents account for a small proportion of deaths. improvements in conditions and strong legislation on health and safety at work are therefore needed to prevent such situations. i therefore voted in favour of the report on the eu strategic framework on health and safety at work 2014-2020.
in writing. ‒ a healthy, functional society needs healthy people, and a healthy work environment will improve employee productivity. the promotion of health and safety at work and the protection of workers at work are essential to improving working conditions and, consequently, to protecting workers' health. the european parliament's report draws attention to this important issue and calls on the european commission to review legislation on health at work. improving the efficiency and effectiveness of the legislative framework in this area is essential for the protection of workers. the report also makes a number of recommendations on improving legislation on occupational diseases and stresses the importance of protecting workers from exposure to carcinogens, mutagens and toxic substances for reproduction. the report also draws attention to the need for increased exchange of information and good practice between member states and the importance of supplementing existing resources to increase the efficiency of labour inspectorates. working conditions must be in accordance with the legislation in force, this being not only the responsibility of law enforcement bodies but also of employers and employees. i voted in favour of this report.
