in writing. ‒ trade liberalisation is an important tool for ensuring sustainable economic growth and development, an objective on which the european union was built and which remains the main factor of cohesion between member states. however, such liberalisation needs to be accompanied by appropriate supportive policies, including measures at macro and microeconomic level, including fiscal transparency, fiscal policies and fiscal equity, administrative simplification, education and training, institutional reforms and social policies, in order to maximise and better distribute the benefits of trade reforms and effectively counterbalance any negative effects. all of these are specified in the parliament's resolution, along with the principle of special and differential treatment, the benefit of economic development of all continents and the contribution to poverty reduction. the doha round was launched with the objective of creating new trade opportunities, strengthening multilateral trade rules and addressing current trade system imbalances, with the needs and interests of developing countries, and in particular least developed countries, at the heart of the negotiations. i voted in favour of this resolution as i consider its completion essential and will therefore support the objectives it proposes.
in writing. ‒ as the reform of the common agricultural policy is the european union's contribution to the expectations of the doha round, i believe that wto member countries must proactively support efforts to create efficient and effective channels of work and to strengthen wto cooperation with other international organisations whose work has an influence on global trade negotiations, in particular the international labour organisation, the world health organisation, the un and its agencies and bodies, such as the un conference on trade and development, the food and agriculture organisation, the un environment programme, the un development programme and the un framework convention on climate change.
in writing. ‒ the doha round creates new trading opportunities, strengthens multilateral trade rules and addresses current imbalances in the trading system by placing the needs and interests of developing countries and especially of the least developed countries (ldcs) at its centre. thus, it contributes to fair and free trade at the service of the economic development of all continents and the alleviation of poverty. i support full commitment to the enduring value of multilateralism, respect for special and differential treatment in the negotiations, and the call for speedy ratification and implementation of the trade facilitation agreement. moreover, structural reform of the wto is needed in order to better guarantee an open, fair and non-discriminatory trading system based on shared rules, and which takes greater account of the role and interests of smes. finally, i believe the eu should continue to play a leading role in promoting tangible progress in the ongoing wto negotiations with a view to the full conclusion of the doha development round in the foreseeable future, as well as in facilitating the full participation of ldcs in global trade by acting as a bridge between the various positions of the wto members.
in writing. ‒ in light of the 10th wto ministerial conference which will take place in nairobi from 15 to 18 december 2015, the european parliament stresses the importance of a trade agenda based on free and fair trade and with development at the centre of the process. the principle of special and differential treatment should continue to be an integral part of the negotiations as it recognises the special needs of low-income and least developed countries, in particular in implementing trade provisions. we call for a speedy ratification of the trade facilitation agreement – the successful outcome of the 9th wto ministerial conference in 2013 – by all wto members. it was the first multilateral trade agreement concluded after the establishment of the wto in 1995 and will bring significant benefits in particular to developing country members. finally, we also welcome the progress made so far in plurilateral negotiations such as the environmental goods agreement, the information technology agreement and the trade in services agreement with a view to their multilateralisation once a critical mass of participants has been reached.
in writing. ‒ i have voted for this resolution that will encourage fair and free trade through increasingly just and equitable rules, with the purpose of creating economic development across the globe.
in writing. ‒ the european union has always been a supporter of free trade worldwide. this has been manifested by support for the creation of the world trade organization (wto) and through various bilateral free trade agreements with other states or multilateral ones involving other regional structures. at the same time, however, the eu has consistently advocated addressing the current imbalances in the trading system through differential treatment of the least developed countries, in order to support their development as a result of free trade and the rejection of protectionist barriers. in this respect, the eu is in favour of a structural reform of the wto that guarantees an open, fair and non-discriminatory international trade system and that gives a privileged place to small and medium-sized enterprises. the eu also supports the importance of dispute settlement mechanisms and greater transparency in the assessment of trade policies. the european parliament, as the direct representative of european citizens, also supports the development of the parliamentary dimension of the wto, which is intended to ensure the legitimacy of the organisation. the completion of the doha development agenda at the 10th wto ministerial conference can be an important step towards achieving these generous goals. i therefore believe that the european parliament must support this ambitious eu mandate for the next wto ministerial conference.
in writing. the wto needs a substantial structural reform to ensure a fairer, more open and non-discriminatory multilateral trading system based on clear rules shared and applied by all members of the organisation. common rules should take greater account of the interests of all wto members, including developing and least developed countries. i join the majority of the ep in calling for a more balanced system that takes into account the interests of all economic operators with a focus on smes and micro-enterprises, not just the interests of large multinational corporations. it is very important to strengthen the parliamentary dimension of the wto through the future structural reform of the organisation because only then can we ensure that transparency and democratic legitimacy that is lacking today. we live in a new era of global trade that is characterised by the legitimate demand of citizens to understand and follow multilateral trade negotiations in such a way as to ensure that the interests of nations and large global corporations do not conflict with the legitimate interests of citizens in all corners of the world. involving national parliaments and the ep in the process of negotiating and implementing trade agreements is the only way to meet the legitimate demands of citizens.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this resolution because i believe that strong trade is one in which the diversity of products and the number of members is constantly increasing, in a centralised market, where the rules applied are transparent and fair. a step towards such trade was taken by ecuador's accession to the trade agreement with colombia and peru, another decisive step in aligning with important, like-minded and rapidly developing countries in a region that is increasingly oriented towards asia and the pacific. the ecuadorian government has made numerous developments in recent years in all sectors, from protecting vulnerable social classes through strengthening human and workers' rights, to environmental rights, with ecuador hosting the highest concentration of species in the world's biodiversity. ecuador has also experienced economic growth, coupled with a reduction in poverty, and has ratified some ilo conventions.
in writing. ‒ i support the accession of ecuador to the trade agreement with colombia and peru, as it will open up markets and increase the stability and predictability of the trading environment. the accession of ecuador to the trade agreement with colombia and peru is another decisive step forward in the alliance with important, like-minded, and fast-growing countries and regions. i would like to call for a prompt implementation of the free trade agreement with ecuador, as it will contribute to reinforcing the social development model of the country, ensuring the necessary respective safeguard structures, the elimination of inequalities and the protection of workers, peasants and the environment. the agreement will provide improved access to the ecuadorian market for many key eu exports, for example in the automotive sector or for alcoholic beverages. however, the agreement will not only secure access to markets; more importantly it will also create a stable and predictable environment that will help boost and diversify trade and investment on both sides.
in writing. ‒ the accession of ecuador to the eu-colombia and peru fta represents an important step in strengthening eu trade relations with the andean community and more generally with latin america. the agreement is expected to boost trade and investment in both sides. more importantly, it will contribute to alleviating poverty and reducing inequality in ecuador. i highlight in particular the inclusion of trade and sustainable development provisions which will promote compliance and enforcement of the relevant ilo and environmental conventions in the three countries.
in writing. ‒ i voted for this resolution that enhanced the protocol on ecuador’s accession to the trade agreement between the eu, colombia and peru. ecuador’s exports to the eu will benefit both parties involved as this will ensure progressive social development, as well as transparency and sustainable development of policies.
in writing. ‒ the european union supports a policy of encouraging good relations and free trade in goods with latin american countries. in this context, relations with the andean countries are a priority. the union has already concluded a multilateral free trade agreement with colombia and peru in 2012. it is intended to replace the old general preferential scheme (gsp+) agreements which expired on 1 january 2015. ecuador thus remained outside a formal free trade agreement, although in practice it benefits from temporary preferential tariffs. despite the problems with fresh banana imports from ecuador last year, the accession of ecuador to the eu-colombia-peru multilateral agreement is necessary for the development of trade between the union and ecuador and the increase of mutual investments. this does not, however, mean that the eu must renounce certain conditionalities that it is imperative that the ecuadorian side meet, such as the respect of certain social conditions for workers in this country and respect for the environment. without these clauses, which are in line with the values promoted by the eu internationally, the signing of the agreement would not have the expected effects on the development of ecuador. the current initiative is an important step in that direction.

in writing. ‒ i voted for this resolution in order to maintain a cohesive and well-functioning internal market based on the eu legislation related to animal welfare, as well as to ensure that eu citizens are increasingly informed regarding their consumer choices.
in writing. ‒ i supported this text as all our voters agree on some very clear principles which need to be reflected in the unified eu strategy on animal welfare, but also in all national legislations. animals should not be made to suffer needlessly, regardless of cultural customs or traditions, as we are now living in a modern society. all acts related to animals, both pets and livestock, need to be properly regulated across the eu to insure a maximum level of quality of life and treatment for these animals. it is also a matter of human health – as the consumption of meat increases, animals which were mistreated, crowded, fed unhealthy feed or otherwise abused will have negative effects on the health of our citizens. therefore, both for the sake of the animals but also of european people, this new strategy should be properly implemented by the commission and member states.
in writing. ‒ the way a society treats animals, domestic or wild, is defining for its degree of civilization. the avoidance of ill-treatment of animals and the recognition of their rights are thus essential principles that deserve to be upheld by the european union. the current european regulations are insufficient and need a harmonised strategic framework for the next period, conferred by european parliament resolutions. this framework covers issues relating to the livestock sector, but also to the environment, public health, the internal market and the free movement (of pet animals). important issues are the persistence of the abominable practice of dog fighting, the presence of stray dogs in large cities, the violent killing of domestic animals, the use of animals as guinea pigs, the threat of extinction in the case of elite breeds or the use of wild animals in circuses. to avoid these practices, an integrated approach, promoted by the european commission for the period 2016-2020 and based on rigorous scientific criteria, is needed. the current resolutions are absolutely necessary for a united approach to the problem and for the general improvement of the animal situation in the territory of the member states.
in writing. ‒ in areas of the world affected by conflict or natural disasters, children are the most disadvantaged group. the fundamental right to education is an essential factor in the training of future professionals and must be protected at all costs. we cannot afford to have generations of children killed by various political crises or wars, and their prospects reduced by lack of education. children will only be able to deeply understand all other rights - social, economic, cultural and political - after they have acquired the education through which they will operate. education also plays a fundamental role in creating health awareness, thus facilitating health and sanitation interventions. in addition, lack of education should not be a factor of discrimination in the future. i believe that the role of host countries and international donors is essential in delivering this fundamental right through deeper involvement in education, psychological support and promotion of learning the language of the host country, to ensure better integration of refugee children. i therefore support the motion for a resolution - education for children in emergency and protracted crisis situations.
in writing. ‒ i believe that the european union must work with partner countries, other donors, the private sector and civil society to improve the prospects for education for young people in conflict and emergency situations, given the crucial importance of the stabilising role that young people can play after the end of conflict thanks to their eventual acquired skills for rebuilding infrastructure, basic services, health care and education systems, and to reduce the risks of an unemployed young population causing social unrest or slipping back into the vicious circle of violence.
in writing. ‒ education is a fundamental human right and the right of every child. it is vital in order to be able to enjoy in full all other social, economic, cultural and political rights. it is a catalyst for development, which improves the prospects of other interventions in the areas of health, sanitation, disaster risk reduction, job creation, poverty reduction and economic development. efforts in this direction will ensure that the principle of policy coherence is respected. i therefore absolutely agree on the need to ensure a more integrated, systematic and effective response to education needs in emergencies and i strongly believe that the eu must work with partner countries, other donors, the private sector and civil society to improve educational opportunities for young people in conflict situations. education has to be considered as an integral part of the humanitarian response. all actors must increase their commitment to education by mobilising the education cluster in the early stages of an emergency and by ensuring that sufficient funds are dedicated to it.
in writing. ‒ i voted for this resolution that will instate equal rights for every child, regardless of their ethnic origin and social, migration or residence status, particularly in terms of educational opportunities for young people in conflict or emergency situations.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this text as it is an important text on child protection and care in the european union. as the most vulnerable and yet the most important part of human society, it is vital that children are educated and prepared to deal with a wide variety of crises. it is a matter of survival but also societal development and all efforts should be made in ensuring adequate financing programmes for access to training courses and long-term education for children in emergency or extraordinary situations, both for those in the eu and those outside our borders.
in writing. ‒ children are the most vulnerable human group in the face of emergencies and crises. they should therefore be adequately protected against those risks. the right to education of a significant proportion of children worldwide is affected by armed conflicts, social unrest or natural disasters. also, a significant number of children are refugees or displaced. education is a fundamental right of children, which can provide them with prospects for a better life and the chance to overcome the difficult situations in which they find themselves. unfortunately, this right is not guaranteed everywhere by the states and governments in power. the european union has been involved in addressing the situation through the 'children for peace' initiative and through participation in un programmes. however, more is needed to eliminate discrimination against girls and children with disabilities, to prevent school drop-out, to combat illiteracy, to ensure education for children in crisis areas, to provide psychological support for children in conflict areas, to socialise refugee children, and to prevent child abuse and trafficking. a number of funds have already been created, but more humanitarian funds need to be allocated to education. it is therefore necessary to adopt this resolution.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this resolution because i consider cohesion policy to be one of the most important tools the european union has to combat inequality and support territorial and social cohesion in its regions. the 2014-2020 programming period has brought remarkable changes in the simplification approaches addressed in cohesion policy, but nevertheless certain reporting procedures, controls in relation to the european structural and investment funds are still burdened by bureaucratic mechanisms. these types of burdensome procedures become an impediment both for beneficiaries, especially small and medium-sized enterprises, ngos and municipalities with limited administrative and financial capacity, and for managing authorities. furthermore, another obstacle faced by the beneficiaries mentioned above is generated by the current over-regulation which causes delays, entailing certain indirect costs for those eligible to receive eu funding. all these difficulties lead to negative outcomes, reducing the impact of investments from european funding. immediate steps are needed to simplify and make cohesion policy more performance-oriented in order to increase the impact of european projects and to attract beneficiaries on a continuous basis.
in writing. ‒ although the reform of cohesion policy for the 2014-2020 programming period - which addresses simplification, application, management, reporting and control methods in relation to the european structural and investment funds - is still burdensome for both beneficiaries and managing authorities, especially those with the least administrative and financial capacity, i believe that the simplification of the rules on financial instruments under the esi funds should be promoted in order to align them more closely to the needs of beneficiaries and ultimately improve their use.
in writing. ‒ despite the reformed cohesion policy for the 2014-2020 programming period, in which simplification methods are addressed, application, management, reporting and control with respect to the european structural and investment funds are still cumbersome for both beneficiaries and managing authorities. complicated procedures can place a significant burden on beneficiaries. i therefore believe that the commission should introduce detailed guidelines on simplification in order to make the member states and their regions aware of their task of eliminating, or at least significantly reducing, the administrative burden and gold-plating arising at national and local levels. moreover, the commission should provide the member states and their regions with a roadmap for streamlining and simplifying control, monitoring and reporting activities.
in writing. ‒ i strongly agree with the commission providing the member states with a roadmap for simplifying control, monitoring and reporting activities. moreover, what is very needed is a simplification of the rules governing financial instruments within esi funds.
in writing. ‒ i voted for a reformed cohesion policy that will reduce the burden of complicated procedures on beneficiaries, particularly small and medium-sized businesses, ngos and municipalities, which are in need of eu funding.
in writing. ‒ there is a wide consensus across the european union that the level of bureaucratic hurdles, administrative burdens and lack of access to information are severe enough to deeply hinder the implementation of the cohesion policy. we have a wide number of reports, from grass-root organisations to administration officials, that there are problems with its transparency, with its language, with its accessibility for all stakeholders. that is why i voted for this motion for a resolution and i sincerely hope its recommendations will be taken into account.
in writing. ‒ i voted for the resolution entitled ‘towards simplification and performance orientation in cohesion policy 2014-2020’. i believe that, despite the considerable steps towards more clarity and coherence in european structural and investment fund management in the 2014-2020 multiannual financial framework, there is still room for simplifying the application, implementation and reporting tasks for beneficiaries. in my view, this would especially require more guidance by the commission towards member states on administrative streamlining and promotion of best practices. nevertheless, simplification should never be carried out to the detriment of the safe use of esi funds and ultimately of the eu budget. this is why i believe that there is a need to ensure a proper balance between simplification and the detection and prevention of irregularities and fraud through the use of operational tools like the arachne database.
in writing. ‒ effective implementation of eu cohesion policy requires simplifying current procedures and focusing on achieving tangible results. important steps have been taken so far to simplify the agenda for the 2014-2020 multiannual financial framework. despite these steps, however, the implementation, management, reporting and control of the structural and investment funds remain cumbersome processes for beneficiaries and implementing authorities. the most important impact is felt by small and medium-sized enterprises, non-governmental organisations and municipalities, which are in the greatest need of european funding. this significantly reduces the impact of european funds on the development of the regions of the member states. at the same time, the duplication and differences that arise in audit work and methodology require a unification of practices and a greater focus on efficiency and results. in this regard, the commission should develop detailed guidelines on simplifying administrative procedures at member state level and developing common practices at european level, in order to avoid the bottlenecks that arise. digitalisation and simplification of application procedures by providing all relevant information can be useful for this purpose, if a stronger focus is placed on the needs of beneficiaries. the present resolution is a first step in the right direction.

in writing. the european commission adopted today a package of legislative proposals on the circular economy. the circular economy has a direct impact not only on the environment, but also on jobs, industry, energy, research, etc. the key actions in this package must aim at transforming the eu economy into a sustainable and competitive one. so, beyond the mandatory product design requirements, we need to encourage research and innovation and continuous training of the workforce. i also stress that often price is sometimes a barrier to putting circular economy principles into practice. as long as a product (electronic, electro-manager or other) costs less when new than when repaired, the consumer's choice is obvious. last but not least, ensuring sustainable access to raw materials is essential for the competitiveness and growth of the eu economy and for the objectives of the europe 2020 strategy. main raw materials, including renewable and secondary raw materials, need to play an important role in production processes in the circular economy. therefore, we need to improve the availability of secondary raw materials data and support eu-wide research on the flow of raw materials.
in writing.– there are lots of compelling benefits of a circular economy. most of them are environmental, such as the improvement of our living environment, the protection of scarce natural resources or the reduction in greenhouse gas emissions. there are strong economic benefits as well, like the sustainable availability of raw materials, job creation within a more labour intensive production model and the decoupling of economic growth from the use of resources. nevertheless, the real driver behind the need for a new economic and consumption model is that we do not have a choice; we are already witnessing the irreversible ecological damage we are doing to our land and marine environment. i am happy that the commission stuck to its promise to present its new circular economy strategy before the end of the year and i am looking forward to exploring it in detail. i do hope that through this strategy we can ensure the long-term economic predictability that is needed to enable the technological development and investment in a new, circular economy.
in writing. the concern of the author of this report for the respect of human rights with regard to economic migrants and asylum seekers is admirable. but turning frontex into an institution that deals with alleged violations of immigrants' rights is unacceptable. the purpose of frontex is to defend and protect the eu's borders and, in the meantime, to prevent by specific means the entry of persons who could trigger attacks such as the one in paris. the recommendation to create a mechanism for refugees to complain about human rights violations is welcome, but it does not need to be set up within frontex, which is an operational institution and must be a body whose purpose is the security of the eu and its citizens. by giving frontex another, predominantly bureaucratic, mission, the commission will only diminish its ability to effectively cope with the mission entrusted to it at its inception and i therefore believe that it would be a mistake at this time when the eu's borders are being weakened. i therefore believe that measures should be taken to strengthen and increase the response capacity of frontex to ensure the security of the eu's borders and not invent bureaucratic obstacles.

demonstrates how much thought and energy went into it. the report showed that cities are of an ever—growing importance for all of us, quite simply because more and more of us are living in the city – 80% of europeans live in urban areas. so it is logical that we have to tackle some serious challenges in urban areas: congestion, demographic change, road safety, access to mobility and air pollution, including co2. the report reflects these challenges and proposes solutions that can be manifested. i will not go through all of them, but will mention only three that i find particularly important at this point. first, sustainability and urban mobility plans. these have proven to be a very useful instrument and show that voluntary instruments can work very well. this is encouraging for our efforts to support cities through the exchange of best practices and guidance. so, i would ask members, when back in their constituencies, to support the commission in promoting these. an intelligent transport system is the second area. members may be aware that the commission is running a platform for cooperative intelligent transportation systems (c—its). the aim is to deploy c—its as soon as and city logistics. we fully agree on this point. digitalisation of transport is therefore a personal priority for me as well. the third area is investment and innovation. both are key enablers for jobs and growth. let us reflect together on how we can support cities in attracting more investment and how this investment can support innovation and how innovation can support sustainability. the report confirms that innovation in urban mobility offers huge opportunities. just take clean transport and the multiple benefits that decarbonisaton of transport offers. let us stop associating decarbonisation with cost and start thinking of it in terms of investment. with urbanisation as a global mega-trend, i am convinced that it will really pay off and will contribute to the commission’s agenda for growth and new jobs. let me also mention efsi at this point, which is an appropriate mechanism to address its needs. urban mobility is such a rich topic that i would need to mention many more issues to be complete – road safety, the sharing economy, active mobility, efsi, save and the cohesion funds, multimodality and many more. but now it is time for the debate. i am really looking forward to hearing members’ concrete comments and i will be very happy to respond to their proposals at the end of the debate.

in writing. ‒ i voted for this report that calls for the setting up of a frontex individual complaints mechanism, laying down the structure, lodging and admissibility of complaints.
in writing. ‒ the ombudsman and the european parliament are right in calling for an effective mechanism to monitor respect for fundamental rights in all the activities of frontex, as it is also the case of other eu institutions, bodies and agencies. the setting—up of an individual complaint mechanism is especially important in the light of the highly sensitive nature of frontex’s activity, and also if we consider the long-term plans to extend the current legal remit of frontex and to transform it into an independent border guard service. nevertheless, i believe that any new legal obligation concerning an individual complaint mechanism should be matched with adequate financial and human resources and, on the other hand, should contain appropriate safeguards preventing the misuse of a complaint mechanism in a way to ensure that frontex is still able to effectively perform its tasks.
in writing. ‒ the intensification of migration to eu member states in recent months requires amendments to certain regulations on european migration management tools. one such instrument is frontex, which contributes to the defence of the union's external borders. ensuring the security of the member states is a key condition for the viability of the european construction. however, in the context of the intensification of the terrorist phenomenon, there is a tendency to attribute to all migrants from conflict zones close to the union's borders intentions that they do not have and to manage this problem by limiting their legitimate rights. in the event of such a breach, migrants should have the right to petition frontex individually, either in person or through representatives. the complaint to the european ombudsman concerns this very issue, which is not currently covered by any european regulation. if frontex staff were responsible for the violation of the fundamental rights of migrants, then these rights would be significantly reduced and there would be no danger of inhuman treatment of these groups. of course, that mechanism must also act as a filter on the admissibility of those petitions on a case-by-case basis. the adoption of the current document is necessary to avoid potential abuses.
in writing. ‒ in 2012, the european ombudsman opened an own-initiative inquiry into frontex's implementation of its fundamental rights obligations. in view of the increasing humanitarian and legal challenges facing the eu at its external borders and the intensification of the operations carried out by frontex, a mechanism capable of processing individual complaints concerning alleged violations of fundamental rights occurring during the agency's operations or cooperation with third countries is necessary, thus becoming a body of first instance for the submission of complaints. an individual complaint mechanism can only be effective if both potential complainants and agents taking part in frontex operations are informed about the right of persons to complain, through effective and gender-sensitive information, in the official languages of the eu, as well as in languages that asylum seekers and migrants understand. the establishment of a transparent and effective mechanism for individual complaints would provide citizens with the opportunity to exercise their right to an effective remedy when their fundamental rights are threatened. the report deals with these issues, and i therefore voted in favour of it.
in writing. i voted in favour of the special report of the european ombudsman on the own-initiative inquiry into frontex. the report welcomes the european ombudsman's own-initiative inquiry into frontex, but also frontex's current efforts towards stronger respect for fundamental rights. among the proposals included in the report is the establishment of a mechanism capable of handling individual complaints about alleged violations of fundamental rights during frontex operations or cooperation with third countries, with the aim of making it a first-instance complaints body.
in writing. ‒ sustainable urban mobility has to be one of our main priorities and a key to boost the social and economic conditions in cities whilst preventing growing inequalities and fighting against climate change. cities are the drivers of growth and economic activity, generating over 80% of eu gdp, but they are also often unequal places, with extreme divisions and with inadequate attention given to the needs of disabled people, the elderly, and others who are vulnerable. supporting and promoting walking and cycling in particular should be a high priority. i support the sustainable urban mobility plans as an important tool for providing adequate and safe mobility solutions for all citizens (including also persons with reduced mobility), improving quality of life in cities by fostering modal shift towards sustainable modes of transport, and promoting efficient, affordable, safe and accessible public transport as an integral part of sustainable urban development.
in writing. ‒ i understand the importance of urban mobility, which is why i voted for the report as a whole. we need sustainable strategies that require investment. we need to move towards the digitisation of transport and we need to decarbonise it, but through investment and not by banning a particular type of fuel. that's why i didn't vote for the amendment calling for the end of fossil fuel subsidies. the amendment didn't pass. i think we need to set ourselves targets that each member state can achieve through investment. for this reason, i did not vote for amendment no 32 part 3. reducing emissions is necessary to improve lives, but we need to gradually set targets that can be supported by investment without affecting jobs.
in writing. ‒ i fully agree with the view that land planning is crucial to creating long-term, efficient and safe transportation networks that will have a strong impact on traffic volumes. safety is essential to the development of any sustainable urban projects. furthermore, all stakeholders, especially eu citizens, must be consulted and informed in order to ensure transparent planning, development and decision-making of urban development strategies. thus, i would like to call upon the member states to construct sustainable urban mobility plans.
in writing. ‒ urban mobility is often experienced as a constraint arising from over-reliance on private cars powered by traditional fuels. i voted for this report that calls for a faster shift to more sustainable modes of transport taking into consideration that today the mobility of eu citizens is still essentially based on cars.
in writing. ‒ there are numerous harmful effects of the current transport model on the fundamental elements of the natural environment, including air, water, soil and various ecosystems. as there is no one-size-fits-all solution for urban areas, as cities in the european union have specific situations and needs, which are determined by geographical location, climate or demographic structure, safety must always be considered a key element of all sustainable urban transport plans. estimates show that 82% of eu citizens will live in urban areas by 2050. new practices such as car-sharing alongside cycling, walking and public transport are developing. energy efficiency and the use of energy from renewable sources, which imply a low level of carbon emissions, are essential for achieving sustainable urban mobility. i believe that supporting urban mobility is possible and necessary for an integrated approach, with sustainable urban transport contributing to reducing energy consumption, air and noise pollution, accidents, traffic congestion, land use and soil sealing, and can also be one of the key drivers of sustainable economic growth.
in writing. i voted for the own-initiative report on sustainable urban mobility. the report finds that the transition to more sustainable modes of transport is very slow. the rapporteur therefore proposes that the european commission should require all member states and local authorities to have a sustainable urban mobility plan. such plans are absolutely necessary given that, according to forecasts, 80% of europeans will live in cities in the near future. urban mobility needs to be reoriented towards sustainable modes of transport in order to meet the major challenges of this century: climate, health and environmental protection.

mr president, the single market means first and foremost networks: gas and electricity, mainly. investment is needed in interconnecting national networks, and for this, not only funding but also political will is needed. joint projects are a win. the commission has to decide at national network level on the list of joint projects taking into account the level of interconnection with neighbouring states, available delivery capacity, existing absorption capacity, development of national networks. i think more important than the 10% or any other percentage in the future is the assessment of the need for interconnection based on the production-consumption situation in each member state. the energy mix is a national attribute. we have to respect the environment, but also the needs of the economy. coal must remain the raw material for energy production, with the application of modernisation and emission-related measures.
commissioner, ladies and gentlemen, when we launched the energy union framework strategy, we set out to target measures specifically on lowering energy costs for household consumers. one year on, i am concerned that more work is needed to achieve an energy market that supports european households and where the reduction in energy prices is reflected in the bills paid. the specific energy mix of each state should include both indigenous and locally or individually developed sources, in particular renewable sources. a favourable investment climate for them can contribute to the modernisation of energy infrastructure. in addition, access to low-cost energy-efficient technologies can encourage entrepreneurship, especially among young people. energy security is an essential element of the energy union. in this regard, projects linking the electricity markets of the cee region should be opened to the south-east and alternative energy supply routes should be continuously exploited.
in writing. the eu's internal energy market needs common standards for smart grids, which are key elements in ensuring stable supply and free flow of energy across borders, as well as investments in the interconnection of smaller-scale gas and electricity networks linking neighbouring regions. in order to develop these interconnections, it is beneficial for all european citizens to have better cooperation between the commission and the member states and, in particular, between the commission and the regional authorities. in addition, such cooperation can contribute to the proper planning of energy demand and supply in the eu internal energy market and can ensure cost-optimal security of supply. moreover, those interconnectors will allow electricity grids to redirect energy from surplus areas to deficit areas, thus allowing the market to respond instantly to supply shortages wherever they occur and to compensate for circadian and seasonal cycles.
in writing.– in light of the long-term target of achieving 80-95% reduction of greenhouse gases by 2050, the purpose of the future energy union is to ensure a free flow of energy across member states. i support the initiative of a future energy union plan that enables eu consumers to access gas, electricity and heating in a sustainable, democratic and cost-effective manner. according to the report, the eu’s fragmented energy market has a severe impact on europe’s competitiveness and energy security. the report stresses the increased demand for an efficient internal energy market that can deliver energy taking into account factors such as safety, social and environmental responsibility and affordable distribution. alongside market integration, price convergence is also a pressing concern taking into account the variable costs provided by different energy sources. the report underlines that it is imperative to support local production of energy (primarily renewable) and to pursue up-to-date technological changes, alongside new modes of production and consumption trends such as electric vehicles. as mentioned in the report, i emphasise the upmost importance of a cohesive internal energy market, alongside interconnectedness and resilience between the national and the union’s energy security and market objectives.
in writing. we are again discussing in the european parliament the single european energy market, which does not exist. this is why european citizens pay more for energy. in the absence of a single market and therefore of competition at european level, large national energy companies have the possibility of charging rents to consumers in each member state. it is inexplicable and reprehensible that some member states, which do not really want competition at european level, are resisting by defending their own companies. that is why it is time to make visible progress towards the achievement of the european single energy market.
mr president, modernising the trade mark regime at european level will help the system to work better. this instrument allows, in particular, the effective fight against counterfeiting and piracy. the costs of counterfeiting go up to 8% of international trade, and the real losers are consumers. that is why our key objectives through this legislation have been related to public health, the protection of jobs, but also the defence of fundamental rights. i am pleased that the european parliament has been able to reduce red tape by using this mechanism, increasing efficiency but also reducing costs by up to 37%. the new rules reduce the possibility of exceptions that can lead to abuse, but also allow for better coordination on products in transit. the generalisation of this system at european level will help the beneficiaries. the consideration of balancing revenues for national trade mark bodies will increase the fairness of the european system. in my country, i must say, romania, consumers, that is, citizens, are unfortunately often misled by counterfeit products. it is therefore essential that the european union intensifies information and communication campaigns aimed at both citizens and companies - i am referring in particular to smes - wishing to secure the protection of trade marks. a strong common system of trademark protection will strengthen the european economy in relation to its competitors and i want as many informed beneficiaries as possible from all european countries and, in particular, from my country, romania.

president of the eurogroup.– mr president, i think it was mr annemans who said that we have here a divided parliament. now, i have been a member of a national parliament for 12 years and i always think that it is a good thing that parliaments are divided, for the obvious reason that we have to represent different political ideas in our society. the real question is whether we can share common goals, whether we can find an agreement on the way forward, on the choice of instruments. i think, listening also to the different contributions from parliament, that there is quite a large agreement on the way forward, and it is about the right policy mix. those of you have said that we have made mistakes over the course of the crisis are right. we went into unknown territory at the beginning of the financial crisis, in the eurozone crisis, and we developed our instruments and we developed new frameworks for policy. we set up emergency mechanisms, we created new institutions to strengthen our economic cooperation, and we have come a long way, so there is no reason for cynicism. there is reason for optimism, for example if you see at what pace we have designed and set up the banking union, and yes, everyone who says we need to complete it now is right. one of the lessons that we should learn over the course of the history of the european union is that we should finish our projects and not set up a framework and leave it half finished. so let us finish the banking union. i am convinced that setting up and finishing the banking union will be more important for economic recovery than any other project at the moment. so that is what we should do and we know what we need to do. we need to fight the risks that are remaining in our banks and we need to make sure that it becomes more solid. as president juncker said, it protects the deposits, which is key for our citizens. let us get it done. part of that mix of instruments should also be strengthening investments. the commission has taken a strong initiative with the efsi. let us get it up and running. let us expand it if necessary. let us see that we get the investments going. completing the banking union will be crucial to get a stronger credit flow back to our smes, companies wanting to reinvest again and others opening for business. a lot of young people all over europe want to start businesses. can they get their hands on credit? that is what the capital markets union is about, that is what completing the banking union is about. and yes, part of that policy mix also has to be growth-friendly fiscal policy. one of the key issues that is holding us back, holding back our economic recovery, is the indebtedness of our societies – governments with high debt, households with high debt, smes sometimes with high levels of debt, which is holding back our recovery. but there is no quick fix. anyone who believes that with a snap of one’s fingers one can get rid of those high levels of debt is mistaken. it will take time, but we have to get through it and we have to get financing and credits for our economies. that is key, and fiscal policy will support that. demand is returning in many of our eurozone countries. growth has returned to all of our countries except for greece, and i am sure that working with greece as we are now in a very constructive mode, and taking difficult measures that will help get the greek economy back on track, is the way forward. yes, there are issues of balance – political balance, economic balance – within our eurozone, but do not be negative about what we have accomplished. we have come out of a deep crisis, we have strengthened our cooperation, we have strengthened our monetary union in many respects and let us continue to do that, but let us do it in a way that sticks and not in a way that brings us new problems. so if we take new steps forward, and we will do in the second phase of the five presidents’ report, let us design it well. let us build a monetary union that becomes more resilient to shocks, rather than creating new ones.

in writing. ‒ the european asylum support office is a body whose purpose is to strengthen cooperation on asylum between member states, to strengthen the implementation of the common european asylum system and to provide support to member states whose asylum and reception systems are under particular pressure. the european asylum support office benefits from the input of both the member states and some associated countries, in particular switzerland, iceland, liechtenstein and norway. the agreement with the swiss confederation has thus developed naturally, given the openness of that office towards countries which have concluded agreements with the union. the involvement of the swiss confederation in the work of the office has a positive impact on the support provided by the office, namely the exchange of good practices and expertise, the permanent and emergency assistance provided by the support office, the collection and analysis of information by the support office and the early warning and preparation system of the support office, which is why i voted in favour of this agreement.
in writing. ‒ the purpose of this proposal is to conclude the arrangement with switzerland on the modalities of its participation in the european asylum support office (easo). the main provisions of the arrangement foresee the full participation of switzerland in the activities of the support office, representation in the support office’s management board as an observer and without voting rights, and annual financial contributions by switzerland to the budget of the support office by an annual sum calculated, in accordance with its gdp, as a percentage of the gdp of all states participating in the support office’s work. switzerland accepted provisions concerning a possible increased contribution if the union contribution is increased. i support the adoption of the report, since i believe that member states must cooperate more closely on asylum matters.
in writing. ‒ i have voted in favour of this recommendation on the draft council decision on the conclusion that will set out preparations for the swiss confederation regarding the modalities for its participation in the european asylum support office.
in writing. ‒ through its bilateral treaties with the european union the swiss confederation has adopted various provisions of european union law in order to participate in the union’s single market. i have voted for this recommendation on the draft council decision that will define the modalities of the swiss confederation’s participation in the european asylum support office.
in writing. ‒ the existence of conflicts and crises in certain countries of the world means that the number of people seeking asylum for various reasons in the territory of the member states of the union, but also in neighbouring countries, is increasing accordingly. in accordance with the rules of international and humanitarian law, member states are obliged to grant these rights to persons who justifiably request them. the work of the european asylum support office is designed to coordinate and support asylum-seekers' assistance policies in host countries. this activity would not be possible, however, without the involvement of the member states and the eu associated states. the involvement is realised in concrete terms, at the level of day-to-day activities, but also by providing financial support to support these activities. the participation of switzerland in the bureau complements the institution's jurisdiction over the whole european territory. as a country located in the heart of the continent and heavily targeted by asylum seekers from all over the world, switzerland's participation in this european policy is beneficial both for the union and for the swiss state. the adoption of the present agreement is therefore necessary in order to achieve the most coherent european asylum policy.

in writing. ‒ the european union has good cooperative relations with all countries in the world that share its democratic values and norms. to this end, the european commission is in constant dialogue with those states interested in intensifying their cooperative relations with the union and the member states. an important area of cooperation is the issue of visa-free travel for short stays. these periods are usually for tourist or business travel. the abolition of the visa regime is a significant boost to the development of the two-way tourism sector. the caribbean is a favourite holiday region for citizens of the member states of the union, as it offers excellent natural conditions at any time of the year. in these circumstances, the abolition of the visa requirement for european citizens would facilitate organisational arrangements and increase the number of european tourists to the states in the area, with significant effects on the economies of those states. the benefits would be mutual, allowing our citizens easier access to holidays in this region of the world. for these reasons, i consider that supporting the adoption of the agreement between the eu and dominica, but also between the eu and trinidad and tobago, grenada, saint lucia, saint vincent and the grenadines, with a view to the abolition of short-stay visas, is an important impetus for the development of tourism.

in writing. ‒ the own resources decision is the key legal instrument that sets out the main elements of the system, in this case the size of the union budget. the new provisions are in support of the consolidation of the union budget and the prevention of potential losses. the member states must therefore have an own resources account opened in their treasuries on behalf of the commission or designate a body to do so. moreover, one of the provisions indicates the guarantee that no commissions or negative interest are charged for the own resources accounts, precisely to avoid exposing the budget to various risks. it also provides for the rationalisation of the annual adjustments to vat own resources and gni own resources. this report sets out concrete methods and procedures to meet the needs of the treasury and to avoid situations where the union budget could be exposed to financial risks, which is why i voted in favour of this report.
in writing. ‒ this report deals with the rules on making own resources available and the measures to meet cash requirements. it contains practical arrangements in respect of the establishment of traditional own resources, conservation of supporting documents, administrative cooperation, the applicable rate for the gni-based own resource, accounts to be kept for own resources, the timing for making them available and for making adjustments and provisions concerning cash management and irrecoverable amounts. by modifying the rules, the commission aims to avoid any problematic situation linked to technical recalculations. i voted in favour of the report.

in writing. ‒ like its title, this report deals with the rules on making own resources available and the measures to meet cash requirements. it contains practical arrangements in respect of the establishment of traditional own resources, such as the period for member states to be making the payments, the applicable rate for the gni-based own resource, the accounts to be kept for own resources, and provisions concerning cash management and irrecoverable amounts. by modifying the rules, the commission aims to avoid problematic situation linked to technical recalculations of the contributions to the european union’s budget. given the complexity of the european union’s own resources system, setting in place more efficient rules on how member states make their timely contributions to the european union budget available is essential to allow the commission to effectively manage its treasury. this report, which also highlights the curtail work of the high level group on own resources in delivering proposals for overcoming the deficiencies of the current system, will help us in making the own resources system more transparent and more efficient.

in writing. ‒ the european globalisation adjustment fund was set up to provide additional support to workers affected by the major structural changes in world trade practices brought about by globalisation. the purpose of the fund is therefore to provide support for redundant workers by providing assistance for reintegration into the labour market and a range of related measures, including benefits and various incentives. following the redundancies of 1 603 workers in 69 enterprises operating in the economic sector, finland submitted an application for custom software activities in order to be eligible for a financial contribution from the european globalisation adjustment fund to support these workers. the finnish authorities shall ensure that the principles of equal treatment and non-discrimination in access to the proposed actions are respected and shall ensure to the union structures that this financial contribution from the egf will comply with the procedural and substantive rules of the union on state aid. i believe it is important to provide financial support and to improve the access to employment of people who have been made redundant, which is why i voted in favour of this report.
in writing. ‒ the plenary voted on a report giving the green light for the mobilisation of the european globalisation adjustment fund (egf) in finland the application relates to 1 603 redundancies (almost half of them relate to microsoft mobile oy) in 69 enterprises operating in the area of computer programming/consultancy in several finnish regions within the reference period 30 july 2014 to 30 april 2015. the egf funding of eur 2 623 200 will contribute to help around 1 200 redundant workers via different types of measures such as coaching, employment and business services, training, subsidies, start-up grants, etc. the redundancies were caused by the major structural changes in the electronics industry. i therefore supported mobilisation of the egf.

in writing. ‒ the current report concerns the mobilisation of the eu globalisation adjustment fund (egf) for a total amount of eur 2 623 200 for the 1 603 workers made redundant in 69 enterprises operating in regions covering the whole of finland. the egf aims to enable a rapid, efficient and flexible response to emergency situations i therefore welcome the speedy evaluation period for this application, which was less than five months. i also welcome the measures taken by the finnish government to use this application for providing redundant workers with coaching and training, pay subsidies, start-up grants, and other means that steer towards entrepreneurship. i view that as an important step to tackle the decline in the ict sector finland has experienced in the past years. the egf is an important legislative and budgetary instrument the union has to provide additional support to workers across the union, who are suffering from the consequences of the global financial and economic crisis and to assist their reintegration into the labour market. for this reason i voted in favour of this current report.
i voted in favour of this report because i support the idea of promoting innovation and economic growth through more accessible and more efficient trademark registration systems for all european citizens. in the union, a trade mark may be registered either at national level, at the level of industrial property of each country or at the level of the union. this relationship implies coexistence and complementarity between national and european trade mark systems, in order to make them more efficient for businesses in terms of reducing the cost and complexity and shortening the time required to register those trade marks. it will also increase predictability and legal certainty. this commission initiative does not involve a new system but a modernisation and harmonisation of the trade mark registration system. i support this agreement, which supports most of the users' interests. but we must be careful in implementing it and make sure that it does not lead to high procedural costs for citizens in the various countries of the union.
in writing. ‒ protecting the community market against the penetration of counterfeit goods, particularly in relation to internet sales, is a key element for the community market. the proposal aims to strengthen cooperation between the european union intellectual property office and the offices in the member states, which will allow the agency to coordinate projects in the interest of the union. it is also desirable to ensure transparency of information to buyers so that they are aware of the measures they can take against counterfeit goods which infringe their eu trade marks. the importance of such communication and cooperation has been demonstrated through the conclusion of several union acts and commitments, and its efforts have had an impact on the perspective of intellectual property rights holders, whose property enjoys greater protection throughout the union. in order to strengthen the protection of registered trade marks and to combat counterfeiting of goods more effectively, without prejudice to wto rules, in particular the freedom of transit, the proprietor of a registered trade mark should be able to prevent third parties from importing goods into the union without authorisation and provided that they are identical with a registered european trade mark, or to support that purpose.

in writing. ‒ the trade marks package represents a key legal tool in order to fight against counterfeiting of products. it will foster innovation and economic growth by making trademark registration systems all over the eu more accessible and efficient. the system is already in place, but with the current modernisation it will be better functional. our priorities must be to preserve public health, safety and jobs, and to defend fundamental rights. parliament also achieved lower fees of up to 37%, less bureaucracy, more efficiency and a system that benefits the users of trade marks. i welcome the fact that the agreement found on goods in transit will ensure the smooth transit of generic medicines to developing countries. i believed that we secured a more effective way of combatting counterfeiting whilst at the same time ensuring that legitimate trade interests are not adversely affected.

in writing. ‒ the european trade mark must guarantee, in that order: reducing red tape, reducing waiting time, reducing costs, increasing protection and guaranteeing validity in the european trade mark system. i support the reform of the european trade mark award and administration system, but i also believe that we need to pay particular attention to the system of legislative harmonisation at member state level. we must strive to move in the same direction and to intervene at the level of the european commission when we see that harmonisation is not progressing as it should. i voted for the form proposed by the european parliament and the council because we need a coherent and uniform system of trademark management at european union level as soon as possible.
in writing. ‒ some of the european union's objectives can only be achieved through uniform legislation throughout the community, and one of these objectives is to protect registered community trade marks and to protect the community market against the penetration of counterfeit goods. the union framework needs legislative coherence in relation to intellectual property rights, which is necessary to better protect those rights and to enable any citizen of the union to benefit from them, regardless of the member state in which he or she is located. this appropriation is intended to cover the financing of the expenditure relating to the european union agency for fundamental rights and the european border and coast guard agency. for these reasons, i support increased protection of registered trade marks and more effective fight against counterfeiting of goods, without prejudice to wto rules, in particular the freedom of transit, and support this harmonisation, voting in favour.
in writing. ‒ i believe that this revision of the directive harmonising certain aspects of the trade mark legislation of the member states of the european union, which has been in existence for over 20 years, provides an opportunity to learn from the good practices identified and to further strengthen the harmonisation measures adopted by national trade mark offices in respect of the substantive and procedural aspects of trade mark legislation.
in writing. ‒ this directive aims at approximating eu countries' laws relating to trade marks, in order to foster the free movement of goods and services and free competition within the internal market. this approximation concerns the fundamental rules on trade marks acquired by registration. eu countries retain the right to organise the procedural aspect and the protection of trade marks acquired through use.

in writing. ‒ the report on the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council establishing a control and enforcement system applicable in the area covered by the convention on future multilateral cooperation in the north-east atlantic fisheries introduces new monitoring and enforcement measures in relation to fishing activities in the north-east atlantic. the main changes introduced by this proposal concern new measures on the prevention, deterrence and elimination of illegal, unreported and unregulated fishing, which are the responsibility of the port state, but also the integration of the notification procedures on port state control of foreign fishing vessels into a technological application, to the detriment of the traditional paper-based system. the european union is a contracting party to the convention on future multilateral cooperation in the north-east atlantic fisheries and it is therefore a matter of concern for the union's structures to ensure the long-term conservation and rational use of fisheries resources in the north-east atlantic area. i believe that a sustainable approach to these types of resources and the generation of social benefits is necessary, which is why i voted in favour of this report.
in writing. ‒ regulation (eu) no 1236/2010 is amended in order to incorporate three neafc (north-east atlantic fisheries commission) recommendations which have become binding for the contracting parties to neafc and consequently for the eu. the scheme will include further measures to help the fight against iuu fishing; other changes concern new provisions for transhipment operations as well as revised notification procedures.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report that will align the scheme with the fao agreement on port state measures to prevent, deter and eliminate illegal, unreported and unregulated fishing, approved by the eu in 2011 and instated since 1 july 2015.
in writing. ‒ the european union is a contracting party of the convention on future multilateral cooperation in northeast atlantic fisheries, which aims to ensure the long-term conservation and optimum utilisation of the fishery resources of the north-east atlantic area, providing sustainable environmental and social benefits. i have voted for this report that will establish the principle that vessels involved in a trans-shipment operation in the regulatory area as the receiving vessel must communicate the port of landing regardless of whether the landing is to take place in a port inside or outside the convention area.
in writing. ‒ fishing is one of the main economic activities in the member states of the european union. one of the areas with the largest contribution to the fishing quotas set annually by the european institutions is the atlantic area. fishing in this region is governed by the recently adopted convention on multilateral cooperation in the north-east atlantic fisheries, to which the european union is a contracting party and one of the main supporters. the convention aims at the long-term conservation and optimum use of fisheries resources in the north-east atlantic area and at the generation of sustainable social and environmental benefits. this document proposes to implement this convention and the recommendations adopted by the north-east atlantic fisheries commission by amending regulation (eu) no 1236/2010 to incorporate the provisions of the convention into european law. the amendment involves aligning the system with the fao agreement on port state competence measures to prevent, deter and eliminate illegal, unreported and unregulated fishing, as well as clarifying and monitoring by computer the activity of vessels involved in transhipment operations. i believe that the amendments proposed in the present report make an important contribution to the rational exploitation of marine resources in the north-east atlantic. i therefore support the adoption of this document in its current form.
in writing. ‒ the transit measures adopted by the union in relation to the candidate countries are designed to adjust the economic, social and political pace of the latter to the realities of the union institutions. however, any transit measure is only a temporary advantage to obtain a commercial framework and strengthen citizens' rights. naturally, such concessions or their possible suspension should be seen as an incentive to accelerate the political and socio-economic reforms outlined in the 'growth pact', which are indispensable for the western balkan countries to meet the requirements of the copenhagen criteria and the acquis. to this end, bosnia and herzegovina was urged to adapt the interim agreement on preferential trade with croatia following the accession of the latter to the european union on 1 july 2013. the commission proposal also seeks to eliminate an existing shortcoming, namely the absence of a human rights clause, or this idea should be welcomed, as a practical application of the treaties. for all these reasons, i give my vote to this measure.
in writing. ‒ the eu has granted autonomous trade measures (atm) since 2000 to the western balkan countries. these are unilateral preferences which allow unlimited duty-free access to the eu. the atms will expire after december 2015. the commission proposes to extend them until the end of 2020 for serbia, kosovo, albania, fyrom, montenegro, and bosnia and herzegovina. the proposal includes a human rights clause, which is important for us. previously, it was not possible to suspend trade preferences in the event of systemic breaches of human rights and the rule of law. because of croatia's accession to the eu it is necessary to adapt the trade part of the stabilisation and association agreements in force. these negotiations have been concluded with all western balkan countries, except bosnia and herzegovina, where they remain blocked. to increase leverage the commission proposal includes a provision to suspend the atms for bosnia as of 1 january 2016 if by then no solution has been found. the annual loss for bosnia and herzegovina is estimated not to be economically critical but it is a politically symbolic point. i supported this approach in order to get bosnia to engage in the negotiations while stressing the need for a mutually acceptable solution.
in writing. ‒ following the accession of croatia to the eu on 1 july 2013, bosnia and herzegovina has not yet agreed to adapt the interim agreement in order to take into account the preferential traditional trade between croatia and bosnia and herzegovina under the central european free trade agreement (cefta) which linked the two countries before 1 july 2013. i voted in favour of this report on the suspension of special commercial measures concerning bosnia and herzegovina until its acceptance of the interim agreement.
in writing. ‒ the european parliament has approved today the outcome of the interinstitutional negotiations on the amendment of the regulation concerning the autonomous trade measures for the western balkans. i welcome in particular the introduction of the possibility to temporarily suspend preferential trade measures in case of systematic violations of human rights. to this purpose the use of delegated acts is foreseen which guarantees the full involvement of the european parliament in the process.
in writing. ‒ trade between the eu and the western balkan countries is liberalised through a number of stabilisation and association agreements (saa) and an interim agreement (ia) in the case of bosnia and herzegovina. i have voted for this report on the european union’s stabilisation and association process and suspending its application with regard to bosnia and herzegovina until bosnia and herzegovina accept the eu methodology regarding the adaptation of the interim agreement.
in writing. ‒ the european union has always had cordial relations with bosnia and herzegovina, a country it has been involved in strengthening since its declaration of independence. one of the decisive areas for the country's development and stabilisation is free trade. in this respect, the eu has concluded an interim agreement with bosnia and herzegovina since 2000, which is a unilateral preferential arrangement under which it enjoys duty-free access to the eu for an unlimited period of time for most products, especially agricultural products. the commission is now proposing three main amendments to the agreement by extending the current preferences to allow time to align the preferences with those provided for in the stabilisation and association agreement, the introduction of a 'human rights' clause in the agreement allowing for the suspension of preferences in case of serious violations and the possible suspension of the agreement as of 1 january 2016 if the agreement is not adapted to include croatia in the preferential practices. the present report accepts these amendments, which it qualifies as conditional on the agreement respecting the principles of democracy and the rule of law, the implementation of effective economic reforms, regional cooperation with other western balkan countries and the strengthening of the administrative institutions of the bosnian state. in conclusion, the present document is an important step forward.

in writing. ‒ the report 'towards a european energy union' raises the issue of the global challenges facing the european union's energy system and highlights the need for a strategy to increase energy security, sustainability and accessibility. the achievement of these targets is thus achieved with a view to ensuring security of energy supply and reducing emissions, especially as the eu's 2030 energy targets include a 40% reduction in greenhouse gas (ghg) emissions compared to 1990 levels. furthermore, other dimensions to be achieved in order to build a secure and sustainable energy system are the completion of a fully integrated internal energy market at eu level, the reduction of energy consumption, which will lead to a reduction in energy imports and pollution, and, not least, the continuation of research and innovation projects. i voted in favour of this report because i believe that a joint effort by all member states is needed to make energy safe, sustainable and accessible for the citizens of the union.
in writing. ‒ the ep resolution of 5 february 2014 calls for the adoption of three mandatory targets: an energy efficiency target of 40%, a renewable energy target of at least 30% and a greenhouse gas emissions reduction target of at least 40% compared to 1990. the latter underpins the development of the decarbonisation dimension of the energy union and constitutes the most ambitious contribution to the international climate change negotiations with a view to a binding climate change agreement at cop 21 of the unfccc, paris, december 2015. i support a multidimensional approach to climate and energy policies for 2030, based on mutually reinforcing, coordinated and coherent targets on greenhouse gas emission reductions, renewable energy sources and energy efficiency. i consider that a transparent, open, robust and inclusive governance system for 2030 is crucial to ensure that the objectives are implemented in a transparent and democratic way, ensuring regular information exchange, reporting and ensuring the full participation of the ep through the ordinary legislative procedure.
