in writing. ‒ respect for and promotion of the indivisibility and universality of human rights and their defence is one of the union's concerns, as it is committed to developing a common foreign and security policy guided by the principles of democracy, the rule of law, the universality and indivisibility of human rights and fundamental freedoms, respect for human dignity, and the principle of equality and solidarity. there are a number of rights that are threatened on a large scale, such as freedom of thought, conscience, religion and belief. the number of infringements is increasing considerably, particularly in third countries. the union must take prompt and responsible action when it is informed of serious human rights violations in third countries, especially those led by authoritarian regimes. it is also important to take measures at the domestic level, given the cases of discrimination and violation of rights that occur in the roma situation, in the situation of migrants and refugees. immediate responses are needed in such cases in order to maintain the credibility and consistency of the union's external human rights policy. i voted in favour of this report because i believe that it is imperative to guarantee human rights and democratic values and to have internal and external policies to transpose these principles.
in writing. ‒ i welcome the final agreement reached on the opinion on annual report on human rights and democracy in the world 2014. negotiations have been positive and enriching, and i believe the opinion will support the work of our colleagues in the afet committee. we made a strong connection between insisting on human rights, gender equality, good governance, peace and security and the goal of eradicating poverty and inequalities as well as achieving the sdgs. moreover, we recalled that cultural diversity cannot be invoked to infringe human rights guaranteed by international law. human rights must be at the core of our development agenda: we therefore stressed the need to ensure that the 2030 agenda for sustainable development is underpinned by a human rights based approach. we mentioned the importance of the addis ababa agenda and we decided to strongly condemn, in the opinion, the use of harmful practices on women and of the use of rape as a weapon of war. last but not least, we reminded the commission and member states that the agreements concluded with developing countries must include binding clauses on human rights and that the commission must conduct systematic human rights impact assessments of trade and investment agreements.
in writing. ‒ i supported this text as it outlines some of the most important developments in the world and in the eu on human rights. unfortunately, i do not believe the overall situation is improving – in fact, there is a clear deterioration in the universal protection of human rights in many parts of the world. more than ever, the eu needs to be cohesive and coherent in its external dialogue, and this means a lot more coherence between the member states and the eeas and council. at the same time, i expect that we have learned much from past mistakes, being capable of investing in smarter policies and having more lasting dialogues with actors who can influence the balance on these issues.
in writing. ‒ the annual human rights report is a basic instrument of european democracy. it is therefore commendable that the eu is also using this tool to promote and protect human rights and support the foundations of democracy around the world. i also want to stress the need to implement the action plan for human rights and democracy 2015-2019 adopted by the council. however, implementation needs to be accompanied by ample resources and constant support, including from member states. another point i want to stress in this explanation of vote is the relationship between the business environment and human rights. even if it does not seem so at first sight, a primary responsibility for the impact of policies and instruments for the protection and promotion of fundamental human rights lies with the private sector. according to this report, european companies must contribute to the establishment and promotion of human rights and in no way, through their main or secondary activity, in any way affect their universality.
in writing. ‒ the 2014 annual report on human rights and democracy in the world and the european union's policy on the matter is based on the principles of democracy, the rule of law, the universality and indivisibility of human rights and fundamental freedoms, respect for human dignity, and respect for the un charter, the eu charter of fundamental rights and international law. one of the major concerns highlighted in this report is that human rights and democratic values are increasingly under threat, especially in authoritarian regimes, especially those relating to freedom of expression, thought, conscience and religion, assembly and association, as the number of human rights defenders who are under attack globally increases. i commend the european external action service (eeas) and the commission for their comprehensive reporting on the eu's human rights activities in 2014 and would like to underline that enhanced cooperation between the commission, the council, parliament, the eeas and eu delegations is vital as it is at the heart of all eu policies with an external dimension, especially on security, employment and migration.
in writing. ‒ one of the bloodiest conflicts in europe since the second world war was in the balkans, and its end was marked by the peace agreement of 14 december 1995, which also aimed to create a functioning state in which the three constituent nations could live in harmony in a state governed by the rule of law in bosnia and herzegovina. the european council welcomes the fact that the european union has taken the necessary steps to ensure that the european union's external relations are as close as possible to those of the member states, and that the european union is able to contribute to the implementation of the lisbon strategy, in particular by supporting the implementation of the lisbon strategy, and by supporting the implementation of the lisbon strategy. i support this resolution, given both the state's candidacy for the european union and the need to bring to justice the perpetrators of war crimes, in order to facilitate the process of reconciliation and peaceful coexistence of all three ethnic communities. that is why i voted in favour of this resolution.
in writing. ‒ the dayton agreement marked a great victory for diplomacy over war, putting an end to a conflict that fuelled atrocities that horrified the world, claimed over 100 000 lives and displaced millions of people, and laid the foundation of the territorial integrity, sovereignty, international personality, and political independence of bosnia and herzegovina. i support the call for better coordination of efforts at all levels and more attention to the most vulnerable displaced people, including roma and women victims of violence. more efforts are needed in the field of reconciliation and democratic development and consolidation as bosnian society is still divided along ethnic lines. i believe we can play an important role towards facilitating an agreement among the constituent peoples on the implementation of the ruling which will guarantee equal rights for all citizens of bosnia and herzegovina, further enhancing human rights commitments.
in writing. the dayton agreement adopted in 1995 marked a watershed moment in the history of the western balkans and the bloody conflicts that have plagued the region in the recent past. beyond the atrocities committed by the warring sides in the bosnian war, the dayton agreement is a triumph of diplomacy over arms and a sign that solutions achieved through dialogue between all the parties concerned are the only alternative to the conflict. by adopting this agreement, the foundations of the current state of bosnia and herzegovina were laid, with respect for the will of each of the three constituent ethnic communities: muslim, serb and croat. the european union was the main supporter of this agreement and continues to support the state development of bosnia and herzegovina on its path towards full integration into the european community. it involves strengthening internal democracy and the rule of law, as well as implementing economic reforms to bring it into line with european structures and raise the living standards of the population. dayton continues to be a model for resolving a crisis by peaceful means, a good example for the ongoing conflicts in ukraine, syria, iraq, libya and yemen.
it is important to emphasise that the regulation of arms exports by member states is essentially a matter of national competence. the council common position only provides for communication between member states. although the report criticises the member states for their systematic violations of point 8 of the common position and calls for the establishment of a sanctions system, i think we should take note that in this sensitive area the member states will never surrender their sovereignty. i feel that the question of the compatibility of the arms export activities of the member states with the union's foreign policy objectives is a more important one. i feel the need for increased coordination particularly in this negotiating framework. the existence of common foreign policy guidelines presupposes that the arms export policies of the member states do not undermine our common interests.
in writing. ‒ the spread of armed conflict is a matter of european union security itself and, in an increasingly globalised world, a threat to global stability and security, and this includes in particular the conflicts in ukraine, syria, iraq, libya and yemen, as well as all international conflicts. in addition to the humanitarian support the eu provides, the sources of these conflicts must be addressed, and arms transfers to states in conflict have contributed to these conflicts. the defence industry should serve as a tool for guaranteeing the defence and security of the member states, ensuring a secure supply regime in the eu and at the same time contributing to the implementation of the cfsp and the csdp in an enhanced manner and should not fuel insecurity and armed conflict, inherently linked to serious violations of human rights and fundamental freedoms. in the context of the large and profitable business of the illicit arms trade, effective arms export control regimes need to be put in place. i consider that an important step has been taken by the entry into force of the arms trade treaty, which is why i voted in favour of this report.
in writing. ‒ the european union, in the post-world war ii context, was founded on the principles of peace and prosperity. we are aware that the uncontrolled spread of weapons poses a serious threat to peace and security, but also to human rights and sustainable development. the fact that, globally, every minute, a person dies from gun violence, and in the same period, 15 new weapons are manufactured is disturbingly worrying. the council common position of 8 december 2008 on the definition of common rules governing the control of exports of military technology and equipment has not been fully implemented and consistently interpreted by the member states. it is therefore essential to pursue the consistent application of the eight criteria. in addition, the lack of mechanisms to sanction breaches of the criteria is a concern and therefore the common position should provide for the modalities for carrying out independent checks and for the application of sanctions in case of breaches of the criteria. i therefore support the report on arms exports - implementation of common position 2008/944/cfsp.
in writing. ‒ the unprecedented spread of armed conflicts is a huge threat to world stability and security and has determined a less stable and less secure neighbourhood for the eu area; arms transfers to states in conflict are significantly contributing to these conflicts and situations. i therefore strongly support the report, which will allow better regulation for arms exports. we have a key role in preventing irresponsible exports of arms to countries that violate human rights and fundamental freedoms, and regulating the international arms trade must be a global ambition. it is fundamental to support transparency, and to promote adherence to the highest regional and international standards, such as the arms trade treaty and the eu common position on arms export control. this legally binding framework demonstrates the determination of eu member states to prevent the export of military technology and equipment that might be used for undesirable purposes such as internal repression or international aggression, or contribute to regional instability; we therefore have to fully support its implementation.
in writing. ‒ i have voted in favour of this text as it is vital in the context of greater efforts for world security to step up our efforts in controlling arms trade and proliferation. the near vicinity of the eu has grown more unstable in the past few years, and small and large weapons are a basic source of instability. the arms trade treaty was a welcome development in this context, just like the recent efforts of the member states in upholding the provisions of the common positions. however, the development of new technologies puts even more urgency in the eu's efforts - as the risks for these technologies to fall in the wrong hands through unregulated exports are great.
in writing. ‒ the european union and its member states have a significant arms industry, with total exports of €36.7 billion, thus contributing a significant share to the union's economy. at the same time, however, the global security environment has seen a worrying proliferation of armed conflicts with high civilian casualties, many of them close to the union's borders and adversely affecting member states. on the other hand, the use of arms exported by eu countries for self-defence purposes is considered legitimate, especially in the case of the conflicts in ukraine and iraqi kurdistan. in this regard, strict regulation of arms exports to third countries is necessary on the basis of the arms trade treaty. the adoption of common position 2008/944/cfsp, to which a number of western balkan states, efta and canada have also subscribed, is an obvious step forward in this area, by making exports subject to respect for certain european values and freedoms and human rights in third countries, as well as to european security imperatives. more transparency in the publication of annual reports on arms exports is recommended, as well as public scrutiny of dual-use military products, in particular new technologies.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on arms exports, as the uncontrolled proliferation of weapons poses a serious threat to peace and security, human rights and sustainable development. worldwide, one person dies every minute from gun violence, and 15 new weapons are manufactured in the same period. moreover, arms transfers to unstable regions can contribute to the emergence of new conflicts and the eu needs to be extremely vigilant in this regard, as eu member states were responsible for 25.4% of global arms deliveries in 2010-2014. arms export control is part of the eu's foreign and security policy and must be carried out in accordance with the principles enshrined in the founding treaties, such as promoting democracy and the rule of law, preventing conflicts and strengthening international security. the eu must ensure a coherence between arms exports and its credibility as a global human rights promoter. a common position is therefore needed on arms exports, and relations between member states in this area, which is the exclusive competence of the states, need to be strengthened.
in writing. ‒ food security has always been a concern of the european institutions, taking into account that the un estimates that by 2050 the global population will increase by 25% to 9.7 billion. cheap, quality food, easily accessible to consumers, requires a balance between all the actors involved in this process. there is no doubt that stimulating innovation and the development of new plant varieties can be responses to these challenges, and plant breeders play a key role in species diversification and productivity gains. plant breeding is essential for food security and the effective protection of those working in research guarantees the development of this sector. at the same time, we need to ensure that all legal uncertainties regarding the rights of patent holders and the exceptions granted to breeders are fully clarified, so as to avoid anything that could affect the development of the plant breeding sector and, by implication, the possibility for farmers to benefit from productive and accessible varieties. the european patent office has to be extremely careful in its work, lest it end up patenting something that has been around for hundreds of years and that will certainly endanger food safety.
in writing. ‒ access to biological plant material encompassing plant traits is absolutely necessary for boosting growth and innovation and developing new varieties in order to guarantee global food security, tackle climate change and prevent monopolies within the breeding sector, while at the same time providing more opportunities for smes. unrestricted access to biological material will stimulate the innovative strength of the plant breeding sector. undermining the innovative ability of the plant breeding sector to develop new varieties poses a threat to global food production and food security and will have a negative impact on european competitiveness and may lead to monopolies on the food market. i therefore would like to express my concern about the recent decision of the enlarged board of appeal of the epo in cases g2/12 (tomatoes) and g2/13 (broccoli), which could lead to an increase in the number of patents, granted by the epo, for natural traits which are introduced into new varieties by using essentially biological processes such as crossing and selection.
in writing. the european union's agriculture and food policy focuses on ensuring that adequate quantity and quality of food is provided to european consumers. the recent decision by the european patent office to patent certain plant characteristics is a restrictive interpretation of the european patent convention, which may have a negative effect on european competitiveness and lead to monopolies on the food market by reducing the diversity of consumer products on offer. however, biological hybridisation processes are essential practices to increase plant resistance to various pests or diseases that may occur and that may endanger the food security of european citizens. unrestricted access to biological material is necessary to stimulate research and innovation in this field, which is jeopardised by the decision of the european patent office. for this reason, i believe that a single european policy on hybridisation is needed, which supports the production of resistant plant varieties, does not affect european and global agricultural production and continues to offer the widest range of products to european consumers.
in writing. ‒ the eu's commitment to human rights, the rule of law and democracy and to all peoples of the world, including the burundian people, leads to a strong condemnation of the actions taking place in burundi, such as the use of force against peaceful, unarmed demonstrators, human rights abuses by state officials, extrajudicial executions, arbitrary arrests and detentions, torture, attacks on independent media, harassment and assassination of human rights defenders, unjustified restrictions on freedom of peaceful assembly and expression, and the displacement of over 200 000 people as a result of violence. the eu's partnership with burundi is governed by the cotonou agreement, which provides that all parties are obliged to respect and implement the provisions of this agreement, in particular with regard to human rights. the union supports the establishment by the prosecutor-general of the republic of burundi of a commission of inquiry to investigate the api crimes of 13 october 2015, in particular as burundi is also a party to the international criminal court and has undertaken to combat impunity for crimes within its jurisdiction. we are in danger of a regional crisis, as evidenced by the constant exodus of refugees to neighbouring countries, and that is why i voted in favour of this proposal.
in writing. ‒ the increasingly pronounced insecurity and the constant worsening of violence in burundi (a recent massacre took place in the past few days that killed about 90 people) have dramatic consequences for the country and the entire region. the burundian authorities should participate in consultations with a view to finding a solution acceptable to the parties in order to put an end to the violation of human rights, democratic principles and the rule of law. the security and freedom of citizens, human rights defenders, journalists and the press, as well as the restoration of the rule of law, are essential. i strongly support the immediate cessation of violence, human rights violations, political intimidation of opponents and the immediate disarmament of all armed groups allied to political parties, in strict accordance with international law and human rights. the eu must continue to actively support all diplomatic efforts to find a consensual solution to the crisis and be ready to come up with new solutions as the situation evolves. the eu must also adopt new restrictive measures targeting those who, by their actions or by their promoted speech, have provoked or could provoke acts of violence, repression and serious human rights violations.
in writing. ‒ i would like to express my fear for the escalation of violence in burundi and my solidarity with all victims of violence, as well as with the people forced to move in an atmosphere of insecurity and uncertainty. i regret the continuing political impasse in the country, marked by the refusal of a real dialogue between the actors. any speech and incitement to hatred could aggravate the already precarious situation and is therefore totally unacceptable. these developments may have tragic consequences for burundi and for the entire region. we must by all means cooperate to find a solution to stop the violence in the country. i support the call on all parties, both government and opposition, to show the utmost restraint in language and to avoid triggering a cycle of violence at all costs. i also would like to recall that it is primarily the responsibility of the burundian government to protect its population.
in writing. ‒ the european union is one of the world's leading advocates of human rights and fundamental freedoms. the union also places particular emphasis on the development of democratic practices and the rule of law in the various countries of the world. burundi is a developing african state where these eu-promoted values are threatened by the current regime in power. specifically, we're talking about an ongoing humanitarian catastrophe, with 200,000 refugees in neighboring countries and about 250 people killed this year alone. he was also responsible for the repression of the opposition and the repression of the civil society. the situation thus created is likely to threaten the security of the entire east african area and to generate a new outbreak of immigration. the un security council has already adopted a resolution calling on the incumbent government to remedy the situation as a matter of urgency, but this has not yet happened. the eu has introduced a series of sanctions against the current burundian president's entourage, under article 96 of the cotonou agreement. however, the measures taken may prove insufficient and if dialogue is not a solution, the deployment of peacekeeping troops is the last alternative.
in writing. ‒ virunga national park (vnp) is africa's oldest national park and a unesco world heritage site, recognised worldwide for its unique habitats with the highest biodiversity in africa. currently, concessions have been negotiated between the drc and soco (uk) and total (france) in the protected area of the park, which is unacceptable as the exploitation of oil will cause irreversible damage to the pnv. in addition, these agreements were made in violation of the paris convention for the protection of the world cultural and natural heritage, the 1992 convention on biological diversity, the ramsar convention and congolese law. knowing that the pnv currently generates an annual economic value equivalent to usd 48,9 million and that in a stable situation the park could contribute to economic growth and tourism development and could generate usd 1 billion in annual value, creating 45 000 jobs, i encourage the european external action service to take all necessary measures to ensure that soco international plc and its drc subsidiary publicly commit to cease all exploration and exploitation activities for the resources of the virunga park. i chose to vote in favor of this resolution.
in writing. ‒ the virunga national park is a park rich in biodiversity in africa, and a unesco world heritage site. however, oil and logging concessions were permitted there, especially for the benefit of european companies, in violation of international environmental agreements signed by the drc. the park has also become the place of illegal practices such as poaching. moreover, the presence of armed groups that control these concessions give rise to abuse and serious violations of human rights. the commission has to make active steps and build viable strategies to help protect virunga national park and to support sustainable development in the democratic republic of congo. we must emphasise the importance of virunga national park, address the root causes of armed conflicts in the region and ask the government of the drc to protect the park and support development.
